129.title: Stability & Control of Aerospace Vehicles
129.description: Aircraft and spacecraft stability and control. Derivation of fundamental equations of motion for aircraft/spacecraft. Fundamentals of feedback. Aircraft flight control systems. Spacecraft attitude control systems.

130A.title: Aircraft Performance & Design
130A.description: Major aircraft design experience with multiple realistic constraints including aerodynamics, performance analysis, weight estimation, stability and control, and appropriate engineering standards.
130A.prereq_text: EAE 127 C- or better; EAE 129 C- or better (can be concurrent).

135.title: Aerospace Structures
135.description: Analysis and design methods used in aerospace structures. Shear flow in open, closed and multicell beam cross-sections, buckling of flat and curved sheets, tension field beams, local buckling.
135.prereq_text: ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better; EAE 126 or EAE 127 recommended.

138.title: Aircraft Propulsion
138.description: Analysis/design of modern aircraft gas turbine engines. Development/application of cycle performance prediction techniques. Introduction to design of inlets, compressors, burners, turbines, and nozzles. Cycle design for specific applications.

142.title: Orbital Mechanics
142.description: Satellite orbits, multistage rockets, current global boosters, and new technologies. Design application problems include satellites, trajectory optimizations, and interplanetary trajectories.
142.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed EAE 189B prior to Fall Quarter 2013.

143A.title: Space Vehicle Design
143A.description: Governing equations and operational practices of robotic and human space travel. Principles of Systems Engineering are introduced and are used as a basis for a team project in spacecraft reverse-engineering and design.
143A.prereq_text: EAE 140 C- or better; EAE 142 C- or better.

012.title: Introduction to African Studies
012.description: Introduction to African Studies which will focus on the various disciplinary perspectives through which African society and culture are generally studied. A survey of methods, resources and conceptual tools for the study of Africa.

017.title: Women in African Societies
017.description: Gender relations in traditional and contemporary African society. Involvement of African women in politics, religion, the economy, the arts. African responses to feminist theory. Images of women in African literature.

083.title: The Politics of Black Food
083.description: Critical examination of the histories and politics of Black food traditions in the United States

107A.title: African Descent Communities & Culture in the Caribbean & Latin America
107A.description: Origin and development of African descent communities and cultures in the Caribbean, and Latin America. Similarities and differences among African descent communities and cultures in terms of religious practices, music, and national identity.

145A.title: Black Social & Political Thought
145A.description: Exploration and analysis of Black social and political thought in the Americas.

176.title: The Politics of Resources
176.description: Examination of the ways in which the processes of the extraction, purification and use of natural resources and the complex regimes of valuation and commodification they (re)produce lead to cooperation and conflict in contemporary Africa and beyond.

190.title: Topics in African & African-Diaspora Studies
190.description: Intensive treatment of a special topic or problem in African or African Diaspora Studies.
190.prereq_text: Upper division standing in African American & African Studies (AAS) courses or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in African-American & African Studies
192.description: Supervised internship in community, government, or private institutions, in all subject areas offered by the African American & African Studies Program.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 12 units of upper division study in African American & African Studies (AAS) courses; upper division standing.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in preparation of a senior honors thesis under the direction of faculty advisor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Afro-American Studies
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of major committee; upper division standing with major in African American & African Studies.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

298A.title: Directed Group Study in African American & African Diaspora Studies

298B.title: Directed Group Study in African Studies
298B.description: Directed group study in African Studies.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Selected topics in agricultural and environmental chemistry, presented by students.

299.title: Research
299.description: Arrangements should be made well in advance with a faculty member of the Group in Agricultural & Environmental Chemistry.

016.title: Metal Properties & Fabrication
016.description: Metal properties and techniques for fabricating in metal. Physical principles, design considerations, effects of techniques on quality and appearance, and evaluation procedures. Laboratory experience working with metal.
016.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ABT 016

020.title: Sustainable Energy Technologies
020.description: Sustainable and efficient energy technologies and their application in agriculture and other sectors. Basic principles of energy efficiency, conservation, and conversion technologies using solar, wind, water, biomass, geothermal, and other renewable sources. Environmental impacts and energy policy. Experiential learning about solar drying, controlled environment agriculture, net-zero energy building, electricity generation, energy storage, biofuels, and integrated waste management; field visits.

192.title: Internship in Agricultural & Environmental Technology
192.description: Supervised internship in agricultural and environmental technology.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; approval of project prior to period of internship.

199.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
199.description: Special study for upper division students. May be taught abroad.

018.title: Business Law
018.description: General principles of business law in the areas of contracts, business organization, real property, uniform commercial code, sales, commercial paper, employment relations, and creditor-debtor against a background of the history and functioning of our present legal system.

100A.title: Intermediate Microeconomics: Theory of Production & Consumption
100A.description: Theory of individual consumer and market demand; theory of production and supply of agricultural products, with particular reference to the individual firm; price determination, and employment of resources under pure competition.
100A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECN 100.
100A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 019A C- or better,  MAT 019B C- or better,  MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better,  MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better,  MAT 021B C- or better)).

100B.title: Intermediate Microeconomics: Imperfect Competition, Markets & Welfare Economics
100B.description: Price determination, and employment of resources under conditions of monopoly, oligopoly, and monopolistic competition.
100B.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; ((ECN 001A C-  or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better,  MAT 016B C- or better,  MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better,  MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better,  MAT 021B C- or better)); ARE 018 C- or better.

106.title: Econometric Theory & Applications
106.description: Statistical methods for analyzing data to solve problems in managerial economics. Topics include the linear regression model, methods to resolve data problems, and the economic interpretation of results.
106.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have enrolled in or completed ECN 140.
106.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better); STA 103 C- or better.

107.title: Econometrics for Business Decisions
107.description: Covers state-of-the art econometric and statistical methods for causal and predictive modeling with applications to finance, marketing, and public policy.
107.prereq_text: ARE 106 C- or better; STA 103 C- or better.

112.title: Fundamentals of Organization Management
112.description: Role of organizational design and behavior in business and public agencies. Principles of planning, decision making, individual behavior, management, leadership, informal groups, conflict and change in the organization.

115A.title: Economic Development
115A.description:
Major issues encountered in emerging from international poverty, problems of growth and structural change, human welfare, population
growth and health, labor markets and internal migration. Important issues of policy concerning international trade and industrialization.
115A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

118.title: Tax Accounting
118.description: Development and application of a framework to understand the tax effects of typical management decisions on both entities and their owners. Impacts that different methods of taxation have on business entities with emphasis on tax planning, using income and deduction strategies, retirement plans, and choice of business entity for tax minimization. Irregularly offered.
118.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better; ARE 018 recommended.

121.title: Economics of Agricultural Sustainability
121.description: Application of economic concepts to agro-environmental issues relevant to agricultural sustainability. Topics include market efficiency, production externalities, government policies, agricultural trade, product differentiation, all linked to sustainability issues. Case studies include biofuels, genetically modified foods and geographically differentiated products.
121.prereq_text: ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better. or ECN 001AV C- or better.

130.title: Agricultural Markets
130.description: Nature, function, organizational structure, and operation of agricultural markets; prices, costs, and margins; market information, regulation, and controls; cooperative marketing. Irregularly offered.
130.prereq_text: ARE 106 C- or better; ARE 100A C- or better; (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better); STA 103 C- or better.

136.title: Managerial Marketing
136.description: Application of economic theory and econometrics to the study of marketing and consumer research. Emphasis on industry structure, history, regulatory aspects, integrated brand promotion, market segmentation, optimal product mix, message placement.
136.prereq_text: (ARE 100B C- or better or ECN 100B C- or better); ARE 106 C- or better; STA 103 C- or better.

144.title: Real Estate Economics
144.description: Economic theory, analysis, and institutions of real estate markets and related financial markets. Techniques for appraising property values. Cases drawn from the raw land, single family, multifamily, industrial and office real estate markets.

145.title: Farm & Rural Resources Appraisal
145.description: Principles and procedures of the valuation process with emphasis placed on rural real estate. Includes identification of the major physical and economic determinants of value, the three primary appraisal approaches to valuation, discussion of appraisal activity and practice.

146.title: Economics of Business Regulation
146.description: Variety, nature and impact of government regulation: anti-trust laws and economic and social regulation. Nature of the legislative process, promulgation of regulations, and their impact, especially as analyzed by economists.

155.title: Operations Research & Management Science
155.description: Introduction to quantitative methods used to analyze business and economic processes: decision analysis for management, mathematical programming, competitive analysis, and other methods.
155.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better); STA 103 C- or better.

166.title: Economics of Global Poverty Reduction: What Works & Why
166.description: Application of microeconomic theory and econometrics to understand causes of poverty and critically evaluate poverty alleviation policies in low income countries. Irregularly offered.
166.prereq_text: (ARE 100B C- or better or ECN 100B C- or better); (ARE 106 C- or better or ECN 140 C- or better); (ARE 115A C- or better or ECN 115A C- or better).

171.title: Principles of Finance
171.description: Principles of corporate financial management. Time value of money, interest rates, principles of valuation, NPV, risk and return, and cost of capital.
171.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECN 134 or ECN 134Y.
171.prereq_text: ARE 100A C- or better; ARE 106 C- or better; (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better.

172.title: Corporate Finance
172.description: Financial analysis at the firm level: optimizing capital structure; minimizing the cost of capital; dividend policies; mergers and acquisitions; real options; and risk management.
172.prereq_text: ARE 171 C- or better; ARE 106 C- or better; (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Internship experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Agricultural & Resource Economics. Internships are supervised by a member of the staff.

197T.title: Tutoring in Managerial Economics
197T.description: Undergraduates assist the instructor by tutoring students in one of the department's regularly scheduled courses.
197T.prereq_text: Senior standing in Managerial Economics and consent of Department Chairperson.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

200C.title: Microeconomic Theory
200C.description: Uncertainty and information economics. Individual decision making under uncertainty. Introduction to game theory, with emphasis on applications to markets with firms that are imperfect competitors or consumers that are imperfectly informed.

202B.title: Applied Microeconomics: Consumer & Producer Behavior
202B.description: Application of consumer and producer theory in models of individual behavior and market-level phenomena. Implications of consumer and producer theory for specification of empirical models of supply and demand for inputs and outputs and market equilibrium displacement models.

215B.title: Open Macroeconomics of Development
215B.description: Models and policy approaches regarding trade, monetary and fiscal issues, capital flows and debt are discussed in the macroeconomic framework of an open developing country. Basic analytical focus is real exchange rate and its impact on sectoral allocation of resources.
215B.prereq_text: (ARE 200A or ARE 204A); (ARE 214 or ARE 215A); (ARE 200D or ARE 205).

232.title: Agricultural Commodity Markets
232.description: Economic analysis of industries that produce, market, transport, store, and process basic commodities. Analysis of market equilibrium under perfect and imperfect competition, with and without government involvement.
232.prereq_text: ARE 200A; ARE 202A; ARE 240A; or consent of instructor.

240A.title: Econometric Methods
240A.description: Least squares, instrumental variables, and maximum likelihood estimation and inference for single equation linear regression model; linear restrictions; heteroskedasticity; autocorrelation; lagged dependent variables.

240C.title: Time Series Econometrics
240C.description: Probability theory; estimation, inference and forecasting of time series models; trends and non-standard asymptotic theory; vector time series methods and cointegration; time series models for higher order moments and transition data; state-space modeling; the Kalman filter.

240F.title: Topics in Cross Section Econometrics
240F.description: Modern econometrics techniques for cross-section data. Expand on topics covered in ECN 240A, ECN 240B and ECN 240D. Contents vary from year to year.

256B.title: Applied Econometrics II
256B.description: Second of two courses in the Masters-level econometrics sequence. The linear regression model and generalizations are applied to a variety of topics in applied economics. Tools for empirical research for problems requiring more sophisticated tools than standard regression models are emphasized.

276A.title: Environmental Economics: Externalities
276A.description: Introduces fundamental and recent research in environmental economics, focusing on the design, implementation and evaluation of environmental policy instruments to correct market failures. Exposure to economic theories and empirical techniques frequently used in this field.
276A.prereq_text: Students should have completed the first year graduate level sequence in microeconomics and econometrics.

298.title: Directed Group Study
298.description: Advanced study through special seminars, informal group studies, or group research on problems for analysis and experimentation. Sections:(1) Managerial Economics; (2) Agricultural Policy; (3) Community & Regional Development; (4) Natural Resources; (5) Human Resources; (6) Research Methods & Quantitative Analysis.

299.title: Individual Study
299.description: Sections: (1) Managerial Economics; (2) Agricultural Policy; (3) Community & Regional Development; (4) Natural Resources; (5) Human Resources; (6) Research Methods & Quantitative Analysis; and (7) Dissertation Research Prospectus.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship off and on campus in areas of agricultural education.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.description: AED support moved to ANS, informed July 2018 by Lisa Holmes. Subject moved in ICMS, took some time.

100.title: Concepts in Agricultural & Environmental Education
100.description: Philosophy and nature of formal and non-formal agricultural and environmental education programs. Emphasis on understanding the role of the teacher and observing a variety of programs.

190.title: Seminar in Agricultural Education
190.description: Discussion of selected critical issues in agricultural education.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Supervised internship off and on campus in areas of agricultural education.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

001E.title: Nature & Culture in America
001E.description: Uses and abuses of nature in America; patterns of inhabitation, exploitation, appreciation, and neglect; attention to California; emphasis on metaphor as a key to understanding ourselves and the natural world; attention to models of healing: stewardship, ecology, the "rights" movement.

005.title: Technology in American Lives
005.description:
Technology as both a material cultural force and a symbol in American
culture; the lives of engineers at work and play; images of the engineer and technology in popular culture; social political and ethical issues raised by technology.

010.title: Introduction to American Studies
010.description: Ideals, conflicts, and realities defining American Cultures through study of popular music, advertising, and other media. Themes include Imagining America, Citizenship and Belonging, and Cultural/Spatial Practices.

018Y.title: Climate Justice Cultures
018Y.description: Climate justice concepts, fields of interdisciplinary knowledges, and social movements that treat climate justice as an interconnected set of political, economic and cultural systems. Climate science, just transition, Indigenous climate action, cultural approaches (literary and other media) and natural climate solutions.

030.title: Images of America & Americans in Popular Culture
030.description: Investigation of verbal and visual discourses about American identity in various popular culture products, including film, television, radio, music, fiction, art, advertising, and commercial experiences; discourses about the United States in the popular culture of other societies.

059.title: Music & American Culture
059.description: Examination of music and American culture. Studies will explore music in its cultural contexts, which may include examinations of recording and broadcasting, of race, class, and gender, the role of technology, and relationships between musical production, consumption and listening.

095.title: Careers & Identity in American Culture
095.description: Defining one's identity through the career. Life course, preparation, and choices. Personality and career. Ethics. Gender, ethnicity, sexuality, and social class in the workplace. Transnational workplace. Conflicts between the career and other social roles.

101H.title: Special Topics: Problems in Cross-Cultural American Studies
101H.description: Intensive reading, writing, and special projects. Interdisciplinary group study of special topics in American Culture Studies, designed for non-majors as well as majors.

130.title: American Popular Culture
130.description: American popular expression and experience as a cultural system, and the relationship between this system and elite and folk cultures. Exploration of theories and methods for discovering and interpreting patterns of meaning in American popular culture.

151.title: American Landscapes & Places
151.description: Comparative study of several American cultural populations inhabiting a region, including their relationship to a shared biological, physical, and social environment, their intercultural relations, and their relationships to the dominant American popular and elite culture and folk traditions.

153.title: The Individual & Community in America
153.description: Interdisciplinary examination of past and present tensions between the individual and the community in American experience, as those tensions are expressed in such cultural systems as folklore, public ritual, popular entertainment, literature, fine arts, architecture, and social thought.

158.title: Technology & the Modern American Body
158.description: History and analysis of relationships between human bodies and technologies in modern society. Dominant and eccentric examples of how human bodies and technologies influence one another and reveal underlying cultural assumptions.
158.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken TCS 158.

160.title: Undergraduate Seminar in American Studies
160.description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing by small groups in selected topics of American Studies scholarship; emphasis on theory and its application to American material.

190A.title: Senior Thesis Research Seminar
190A.description: Research and prospectus writing for senior thesis.

190B.title: Senior Thesis
190B.description: In consultation with advisor, student writes an extended research paper on a topic proposed in AMS 190A.

192.title: Internship in American Studies
192.description: Supervised internship and study in social & community organizations, schools, cultural institutions (e.g., libraries, museums, and archives), or other work sites. Final written report and other assignments as per contract with supervisor.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment dependent on availability of intern positions, with priority to American Studies majors.

197T.title: Tutoring in American Studies
197T.description: Tutoring in lower division American Studies courses, usually in small discussion groups. Periodic meetings with the instructor in charge; reports and readings.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of Chairperson of American Studies Program.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and chairperson of American Studies Program.

126.title: Fundamentals of Immunology
126.description: Fundamental concepts of immunology including components of the immune system, initiation and regulation of the immune response, infection and immunity, allergy and hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, and transplantation.
126.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 105 or ABI 102; or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Internship experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Anatomy, Physiology & Cell Biology. Internships are supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of internship.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Discussion and critical evaluation of advanced topics and current trends in research.

192.title: Internship in Anesthesiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in anesthesia and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

455.title: Externship in Anesthesiology
455.description: Away clinical rotation in Anesthesiology or Pain Medicine.

218B.title: Fundamentals of Animal Behavior
218B.description: Survey of the phenomena and theory of animal behavior from the perspectives of multiple biological disciplines, including evolution, ecology, psychology, genetics, neurobiology, endocrinology, and animal science.
218B.prereq_text: ANB 218A or PSC 218A; or ECL 218A; consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar in Animal Behavior
290.description: Selected topics in animal behavior.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Lectures and/or discussion of current issues, problems, or techniques in animal behavior.

299.title: Research
299.description: Advanced research in one of the specialty areas in animal behavior

050B.title: Animal Biology
050B.description: Basic biological disciplines important to an understanding of practical animal biology issues including the evolution of animal groups, genetic mechanisms, animal physiology as it relates to maintenance and production, and aspects of comparative anatomy, behavior and ecology.

092.title: Internship in Animal Biology
092.description: Office, laboratory or fieldwork off or on campus in research, governmental regulation, policy making, and private enterprise dealing with animal related issues of production, welfare, pest management, biodiversity and the environment. All requirements of Internship Approval Request form must be met.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

102.title: Animal Biochemistry & Metabolism
102.description: Water and biological buffers; thermodynamics of metabolism; structure and function of biomolecules; enzyme kinetics and function; membrane biology; digestion and absorption; carbohydrate metabolism.
102.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 102.

103.title: Animal Biochemistry & Metabolism
103.description: Physiological function and metabolism of lipids and amino acids; integrative metabolism; biochemical basis for nutrient requirements; structure and function of vitamins; mineral metabolism and requirements.
103.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 103.

187.title: Animal Biology Seminar
187.description: Seminar leading to development of the Major Proposal for the Animal Biology major.

189.title: Senior Practicum
189.description: Practicum may be an experimental research project, a library research project or some other creative activity that will serve as a capstone experience for the Animal Biology major.
189.prereq_text: ABI 050A; ABI 050B; ABI 050C; ABI 187; Junior standing.

192.title: Internship in Animal Biology
192.description: Office, laboratory or fieldwork off or on campus in research, governmental regulations, policy making, and private enterprise dealing with animal related issues of production, welfare, pest management, biodiversity and the environment. All requirements of Internship Approval Request form must be met.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

290.title: Seminar in Animal Biology
290.description: Seminar on advanced topics in animal biology. Presentations by members of the Animal Biology Graduate Group and guest speakers.

299.title: Research
299.description: Research with a faculty member in Animal Biology Graduate Group.

111.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory Techniques
111.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in molecular biology; the role of this technology in both basic and applied animal research, and participation in laboratories using some of the most common techniques in molecular biology.
111.prereq_text: BIS 002C; (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V or ABI 102); (BIS 103 or ABI 103).

185.title: Science of Captive Breeding & Reintroduction
185.description: Explore peer-reviewed literature surrounding the latest advances in captive breeding and reintroduction biology.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Selected topics relating to animal genetics.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Lectures and discussions of advanced topics in animal genetics.

015.title: Introductory Horse Husbandry
015.description: Introduction to care and use of light horses emphasizing the basic principles for selection of horses, responsibilities of ownership, recreational use and raising of foals.

041L.title: Domestic Animal Production Laboratory
041L.description: Animal production principles and practices, including five field trips to dairy cattle, beef cattle, sheep, and swine operations and campus labs.

042.title: Introductory Companion Animal Biology
042.description: Companion animal domestication. Historical, contemporary perspectives. Legislation concerning companion animals. Selected topics in anatomy, physiology, genetics, nutrition, behavior and management. Scientific methods in studying the human-animal bond. Discussions: application of biological concepts to problems related to companion animals.

049C.title: Animal Management Practices: Dairy
049C.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049F.title: Animal Management Practices: Laboratory Animals
049F.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

049G.title: Animal Management Practices: Meats
049G.description: Application of the principles of elementary biology to the management of a specific animal species. Up to four different topics may be taken.

090C.title: Research Group Conference
090C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the animal sciences.

092.title: Internship in Animal Science
092.description: Internship off and on campus in dairy, livestock, and aquaculture production, research and management; or in a business, industry, or agency associated with these or other animal enterprises. All requirements of Internship Approval form must be met.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

100.title: Animal Physiology
100.description: Basic principles of animal physiology in domesticated and captive animals with a comparative approach. Molecular, biochemical, chemical and physical aspects and their influences on function of physiological systems in animals.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken NPB 101.

106.title: Domestic Animal Behavior Laboratory
106.description: Research experience with the behavior of large domestic animals. Experimental design, methods of data collection & analysis, and reporting of experimental results.
106.prereq_text: ANS 104 or NPB 102; or consent of instructor.

108.title: Equine Behavior & Welfare
108.description: Improve the understanding and application of good welfare practices when managing, training, transporting, treating, or breeding equine. Recognize changes in behavior or causes related to comprised health or welfare.

120.title: Principles of Meat Science
120.description: Anatomical, physiological, developmental, and biochemical aspects of muscle underlying the conversion of muscle to meat. Includes meat processing, preservation, microbiology, and public health issues associated with meat products.

120L.title: Meat Science Laboratory
120L.description: Laboratory exercises and student participation in transformation of live animal to carcass and meat, structural and biochemical changes related to meat quality, chemical and sensory evaluation of meat, and field trips to packing plant and processing plant.

128.title: Agricultural Applications of Linear Programming
128.description: Applications of linear programming in agriculture, emphasizing resource allocation problems and decision making. Problems include crop production, ration formulation, and farm management. Hands-on experience in developing linear programs and interpreting the results.
128.prereq_text: (PLS 021 or PLS 021V) or ECS 015; or consent of instructor.

146.title: Dairy Cattle Production
146.description: Scientific principles from genetics, nutrition, physiology, and related fields applied to conversion of animal feed to human food through dairy animals. Management and economic decisions are related to animal biology considering the environment and animal well-being. Mandatory Saturday field-trip.
146.prereq_text: NUT 115; or consent of instructor; ANG 107 recommended.

148.title: Enterprise Analysis in Animal Industries
148.description: Examination and application of decision making and problem solving in the production enterprise. Areas of production analysis, problem solving, risk analysis and cost-benefit analysis will be examined in terms of the total enterprise.

150.title: Animal Health & Disease
150.description: Basic concepts of animal immunology, microbiology, parasitology, epidemiology, vaccination, and how the knowledge can be used to improve animal health and prevent animal infection & disease. Includes relevant health and disease issues.

170.title: Ethics of Animal Use
170.description: Ethical issues relating to animal use in contemporary society. Integration of philosophical theories with scientific evidence relating to animal behavior, mentality, and welfare. Uses of animals in agriculture, research, and as companions. Ethical responsibilities regarding wildlife and the environment.
170.prereq_text: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or CMN 001 or CMN 001V or COM 001 or COM 002 or COM 003 or COM 004 or ENL 003 or ENL 003V or NAS 005 or NAS 005V.

190C.title: Research Group Conference
190C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the animal sciences.

192.title: Internship in Animal Science
192.description: Internship off and on campus in dairy, livestock and aquaculture production, research and management; or in a business, industry, or agency associated with these or other animal enterprises. All requirements of Internship Approval Form must be met.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194.title: Research in Animal Science
194.description: Research with a faculty mentor. Weekly discussion and laboratory on specific research topic. May include a seminar to research group. Choose from sections: (1) Animal Behavior; (2) Animal Genetics; (3) Animal Nutrition; (4) Animal Physiology.
194.prereq_text: ANS 106 or ANS 135 or ANS 136 or ANS 137 or ANS 139 or ANG 111; or ANS 133; and consent of instructor.

194HB.title: Undergraduate Honors Thesis in Animal Science
194HB.description: Carry out a research project (chosen from faculty-suggested or approved proposals) during the academic year under the guidance of a faculty member. Upon completion, write a thesis and present a public seminar describing his/her research.
194HB.prereq_text: (NPB 101 or NPB 101V or ANS 100); (ABI 103 or BIS 103); and consent of instructor; minimum cumulative GPA of 3.200 and selection by the Honors Selection Committee.

197T.title: Tutoring in Animal Science
197T.description: Tutoring of students in courses taught by instructors in the Department of Animal Science; weekly conference with instructor(s) in charge of the course; written critiques of teaching procedures; assist in preparation and development of instructional materials.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; animal Science or related major; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Selected topics relating to the animal sciences.

290C.title: Research Group Conference
290C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the animal sciences.

297.title: Supervised Teaching in Animal Science
297.description: Practical experience in teaching Animal Science at University level; curriculum design and evaluation; preparation and presentation of material. Assistance in laboratories, discussion sections, and evaluation of student work. Evaluation letter sent to the graduate advisor with copy to the student.

298.title: Group Study
298.description:
Lectures and discussions of advanced topics in the animal sciences.

(Sect. 1, 2, 3-letter grading; from Sect. 4 on-S/U grading only.)

001.title: Human Evolutionary Biology
001.description: Evolutionary theory and mechanisms of evolution; basic population and quantitative genetics; primatology; biological and cultural diversity within Homo sapiens; paleoanthropology.

002.title: Cultural Anthropology
002.description: Introduction to cultural diversity in its many forms and methods used by anthropologists to account for it. Relational dynamic of culture, history, and power in constituting "social facts" and "realities." Critical thinking of contemporary concerns.

003.title: Introduction to Archaeology
003.description:
Development of archaeology as an anthropological study; objectives
and methods of modern archaeology.

021.title: Zombies
021.description: Figure of the zombie as window into ideas about race, economic exploitation, and what it means to be human. Zombie lore in the Afro-Atlantic world and its re-imagining in contemporary pop culture.

024.title: Ancient Crops & People
024.description: The archaeological evidence for domestication of plants and the origins of agricultural societies. Anthropological context of agriculture and the effects on sexual division of labor, social inequality, wealth accumulation, warfare, human health, and sedentism.

031.title: Shamanism & Witchcraft
031.description: Introduction to shamanism and witchcraft, focusing especially on shamanism. Cross-cultural patterns, evolutionary and psychological foundations, archaeological evidence, and analogues such as money managers. Concepts examined via comparative and cognitive approaches.

034.title: Cultures of Consumerism
034.description: Aspects of modern consumer cultures in capitalist and socialist countries. Transformations of material cultures over the past century. Case studies on the intersections of gender, class, and culture in everyday consumption practices.

107.title: Law, Power, Violence
107.description: Cultural dimensions of law and political power.  Colonial and postcolonial legal regimes, bureaucratic reason, legalized violence, sovereign power, and human rights.

128A.title: Kinship & Social Organization: From Clans to Countries
128A.description: Family, marriage, household and social organization from a cross-cultural and evolutionary perspective. Emphasis on case studies that illustrate human variation, theories that account for this variation, and recent advances in the treatment of this data.
128A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 128. (Former ANT 128.)

129.title: Health & Medicine in a Global Context
129.description: Recent works in medical anthropology and the science studies of medicine dealing with social and cultural aspects of global health issues such as AIDS, pandemics, clinical trials, cultural differences in illnesses, diabetes, organ trafficking, medical technologies, illness narratives, and others.

131.title: Ecology & Politics
131.description: Analysis of the complex interactions between ecological dynamics and political processes employing the emerging approach of political ecology. Case studies of environmental degradation (e.g., desertification, logging, mineral extraction, petroleum, water) from various cultural and geographic regions.

132.title: Psychological Anthropology
132.description: History of the relationship between anthropology and psychoanalysis. Exploration of anthropology of emotions, colonial psychology, contemporary ethno-psychiatry, studies on personhood, possession, magic, altered states, subjectivity, and definitions of the normal and the pathological in different contexts and cultures.

134.title: Buddhism in Global Culture
134.description: Buddhist meditation and ritual as a cultural system that adapts to global and local forces of change. Anthropological theory and method in understanding global culture transmission, including Buddhist reform movements in Asia and Buddhist practice in the West.

136.title: Ethnographic Film
136.description: Overview of the use of film in anthropology and its advantages and limitations in comparison to written ethnographic descriptions. Essential features of ethnographic films. Film production in anthropological research and problems encountered in producing films in the field.

138.title: Ethnographic Research Methods in Anthropology
138.description: Basic concepts in and approaches to ethnographic field research. Problem formulation, research design, qualitative and quantitative data collection procedures, and techniques for organizing, retrieving, and analyzing information. Ethnographic description and constructed inference. Students will organize and conduct individual research projects.

139AN.title: Race, Class, Gender Systems
139AN.description: Comparative analysis of class/race/gender inequality, concentrating on the ways in which beliefs about descent, "blood," and biological difference interact with property and marital systems to affect the distribution of power in society.
139AN.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 139. (Former ANT 139.)

142.title: Peoples of the Middle East
142.description: Peoples of the Middle East (including North Africa). Discussions of class relations, kinship organization, sex/gender systems, religious beliefs and behavior, ethnic relations, political systems. Impact of world systems, political and religious movements and social change. (Former ANT 136.)

152.title: Human Evolution
152.description: Nature and results of the evolutionary processes involved in the formation and differentiation of humankind.

153.title: Human Genetics: Mutation & Migration
153.description: Introduction to human genetics. Principles of inheritance, the human genome, population genetics, mutation, genetic diversity, using DNA to study ancient human history, personal genomics. Human genetics as a tool to understand the patterns and processes of human migration. Introduction to the major concepts in human genetic and genomic research.
153.prereq_text: (BIO 001 C- or better, BIO 001L C- or better) or MCB 010 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

180.title: Zooarchaeology
180.description: Theories and methods for studying animal skeletal remains from archaeological sites. Identification and quantification of zooarchaeological material, cultural and natural processes affecting animal bones pre- and postburial, and use of faunal remains for determining past human diets and past environments.

182.title: Archaeometry
182.description: Scientific techniques used to study the chemical and physical properties of archaeological materials. Types of anthropological questions that can be addressed with different methods. Preparation and analysis of archaeological materials.

200.title: History of Anthropology
200.description: Historical development of socio-cultural theory within anthropology, from mid-19th to mid-20th centuries. Focus on original theory texts in context of historical developments in the field as a whole.

204.title: Contemporary Issues in Anthropological Theory
204.description:
Advanced consideration of fundamental issues in anthropological theory.
Emphasis on critical examination of major contemporary debates between proponents of competing theories.
204.prereq_text: ANT 002; ANT 137; or consent of instructor.

210.title: Aspects of Culture Structure
210.description: Analysis of various phases of culture, such as religion, economics, law, and folklore.

216.title: Problems in Archeological Method
216.description: Techniques for analyzing archeological data; application to various prehistoric cultures.

256.title: Primate Conservation Biology
256.description: Application of understanding of primate biology to conservation of primates and their habitat. Topics include evolutionary anthropology, behavioral ecology, biogeography, macroecology, population biology, and socio-ecology of primates.
256.prereq_text: ANT 154; Graduate standing, or upper division undergraduates with consent of instructor.

270.title: Anthropology Colloquium Seminar
270.description: Reports and discussions of recent advances in the four subfields of anthropology. Presented by guest speakers.

052.title: Field Equipment Welding
052.description: Intermediate welding to include hardfacing and inert gas welding. Class projects on repair and fabrication by welding. Troubleshooting and major repair of field equipment.

101.title: Engine Technology
101.description: Principles of 2-stroke cycle, 4-stroke cycle gasoline and 4-stroke cycle diesel engine construction and operation. Engine systems, performance, troubleshooting, and overhaul.
101.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

150.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
150.description: Basic concepts, principles, and methods of GIS are presented. Data structures, database design, GIS data creation, GPS, and spatial analysis. May be taught abroad.
150.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ABT 180/PLS 180, ABT 181N; LDA 150, LED 150, ABT 150.

181N.title: Concepts & Methods in Geographic Information Systems
181N.description: Data representation and analysis in geographic information systems (GIS). Creation of spatial data sets from analog and digital sources such as aerial photography and maps; data structures, data management, database design, georeferencing, georectification, surface models, analysis, and spatial data visualization.
181N.prereq_text: LDA 150 or ABT 150; or consent of instructor.

190C.title: Research Conference for Advanced Undergraduates
190C.description: Research conferences for specialized study in applied biological systems technology.

197T.title: Tutoring in Applied Biological Systems Technology
197T.description: Tutoring individual students, leading small voluntary discussion groups, or assisting the instructor in laboratories affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference
290C.description: Research problems, progress, and techniques in applied biological systems technology.

002.title: Elementary Arabic 2
002.description: Continuation of basic Arabic from ARB 001. Interactive and integrated presentation of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, including syntax. Focus on standard Arabic and limited use of spoken Egyptian and/or one other colloquial dialect.

022.title: Intermediate Arabic 22
022.description: Continuation of ARB 021. Interactive and integrated presentation of listening, speaking, reading, and writing, including idiomatic expression. Focus on standard Arabic with limited use of Egyptian and/or one other colloquial dialect.

122.title: Advanced Arabic
122.description: Continuation of ARB 121. Further development of advanced skills in reading, listening, writing, and speaking standard Arabic through work with texts, video, and audio on cultural and social issues. Limited use of one colloquial dialect.

140.title: A Story for a Life: The Arabian Nights
140.description: In-depth exploration of The Arabian Nights, the best-known work of pre-modern Arabic literature and a major work of world literature. Analysis of the work in its historical context and in comparison to other frame tales in world literature.

001B.title: Medieval & Renaissance Art
001B.description: Christian, Barbarian, Moslem, and Classical traditions in European Art from the 4th through the 16th centuries.

101.title: Understanding Museum Practices
101.description: Museum theory and practice. Mission of the museum to collect, preserve and educate. Museum administrative structure and the role of the curator. Visitor engagement, ethics of display, interpretation and content production.

154.title: The Hindu Temple
154.description: Comparative history of architecture and symbolism of the Hindu Temple in India, Southeast Asia and the United States. Attention to the temple as expression of religious knowledge, political authority, and cultural heritage through the lens of colonialism and postcolonialism.

179B.title: Baroque Art
179B.description: Painting, sculpture and graphic arts in the 17th century, including such artists as Caravaggio, Rubens, Rembrandt, and Velázquez in their political and social context.

188C.title: American Art to 1910
188C.description: Major movements in American art from the 17th-century English-speaking colonies to the onset of World War I.

190F.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Art History: Chinese
190F.description: Study of a broad problem or theoretical issue in art, architecture, or material culture. Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing.
190F.prereq_text: Upper division standing; significant training in Art History recommended; or consent of instructor.

200B.title: Research & Writing Methods in Art History
200B.description: Development of the research, writing, and editing skills necessary for producing publishable work. Focus on reference tools used by art historians and the mechanics of scholarship, from question framing and organization of ideas to writing clear, effective prose.

200C.title: Thesis Writing Colloquium
200C.description: Meeting concurrently with AHI 200B, the colloquium provides a structured, supportive environment for second-year Art History graduate students drafting masters' theses. Offers a forum for technical discussions, discussion of writing/editing procedures, and peer review of writing in progress.
200C.prereq_text: AHI 200B; taken by all Art History M.A. students in their first year.

290.title: Special topics in Art History
290.description: Special research seminar in the theory or methods of Art History, or in a period of Art History. Topic varies depending on the interests of the instructor or students.

002.title: Beginning Drawing
002.description: Introduction to drawing using various black and white media to articulate forms and organize space, with reference to historical and contemporary works. May be taught abroad.

005.title: Beginning Sculpture
005.description: Basic sculpture techniques using a variety of media. Form in space using cardboard, plaster, and/or cement, wood and/or metal and other media.

007.title: Beginning Painting
007.description: Introduction to techniques and concepts in the practice of painting.

008.title: Beginning Ceramic Sculpture
008.description: Introduction to ceramic sculpture construction and processes. Large scale hand-building, glazing, kilns and kiln firing technology.

009.title: Beginning Photography
009.description: Introduction to visual language of photographic art and technique. Manual camera operation and printing techniques. Concept and practice of photography as an art form and creating photographic projects.

010F.title: Contemporary Art Appreciation
010F.description: Survey of contemporary art since 1960; includes fieldwork. Explores contemporary thought within the visual arts using forms and strategies of painting, sculpture, installation, performance, photo and video in collaborative, ephermeral and multimedia approaches. For Art and non-Art majors.
010F.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ART 010D.

011.title: Beginning Printmaking
011.description: Introduction to printmaking such as monoprint, intaglio, lithography, relief and digital techniques. Practical methods taught within a workshop environment using art historical and contemporary examples.

012.title: Beginning Video
012.description: Production techniques of video shooting, editing, lighting, sound and effects.  A conceptual framework for video-art techniques.

101A.title: Intermediate Painting
101A.description: Individualized projects exploring color and space in a variety of subject matter and approaches. Builds on basic skills and concepts from beginning drawing and painting courses. Study of historical and contemporary art in relation to studio practice.

101C.title: Intermediate Painting: Watercolor
101C.description: Watercolor as a means of visual expression. Techniques and medium used in water media.

105A.title: Advanced Drawing: Studio Projects
105A.description: Exploration of composition and process in drawing. Emphasis on the role of drawing in contemporary art and on drawing as an interdisciplinary practice.

110B.title: Intermediate Photography: Digital Imaging
110B.description: Introduction to digital photography on screen and paper. Technical demonstrations, workshops, and critique. Development of photographic project.

114C.title: Intermediate Video: Performance Strategies
114C.description: Use of video to expand performance art production. Exploration of improvisation, direction, projection, and image processing in real time.

142B.title: Intermediate Ceramic Sculpture: Material Study
142B.description: Study of ceramic materials and processes. Areas studied include clay and clay bodies; glaze materials through temperature, color and texture; history and technology of kilns and kiln firing. Examination of material properties and characteristics through experimentation.

151.title: Intermediate Sculpture
151.description: Individualized explorations through multiple projects in a variety of sculpture media and techniques. Builds upon technical skills and concepts covered in ART 005.

195.title: Expanded Field: Artist Lecture Series
195.description: Exploration of the expanded field of practice, theory and criticism in the visual arts. Presentations and discussions with professional practitioners in the field.

220.title: Research Methods for Artists
220.description: Research methods for artists through critical reading and writing, studio practice, presentations, site-visits, and professional engagement related to the field of visual art.

225.title: Professional Practice in Contemporary Art
225.description: Fluctuating critical and cultural environment of the professional art world. New strategies to support the social and philosophical networks and frameworks that inform contemporary cultural production. Emphasis on new esthetics concepts, practices and technologies.

290B.title: Critical Discourse in Studio Practice
290B.description: Advanced course for second-year graduate students. Critical discussion and contemporary readings pertinent to studio practice and artwork, including video, installation, photography, interactive arts, performance, sculpture, painting, printmaking, ceramics, sound, and all other mediums.

290E.title: Critical Discourse on Media
290E.description: Critical discussion and contemporary readings pertinent to artwork that uses digital media including video, installation, photography, interactive arts, performance, sculpture, painting, printmaking, ceramics, sound, and all other mediums.

001.title: Historical Experience of Asian Americans
001.description: Introduction to Asian American Studies through an overview of the history of Asians in America from the 1840s to the present within the context of the development of the United States.

003.title: Methods in Asian American Studies
003.description: Diverse research methods used in the multidisciplinary field of Asian American studies and research by department faculty. Application of methods to case studies of Asian American communities and issues. Methods include: historical/ archival research, literary analysis, feminist methods, media analysis, visual critique, ethnography, interviews, community-engaged research, and quantitative methods. Faculty guest lectures on relevant scholarship and their own research.

102.title: Theoretical Perspectives in Asian American Studies
102.description: Critically examines major theoretical perspectives and approaches central to the intellectual and political concerns of Asian American studies as a distinct field of intellectual inquiry and sustained site of critique.

114.title: Asian Diasporas
114.description: Asian diasporic communities and the experiences of its members in the United States and internationally. Community building, cyberspace, gender issues, labor, transnational practices, effects of globalization, political organizing, homeland politics, humanitarian projects, citizenship and nationalism.

132.title: Health Issues Confronting Asian Americans & Pacific Islanders
132.description: Health issues confronting Asian Americans & Pacific Islanders.

150D.title: Korean American Experience
150D.description: Interdisciplinary survey of the historical and contemporary experiences of Koreans in the United States from the late-19th century to the present.

189D.title: Topics in Asian American Studies: Policy & Community
189D.description: Intensive treatment of a topic in Asian American Studies: policy and community.

189G.title: Topics in Asian American Studies: Race, Class, Gender, & Sexuality
189G.description: Intensive treatment of a topic in Asian American Studies: race, class, gender, and sexuality.

189I.title: Topics in Asian American Studies: Politics & Social Movements
189I.description: Intensive treatment of a topic in Asian American Studies: politics and social movements.

010S.title: Astronomy of the Solar System
010S.description: Introduction to naked eye and telescopic observations of events in the night sky: positions of sun, moon, planets throughout the year.  Historical perspective on how our understanding of the solar system evolved to current non-mathematical astrophysical interpretation of planetary systems.
010S.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken AST 002, any quarter of PHY 009 or PHY 009H, or any upper division PHY course (other than PHY 137 or PHY 160).

010.title: Severe & Unusual Weather
010.description: Introduction to physical principles of severe and unusual weather: flood, blizzards, thunderstorms, lightning, tornadoes, and hurricanes. Emphasis on scientific perspective and human context. Not open to students who have received credit for ATM 100. (Former ATM 100.)

092.title: Atmospheric Science Internship
092.description: Internship off and on campus in atmospheric science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

110.title: Weather Observation & Analysis
110.description: Acquisition, distribution and analysis of meteorological data. Vertical sounding analysis, stability indices, probability of local severe weather, weather map analysis. Use of National Weather Service analyses and forecast products. Laboratory makes use of computer-generated analyses.

121A.title: Atmospheric Dynamics
121A.description: Fundamental forces of atmospheric flow; noninertial reference frames; development of the equations of motion for rotating stratified atmospheres; isobaric and natural coordinate systems; geostrophic flow; thermal wind; circulation and vorticity.

133.title: Biometeorology
133.description: Atmospheric and biological interactions.  Physical and biological basis for water vapor, carbon dioxide and energy exchanges with the atmosphere associated with plants and animals, including humans.  Microclimate of plant canopies and microclimatic modification such as frost protection and windbreaks.
133.prereq_text: MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B; one course in a biological discipline or consent of instructor.

149N.title: Air Pollution
149N.description: Physical and technical aspects of air pollution. Factors that determine local, regional, and global air quality; climate change; and physical and chemical properties of pollutants.
149N.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ATM 149.
149N.prereq_text: MAT 021D; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B); CHE 002B C- or better; (ATM 121A or ENG 103 C- or better or ECI 100 C- or better).

192.title: Atmospheric Science Internship
192.description: Internship off and on campus in atmospheric science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Completion of 84 units.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; three upper division units in Atmospheric Science.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; three upper division units in Atmospheric Science and at least an overall B average.

255.title: Numerical Modeling of the Atmosphere
255.description: Principles of numerical modeling of the dynamic, thermodynamic and physical processes of the atmosphere. Hands-on experiments on model development using the shallow water equations and the primitive equations. Operational forecast models.

270A.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Meteorological Statistics
270A.description: Applications and concepts in meteorological statistics.

270E.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Aerosol & Cloud Physics
270E.description: Applications and concepts in aerosol and cloud physics.

270F.title: Topics in Atmospheric Science: Atmospheric Chemistry
270F.description: Applications and concepts in atmospheric chemistry.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Current developments in selected areas of atmospheric research. Topics will vary according to student and faculty interests.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Atmospheric Science or related field.

291A.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Air Quality Meteorology
291A.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Air Quality Meteorology.

291B.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Biometeorology
291B.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Biometeorology.

291C.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Boundary Layer Meteorology
291C.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Boundary Layer Meteorology.

291D.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: Climate Change
291D.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in Climate Change.

291E.title: Research Conference in Atmospheric Science: General Meteorology
291E.description: Review and discussion of current literature and research in General Meteorology.

092.title: Internship in the Avian Sciences
092.description: Internship on and off campus in poultry, game birds or exotic bird production, management and research; or in a business, industry, or agency concerned with these entities. Compliance with Internship Approval form essential.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Sophomore standing preferred.

160.title: Designing & Performing Experiments in Avian Sciences
160.description: Experiments in current problems in avian biology. Introduction to experimental design. Students choose a project, design a protocol, perform an experiment and report their findings.
160.prereq_text: AVS 100 or WFC 111; or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Avian Sciences
192.description: Internship on and off campus in poultry, game birds or exotic bird production, management and research; or in a business, industry, or agency concerned with these entities. Compliance with Internship Approval form essential.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

195.title: Topics in Current Research
195.description: Discussion of topics of current interest in avian sciences.

197T.title: Tutoring in Avian Sciences
197T.description: Tutoring of students in lower division avian sciences courses; weekly conference with instructors in charge of courses; written critiques of teaching procedures.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description:
Major professors lead research discussions with their graduate students. Research papers are reviewed and project proposals
presented and evaluated. Format will combine seminar and discussion.

297T.title: Supervised Teaching in Avian Sciences
297T.description: Tutoring of students in lower, upper division, and graduate courses in Avian Sciences; weekly conference with instructor in charge of course; written critiques of teaching methods in lectures and laboratories.

BCB.name: Bio, Molec, Cell, Dev Bio GG

212.title: Cell Biology
212.description: Analysis of basic processes governing cell organization, division, and transport. Study of the integration and regulation of cell behavior in response to changes in cellular environment.
212.prereq_text: BIS 104; or the equivalent, or consent of instructor.

213.title: Developmental Biology
213.description: Fundamental principles in embryonic development that guide application of modern cellular and genetic approaches to understand developmental mechanisms. Emphasis on experimental approaches used to critically address scientific questions.
213.prereq_text: Undergraduate biology course or consent of instructor.

220L.title: Advanced Biochemistry Laboratory Rotations
220L.description: Two five-week assignments in BMCDB research laboratories. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience, experimental design, proposal writing and oral communication of results.
220L.prereq_text: BCB 210; BCB 211 (can be concurrent); BCB 120L or the equivalent.

255.title: Molecular Mechanisms in Pattern Formation & Development
255.description: Genetic and molecular analysis of mechanisms that control animal development after fertilization.  Establishment of embryonic axes, cell fate and embryonic pattern; induction, apoptosis, tissue patterning. Critical reading of current literature in C.elegans, Drosophila, and mouse genetic model systems.
255.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; introductory background in developmental biology and/or genetics recommended.

256.title: Cell & Molecular Biology of Cancer
256.description: Analysis of the pathologic alterations of cancer cells and therapeutic opportunities; with emphasis on animal models, tumor immunotherapy, stress response, metabolism, epigenetics, microRNAs and non-coding RNAs, and microbiota and inflammation.

092.title: Internship in Biological Chemistry
092.description: Supervised work experience in biological chemistry and related fields
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Biological Chemistry
192.description: Supervised work experience in Biological Chemistry and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to internship by preceptor.

198.title: Group Study
198.description: For undergraduate students desiring to explore particular topics in depth. Lecture and conferences may be involved.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: For graduate students desiring to explore particular topics in depth. Lectures and conferences may be involved.

497T.title: Tutoring in Biological Chemistry
497T.description: Assist instructor by tutoring medical students in preparation for one of the departmental courses that is a component of the required curriculum of the School of Medicine.
497T.prereq_text: Advanced standing or consent of instructor.

498.title: Group Study
498.prereq_text: Medical students with consent of instructor.

499.title: Research
499.description: Research with Department of Biological Chemistry.
499.prereq_text: Medical students with consent of instructor.

002A.title: Introduction to Biology: Essentials of Life on Earth
002A.description: Essentials of life including sources and use of energy, information storage, responsiveness to natural selection and cellularity. Origin of life and influence of living things on the chemistry of the Earth. May be taught abroad.
002A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 001A with a grade of C- or better.
002A.prereq_text: CHE 002A or CHE 004A or equivalent recommended.

002B.title: Introduction to Biology: Principles of Ecology & Evolution
002B.description: Introduction to basic principles of ecology and evolutionary biology, focusing on the fundamental mechanisms that generate and maintain biological diversity across scales ranging from molecules and genes to global processes and patterns.
002B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 001B with a grade of C- or better.

002C.title: Introduction to Biology: Biodiversity & the Tree of Life
002C.description: Introduction to organismal diversity, using the phylogenetic tree of life as an organizing theme. Lectures and laboratories cover methods of phylogenetic reconstruction, current knowledge of the tree of life, and the evolution of life's most important and interesting innovations.
002C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 001C with a grade of C- or better.
002C.prereq_text: BIS 001B C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better.

010.title: Everyday Biology
010.description: Everyday biological concepts using contemporary readings for non-scientists.  Key topics include: personal genomics; food & health; climate & evolution; brain biology & the law. Innovative projects apply biological concepts to current events. For students not specializing in biology.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 002A or NEM 010V or equivalent.

015L.title: Introduction to Data Science for Biologists
015L.description: Introduction to data science with a focus on developing practical computational skills for biologists. Data management, transformation, visualization, and analysis using R. Fundamentals of the UNIX shell including navigation and automation. Computational resources for biologists with emphasis on the management of genomic data.

027A.title: Linear Algebra with Applications to Biology
027A.description: Introduction to linear algebra with biological, medical, and bioengineering applications. Matrix algebra, vector spaces, orthogonality, determinants, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, principal component analysis, singular value decomposition, and linear transformations. Computer labs cover mathematical and computational techniques for modeling biological systems.
027A.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit for students who have completed MAT 022A.
027A.prereq_text: MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better.

070.title: Biodiversity & the Tree of Life
070.description: Introduction to organismal diversity, using the phylogenetic tree of life as an organizing theme. Methods of phylogenetic inference, current knowledge of the tree of life, and the evolution of life's most important and interesting innovations.
070.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken BIS 002C.

092.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
092.description: Internship in Biological Sciences.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Primarily for lower division students. May be taught abroad.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

101.title: Genes & Gene Expression
101.description: Nucleic acid structure and function; gene expression and its regulation; replication; transcription and translation; transmission genetics; molecular evolution.
101.prereq_text: (BIS 002A C- or better or BIO 002 C- or better); (BIS 002B C- or better or BIO 001 C- or better); (CHE 008A or CHE 118A or CHE 128A); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100 or STA 102 or STA 130A); STA 100 preferred.

102.title: Structure & Function of Biomolecules
102.description: Structure and function of macromolecules with emphasis on proteins, catalysis, enzyme kinetics, lipids, membranes, and proteins as machines. May be taught abroad.
102.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit for students who have completed ABI 102; only 1.5 units of credit for students who have completed BIS 105.
102.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or BIO 002); (CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B).

103.title: Bioenergetics & Metabolism
103.description: Fundamentals of the carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles in nature, including key reactions of biomolecules such as carbohydrates, amino acids, lipids, and nucleotides, and of energy production and use in different types of organisms. Principles of metabolic regulation.
103.credit_limit_text: 1.5 units of credit for students who have completed BIS 105; 1 unit of credit if students who have completed ABI 103.

104.title: Cell Biology
104.description: Membrane receptors and signal transduction; cell trafficking; cell cycle; cell growth and division; extracellular matrix and cell-cell junctions; cell development; immune system.
104.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 105 or ABI 102 C- or better).

105.title: Biomolecules & Metabolism
105.description: Fundamentals of biochemical processes, with emphasis on protein structure and activity; energy metabolism; catabolism of sugars, amino acids, and lipids; and gluconeogenesis.
105.credit_limit_text: 1.5 units of credit for students who have completed BIS 102 or BIS 103; no credit for students who have completed both BIS 102 and BIS  103; 1 unit of credit for students who have completed ABI 102 or ABI 103; no credit for students who have completed both ABI 102 and ABI 103.
105.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or BIO 002); (CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B).

192.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
192.description: Internship in Biological Sciences.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

194H.title: Research Honors
194H.description: Students majoring in Biological Sciences who have completed two quarters (3-5 units per quarter) of 199 and who qualify for the honors program as defined by the current catalog. Opportunity for Biological Sciences majors to pursue intensive research culminating in the writing of a senior thesis with the guidance of faculty advisors.

197T.title: Tutoring in Biological Sciences
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in one of the Biological Sciences' regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: College of Biological Sciences staff members offer group study courses under this number.

075.title: Properties of Materials in Biological Systems
075.description: Properties of typical biological materials; composition and structure with emphasis on the effects of physical and biochemical properties on design of engineered systems; interactions of biological materials with typical engineering materials.

090C.title: Research Group Conference in Biological Systems Engineering
090C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing in Biological Systems Engineering or Food Engineering.

092.title: Internship in Biological Systems Engineering
092.description: Supervised work experience in biological systems engineering.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing; project approval prior to period of internship.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Group study of selected topics; restricted to lower division students.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

130.title: Modeling of Dynamic Processes in Biological Systems
130.description: Techniques for modeling processes through mass & energy balance, rate equations, and equations of state. Computer problem solution of models. Example models include package design, evaporation, respiration heating, thermal processing of foods, and plant growth.
130.prereq_text: (ENG 006 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV ); (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better); EBS 075.

161.title: Kinetics & Bioreactor Design
161.description: Provide the basic principles of reactor design for bioprocess applications. Emphasizes the following topics: 1) kinetics and reactor engineering principles; 2) bio-reaction kinetics; and 3) bioreactor design.

170B.title: Engineering Projects: Design
170B.description: Individual or group projects involving the design of devices, structures, or systems to solve specific engineering problems in biological systems.  Project for study is jointly selected by student and instructor.
170B.prereq_text: EBS 170A; EBS 170BL (can be concurrent); EBS 170BL required concurrently.

170BL.title: Engineering Projects: Design Laboratory
170BL.description: Individual or group projects involving the design of devices, structures, or systems to solve specific engineering problems in biological systems.
170BL.prereq_text: EBS 170B (can be concurrent); EBS 170B required concurrently.

189A.title: Special Topics in Biological Systems Engineering: Agricultural Engineering
189A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Engineering.

190C.title: Research Group Conference in Biological Systems Engineering
190C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Biological Systems Engineering of Food Engineering.

192.title: Internship in Biological Systems Engineering
192.description: Supervised work experience in biological systems engineering.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

197T.title: Tutoring in Biological Systems Engineering
197T.description: Tutoring individual students, leading small voluntary discussion groups, or assisting the instructor in laboratories affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

265.title: Design & Analysis of Engineering Experiments
