265.description: Simple linear, multiple, and polynomial regression, correlation, residuals, model selection, one-way ANOVA, fixed and random effect models, sample size, multiple comparisons, randomized block, repeated measures, and Latin square designs, factorial experiments, nested design and subsampling, split-plot design, statistical software packages.
265.prereq_text: STA 100; ASE 120; or an introductory course in statistics.

289C.title: Selected Topics in Biological Systems Engineering: Biological Engineering

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Weekly seminars on recent advances and selected topics in biological systems engineering. Theme changes from quarter to quarter.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference
290C.description: Research problems, progress and techniques in biological systems engineering.

390.title: Supervised Teaching in Biological & Agricultural Engineering
390.description: Tutoring and teaching students in undergraduate courses offered in the Department of Biological and Agricultural Engineering. Weekly conferences with instructor; evaluation of teaching. Preparing for and conducting demonstrations, laboratories and discussions. Preparing and grading exams.

001.title: Introductory Biology: Ecology & Evolution
001.description: Fundamentals of ecology, evolution, and heredity. Processes that generate and maintain biological diversity, spanning genes to ecosystems. May be taught abroad.
001.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken BIS 002B.

001L.title: Introductory Biology Lab: Ecology & Evolution
001L.description: Inquiry-based, hands-on field and lab experience in ecology, evolution, and heredity. Processes that generate and maintain biological diversity, spanning genes to ecosystems.
001L.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken BIS 002B.

002.title: Introductory Biology: Molecules to Cells
002.description: Molecular basis of life, illustrating mechanistic underpinnings and evolution. Fundamentals of molecular biology, cellular biology, and metabolism. May be taught abroad.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken BIS 002A.
002.prereq_text: BIO 001 C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better.

002L.title: Introductory Biology Lab: Molecules to Cells
002L.description: Inquiry-based, hands-on laboratory experience in molecular and cellular biology. Interactions and responses of cells to a changing environment.
002L.prereq_text: (BIO 001L C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better); BIO 002 (can be concurrent).

003.title: Introductory Biology: Cells Through Organisms
003.description: How multicellular organisms solve life’s problems, including basics of cell communication and organization into tissues and organs. Examples from across the tree of life illustrate how organisms sense and respond to abiotic and biotic environments, acquire resources, maintain homeostasis, prevent disease, and reproduce. Interactive laboratory and discussion activities emphasize critical thinking, data analysis, and direct observation of these key biological phenomena.
003.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have taken BIS 002D.
003.prereq_text: (BIO 001 C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better); (BIO 002 C- or better or BIS 002A C- or better).

088V.title: Introduction to Research
088V.description: Introduction to types of research, including the basics of joint research with a faculty mentor. Self-assessments to identify areas of interest, priorities, and fit. Literature search and library skills used in early stages of research. Research safety, integrity, and intellectual property.

089C.title: Topics in Biomedical Engineering
089C.description: Topics in Biomedical Engineering. (C) Biomedical Engineering.

106.title: Biotransport Phenomena
106.description: Principles of momentum and mass transfer with applications to biomedical systems; emphasis on basic fluid transport related to blood flow, mass transfer across cell membranes, and the design and analysis of artificial human organs.
106.prereq_text: BIM 020 C- or better; BIM 020L; (BIM 116 or BIM 181 or NPB 101); PHY 009B; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B).

107.title: Manufacturing Processes for BME
107.description: Manufacturing processes and computer numerical control methods applied to the design and fabrication of biomedical devices.
107.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have previously taken EME 050.
107.prereq_text: BIM 020 C- or better; BIM 020L  C- or better.

110B.title: Biomedical Engineering Senior Design Experience
110B.description: Application of bioengineering theory and experimental analysis to a design project culminating in the design of a unique solution to a biomedical problem. Continues in BIM 110C.

141.title: Cell & Tissue Mechanics
141.description: Mechanical properties that govern blood flow in the microcirculation. Concepts in blood rheology and cell and tissue viscoelasticity, biophysical aspects of cell migration, adhesion, and motility.

142.title: Principles & Practices of Biomedical Imaging
142.description: Basic physics, engineering principles, and applications of biomedical imaging techniques including x-ray imaging, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound and nuclear imaging.

144.title: Principles of Biophotonics
144.description: Principles of biophotonics, emphasizing quantitative description of light propagation, light tissue interactions, and working operation and design of biosensors and devices for optical imaging for detection of biomolecules. Key technologies and illustrative applications in basic research, clinical diagnostics, and therapy.
144.prereq_text: PHY 009B; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B); or consent of instructor; BIM 108 or equivalent helpful.

145.title: Immuno-Engineering
145.description: Basic immunology and immunological tools. Survey of current immuno-therapeutic strategies. Ongoing research efforts to engineer the immune system for positive diagnostic and therapeutic outcomes.

151.title: Computational Tools & Applications in Bioengineering & Biomedicine
151.description: State-of-the-art computational tools and methods for biomolecular systems in bioengineering and biomedicine applications. Foundations, methods, and tools for the design of aptamers in biosensor applications, design of cancer vaccines, identification of therapeutic targets in cancer pathways, control of signal transduction networks disrupted in disease, and design of transcriptional programs for genetic engineering.
151.prereq_text: BIS 002A; PHY 009B; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B).

152.title: Molecular Control of Biosystems
152.description: Fundamentals of molecular biomedicine covering state-of-the-art methods for quantitative understanding of gene regulation and signal transduction networks at different levels of organization in health and disease. Topics include classic genetic systems, synthetic circuits, networks disrupted in disease and cancer.
152.prereq_text: BIS 002A; PHY 009B; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B).

173.title: Cell & Tissue Engineering
173.description: Engineering principles to direct cell and tissue behavior and formation. Cell sourcing, controlled delivery of macromolecules, transport within and around biomaterials, bioreactor design, tissue design criteria and outcomes assessment.
173.prereq_text: BIM 106 C- or better; BIM 109 C- or better.

239.title: Advanced Finite Elements & Optimization
239.description: Introduction to advanced finite elements and design optimization methods, with application to modeling of complex mechanical, aerospace and biomedical systems. Application of states of the art in finite elements in optimum design of components under realistic loading conditions and constraints.

241.title: Introduction to Magnetic Resonance Imaging
241.description: Basic hardware, acquisition, and reconstruction of MRI. Basic and advanced pulse sequences, MRI sequence design and sampling requirements, and image reconstruction strategies. Clinical applications of MRI.

243.title: Radiation Detectors for Biomedical Applications
243.description: Radiation detectors and sensors used for biomedical applications.  Emphasis on radiation interactions, detection, measurement and use of radiation sensors for imaging. Operating principles of gas, semiconductor, and scintillation detectors.

280.title: Neural Signals & Machine Learning Tools for Neural Data
280.description: Select and use machine learning tools to analyze neural data. Knowledge of the definitions and fundamental principles of data analytics related to neural data including field potentials (EEG, iEEG, local field potentials, EMG) and single neuron or muscle action potentials. Neural decoding/encoding, how to apply classifiers, regression and dimension reduction techniques, factor analysis and dynamic modeling.

284.title: Mathematical Methods for Biomedical Engineers
284.description: Theoretical applications of linear systems, ordinary and partial differential equations, and probability theory and random processes that describe biological systems and instruments that measure them. Students will be introduced to numerical solution techniques in MATLAB.
284.prereq_text: MAT 022B; STA 130A; or consent of instructor; upper division biomedical engineering majors, and graduate students in sciences and engineering; priority given to Biomedical Engineering graduate students.

286.title: Nuclear Imaging in Medicine & Biology
286.description: Radioactive decay, interaction of radiation with matter, radionuclide production, radiation detection, digital autoradiography, gamma camera imaging, single photon emission computed tomography, positron emission tomography and applications of these techniques in biology and medicine.

288.title: Living Matter: Physical Biology of the Cell
288.description: Introduction to the origin, maintenance, and regulation of the dynamic architecture of the cell, including cellular modes of organization, dynamics and energy dissipation, molecular transport, motility, regulation, and adaptability.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar in biomedical engineering

201.title: Current Topics in Biophotonics & Bioimaging Research
201.description: Designed to help graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in the field of Biophotonics and Bioimaging research and related areas.

200A.title: Current Techniques in Biophysics
200A.description: Current Techniques in Biophysics. Topics include mathematical methods, modeling, mass spectrometry, stochastic process, scanning probe microscopy, electron microscopy, fluorescence, membrane diffusion/mechanics, and single particle tracking.
200A.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; CHE 110A; or equivalents.

200LA.title: Biophysics Laboratory
200LA.description: One five-week laboratory assignment in the research laboratory of a Biophysics Graduate Group faculty member. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design.

200LB.title: Biophysics Laboratory
200LB.description: Two five-week laboratory assignments in the research laboratories of Biophysics Graduate Group faculty members. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design.

288.title: Living Matter: Physical Biology of the Cell
288.description: Introduction to the origin, maintenance, and regulation of the dynamic architecture of the cell, including cellular modes of organization, dynamics and energy dissipation, molecular transport, motility, regulation, and adaptability.

290.title: Biophysics Seminar
290.description: Presentation of current research by experts in biophysics.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

290C.title: Research Conference in Biophysics
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate-student research in biophysics.
290C.prereq_text: BPH 299 (can be concurrent); graduate standing in Biophysics and/or consent of instructor.

223.title: Biostatistics: Generalized Linear Models
223.description: Likelihood and linear regression; generalized linear model; Binomial regression; case-control studies; dose-response and bioassay; Poisson regression; Gamma regression; quasi-likelihood models; estimating equations; multivariate GLMs.

290.title: Seminar in Biostatistics
290.description: Seminar on advanced topics in the field of biostatistics. Presented by members of the Biostatistics Graduate Group and other guest speakers.

299.title: Special Study for Biostat Graduate Students
299.description: Special topics in Biostatistics appropriate for directed individual study on advanced topics not otherwise covered in the Biostatistics curriculum.

299D.title: Dissertation Research
299D.description: Research in Biostatistics under the supervision of major professor.
299D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advancement to Candidacy for Ph.D.

091.title: Undergraduate Seminars in Biotechnology
091.description: Undergraduate oriented seminar series focused on biotechnology research and product development. Speakers from campus and the private sectors discuss ongoing research, product development and biotechnology careers.

092.title: Internship in Biotechnology
092.description:
Work experience on or off campus in subject area pertaining to biotechnology or in a business, industry or agency associated with
biotechnology. Internship supervised by faculty member in the animal or plant sciences.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

150.title: Applied Bioinformatics
150.description:
Concepts and programs needed to apply bioinformatics in biotechnology research. Sequence analysis and annotation and use of plant and animal databases for students in biological and agricultural sciences. 

BIS 101V added to prereqs effective 202501. 9/11/24 DV
150.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed ECS 124.
150.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 032B or ECS 010 or ECS 015 or PLS 021 or PLS 021V); (PLS 120 or STA 013 or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y or STA 100); or consent of Instructor.

161A.title: Genetics & Biotechnology Laboratory
161A.description: Techniques of genetic analysis at the molecular level including recombinant DNA, gene mapping and basic computational biology.
161A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 161A.
161A.prereq_text: PLS 152 or BIS 101 or BIS 101v; and consent of instructor.

161B.title: Plant Genetics & Biotechnology Laboratory
161B.description: Advanced techniques of genetic analysis at the molecular and cellular levels, including plant transformation, plant genome editing, and analysis of transgenic plants.
161B.prereq_text: PLS 152 or BIS 101 or BIS 101V; consent of instructor.

189L.title: Laboratory Research in Genomics & Biotechnology
189L.description: Formulating experimental approaches to current questions in biotechnology; performance of proposed experiments.

192.title: Internship in Biotechnology
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in a subject area pertaining to biotechnology or in a business, industry or agency associated with biotechnology. Internship supervised by faculty member in the animal or plant sciences.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

194H.title: Honors Thesis in Biotechnology
194H.description: Independent study of selected topics under the direction of a member or members of the staff. Completion will involve the writing of a senior thesis.
194H.prereq_text: BIT 188; BIT 189L; consent of instructor; senior standing in Biotechnology with 3.250 GPA or higher.

422.title: Data Design & Representation
422.description: Introduction to business applications involving standard, streaming, and network data. Emphasis on scalable technologies for processing and analyzing big data for diverse applications.

442.title: Advanced Statistics
442.description: Continue exploring statistical reasoning using maximum likelihood estimation, Bayesian models, nonparametric models, Monte Carlo Markov Chain, time series, model specification, model selection, and dimension reduction.

452.title: Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence
452.description: Construct algorithms for learning from data and analyze the process for deriving business intelligence. Coverage of supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, etc.

463.title: Practicum Analysis & Implementation
463.description: Focus on completing project deliverables by polishing statistical and non-statistical quantitative analysis, generating insights for technical and business stakeholders, integrating proposed solutions into partner workflows and organizations, and disseminating the findings and outcomes through presentations and publications.

192.title: Internship in Cardiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in cardiology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

199.title: Cardiology Research
199.description: Special study by individual arrangement in cardiovascular medicine. Work will include directed readings, laboratory and discussions.

498.title: Special Group Study: EKG Unit
498.description: Special group study in cardiology for medical students in EKG unit. May include lectures, directed reading, and/or discussion groups.
498.prereq_text: Medical student with advance approval by monthly attending faculty.

101.title: Human Gross Anatomy
101.description: Detailed study of the gross anatomical structure of the human body, with emphasis on function and clinical relevance to students entering health care professions.
101.prereq_text: BIS 002A; concurrent enrollment in EXB 106L or CHA 101L strongly recommended.

101L.title: Human Gross Anatomy Laboratory
101L.description: Detailed study of prosected human cadavers in small group format with extensive hands-on experience.
101L.prereq_text: BIS 002A; (EXB 106 (can be concurrent) or CHA 101 (can be concurrent)); if EXB 106 or CHA 101 is not taken concurrently, it must have been already completed.

192.title: Internship in Morphology
192.description: Experience of supervised internship in research laboratories of members of the department.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; laboratory science experience including some chemistry; approval of project by preceptor prior to period of internship.

197T.title: Tutoring in Cell Biology & Human Anatomy
197T.description: Provides laboratory instruction in gross and microscopic human anatomy, with small groups of undergraduates under the supervision of the instructor.
197T.prereq_text: CHA 101 B or better; and consent of instructor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed reading, discussion, and/or laboratory experience on selected topics.

290C.title: Research Group Conference
290C.description: Discussion of problems, progress and literature groups relevant to current research undertaken by laboratory groups Human Anatomy.
290C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate student with research experience (may be taken concurrently).

497T.title: Tutoring in Human Anatomy
497T.description: Assist instructor by tutoring medical students in preparation for one of the departmental courses that is a component of the required curriculum for the School of Medicine.
497T.prereq_text: Advanced standing or consent of instructor.

498.title: Advanced Group Study
498.description: Directed reading and group discussions and/or laboratory experience on selected topics.
498.prereq_text: Medical students, interns, and residents with consent of instructor.

001Y.title: Design of Coffee–An Introduction to Chemical Engineering
001Y.description: Non-mathematical introduction to how chemical engineers think, illustrated by elucidation of the process of roasting and brewing coffee. Qualitative overview of the basic principles of engineering analysis and design. Corresponding experiments testing design choices on the sensory qualities of coffee.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 001, ECM 001, ECM 005 or ECH 005.

002Y.title: World Coffee Cultures
002Y.description: Coffee cultural traditions and practices from around the world. Historical perspectives and analysis of future trends. Corresponding experiments testing distinct cultural influences on the sensory qualities and nutritional aspects of coffee beverages.

005.title: Introduction to Analysis & Design in Chemical Engineering
005.description: Quantitative introduction to the engineering principles of analysis and design. Applications of differential and integral calculus. Laboratory experiments using coffee to illustrate chemical engineering concepts and to conduct an engineering design competition.
005.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed ECM 001 or ECH 001; not open for credit to students who have completed ECM 005.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing.

142.title: Heat Transfer for Biochemical & Chemical Engineers
142.description: Conduction, convection, and radiation of thermal energy in applications to chemical and biochemical engineering. Derivation of thermal and mechanical energy equations. Thermal boundary layers. Macroscopic balances. Applications: heat transfer in tubes, channels, and integrated circuits, and analysis of heat exchangers.
142.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 153.

145A.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics Laboratory
145A.description: Laboratory experiments in chemical engineering thermodynamics.
145A.prereq_text: ECH 140; ECH 152A (can be concurrent); UWP 102E (can be concurrent).

148B.title: Chemical Kinetics & Reaction Engineering
148B.description: Design and analysis of non-isothermal reactors. Reactions in packed beds with pressure drop. Adsorption and heterogeneous catalysis.  Transport limitations.
148B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECH 146. (Formerly ECH 146)

152A.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
152A.description: Application of principles of thermodynamics to chemical processes.
152A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ENG 105 or ENG 105A.

155.title: Chemical Engineering Kinetics & Reactor Design Laboratory
155.description: Laboratory experiments in chemical kinetics, reactor design and process control.
155.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECH 155B.
155.prereq_text: ECH 145B; ECH 148B (can be concurrent); ECH 157 (can be concurrent).

158BN.title: Process Economics & Green Design
158BN.description: Senior design experience in process and product creation and design with multiple realistic constraints. Cost accounting and capital investment estimation. Profitability analysis techniques. Green chemistry, health risk assessment and life cycle assessment concepts.
158BN.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken ECH 158A.

161C.title: Biotechnology Facility Design & Regulatory Compliance
161C.description: Design of biotechnology manufacturing facilities. Fermentation and purification equipment, and utility systems. Introduction to current good manufacturing practices, regulatory compliance, and documentation.
161C.prereq_text: (ECH 158BN (can be concurrent), ECH 161AN, ECH 161BN (can be concurrent )) or DEB 263 (can be concurrent).

192.title: Internship in Chemical or Biochemical Engineering
192.description: Supervised work experience in Chemical or Biochemical Engineering.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of a minimum of 84 units; project approval before period of internship.

253C.title: Advanced Mass Transfer
253C.description: Kinematics and basic conservation principles for multicomponent systems. Constitutive equations for momentum, heat and mass transfer, applications to binary and ternary systems. Details of diffusion with reaction, and the effects of concentration.

256.title: Chemical Kinetics & Reaction Engineering
256.description: Analysis of the performance of chemical reactors and design of chemical reactors based on the principles of chemical kinetics and transport phenomena. Consideration of noncatalytic/catalytic reactions in single fluid phases and emphasis on reactions in multiphase mixtures, especially gas-solid reactors.

289E.title: Special Topics in Chemical Engineering: Biotechnology

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar.

294.title: Current Progress in Biotechnology
294.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subjects of their own research activities.

002A.title: General Chemistry
002A.description: Periodic table, stoichiometry, chemical equations, physical properties and kinetic theory of gases, chemical equilibrium, acids and bases. Laboratory experiments in stoichiometric relations, properties and collection of gases, atomic spectroscopy, introductory quantitative analysis and acids and bases.
002A.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed CHE 004A; not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002AH or CHE 004B.
002A.prereq_text: High school chemistry and physics, and concurrent enrollment in mathematics at or above the level of MAT 012 strongly recommended; must earn a qualifying score of 24 or higher on the Chemistry Placement Exam or complete CHE 001 or CHE 001V with a C- or higher; more information about the Chemistry Placement Requirements can be found at https://chemistry.ucdavis.edu/undergraduate/general-chemistry-series/chemistry-placement-requirements/0000.

002B.title: General Chemistry
002B.description: Continuation of CHE 002A. Thermodynamics, atomic and molecular structure and chemical bonding, condensed phases and intermolecular forces, solubility. Laboratory experiments in thermochemistry, equilibria, and quantitative analysis using volumetric methods.
002B.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed CHE 004A; not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002BH or CHE 004B.

004A.title: General Chemistry for the Physical Sciences & Engineering
004A.description: General chemistry course with a more rigorous treatment of material covered in CHE 002A, intended for students majoring in the physical sciences and engineering.
004A.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed CHE 002A; not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002AH or 002B.
004A.prereq_text: MAT 021A (can be concurrent); must earn a qualifying score of 28 or higher on the Chemistry Placement Exam or complete CHE 001 or CHE 001V with a C- or higher; high school chemistry and physics strongly recommended; more information about the Chemistry Placement Requirements can be found at https://chemistry.ucdavis.edu/undergraduate/general-chemistry-series/chemistry-placement-requirements/0000.

004B.title: General Chemistry for the Physical Sciences & Engineering
004B.description: General chemistry course with a more rigorous treatment of material covered in CHE 002B, intended for students majoring in the physical sciences and engineering.
004B.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed CHE 002A; not open for credit for students who have completed CHE 002B or 002BH.
004B.prereq_text: MAT 021B (can be concurrent); (CHE 004A C- or better or CHE 002AH C- or better); or consent of instructor.

008B.title: Organic Chemistry: Brief Course
008B.description: Laboratory concerned primarily with organic laboratory techniques and the chemistry of the common classes of organic compounds. Lecture portion a continuation of CHE 008A.
008B.credit_limit_text: Varying credit hours according to courses taken previously and corresponding expected workload for this course; full credit to students who complete CHE 118A or 128A; 3 units credit to students who have completed CHE 128A and CHE 129A (students who have completed CHE 129A are exempt from the laboratory portion of CHE 008B); 2 units credit to students who have completed CHE 128B; 1 unit credit to students who have completed CHE 118B or CHE 128B and CHE 129A (students who have completed CHE 118B are exempt from the laboratory portion of CHE 008B).

100.title: Environmental Water Chemistry
100.description: Practical aspects of water chemistry in the environment, including thermodynamic relations, coordination chemistry, solubility calculations, redox reactions and rate laws. Computer modeling of the evolution in water chemistry from contact with minerals and gases.

107A.title: Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences
107A.description: Physical chemistry intended for majors in the life science area. Introductory development of classical and statistical thermodynamics including equilibrium processes and solutions of both non-electrolytes and electrolytes. The thermodynamic basis of electrochemistry and membrane potentials.
107A.prereq_text: (CHE 002C or CHE 002CH or CHE 004C); (MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 021C); (PHY 007C or PHY 009C or PHY 009HC).

107B.title: Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences
107B.description: Continuation of CHE 107A. Kinetic theory of gases and transport processes in liquids. Chemical kinetics, enzyme kinetics and theories of reaction rates. Introduction to quantum theory, atomic and molecular structure, and spectroscopy. Application to problems in the biological sciences.

110B.title: Physical Chemistry: Properties of Atoms & Molecules
110B.description: Group theory. Application of quantum mechanics to polyatomic molecules and molecular spectroscopy. Intermolecular forces and the gas, liquid and solid states. Distributions, ensembles and partition functions. Transport properties.

110C.title: Physical Chemistry: Thermodynamics, Equilibria & Kinetics
110C.description: Development and application of the general principles of thermodynamics and statistical thermodynamics. Chemical kinetics, rate laws for chemical reactions and reaction mechanisms.

115.title: Instrumental Analysis
115.description: Intermediate theory and laboratory techniques in analytical and physical chemistry. Advanced data analysis methods and goodness-of-fit criteria.  Fourier-transform spectroscopic methods and instrumentation. Mass spectrometry. Electrochemistry. Liquid chromatography.

118A.title: Organic Chemistry for Health & Life Sciences
118A.description: The 118A-C series is for students planning professional school studies in health and life sciences. Rigorous, in-depth presentation of basic principles with emphasis on stereochemistry and spectroscopy and preparations and reactions of nonaromatic hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, alcohols and ethers.
118A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit for students who have completed CHE 008A; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 008B or CHE 128A.
118A.prereq_text: CHE 002C C- or better or CHE 002CH C- or better or CHE 004C C- or better.

118B.title: Organic Chemistry for Health & Life Sciences
118B.description: Continuation of CHE 118A, with emphasis on spectroscopy and the preparation and reactions of aromatic hydrocarbons, organometallic compounds, aldehydes and ketones.
118B.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit to students who completed CHE 128B.; not open for credit to students who have completed 8 or more units of CHE 128 and CHE 129.

122.title: Chemistry of Nanoparticles
122.description: Chemical and physical aspects of inorganic nanoparticles. Topics include synthesis, structure, colloidal behavior, catalytic activity, size and shape dependency of physical properties, analytical methods and applications.
122.prereq_text: CHE 110C (can be concurrent) or CHE 107B (can be concurrent).

124A.title: Inorganic Chemistry: Fundamentals
124A.description: Symmetry, molecular geometry and structure, molecular orbital theory of bonding (polyatomic molecules and transition metals), solid state chemistry, energetics and spectroscopy of inorganic compounds.

124B.title: Inorganic Chemistry: Main Group Elements
124B.description: Synthesis, structure and reactivity of inorganic and heteroorganic molecules containing the main group elements.

124L.title: Laboratory Methods in Inorganic Chemistry
124L.description: The preparation, purification and characterization of main group and transition metal inorganic and organometallic compounds.

125.title: Advanced Methods in Physical Chemistry
125.description: Advanced theory and laboratory techniques in analytical and physical chemistry. Advanced spectroscopic methods. Thermodynamics. Kinetics. Chemical literature. Digital electronics and computer interfacing. Laboratory measurements and vacuum techniques.

128A.title: Organic Chemistry
128A.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of organic chemistry with emphasis on stereochemistry and the chemistry of hydrocarbons. Designed primarily for majors in chemistry. Chemistry majors should enroll in CHE 129A concurrently.
128A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit allowed for students who have completed CHE 008A; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 008B or 118A.
128A.prereq_text: CHE 002C C or better or CHE 002CH C or better or CHE 004C C- or better.

128B.title: Organic Chemistry
128B.description: Continuation of CHE 128A with emphasis on the chemistry of alcohols, ethers, their sulfur analogs, and carbonyl compounds. Introduction to the application of spectroscopic methods to organic chemistry. Introduction to synthesis of moderately complex organic molecules.
128B.credit_limit_text: Full credit to students who completed CHE 008B or CHE 118A; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 118B.

129A.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
129A.description: Introduction to laboratory techniques of organic chemistry. Emphasis on methods used for separation and purification of organic compounds.
129A.credit_limit_text: Full credit to students who completed CHE 008B; not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 118B.
129A.prereq_text: (CHE 002C C or better or CHE 002CH C or better or CHE 004C C- or better); CHE 128A (can be concurrent).

129B.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
129B.description: Continuation of CHE 129A. Emphasis on methods used for synthesis and isolation of organic compounds.
129B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHE 118C.

130A.title: Principles of Medicinal Chemistry
130A.description: Examination of the design principles and experimental methods used in pharmaceutical and medicinal chemistry.

130B.title: Computational Drug Design
130B.description: Continuation of CHE 130A with emphasis on case studies of various drugs and the use of computational methods in drug design.

150.title: Chemistry of Natural Products
150.description: Chemistry of terpenes, steroids, acetogenins, and alkaloids: isolation, structure determination, biosynthesis, chemical transformations, and total synthesis.

192.title: Internship in Chemistry
192.description: Supervised internship in chemistry; requires a final written report.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; project approval by faculty sponsor prior to enrollment.

194HA.title: Undergraduate Honors Research
194HA.description: Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in the writing of an extensive report.
194HA.prereq_text: Open only to chemistry majors who have completed 135 units and who qualify for the honors program.

194HB.title: Undergraduate Honors Research
194HB.description: Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in the writing of an extensive report.
194HB.prereq_text: Open only to chemistry majors who have completed 135 units and who qualify for the honors program.

194HC.title: Undergraduate Honors Research
194HC.description: Original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, culminating in the writing of an extensive report.
194HC.prereq_text: Open only to chemistry majors who have completed 135 units and who qualify for the honors program.

205.title: Symmetry, Spectroscopy, & Structure
205.description: Vibrational and rotational spectra; electronic spectra and photoelectron spectroscopy; magnetism; electron spin and nuclear quadrapole resonance spectroscopy; nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy; other spectroscopic methods.

210A.title: Quantum Chemistry: Introduction & Stationary-State Properties
210A.description: Stationary-state quantum chemistry: postulates of quantum mechanics, simple solutions, central field problems and angular momenta, hydrogen atom, perturbation theory, variational theory, atoms and molecules.
210A.prereq_text: CHE 110B; CHE 110C; or consent of instructor.

211B.title: Statistical Mechanics
211B.description: Statistical mechanics of nonequilibrium systems, including the rigorous kinetic theory of gases, continuum mechanics transport in dense fluids, stochastic processes, brownian motion and linear response theory.

219.title: Spectroscopy of Organic Compounds
219.description: Identification of organic compounds and investigation of stereochemical and reaction mechanism phenomena using spectroscopic methods–principally NMR, IR and MS.

219L.title: Laboratory in Spectroscopy of Organic Compounds
219L.description: Practical application of NMR, IR and MS techniques for organic molecules.

222.title: Chemistry of Nanoparticles
222.description: Chemical and physical aspects of inorganic nanoparticles, including synthesis, purification, reactivity, characterization, and applications for technology. Emphasis is on problems from the current literature.
222.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CHE 122.

231A.title: Organic Synthesis: Methods & Strategies
231A.description: Current strategies and methods in synthetic organic chemistry. Focus on construction of carbon frameworks, control of relative and absolute stereochemistry and retrosynthetic strategies. Use of databases and molecular modeling software in multistep strategies.

237.title: Bio-Organic Chemistry
237.description: Structure and function of biomolecules; molecular recognition; enzyme reaction mechanisms; design of suicide substrates for enzymes; enzyme engineering; design of artificial enzymes and application of enzymes in organic synthesis.
237.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Chemistry or consent of instructor.

241C.title: Mass Spectrometry
241C.description: Mass spectrometry and related methods with emphasis on ionization methods, mass analyzers, and detectors.  Related methods may include ion-molecule reactions, unimolecular dissociation of organic and bio-organic compounds, and applications in biological and environmental analysis.

261.title: Current Topics in Chemical Research
261.description: Designed to help chemistry graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in their immediate field of research and related areas.
261.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Chemistry or consent of instructor.

263.title: Introduction to Chemical Research Methodology
263.description:
Introduction to identification, formulation, and solution of meaningful
scientific problems including experimental design and/or theoretical analyses of new and prevailing techniques, theories and hypotheses. May be repeated for credit when topic differs.
263.prereq_text: CHE 293; and consent of instructor; graduate student standing in Chemistry.

264.title: Advanced Chemical Research Methodology
264.description: Applications of the methodology developed in CHE 263 to experimental and theoretical studies. Advanced methods of interpretation of results are developed. Includes the preparation of manuscripts for publication.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar.

294.title: Presentation of Chemistry Research
294.description: Introduces first- and second-year Chemistry graduate students to the process of giving an effective research presentation. Advanced Ph.D. students give formal seminars describing the design and execution of their research projects.

296.title: Research in Pharmaceutical Chemistry
296.description: Laboratory provides qualified graduate students with the opportunity to pursue original investigation in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and allied fields in order to fulfill the letter-graded research requirement of the Integrated B.S./M.S. Program in Chemistry (Pharmaceutical Chemistry Emphasis).
296.prereq_text: CHE 130A; CHE 130B; CHE 135; CHE 233 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

299.title: Research
299.description: The laboratory is open to qualified graduate students who wish to pursue original investigation. Students wishing to enroll should communicate with the department well in advance of the quarter in which the work is to be undertaken.

010.title: Introduction to Chicana/o Studies
010.description: Analysis of the situation of the Chicana/o (Mexican-American) people, emphasizing their history, literature, political movements, education and related areas.

021.title: Chicana/o & Latina/o Health Care Issues
021.description: Overview of health issues of Chicanas/os and Latinas/os in the State of California; role of poverty/lack of education in limited access to health care.

030.title: United States Political Institutions & Chicanas/os
030.description: Overview of the major political institutions and ideologies of the United States and the Chicana/o people's historical and contemporary role in, effects from, and responses to them. Theory, method and critical analysis.

040.title: Comparative Health: Top Leading Causes of Death
040.description: Introduction to the epidemiology of the leading causes of death for ethnic/racial minorities. Assessment of disproportionate rates at which ethnic/racial minorities suffer and die from chronic and infectious diseases and injuries and statistical methods used to calculate these rates.
040.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHI 040S.
040.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013Y; or consent of instructor.

042.title: Food Justice: Chicana/o & Indigenous Communities
042.description: Issues surrounding food justice in Chicana/o and Indigenous Communities. Emphasis on discourses and practices of growing a food justice movement centered on the ecological care of the earth and decolonized environmental methodologies.

050.title: Chicana & Chicano Culture
050.description: Interdisciplinary survey of Chicana/o cultural representation in the 20th century. Examines Chicana/o culture within a national and transnational context. Explores how Chicano cultural forms and practices intersect with social/material forces, intellectual formations and cultural discourses. (Former CHI 020.)

092.title: Internship
092.description: Academic guidance combined with internship in community agencies serving Mexican/Latina/Latino/Chicana/Chicano clients. Students will use their bilingual skills and knowledge of history, culture, economics, politics and social issues.
092.prereq_text: CHI 010 or CHI 010V; or consent of instructor.

112.title: Globalization, Transnational Migration, & Chicana/o & Latina/o Communities
112.description: Chicana/o and Latina/o migration experiences within a global context. Topics include national and/or transnational migration in Mexico, Central America, and the United States.

119V.title: Central Americans in the U.S.: Legacies, Identities, & Social Movements
119V.description: Central Americans in the United States, United States intervention and the consequent diaspora. Identity formations, health status, academic achievement of unaccompanied minors, and refugees are considered using intersectional analysis and with emphasis on how they are shaped by immigration policies.

122.title: Psychology Perspectives Chicana/o & Latina/o Family
122.description: Role of migration and acculturation on family structure and functioning. From a psychological and Chicana/o Studies perspective, contemporary gender roles and variations in family structures are examined. Special topics include family violence, addiction, family resilience and coping strategies.
122.prereq_text: CHI 010 or CHI 010V; and consent of instructor; introductory psychology course highly recommended.

130.title: United States-Mexican Border Relations
130.description:
Theories of U.S.-Mexican border relations, with an overview of the political, economic, and social relationships and an in-depth
analysis of immigration issues, border industrialization, women's organizations, economic crises, and legal issues.

131.title: Chicanas in Politics & Public Policy
131.description: Historical and political analysis of Chicana/Latina political involvement and activities in the general political system, women's movement, Chicano movement, and Chicana movement. Examines the public policy process and the relationship of Chicanas/Latinas to public policy formation.

155.title: Chicana/o Theater
155.description: Examination of the formal and thematic dimensions of Chicana/o theater in the contemporary period with special emphasis on El Teatro Campesino and Chicana Feminist Theater. Bilingual readings, lectures, discussions, and writing in Spanish. (Former course SPA 126B.)
155.prereq_text: Intermediate Spanish or consent of instructor.

160.title: Mexican Film & Greater Mexican Identity
160.description: Survey of the role Mexican cinema plays in consolidation and contestation of post-revolutionary Mexican state and in the formation of a Greater Mexican cultural identity including Chicana/o identity. Showcases genres, perios, auteurs, movements and emphasis on gendered and sexualized narratives.

161.title: Queer Latinidad
161.description: Introduction to queer Latina and Latino studies with a focus on Chicana and Chicano theory and cultural production.

172.title: Chicana/o Voice/Poster Silk Screen Workshop
172.description: The poster as a voice art form used by Chicanas/os and other people of color to point to the defects of social and political existence and the possibility for change, from the Chicana/o artists' perspective.
172.prereq_text: CHI 070 or CHI 073; and consent of instructor.

181.title: Chicanas & Latinas in the U.S.: Historical Perspectives
181.description: Historical issues in the lives of Chicanas and Latinas in the U.S. and their diverse countries of origin.

192.title: Internship in the Chicana/Chicano/Latina/Latino Community
192.description: Academic guidance combined with internship in community agencies serving Mexican/Latina/Latino/Chicana/Chicano clients. Use of bilingual skills and knowledge of history, culture, economics, politics and social issues. Internship project required.
192.prereq_text: (CHI 010 or CHI 010V or CHI 021 or CHI 050); (SPA 003 or SPA 003V or SPA 003Y); or equivalent of SPA 003.

194HA.title: Senior Honors Research Project
194HA.description: Student is required to read, research, and write Honors Thesis on Chicana/o Studies topics.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing in Chicana/o Studies major.

194HB.title: Senior Honors Research Project
194HB.description: Student is required to read, research, and write Honors Thesis on Chicana/o Studies topics.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing in Chicana/o Studies major.

194HC.title: Senior Honors Research Project
194HC.description: Student is required to read, research, and write Honors Thesis on Chicana/o Studies topics.
194HC.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing in Chicana/o Studies major.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
198.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of Program Chairperson.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of Program Chairperson.

241.title: Community Based Participatory Research
241.description: Provides knowledge & skills to plan and implement participatory & community based projects that highlight community empowerment framework.

001.title: Elementary Chinese
001.description: Developing elementary level skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing in Mandarin Chinese in everyday communication settings. Introduction of fundamentals of pronunciation, grammar, and Chinese characters will be introduced.
001.prereq_text: No background in Chinese or placement exam or consent of instructor.

002.title: Elementary Chinese
002.description: Continuation of elementary level skill development in listening, speaking, reading and writing Mandarin Chinese in everyday communication settings.  Continued introduction of basic vocabulary and characters as well as core grammar, and further train pronunciation.
002.prereq_text: CHN 001; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

002BL.title: Accelerated Chinese for Heritage Speakers II
002BL.description: Further trainings on all the communicative skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing for students that already have elementary level ability to understand or speak Mandarin Chinese. Emphases on standard Mandarin pronunciation, Chinese characters, and discourse level conversations.
002BL.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHN 018.
002BL.prereq_text: CHN 001BL; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

003.title: Elementary Chinese
003.description: Continuation of elementary level skill development in listening, speaking, reading and writing Mandarin Chinese in everyday communication settings.  Continued introduction of basic vocabulary and characters as well as core grammar, and further train pronunciation.
003.prereq_text: CHN 002; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

005.title: Intermediate Chinese
005.description: Training continues at intermediate-level in spoken and written Chinese in cultural contexts, based on language skills developed in CHN 004.
005.prereq_text: CHN 004 or placement exam or consent of instructor.

011.title: Great Books of China (in English)
011.description: Readings in English translation of classical and medieval Chinese poetry, Chinese historiography, tales of the supernatural, Tang romances, opera, and late imperial era vernacular literature, with key works by Sima Qian, Gan Bao, Tao Qian, Han Yu, and Feng Menglong. Background information on periods, authors and the interrelationships of culture, literature and social change.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

110.title: Great Writers of China: Texts & Context (in English)
110.description: Examination of major theoretical concepts and interpretive methods in the study of literature by using examples from the Chinese tradition; discussions of classical and modern works with an emphasis on the relations between literature, author, society, and culture.

112.title: Modern Chinese: Reading & Discussion
112.description: Further development of communication skills from CHN 111 in Modern Standard Mandarin-speaking environments. Reading dialogues/articles pertaining to contemporary China issues and discussing ethical, moral, aesthetic, social, and cultural concerns.
112.prereq_text: CHN 111; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

122.title: Business Chinese
122.description: Mandarin Chinese language for business and professional purposes. Appropriate usages and protocols within the context of Chinese business culture.

130.title: Readings in Traditional Chinese Fiction
130.description: Examination of representative works of traditional Chinese fiction popular from the 12th Century until the 17th and 18th centuries. Translations in English of the Chinese texts will be available to students as reference.

150.title: Fifth-Year Chinese: Selected Topics in Chinese Language, Literature, & Culture
150.description: Examination of literary works and scholarly essays on selected topics of Chinese culture and society. Development of a deep understanding of Chinese culture and society through sophisticated Chinese speaking and writing exercises.
150.prereq_text: CHN 120; or placement exam or consent of instructor.

160.title: The Chinese Language
160.description: Introduction to structural features of Chinese (Mandarin) sounds, lexicon, grammar, and writing (characters), as well as relevant dialectal and sociolinguistic issues of the language.
160.prereq_text: CHN 006 (can be concurrent) or CHN 003BL (can be concurrent) or CHN 003CN (can be concurrent) or CHN 004A (can be concurrent); or placement exam or consent of instructor; LIN 001 recommended.

192.title: Chinese Internship
192.description: Work experience in the Chinese language, with analytical term paper on a topic approved by instructor.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing and consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Chinese
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the Department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of Department.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

396.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
396.description: Any course taught by a graduate student under the direction of the Director.

001.title: Introduction to Film Studies
001.description: Analysis of film form and narrative, including cinematography, editing, and sound. Issues in film studies including authorship, stardom, race, gender, class, and cultural identity. Introduction to selected cinematic movements and national film traditions.

003.title: Media Archaeology
003.description: Evolution of media technologies and practices beginning in the 19th century as they relate to contemporary digital arts practices. Special focus on the reconstruction of the social and artistic possibilities of lost and obsolete media technologies.
003.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken TCS 005.

012.title: Introduction to Media Computation
012.description: Introduction to key computational ideas necessary to understand and produce digital media. Fundamentals of programming and analysis of how media are represented and transmitted in digital form. Aimed primarily at non-computer science students.
012.credit_limit_text: Two units of credit for students that have taken ECS 010, ECS 030, ECS 032A, ECS 032AV, ECS 036A, or ENG 006.

040B.title: Media History 2: 1945-Present
040B.description: History of media from 1945 to present, with particular focus on the development of the computer, digital network and internet technologies in the context of other media infrastructures like radio, television and satellite networks.

041A.title: History of Cinema from 1895-1945
041A.description: Examination of the cultural context of the emergence of cinema. Discussion of cinema as a product of the age of industrialization and conquest, as well as an element of urban culture, and mass transportation.
041A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CTS 041A.

072.title: Introduction to Games
072.description: Introduction to the history, theory, and practice of play. Survey of both analog and digital games. Overview of gaming cultures, aesthetics, industries, and technologies.

123.title: Sight & Soundtrack
123.description: Use of sound to articulate, lend mood or subconsciously underscore visual, environmental, or performative situations, combining music, voice, sound effects and other noises to create sound designs that enhance, alter or support action and movement.

158.title: Technology & the Modern American Body
158.description: History and analysis of relationships between human bodies and technologies in modern society. Dominant and eccentric examples of how human bodies and technologies influence one another and reveal underlying cultural assumptions.
158.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken TCS 158.

162.title: Surveillance Media
162.description: Surveillance technologies and media surveillance in daily life. Topics include CCTV, facial recognition, tracking systems, biosensors, data mining, encryption, and AI. Analysis of laws, security measures, and counter-surveillance practices.

166.title: Topics in U.S. Film History
166.description: Study of an aspect of American film history (such as the silent era; the studio system; U.S. avant-garde cinema), including the influences of technological, economic, regulatory, cultural, and artistic forces.

167.title: Topics in Film Genres
167.description: Study of one or more of the film genres (such as musicals, film noir, screwball comedy, or westerns), including genre theory and the relationship of the genre(s) to culture, history, and film industry practices. May be taught abroad.

170.title: Narrative Game Design
170.description: Narrative game design. Character, dialogue, environmental storytelling, procedurally generated text, play as narrative. Workshop, critique, and publish narrative and text-based games.
170.prereq_text: ENL 072 or CDM 072 or ENL 172 or CDM 172 or STS 172; or consent of instructor.

172.title: Video Games & Culture
172.description: Critical approaches to the study of video games, focusing on formal, historical, and cultural modes of analysis. History of software and hardware in North American and global contexts. Relations of games to society, politics, economics, media, etc.
172.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CTS 172 (former course CTS 172).

176.title: Special Topics in Digital Game Development
176.description: Special topics in digital game development for upper division students.
176.prereq_text: CDM 072 or CDM 172 or CTS 172; or consent of instructor. Recommended: CDM 173, CDM 175 or CDM 177.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Supervised internship, on or off campus, in the area of cinema and digital media.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study in cinema and digital media. For students with upper division standing. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study in cinema and digital media. For advanced undergraduates with upper division standing. May be taught abroad.

148B.title: Japanese Literature on Film
148B.description: Survey of films based on works of Japanese literature, emphasis on pre-modern and early modern texts. Introduction to major directors of Japan, with a focus on cinematic adaptation. Lectures and readings in English. Films in Japanese with English subtitles.

016.title: Spatial Data Analysis
016.description: Computer-aided design and geographic information systems in civil engineering practice.

100.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics for Civil & Environmental Engineers
100.description: Fluid flow in civil & environmental engineering, basis for design, buoyancy, hydrostatics, gravity dams, hydraulic modeling: similarity & scaling, conservation laws, flow in bends, nozzles, pipes, pumps, turbines, complimentary lab experiments.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ENG 103.
100.prereq_text: ENG 035 C-  or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better); PHY 009B C-  or better.

114.title: Probabilistic Systems Analysis for Civil & Environmental Engineers
114.description: Probabilistic concepts and models in engineering. Statistical analysis of engineering experimental and field data. Introduction to stochastic processes and models of engineering systems.
114.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed STA 120.

115.title: Computer Methods in Civil & Environmental Engineering
115.description: Presentation, implementation and application of numerical algorithms and computer models for the solution of practical problems in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
115.prereq_text: (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better); programming course.

130.title: Structural Analysis
130.description: Elastic structural analysis of determinate and indeterminate trusses, beams and frames. Plastic bending and limit analysis.
130.prereq_text: (ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A).

133.title: Structure & Properties of Civil Engineering Materials
133.description: Structures & properties of common civil engineering materials including concrete, alloys, plastics, and wood. Mechanical behavior of elastic & plastic response to loading, thermal conductivity and resistivity, diffusivity, and deterioration mechanisms.
133.prereq_text: CHE 002A C- or better; ENG 035 C- or better.

134.title: Structural Loads: Calculation & Modeling
134.description: Structural analysis process and model idealization; design codes, standards, and guidelines (e.g., IBC & ASCE 7); load paths for vertical and horizontal loads; load cases and load combinations; modeling of loads using finite element software; dead and live loads; snow loads; wind loads; climate change effects on snow and wind loads.
134.prereq_text: ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better.

135.title: Structural Design: Concrete Elements
135.description: Strength design procedures for columns, rectangular beams, T-beams and beams of general cross-section. Building code requirements for flexure, shear, combined axial and bending stress, bond and serviceability.
135.prereq_text: ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better.

140B.title: Chemical Principles for Environmental Engineers
140B.description: Aqueous chemistry; equilibrium relationships; carbonate system; thermodynamics; kinetics & rate laws; precipitation, adsorption, & volatilization phenomenon; oxidation & reduction reactions; pH, pE and predominance diagrams; organic chemicals.
140B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECI 140.

144.title: Groundwater Systems Design
144.description: Groundwater occurrence, distribution, and movement; groundwater flow systems; radial flow to wells and aquifer testing; aquifer management; groundwater contamination; solute transport by groundwater; fate and transport of subsurface contaminants.  Groundwater supply and transport modeling.

146.title: Water Resources Simulation
146.description: Computer simulation techniques in the analysis, design and operation of surface water systems; modeling concepts and practices with application to surface runoff; water quality in rivers and streams and dispersion of contaminants in water bodies.

149L.title: Air Pollution Lab
149L.description: Laboratory characterization of air pollutants; data analysis; experimental design
149L.prereq_text: ECI 149N C- or better (can be concurrent).

149N.title: Air Pollution
149N.description: Physical and technical aspects of air pollution. Factors that determine local, regional, and global air quality; climate change; and physical and chemical properties of pollutants.
149N.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECI 149.
149N.prereq_text: MAT 021D; (MAT 022B or MAT 027B); CHE 002B C- or better; (ATM 121A or ENG 103 C- or better or ECI 100 C- or better).

161.title: Transportation System Operations
161.description: Principles of transportation system operations; traffic characteristics and methods of measurement; models of transportation operations and congestion applied to urban streets and freeways.
161.prereq_text: MAT 021C C- or better; PHY 009A C- or better.

171.title: Soil Mechanics
171.description: Soil formations, mass-volume relationships, soil classification, effective stress, soil-water-void relationships, compaction, seepage, capillarity, compressibility, consolidation, strength, states of stress and failure, lateral earth pressures, and slope stability.
171.prereq_text: (ENG 103 (can be concurrent) or ECI 100 (can be concurrent)); (ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better); ECI 171L (can be concurrent); ECI 171L required concurrently.

171L.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
171L.description: Laboratory studies utilizing standard testing methods to determine physical, mechanical and hydraulic properties of soil and demonstration of basic principles of soil behavior.
171L.prereq_text: ECI 171 (can be concurrent); ECI 171 required concurrently.

178.title: Pavement Engineering & Design
178.description: Pavement types (rigid, flexible, unsurfaced, rail), their applications (roads, airfields, ports, rail) and distress mechanisms. Materials, traffic and environment characterization. Empirical and mechanistic-empirical design procedures. Construction quality; asphalt concrete mix design.
178.prereq_text: (ENG 104 C- or better or ENG 104V C- or better); ECI 171 C- or better recommended.

181.title: Construction Cost Estimation & Analysis
181.description: Fundamentals of cost estimation within the construction industry. Methodologies and use of estimating processes through each stage of project acquisition and delivery. Case-study based projects involve current technologies and estimating practices.

189C.title: Selected Topics in Civil Engineering: Engineering Planning
189C.description: Directed group study in Engineering Planning.

191C.title: Civil & Environmental Engineering Career Pathways
191C.description: Demonstration of different civil and environmental engineering career options; engagement with CEE alumni through panels

193A.title: Civil & Environmental Engineering Senior Design
193A.description: Culminating design experience for civil engineering and environmental engineering majors. Student teams work closely with faculty, city officials or consulting clients to propose, implement and validate a unique solution to a real-world problem.
193A.prereq_text: ECI 114 C- or better; (ECI 115 C- or better or ECI 153 C- or better or MAT 118A C- or better); (ECI 140CN C- or better or (ECI 171 C- or better, ECI 171L C- or better) or (ECI 130 C- or better, ECI 132 C- or better, ECI 134 C- or better) or (ECI 130 C- or better, ECI 132 C- or better, ECI 135 C- or better) or (ECI 130 C- or better, ECI 134 C- or better, ECI 135 C- or better) or (ECI 161 C- or better, ECI 162 C- or better) or (ECI 162 C- or better, ECI 163 C- or better) or (ECI 163 C- or better, ECI 161 C- or better) or (ECI 141 C- or better, ECI 141L C- or better)), (UWP 101 or UWP 102E or UWP 102G or UWP 104A or UWP 104E or UWP 104T).

212A.title: Finite Element Procedures in Applied Mechanics
212A.description: Weighted-residual and Rayleigh-Ritz methods.  Weak/variational formulation and development of discrete equations using finite element approximations.  Application to one- and two-dimensional problems (heat conduction).

232.title: Advanced Topics in Concrete Structures
232.description: Ductility of reinforced concrete; strength of two-way slabs; modified compression field theory.

237.title: Bridge Design
237.description: Bridge types, behavior and construction characteristics; design philosophy, details according to Caltrans and American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials codes, principles; seismic design and retrofit of concrete bridges; modern bridges using advanced fiber reinforced polymer composites; fieldtrip required.

240.title: Water Quality
240.description: Quality requirements for beneficial uses of water. Hydrologic cycle of quality. Hydromechanics in relation to quality of surface and groundwaters; transport and fate of waterborne pollutants. Heat budget for surface waters; predictive methods; introduction to water quality modeling.

243B.title: Biological Treatment of Wastewater
243B.description: Regulations; microbiology and kinetics of engineered biological processes; aeration; and activated sludge.

244A.title: Life Cycle Assessment for Sustainable Engineering
244A.description: Life cycle assessment methodology. Emphasis on applications to infrastructure and energy systems. Life cycle design, life cycle cost methods, other tools from industrial ecology, and links to policy.
244A.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken ECI 244.

248A.title: Environmental Health Engineering
248A.description: Principles and practices of environmental health engineering. Identification, evaluation, and management of environmental factors that impact public health with an emphasis on viruses and waterborne pathogens. Wastewater-based epidemiology, quantitative microbial and chemical risk assessment, and the removal and inactivation of pathogens in water and wastewater treatment.

251.title: Transportation Demand Analysis
251.description: Procedures used in urban travel demand forecasting. Principles and assumptions of model components (trip generation, trip distribution, model split). New methods of estimating travel demand. Computer exercises using empirical data to calibrate models and forecast travel demand.

253.title: Dynamic Programming & Multistage Decision Processes
253.description: Operations research. Optimization techniques with a focus on dynamic programming in treating deterministic, stochastic, and adaptive multistage decision processes. Brief review of linear programming and non-linear programming. Applications in transportation networks and other civil infrastructure systems.
253.prereq_text: MAT 021C; MAT 022A; programming course; EAD 115 recommended.

268.title: Infrastructure Economics
268.description: Economics applied to infrastructure engineering planning, operations, maintenance, and management problems; microeconomic and macroeconomic theories; benefit-cost analysis; effect of uncertainty; optimization economics; non-classical economics; public finance.
268.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); ENG 106; or the equivalent.

273.title: Water Resources Systems Engineering
273.description: Planning and management of water resource systems. Deterministic and stochastic simulation and optimization techniques. Capacity design and operation of reservoir systems for water supply, hydropower, flood control, and environmental objectives.

275.title: Hydrologic Time-Series Analysis
275.description: Application of statistical methods for analysis and modeling of hydrologic series.  Statistical simulation and prediction of hydrologic sequences using time series methodology.

278.title: Hydrodynamics
278.description: Perturbation methods. Basic water waves. Governing equations for fluid motion on a rotating earth. Rotation effects, vorticity dynamics, Ekman layer. Stratification effects, internal waves and turbulent mixing. Combined effects.

281C.title: Integrated Site Characterization
281C.description: Integrated site characterization using field and laboratory techniques. Applied within context of slope stability analysis as a representative design problem.
281C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECI 281B.

292B.title: Geotechnical Professional Practice 2
292B.description: Geotechnical practice issues that affect the delivery of technical solutions for geotechnical projects, including business and management practices, contract documents, legal constraints, public policy and societal concerns, ethics, and professional development. Part 2 of three part series that includes a capstone project.

295A.title: Engineering Education I
295A.description: Overview of the discipline of engineering education. One course in a three-course series.

296.title: Topics in Water & Environmental Engineering
296.description: Seminars presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis faculty, researchers, postdocs, and graduate students.
296.prereq_text: Graduate standing; or consent of instructor.

008.title: World Classical Cultures
008.description: Study of selected ancient cultures of the world. Analysis of the construction of terms such as “classics,” “civilization,” and “culture.” Examination of the plural legacies of classical cultures in the modern world. Ancient cultures examined may include the Greco-Roman Mediterranean, Egypt, Maya Mesoamerica, Han China, Maurya South Asia, Mesopotamia.

010.title: Greek, Roman, & Near Eastern Mythology
010.description: Examination of major myths of Greece, Rome, and the Ancient Near East; their place in the religion, literature and art of the societies that produced them; their subsequent development, influence and interpretation.

030.title: Greek & Latin Elements in English Vocabulary
030.description: Knowledge of Latin and Greek not required. Elements of Greek and Latin vocabulary for increased understanding of English word formation and improved ability to understand and retain unfamiliar words. Emphasis on Greek and Latin elements but other languages not neglected.

060.title: Magic in the Ancient Greco-Roman World
060.description: Magical practices and theories in ancient Greece and Rome and in the wider Mediterranean, including Mesopotamia and Egypt. Curses and spells in material culture, literary depictions of spell-casters, magic’s place in ancient society, and the modern afterlife of ancient magical practices.

100B.title: Writing for Ancient Mediterranean Studies
100B.description: Advanced instruction in writing and practice in effective styles of communication for Ancient Mediterranean Studies and related academic and professional fields.

171.title: Mediterranean Bronze Age Archaeology
171.description: Archaeological monuments of the ancient Near East, including Egypt and Mesopotamia, and of Greece and Crete during the Bronze Age. Special emphasis on the problems of state formation and on the co-existence and collapse of Bronze Age societies.
171.prereq_text: A lower division Classics (CLA) course or consent of instructor.

190.title: Senior Seminar
190.description: Advanced interdisciplinary study of a problem in the ancient Mediterranean world using the techniques of history, archaeology, art history and philology.
190.prereq_text: Completion of one upper division course in Latin (LAT), Greek (GRK) or Hebrew (HEB) or consent of instructor.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis under the direction of faculty advisor.
194HA.prereq_text: Admission to the Honors Program; consent of faculty member supervising honors thesis.

197TC.title: Community Tutoring in Classical Languages
197TC.description: Supervised instruction of Greek or Latin in nearby schools by qualified students in department.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

203.title: Methods in Clinical Research
203.description: Overview of major approaches to clinical research, including health services research techniques, informatics, GCRC, and preclinical methodologies to enhance clinical projects. Overview of UC Davis clinical research support infrastructure. Methodologies applicable to clinical research and its multi-disciplinary perspective.
203.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; Completed one of the following degrees: MD, DDS, DMD, OD, ND, DO, PharmD, DVM, PhD or DNS in nursing; application and acceptance into the Clinical Research Graduate Group, TL1/T32, KL2/K12, MCRTP, or other SOM training program.

209.title: Introduction to Grant Writing, II
209.description: Second in a two-quarter series. Two-course sequence provides training in practical aspects of competitive grant writing.

211.title: Critical Assessment of the Biomedical Literature
211.description: Exposure to topical issues and controversies in the design of interdisciplinary translational research, with an emphasis on critical assessment of the biomedical and health sciences literature. Extends students’ knowledge of study design through practical application.

215.title: Clinical Trials in Medicine
215.description: Importance, design, and execution of clinical trials.
215.prereq_text: CLH 244 C or better; SPH 205AY C or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor.

240.title: Predoctoral Clinical Research Training Program Research Integration
240.description: Alternating sessions:  journal club, seminar/discussion, and research integration sessions.
240.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment in the Predoctoral Clinical Research Training Program in the CTSC, School of Medicine.

290C.title: Literature in Stem Cell Biology
290C.description: Critical presentation and analysis of recent journal articles in stem cell biology by students.

298.title: Group Study in Clinical Research
298.description: Special topics in Clinical Research appropriate for group study at the graduate level.

299.title: Clinical Research
299.description: Independent research and special topics in clinical research appropriate for graduate level.

001.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
001.description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary cognitive scientific approach to the study of mind, drawing concepts and methods from psychology, philosophy, linguistics, artificial intelligence, and other disciplines.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

001B.title: First Year Engagement: Career & Professional Development
001B.description: Formal and informal processes of discovering passion and choosing the path in support of this discovery. Campus resources and tools available in pursuit of passion. Expectations of the industry; development of assessment and problem-solving skills necessary for success in the professional world.
001B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously taken LTS 001.

002B.title: Aggie Explorers: Career Exploration
002B.description: Exploratory for first-year students in the College of Letters and Science, who are undeclared or undecided about their major. Career possibilities through self-reflection and experiential learning. How natural talents, interests, and personality relate to career paths and learn methods to prepare for career opportunities.
002B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LTS 002.

098F.title: Student Facilitated Course
098F.description: Student-facilitated (taught) course intended for lower division students.

001.title: Introduction to Public Speaking
001.description: Practice in the preparation and delivery of speeches based on principles and strategies of informing and persuading audiences drawn from the social sciences and humanities.

003V.title: Interpersonal Communication Competence
003V.description: Communication competence in professional settings. Managing face-to-face and virtual teams. Leadership, conflict management and negotiation skills. Communication in diverse organizations. Leveraging communication networks. Effective interviewing.

010V.title: Introduction to Communication
010V.description: Basic principles of communication and communication processes; models of communication; foundations of empirical research in communication; contexts of communication and communication research, including interpersonal, intercultural, news, entertainment, mediated, and others.
010V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 010Y.

012Y.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
012Y.description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

101Y.title: Communication Theories
101Y.description: Forms, functions, development, and testing of communication theory, with emphasis on social scientific approaches. Survey and comparison of significant micro and macro theories and models of face-to-face and mediated communication. Application of theories to real-world problems.
