102V.title: Empirical Methods in Communication
102V.description: Social scientific research methods employed in Communication. Topics include research design, measurement, sampling, questionnaire construction, survey research, experimental design, content analysis and qualitative field methods.
102V.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013Y; or equivalent of STA 013.

114.title: Communication & Cognition
114.description: Relationship between communication and cognition in interpersonal and mediated contexts. Discourse comprehension and production, impact of language attitudes on social judgments, the effects of information processing on decision making.
114.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CMN 138.

120.title: Interpersonal Communication
120.description: Theories and principles of interpersonal communication related to perception, verbal and nonverbal channels, mutual understanding, and relationship development. Communication processes in face-to-face and technologically-mediated encounters. Consideration of different relationship contexts, including friendships, dating and family relationships, and the workplace.
120.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CMN 134.

122.title: Nonverbal Communication
122.description: Examination of the interaction between nonverbal communication and verbal communication channels in influencing outcomes in interpersonal relationships. Underlying functions served by nonverbal communication are considered.
122.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CMN 135.

124.title: Family Communication
124.description: Theories and research on family communication. Communication in courtship, marriage, and relational dissolution. Processes and outcomes of parent-child, sibling, family roles, and inter-generational communication. Interaction patterns associated with marital/family satisfaction, maintenance, divorce, and dysfunction. Cultural influences on family communication.

131.title: Strategic Communication in Public Relations
131.description: Principles, evolution, and professional practice of public relations. Planning and execution of effective, ethical communication strategies and campaigns. Distribution of messages through traditional and new media, including social media. Cultivation of relationships between organizations and their publics. Crisis communication management.

136.title: Organizational Communication
136.description: Organizational communication theory and practice is examined with an emphasis on the use of effective communication strategies for achieving organizational goals.

140.title: Introduction to Mass Communication
140.description: History of mass media and media research traditions. Organization and economics of the media industry. Media policy, law, regulation and ethics.  Impact of the media on individuals and society. Traditional, new and emerging communication technologies.

141.title: Media Effects: Theory & Research
141.description: Social scientific studies of the effects of mass media messages on audience members' actions, attitudes, beliefs, and emotions. Topics include the cognitive processing of media messages, television violence, political socialization, cultivation of beliefs, agenda-setting, and the impact of new technologies.

142.title: Newsmaking
142.description: The making of news. How journalists construct news and how consumers and newsmakers use it.  Effects of news, technology’s challenges to journalism, and the relationship of news to other institutions.

143.title: Analysis of Media Messages
143.description: Examination of alternative approaches to the analysis, interpretation, and evaluation of media messages, including those disseminated through broadcasting, print, and new technologies.

145.title: Political Communication
145.description: Relationships among the mass media, citizens, and politics, production of political news, campaign strategies, and citizens’ attitudes and behaviors. Frameworks for mediated politics, the news, and elite discourse and campaign messages.

146.title: Communication Campaigns
146.description: Strategic uses of media and interpersonal communication channels in health, environmental advocacy, and political campaigns. Emphasis on general principles relevant to most campaign types, including public information, social marketing, and media advocacy campaigns.

147.title: Children, Adolescents, & the Media
147.description: Research on the adaptive and maladaptive effects of media (e.g., television, movies, video games, social media) on the social, emotional, cognitive, and physical development of youth, considering the protective role of parents, teachers, ethics, and policy.

148.title: Contemporary Trends In Media
148.description: Global trends in media, including media and globalization, impacts of the new media economy, media and security, and effects of ownership on media content and culture.

149.title: Race & Media
149.description: Examines how race and ethnicity as social categories are shaped by mass media. Focuses on the impact of race and ethnicity role portrayals in content and style of news, television and cinema.

152V.title: Social Science with Online Data
152V.description: Survey of web-driven social science and its methods. Focus on web scraping and social media API’s. Covers wrangling and analysis of data from social networks, online experiments, and other digital traces. Python programming skills helpful, but not assumed.
152V.prereq_text: Programming experience helpful, but not required.

161.title: Health Communication
161.description: Health communication theories and research. Health literacy, social support and coping, doctor-patient interaction, health communication campaigns, media influences on health, and applications of new technologies in health promotion.

170.title: Digital Technology & Social Change
170.description: Conceptual understanding of how digital communication technologies transform our lives through social media, mobile connectivity, globalization, and big data. Contexts include education, health, entrepreneurship, democracy, and poverty.
170.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed CMN 170V.

172.title: Interpersonal Technologies
172.description: Theories and research findings on how people use technologies for interpersonal and relational purposes, including impression formation, self-presentation, deception, anonymity, friendship maintenance, online dating, and emotional expression.

174.title: Social Media
174.description: Application of communication theories to the study and design of social media. Examination of social media in contexts such as political activism and collaboration. Topics include online credibility, participatory culture, viral media and privacy.

176V.title: Video Games Theory & Research
176V.description: Communication theory and research on the uses and effects of video games. Research methods available for investigating game use and the impact of games on behavior. Application of those methods in a research project.

178.title: Persuasive Technologies
178.description: Designing and testing ethical, technology-based communication interventions in the domains of health, marketing, education, and environment. Social media, mobile apps, wearable devices, recommendation systems, serious games, and augmented reality.

197T.title: Tutoring in Communication
197T.description: Tutoring in undergraduate Communication courses, including leadership of discussion groups affiliated with departmental courses.
197T.prereq_text: Upper division standing with major in Communication and consent of Department Chairperson.

210.title: Experimental Methods & Analysis in Communication
210.description: Experimental designs in communication. Topics include: causation; threats to validity; conceptualization, operationalization, and measurement; hypothesis testing; ethics; data analysis software focusing on the analysis of variance and planned contrasts; and the practical and effective implementation and writing of experiments.
210.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing; one course in inferential statistics.

233.title: Persuasive Technologies for Health
233.description: Theorizing, designing and evaluating ethical technology-based health communication interventions. Uses of social media, mobile communication apps, wearable devices, computer-generated tailored messages, educational games, and computational approaches in health promotion and healthcare delivery.

250.title: Mediated Communication Theory & Research
250.description: Survey of major theories on the intended and unintended effects of mediated communication. Topics include media's effects on learning, political behavior, interpersonal violence, sexual socialization, consumer behavior, race relations, gender socialization, and cultural processes.

275Y.title: Computational Social Science
275Y.description: Survey of modern computational research methods. Big data, social network analysis, machine learning, Agent-based computer simulations. Online lectures are taught by faculty from all 10 UC campuses. Local face-to-face discussion section.
275Y.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have taken CMN 150V.

281.title: Special Topics in Mediated Communication
281.description: Reading, discussion, research, and writing on a selected topic in the specialty of mediated communication.

001.title: The Community
001.description:
Basic concepts of community analysis and planned social change. The dynamics of community change through case studies of communities including peasant, urban ghetto, suburban mainline, and California
farm workers.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

150.title: Quantitative Methods in Community Research
150.description: Introduction to statistical analysis of social data relevant to community research, planning and assessment, emphasizing data sources and acquisition, descriptive and inferential analysis techniques, and data interpretation and presentation. Emphasis on spatial data and methods, focusing on the sources, processing, analysis, and presentation of spatial data in a community assessment context.
150.prereq_text: SOC 046B or STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032; consent of instructor.

158.title: Community Governance
158.description: Governing institutions and political processes at the local level. Local government organization, community autonomy, leadership, political change, policy development, and select policy issues including public finance. Topics change depending on student interest. Field research on coalition building or policy issues in select communities.
158.prereq_text: CRD 001 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or POL 001 or POL 001Y.

164.title: Theories of Organizations & Their Role in Community Change
164.description: Planned change within and through community organizations. Private voluntary organizations, local community associations, and local government. Relationship between community organizations and social capital. Collaborative original data gathering and professional report writing.
164.prereq_text: (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or SOC 046B); (CRD 001 or CRD 002 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or ANT 002).

172.title: Social Inequality: Issues & Innovations
172.description: Focus on the dimensions, causes, and means of alleviating social inequality in the U.S. Examination and analysis of major theories and forms (class, race/ethnicity, gender, and citizenship status) of inequality. Policy-based and grassroots approaches to change.
172.prereq_text: CRD 001 or CRD 002 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or ANT 002; upper division standing recommended.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional
settings.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Completion of 84 units.

197T.title: Tutoring in Community & Regional Development
197T.description: Assisting instructor in one of the Community & Regional Development's regular courses by tutoring individual students or small groups of students in a laboratory, in voluntary discussion groups, or other voluntary activities.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; completion of course to be tutored.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

290.title: Community Development Seminar
290.description: Speaker series on key topics in community development.

292.title: Graduate Internship
292.description: Individually designed supervised internship, off campus, in community or institutional setting. Developed with advice of faculty mentor.

001.title: Major Works of the Ancient World
001.description: Introduction, through class discussion and frequent written assignments, to some of the major works of the ancient world (up to 5th century CE) such as The Odyssey, the Bible, Augustine's Confessions, and works by Plato and Confucius. Examined genres include religious texts, the epic, philosophy, drama, poetry.
001.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

002.title: Major Works of the Medieval & Early Modern World
002.description: Introduction, through class discussion and frequent written assignments, to some of the major works of the medieval and early modern worlds (6th century to the mid-17th century) such as Dante’s Comedy, 1001 Nights, The Tale of Genji, and Elizabethan/Jacobean plays. Examined genres include framed narratives, courtly literature, and early modern drama.
002.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

003.title: Major Works of the Modern World
003.description: Introduction, through class discussion and frequent written assignments, to some of the major works of the modern world (mid-17th to the mid-20th centuries) such as those by Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Flaubert, Woolf, Lu Xun, Borges and Yeats. Examined genres include realist fiction, modernist fiction, and modernist poetry.
003.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

004.title: Major Works of the Contemporary World
004.description: Comparative study of selected major Western and non-Western texts composed in the period from 1945 to the present. Intensive focus on writing about these texts, with frequent papers written about these works.
004.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005.title: Fairy Tales, Fables, & Parables
005.description: Introduction to fairy tales, fables, and parables as recurrent forms in literature, with such readings as tales from Aesop & Grimm, Chaucer & Shakespeare, Kafka & Borges, Buddhist & Taoist parables, the Arabian Nights, and African American folklore.

006.title: Myths & Legends
006.description: Introduction to the comparative study of myths and legends, with readings selected from Near Eastern, Teutonic, Celtic, Indian, Japanese, Chinese, African and Native American literary sources.

053A.title: Literature of East Asia
053A.description:
Introduction to representative masterpieces of East Asia with readings
from such works as The Story of the Stone, The Peach Blossom Fan, T'ang and Sung poetry, classical Japanese poetry, drama, and travel diaries, and The Tale of Genji.

110.title: Hong Kong Cinema
110.description: Hong Kong cinema, its history, industry, styles, genres, directors, and stars. Special attention to its polyglot, multicultural, transnational, colonial, and postcolonial environment.
110.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR), upper division standing, or consent of instructor.

156.title: The Ramayana
156.description: Exploration of the Indian epic, Ramayana, through the lens of literature, performance, and visual art. Emphasis on the text's diversity and its contemporary global relevance. Topics include Ramayanas in Southeast Asia, and in various South Asian diaspora communities.

172.title: A Story for a Life: The Arabian Nights
172.description: In-depth exploration of The Arabian Nights, the best-known work of pre-modern Arabic literature and a major work of world literature. Analysis of the work in its historical context and in comparison to other frame tales in world literature.

192.title: Internship in Comparative Literature
192.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Completion of 84 units.

194H.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194H.description:
Guided research, under the direction of a faculty member approved by the Program Director, leading to a senior honors thesis on a comparative
topic.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Open only to majors of senior standing who qualify for Honors Program.

197T.title: Tutoring in Comparative Literature
197T.description: Tutoring in undergraduate courses including leadership in small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with current courses offered by Comparative Literature.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing with declared major in Comparative Literature.

198.title: Directed Group Study for Advanced Undergraduates

210.title: Topics & Themes in Comparative Literature
210.description: Comparative, interpretive study of the treatment of specific topics and themes in literary works from various periods, societies, and cultures, in light of these works' historical and sociocultural contexts.
210.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Comparative Literature, English, or a foreign-language literature, or consent of instructor.

250A.title: Research in Primary Literature
250A.description: Individually guided research in the primary literature of concentration, under the supervision of a faculty member culminating in a conference paper. Required of M.A. and Ph.D. candidates.

250B.title: Research in Second Literature
250B.description: Individually guided research in the secondary literature of concentration, under the supervision of a faculty member, culminating in a paper. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

250C.title: Research in Third Literature or Special Topic
250C.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, in the third literature of concentration or on a special topic culminating in a paper. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

250D.title: Dissertation Prospectus
250D.description: Individually guided writing of the dissertation prospectus under supervision of a faculty member.  Must be taken prior to completion of the qualifying exam. Required of Ph.D. candidates.

297.title: Directed Independent Study in Primary, Secondary, or Third Literature
297.description: Directed Independent Study in Primary, Secondary, or Third Literature culminating in term paper. Only for languages with no graduate course offerings.

299D.title: Special Study for the Doctoral Dissertation
299D.description: Special study for the doctoral dissertation.

012.title: Introduction to Media Computation
012.description: Introduction to key computational ideas necessary to understand and produce digital media. Fundamentals of programming and analysis of how media are represented and transmitted in digital form. Aimed primarily at non-computer science students.
012.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students that have taken ECS 010, ECS 030, ECS 032A, ECS 032AV, ECS 036A or ENG 006.

017.title: Data, Logic, & Computing
017.description: Display, processing, and representation of information and data on a computer. Understanding and analyzing the digital representations of numbers, images, and sounds. Basic computer operations and their logic. Introduction to discrete mathematics in computer science, including propositional logic, proofs by induction, recursions, and counting. Introduction to algorithms. Uses of computers and their influence on society.
017.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed course ECS 020 or MAT108.
017.prereq_text: MAT 016A (can be concurrent) or MAT 017A (can be concurrent) or MAT 019A { can be concurrent } or MAT 021A (can be concurrent).

020.title: Discrete Mathematics For Computer Science
020.description: Discrete mathematics of particular utility to computer science. Proofs by induction. Propositional and first-order logic. Sets, functions, and relations. Big-O and related notations. Recursion and solutions of recurrence relations. Combinatorics. Probability on finite probability spaces. Graph theory.
020.prereq_text: MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better.

032AV.title: Introduction to Programming
032AV.description: Introduction to programming and problem solving in Python. Aimed primarily at non-major students.
032AV.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 036A, ECS 036B, ECS 036C.

032B.title: Introduction to Data Structures
032B.description: Design and analysis of data structures using Python; trees, heaps, searching, sorting, and graphs.
032B.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B, ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
032B.prereq_text: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better or ECS 036A C- or better.

034.title: Software Development in UNIX & C++
034.description: UNIX Operating system tools and programming environment. Methods for debugging and verification. Principles object-oriented programming in C++.
034.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 036B, ECS 036C, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
034.prereq_text: ECS 032C C- or better; or consent of instructor.

036A.title: Programming & Problem Solving
036A.description: Programming in modern C++ for students with prior experience. Fundamental programming constructs, abstraction using functions and basic classes, algorithmic design, and debugging. Emphasis on good programming style and effective use of UNIX-based development tools.
036A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed ECS 032A or ECS 032AV; no credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 034, ECS 040 or ECS 060.
036A.prereq_text: ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better; or must satisfy computer science placement exam; prior experience with basic programming concepts (variable, loops, conditional statements) required.

036B.title: Software Development & Object-Oriented Programming
036B.description: Advanced software development and object-oriented programming in modern C++. Implementation of substantial programs. Emphasis on software engineering practices, automation, and debugging.
036B.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have completed ECS 032B, ECS 032C, ECS 034, ECS 040, or ECS 060.

092.title: Internship in Computer Science
092.description: Supervised work experience in computer science.
092.prereq_text: Lower division standing; project approval prior to period of internship.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

111.title: Applied Machine Learning for Non-Majors
111.description: Machine learning methods and their application. Theory, design and evaluation of supervised/unsupervised machine learning algorithms. Practical use of matching learning methods and their challenges.
111.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken ECS 171; not intended for Computer Science and Computer Science Engineering Majors.
111.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067); (MAT 135A or STA 035B or STA 131A or MAT 107).

117.title: Algorithms for Data Science
117.description: Algorithms for searching, pattern matching, combinatorial problems, clustering, and time series analysis with practical emphasis.
117.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed ECS 122A
117.prereq_text: ECS 017 or ECS 020; ECS 032B or ECS 036C.

120.title: Theory of Computation
120.description: Fundamental ideas in the theory of computation, including formal languages, computability and complexity. Reducibility among computational problems.

122A.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
122A.description: Complexity of algorithms, bounds on complexity, analysis methods. Searching, sorting, pattern matching, graph algorithms. Algorithm design techniques: divide-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming. Approximation methods. NP-complete problems.

122B.title: Algorithm Design & Analysis
122B.description: Theory and practice of hard problems, and problems with complex algorithm solutions. NP-completeness, approximation algorithms, randomized algorithms, dynamic programming and branch and bound. Theoretical analysis, implementation and practical evaluations. Examples from parallel, string, graph, and geometric algorithms.

124.title: Theory & Practice of Bioinformatics
124.description: Fundamental biological, mathematical and algorithmic models underlying bioinformatics and systems biology; sequence analysis, database search, genome annotation, clustering and classification, functional gene networks, regulatory network inference, phylogenetic trees, applications of common bioinformatics tools in molecular biology and genetics.
124.prereq_text: (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ECS 036A or ENG 006); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or ECS 132 or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or BIM 105); (BIS 002A or MCB 010).

132.title: Probability & Statistical Modeling for Computer Science
132.description: Univariate and multivariate distributions. Estimation and model building. Markov/Hidden Markov models. Applications to data mining, networks, security, software engineering and bioinformatics.
132.prereq_text: (ECS 040 or ECS 034 or ECS 036B); ECS 020; MAT 021C; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

140A.title: Programming Languages
140A.description: Syntactic definition of programming languages. Introduction to programming language features including variables, data types, data abstraction, object-orientedness, scoping, parameter disciplines, exception handling. Non-imperative programming languages. Comparative study of several high-level programming languages.

150.title: Operating Systems & System Programming
150.description: Basic concepts of operating systems and system programming. Processes and interprocess communication/synchronization; virtual memory, program loading and linking; file and I/O subsystems; utility programs. Study of a real operating system.
150.prereq_text: (ECS 034 or ECS 036C or ECS 060); (ECS 154A or EEC 170).

152A.title: Computer Networks
152A.description: Overview of computer networks, TCP/IP protocol suite, computer-networking applications and protocols, transport-layer protocols, network architectures, Internet Protocol (IP), routing, link-layer protocols, local area and wireless networks, medium access control, physical aspects of data transmission, and network-performance analysis.
152A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have taken ECS 157.
152A.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (ECS 132 or EEC 161 or MAT 135A or STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A).

154A.title: Computer Architecture
154A.description: Introduction to digital design. Interfacing of devices for I/O, memory and memory management. Input/output programming, via wait loops, hardware interrupts and calls to operating system services. Hardware support for operating systems software.
154A.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit allowed for students who have taken EEC 170.

154B.title: Computer Architecture
154B.description: Hardwired and microprogrammed CPU design. Memory hierarchies. Uniprocessor performance analysis under varying program mixes. Introduction to pipelining and multiprocessors.
154B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 201A.

160.title: Software Engineering
160.description: Requirements, specification, design, implementation, testing, and verification of large software systems. Study and use of software engineering methodologies.

162.title: Web Programming
162.description: Technical aspects of building websites, including both server-side and client-side software development.
162.prereq_text: ECS 030 or ECS 034 or ECS 036B; or equivalent programming experience in C and the Unix environment.

164.title: Human-Computer Interaction
164.description: Introduction to concepts and practice of modern human-computer interaction design.

170.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
170.description: Design and implementation of intelligent computer systems. Knowledge representation and organization. Memory and inference. Problem solving. Natural language processing.

171.title: Machine Learning
171.description: Introduction to machine learning. Supervised & unsupervised learning, including classification, dimensionality reduction, regression & clustering using modern machine learning methods. Applications of machine learning to other fields.
171.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (STA 032 or STA 035B or STA 100 or STA 131A or MAT 135A or EEC 161 or ECS 132); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

175.title: Computer Graphics
175.description: Principles of computer graphics, with a focus on interactive systems. Current graphics hardware, elementary operations in two-and three-dimensional space, geometric transformations, camera models and interaction, graphics system design, standard graphics APIs, individual projects.
175.prereq_text: (ECS 060 or ECS 034 or ECS 036C); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067).

189G.title: Special Topics in Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence

193A.title: Capstone Project
193A.description: Responding to real-life client design challenges, student teams plan, implement, and evaluate large-scale projects involving computer and computational systems. Project supervised by a faculty member. Must take ECS 193A & ECS 193B to receive credit.
193A.prereq_text: ECS 160 (can be concurrent); ECS 150; upper division standing in Computer Science or Computer Science & Engineering; or consent of instructor.

198F.title: Student Facilitated Course
198F.description: Student facilitated course intended primarily for upper division students.

201A.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
201A.description: Modern research topics and methods in computer architecture. Design implications of memory latency and bandwidth limitations. Performance enhancement via within-processor and between-processor parallelism.
201A.credit_limit_text: One unit of credit if student has previously taken ECS 154B after Fall 2019.

232.title: Theory of Molecular Computation
232.description: Theory of chemical reaction networks, molecular circuits, DNA self-assembly, DNA sequence design and thermodynamic energy models, and connections to the field of distributed computing.
232.prereq_text: ECS 120 or ECS 220 recommended; probability course recommended, for example ECS 132 or MAT 135A or STA 012 or STA 131A or MAT 131A; or consent of instructor.

251.title: Operating Systems
251.description: Models, design, implementation, performance evaluation in operating systems. Algorithms, internal architectures for single processor OS and distributed systems. Concurrency control, recovery, security. OS kernel-level programming. Special topics embedded systems, real-time system, device driver, NPU (Network Processor Unit).

260.title: Software Engineering
260.description: Advanced techniques for domain-specific software reuse.

261.title: Program Verification
261.description: Methods of proving correctness of programs with respect to formal specifications, with attention to those suited for employing automated deduction. Logic background, symbolic execution, techniques suited to iterative programming, methods from denotational semantics, termination, dynamic logic and proofs of concurrent programs.
261.prereq_text: PHI 112; or MAT 125 or familiarity with first-order logic; knowledge of an integrative and functional programming language.

272.title: Information Visualization
272.description: Advanced topics in information visualization: perceptually effective display methods, color design and selection, interaction models and techniques, focus-context techniques, distortion methods, large graph visualization techniques, visual data mining methods, and evaluation methods.

289G.title: Special Topics in Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence

092.title: Internship in Consumer Science
092.description: Internship on and off campus in a consumer science related area.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Consumer Science
192.description: Internship on and off campus in a consumer science related area.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of a minimum of 84 units.

200A.title: Approaches to Critical Theory
200A.description: Critical overview of modern theoretical texts (e.g., semiotics, hermeneutics, deconstruction, social and cultural critique, feminist theory, psychoanalysis).

200B.title: Problems in Critical Theory
200B.description: Focused study of a particular critical theoretical approach, school or perspective. Topics may include but are not limited to: critical approaches to the study of literature, culture, film, historiography, visual culture, the body, and aesthetics.

200B.title: Theories of Cultural Studies
200B.description: Definitions of "critical" scholarship and examination of various contexts in which cultural studies theory has emerged worldwide. Both mainstream and alternative theoretical traditions, such as those developed by people of color and by other minoritized groups.

210.title: Memory, Culture, & Human Rights
210.description: Explores the multiple convergences among memory, culture, and human rights. Discusses diverse approaches to how societal actors in different historical, cultural, and national settings, construct meanings of past political violence, inter-group conflicts, and human rights struggles.
210.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

250.title: Research Seminar
250.description: Designed to facilitate student interaction and promote student research by guiding students through the production of a publishable essay.  Essays submitted, distributed, and discussed by seminar participants.
250.prereq_text: CST 200A; CST 200B; CST 200C; or consent of instructor.

270A.title: Individually Guided Research in Cultural Studies
270A.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Cultural Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270A.prereq_text: CST 200C; CST 250; and consent of instructor.

270B.title: Individually Guided Research in Cultural Studies
270B.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Cultural Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270B.prereq_text: CST 200C; CST 250; and consent of instructor.

270C.title: Individually Guided Research in Cultural Studies
270C.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Cultural Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270C.prereq_text: CST 200C; CST 250; and consent of instructor.

290.title: Colloquium
290.description: Designed to provide cohort identity and faculty student exchange.  Opportunity to present papers, hear guest lecturers, and see faculty presentations, gather for organizational and administrative news, exchange information, and make announcements.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

295.title: Special Topics
295.description: Special topics courses offered according to faculty and student interests and demands.
295.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Cutaneous Biology
192.description: Approval of project prior to internship by preceptor. Supervised work experience involving research on the skin. Final report.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

199.title: Special Study in Cutaneous Biology
199.description: Special study by individual arrangement of specialized topics in biology of skin. Work may be assigned readings, laboratory research or a combination.
199.prereq_text: Advanced undergraduate standing and/or consent of instructor.

299.title: Research in Cutaneous Biology
299.description: Independent research in cellular and biochemical mechanisms of cutaneous biology and pathology.

014.title: Design Drawing
014.description: Drawing as a tool for design. Basic skills in objective observation and representation, including line, shape, tone, and space. Drawing as a tool for formulating and working through design problems.
014.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); students who have prior unarticulated college level credit in design drawing are encouraged to submit a course equivalency review; this can include classes that have been granted Advanced Placement or International Baccalaureate credits; please see Design Department website for submission requirements and deadlines.

015.title: Form & Color
015.description: Understanding color, form and composition as ways of communicating design concepts and content. Color theory, color mixing, interaction of color. Design principles and elements. Gestalt theory. Explores a variety of materials, media and presentation techniques.
015.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

016.title: Graphic Design & Computer Technology
016.description: Introduction to digital tools with emphasis on graphic design including theory, practice and technology. Includes principles of color, resolution, pixels, vectors, image enhancement, layout, visual organization, visual hierarchy, typography.
016.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

021.title: Drafting & Perspective
021.description: Introduction to mechanical drafting, including scaled drawing, orthogonal projection, isometric, axonometric and perspective. Includes basic rendering techniques.
021.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

040A.title: Energy, Materials, & Design Over Time
040A.description: Global history of design across time, viewed through the lens of the effects of the creation and discovery of new energy sources, processes, and materials on design.

050.title: Introduction to Three-Dimensional Design
050.description: Design concept development and detailing as it relates to the making of objects, structures and models using form, scale and materials. Product design and rapid prototyping methods using a range of techniques for advancing the design process.
050.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

051.title: Computer-Assisted Drawing for Designers
051.description: Computer-assisted drawing (CAD) and modeling using a mid-level, multi-use CAD program. Basic architectural drawing and modeling technique in both two-dimensional and three-dimensional CAD environments.
051.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken DES 150A.
051.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

070.title: Introduction to Textile Design Structures
070.description: Introduction to diverse methods for creating textile structures. Exploration of the creative potential of hand-constructed textiles, manipulation of fabric to create dimensional surfaces, and the basics of building and joining fabric structures.
070.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed DES 023 or DES 024; not open for credit for students who have completed both DES 023 & DES 024.
070.prereq_text: DES 001 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

111.title: Coding for Designers
111.description: Programming concepts/skills for design. Algorithm-based design and development flowcharts. Pseudo-code entry level programming. Principles of coding logic syntax structure. Analysis of history. Development iteration presentation of design projects.
111.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who completed DES 037.
111.prereq_text: DES 001; DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

112.title: UI/UX Design: Principles & Practices
112.description: Principles and practices of User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX). Design for digital, interactive media. Iterative design processes, audience research.

115.title: Letterforms & Typography
115.description: Fundamentals of letterforms and typography. Characteristics of typefaces; formatting and composition of type. Principles of legibility, visual hierarchy, grid systems, and the integration of type and image.
115.credit_limit_text: Not available for credit to students who have completed DES 022.
115.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

116.title: Visual Communication: Graphic Design Studio
116.description: Multiple, conceptually-linked assignments focusing on the fundamental choices designers make in translating concepts into effective graphic form. Problem finding and analysis of audience needs. Design process from research and initial concepts to project prototypes. May be taught abroad.
116.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed DES 152 or DES 152A.
116.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; DES 115; or consent of instructor.

117.title: Interactive Media I
117.description: Practice of creating interactive visual media for network-based applications and principles of human computer interaction. Responsive design. User-centered research, information architecture, interface and interaction. Analysis of usability. Development and presentation of design production materials and completed interactive projects.
117.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

127A.title: Sustainable Design
127A.description: Principles, practice and materials of contemporary sustainable design in the context of environmental crisis. History of sustainable design in relation to the fields of product design, material science, energy, architecture, and transportation.

135A.title: Furniture Design & Detailing
135A.description: Development of designs for contemporary furniture. Consideration of behavioral and physical requirements, cultural and historic expression, and structural and aesthetic qualities. Process includes research, drawings, and construction of scale models. Required field trip.
135A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

148.title: Trend Research & Forecasting in Design
148.description: Short term and long term trends, micro and macro trends. Theories of adoption and diffusion of trends. Economic, political, technological and psychological indicators in trend forecasting. Future trends in design using cultural brailing, cross-cultural analysis methods and ethnographic research.

150.title: Computer-Assisted Presentations for Interior Architecture
150.description: Computer-assisted architectural presentation including the development of complex 3D models, techniques of photo-realistic rendering and computer simulation of movement through architectural and interior space.

151.title: Type in Motion
151.description: Fundamentals of creating motion-based, screen-based typography.  Consideration of narrative structures, movement assemblage, and other visual languages, synthesized within a nuanced understanding of typography within digital space.
151.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor. DES 115 recommended.

157A.title: Interactive Media II
157A.description: Technical practice for interactive media using the front-end stack (html, css, js). Conceptual framework, user experience, visual interface and interaction design. Research and written pre-production materials required.
157A.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; DES 117; or consent of instructor; DES 111 recommended.

161.title: Textile Surface Design: Screen & Digital Printing
161.description: Design of textiles and screen printing on fabrics; soft-product development; integration of hand-produced and digitally generated imagery on cloth.

165.title: Studio Practices in Industrial Design
165.description: 3D studio methods for design, including: historic and contemporary developments in industrial design; innovation in material and fabrication technology; design based projects for everyday objects including soft goods, electronics, transportation.
165.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; (DES 050 or DES 050), or consent of instructor.

166.title: Human Centered Design
166.description: Human-centered approach to problem solving, ethnography, ideation, project framing, rapid prototypes, visual communication, and experiential learning. Creative approaches to graphic design, industrial design, fashion, business, and entrepreneurship.

171.title: Fashion Drawing: Technical & Illustration
171.description: Exploration of fashion design processes for industry within the social and physical context. Emphasis on two-dimensional conceptualization of ideas, garment construction, and ideation processes utilizing commercial textiles. Field trip required.
171.prereq_text: DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor; DES 014 recommended.

179.title: Fashion Design: Signature Collection
179.description: Advanced exploration of fashion design with an emphasis on professional portfolio development and presentation. Emphasis on conceptualizing, designing, and fabricating a cohesive line of wearable garments suitable for presenting in a public fashion show.
179.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken more than 8 units of DES 191A.
179.prereq_text: DES 077; (DES 107 or DES 177); DES 001; (DES 014 or DES 021); DES 015; DES 016; or consent of instructor.

180B.title: Advanced Interior Architecture
180B.description: Advanced problems in interior architectural design emphasizing space planning for corporate and institutional environments. Field trips required.
180B.prereq_text: (DES 180A or DES 134B); DES 134A; or consent of instructor.

191D.title: Workshops in Design
191D.description: Faculty initiated workshops featuring advanced studies and applications of original work in Design: Textiles. Letter grading by contract. Field trips included.
191D.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 12 units in one section or a combination of sections.
191D.prereq_text: DES 014; DES 015; and consent of instructor; upper division standing.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in areas of design including graphics, fashion, information, museum, interaction, interiors, lighting, product and textiles.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Design
197T.description: Leading of small discussion groups or studio meetings affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study of Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study of advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

226.title: Studio Practice & Critique
226.description: Development of design mastery through individual design process and projects. Risk taking and development of the ability to add form to ideas both speculative and practical. Various design methodologies and creative making. Presentation of works in progress. Communication of effective feedback.
226.prereq_text: Graduate status in the Department of Design or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar in Design
290.description: Selected topics in design methodology, research, communication, and education.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

292.title: Practicum in Design
292.description: Interaction with a working professional in the student's field of interest to apply theories and concepts to working practice.
292.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Design or consent of instructor.

298.title: Directed Group Study for Graduate Students
298.description: Directed group study for graduate students.

299.title: Individual Focused Study
299.description: Advanced study in studio practice on independent projects with faculty consultation.
299.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Design or consent of instructor.

299D.title: Comprehensive Project
299D.description: Create a body of original work at a professional level, with written and visual documentation of process and concepts underlying the project, culminating in public presentation.
299D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing in Design or consent of instructor; minimum of 22 units must be taken in Project Concentration and Individual Focused Study.

263.title: Biotechnology Fundamentals & Application
263.description: Fundamentals of molecular biology and chemical engineering involved in recombinant DNA technology. Topics: principles of rate processes of biological systems, optimization of bioreactors, and issues related to overexpression and production of recombinant molecules. Participation in student-directed team projects.
263.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V); MIC 102; or consent of instructor; must be a graduate student in good standing.

282.title: Biotechnology Internship
282.description: Research at a biotechnology company or interdisciplinary cross-college lab for a minimum of three months as part of the Designated Emphasis in Biotechnology Program.
282.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

294.title: Current Progress in Biotechnology
294.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subjects of their own research activities.

001.title: Theatre, Performance & Culture
001.description: Introductory investigation of the nature of performance, moving from performance theory to consideration of various manifestations of performance including theatre, film and media, performance art, dance, sports, rituals, political and religious events, and other "occasions."

010.title: Introduction to Performance & Digital Media
010.description: An embodied exploration of the fundamentals of movement, speech, theatre, sound and the foundations of digital media. Collaborative and solo performance (spoken and movement) assignments, selected readings and viewing of live and digital performance productions.

014.title: Introduction to Contemporary Dance
014.description: Introduction to basic issues and methods in contemporary dance. Focus on preparing the student for dancing and dance-making through basic techniques of improvisation and composition. Consideration of dance as a cultural practice.

040A.title: Beginning Modern Dance
040A.description: Fundamentals of modern dance focusing primarily on the development of techniques and creative problem solving. Basic anatomy, dance terminology, and a general overview of modern dance history.

040B.title: Intermediate Modern Dance
040B.description: Modern dance techniques. Basic anatomy, dance terminology and a general overview of modern dance history.

042A.title: Beginning Ballet
042A.description: Fundamentals of ballet, focusing on the development of technique through proper alignment, quality, and rhythm. Basic anatomy, ballet terminology, and dance history.

042B.title: Intermediate Ballet
042B.description:
Barre and center work at the intermediate level. Development and
refinement of technique through proper alignment, rhythmic, and qualitative understanding. Anatomy, ballet terminology, and dance history.

056C.title: History of Theatre & Dance III: Sex, Society & the State
056C.description: Exploration of aesthetic movements in various disciplines of theatre and dance from 1850-1968. Examination of melodrama, popular theatre, naturalism, psychological realism, and the avant-garde using European, North and South American, Asian, and African examples. Offered once a year.

092.title: Internship in Dramatic Art
092.description: Internship outside the Department of Theatre & Dance enabling students to practice their skills.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chairperson.

111.title: Presentation, Communication & Collaboration
111.description: Use of theater techniques for development of clear oral and physical communication skills that build confidence, presentational style and clarity for students whose command of English is at a competent to fluent level.

120.title: Intermediate Acting/Gateway: The Actor's Toolkit
120.description: Implementation of acting tools drawn predominantly from Stanislavsky’s ‘system’. Gateway into the Advanced Acting courses.

124B.title: Principles of Theatrical Design: Scenery
124B.description: Analysis of plays in terms of scene design, elements of design, execution of designs for modern and period plays.

124D.title: Principles of Theatrical Design: Costume
124D.description: Source materials for theatrical costuming, selecting fabrics, elements of design, analysis of plays in terms of costume design, execution of designs for modern and period plays.
124D.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

126A.title: Topics in Entertainment Engineering
126A.description: Engineering topics faced by technical designers in live entertainment. Project-based exploration of: theatrical rigging, scenic automation, the role of the technical director, and structural design for the stage.
126A.prereq_text: DRA 028 C- or better; consent of instructor.

127B.title: Principles of Directing
127B.description: Director's creative approach to the actor.

150.title: American Theatre & Drama
150.description: The history of the theatre from Colonial times to the present. Readings of selected plays.

156B.title: Theatre in History & Place: Local, National & Global Conditions for Production
156B.description: Exploration of local, national and global issues in theatre production, with special attention to historical changes in social and political contexts for performance.

159.title: Contemporary Experimental Performance, Theatre & Drama
159.description: Evaluation and examination of the "New Theatre;" its experimental and innovative nature since the 1960s. Dance, film, stage, performance art and public acts of a performative nature.

180.title: Theatre Laboratory
180.description: Projects in acting, production, scene design, costuming, lighting, directing, and playwriting. Participation in departmental productions.

180A.title: Theatre Laboratory: Performance
180A.description: Rehearsal and performance of a production directed or choreographed by visiting Granada Artists-in-Residence and/or faculty, and/or the UG Edge Festival.

180B.title: Theatre Laboratory: Design
180B.description: Design-related participation in Theatre & Dance productions involves research, creation and implementation of design concept in collaboration with the director and other members of the production team.

180C.title: Theatre Laboratory: Management, Directing, other Production Team
180C.description: Participation in Theatre & Dance production in management, direction, choreography, dramaturgy, writing or other production related role; research, creation and implementation of production concept in collaboration with members of the production team and cast.

180D.title: Theatre Laboratory: Crew
180D.description: Participation in Theatre & Dance productions as backstage running crew which will involve skill development, rehearsal and execution of performance.

180E.title: Theatre Laboratory: Scenic
180E.description: Practical experience working on scenery and properties for Theatre & Dance department productions. Study and execution of basic scenery and prop engineering, construction, painting, rigging. Study of techniques, materials, tools, and equipment use. Skill development, professional etiquette. Safety training requirement.

180F.title: Theatre Laboratory: Costume
180F.description: Practical experience working on costumes for Theatre & Dance department productions. Study and execution of basic costume construction techniques and materials, tools, and equipment use. Skills development, professional etiquette. Safety training requirement.

180G.title: Theatre Laboratory: Lighting/Sound/Projection
180G.description: Practical experience working on lighting, sound or projections for Theatre & Dance department productions. Study and execution of basic techniques, materials, tools, and equipment use. Skill development, professional etiquette. Safety training requirement.

185A.title: Special Topics: Artist in Residence-Seminar
185A.description: Exploration of contemporary topics in Theatre and Dance. Individual and collaborative project-based learning. Topics vary by instructor.

192.title: Internships in Theatre & Dance
192.description: Theatre production experience in creative, technical or management areas.  Experience in galleries, performance sites, or theatre/dance/physical theatre companies.
192.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have completed DRA 192S.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of Theatre & Dance.
194HA.prereq_text: Qualification for Letters & Science Honors Program and admission to Theatre & Dance Senior Honors Program.

194HB.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HB.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of Theatre & Dance.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; qualification for Letters & Science Honors Program and admission to Theatre & Dance Senior Honors Program.

195.title: Senior Capstone Experience
195.description: Capstone experience for majors. Examination, reflection and synthesis on development. Discussion of professional development and translatable skills. Individual project and development of portfolio.

197T.title: Tutoring in Dramatic Art
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division or graduate standing with major in Theatre & Dance; consent of department chairperson.

001.title: The Earth
001.description: Introduction to the study of the Earth. Earth's internal structure; tectonic processes; geological hazards and resources; human relationship to the environment.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 050 or EPS 050; only 2 credits for students who have taken GEL 002 or EPS 002.

003.title: History of Life
003.description: History of life during the three and one-half billion years from its origin to the present day. Origin of life and processes of evolution; how to visualize and understand living organisms from their fossil remains. How to constrain the story of life using testable hypotheses.

012.title: Dinosaurs - Evolution & Ecology
012.description: Introduction to evolutionary biology, paleobiology, ecology and paleoecology, using dinosaurs as case studies.

016V.title: The Oceans
016V.description: Introductory survey of the marine environment. Oceanic physical phenomena, chemical constituents and chemistry of water, geological history, the seas biota and human utilization of marine resources.
016V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 016 or GEL 016V  or GEL 116 or GEL 116N or EPS 116 or ESP 116N.

017.title: Earthquakes & Other Earth Hazards
017.description: Impact of earthquakes, volcanoes,  tsunamis and other Hazards on humans, structures, and the environment. Discussion of the causes and effects of disasters and catastrophes, and on prediction, preparation, and mitigation of natural hazards.
017.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 017 or GEL 017V.

028.title: Astrobiology
028.description: Origin, evolution, and distribution of life in our solar system and the Universe. Detecting habitable worlds, the Drake equations, the necessities and raw materials for life, philosophical implications of the search for life elsewhere.
028.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 028

050.title: Physical Geology
050.description: The Earth, its materials, its internal and external processes, its development through time by sea-floor spreading and global plate tectonics.
050.credit_limit_text: Only 2 credits for students who have taken GEL 001 or EPS 001 or the equivlalent; not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 050.

050L.title: Physical Geology Laboratory
050L.description: Introduction to classification and recognition of minerals and rocks and to interpretation of topographic and geologic maps and aerial photographs.
050L.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 050L
050L.prereq_text: GEL 050 (can be concurrent) or EPS 050 (can be concurrent).

105.title: Igneous Rocks & Magmatic Processes
105.description: Origin of igneous rocks and evolution of magmas. Laboratory exercises emphasize the study of these rocks in hand specimen and thin section and their geochemical characteristics.

107.title: Paleobiology
107.description: The fossilization process and the application of fossils to biological research.
107.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 107
107.prereq_text: GGEL 003 or EPS 003 or GEL 053 or EPS 142 or BIS 002A or BIS 002B or BIO 001.

107L.title: Paleobiology Laboratory
107L.description: Exercises in determining the ecological functions and evolution of individuals, populations, and communities of fossil organisms in field and laboratory.
107L.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 107L
107L.prereq_text: GEL 107 (can be concurrent) or EPS 107 (can be concurrent).

116.title: Oceanography
116.description: Advanced oceanographic topics: Chemical, physical, geological, and biological processes; research methods and data analysis; marine resources, anthropogenic impacts, and climate change; integrated earth/ocean/atmosphere systems; one-day weekend field trip.
116.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 116 or GEL 116N or ESP 116 or ESP 116N
116.prereq_text: GEL 001 or EPS 001 or GEL 002 or GEL 016 or EPS 016 or GEL 016V or EPS 016V or GEL 050 or EPS 050.

141.title: Evolutionary History of Vertebrates
141.description: Evolutionary history of vertebrates based on the fossil record, in a phylogenetic and chronological framework. Ecology, developmental biology, biogeography, and climate change, timing of major evolutionary events, historical setting of the appearance of major vertebrate groups, physical constraints in vertebrate evolution, effects of continental movement on vertebrate evolution.
141.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 141
141.prereq_text: GEL 003 or EPS 003 or GEL 053 or EPS 142 or BIS 002A or BIO 001.

142.title: Geobiology & Geomicrobiology
142.description: Introduction to interactions between Earth and life with an emphasis on how microbial metabolisms, cellular processes, evolution and ecology emerged within natural environments and have changed Earth’s surface.
142.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 053
142.prereq_text: (GEL 001 or EPS 001 or GEL 002 or EPS 002 or GEL 050 or EPS 050); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH or CHE 004B).

150B.title: Geological Oceanography
150B.description: Introduction to the origin and geologic evolution of ocean basins. Composition and structure of oceanic crust, marine volcanism, and deposition of marine sediments. Interpretation of geologic history of the ocean floor in terms of sea-floor spreading theory.
150B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 150B or ESP 150B
150B.prereq_text: GEL 050 or EPS 050 or GEL 116N or ESP 116N or EPS 116.

163.title: Planetary Geology & Geophysics
163.description: Principles of planetary science. Planetary dynamics, including orbital mechanics, tidal interactions and ring dynamics. Theory of planetary interiors, gravitational fields, rotational dynamics. Physics of planetary atmospheres. Geological processes, landforms and their modification. Methods of analysis from Earth-based observations and spacecraft.
163.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 163
163.prereq_text: (GEL 001 or EPS 001 or GEL 002 or GEL 028 or EPS 028 or GEL 036 or EPS 036 or GEL 050 or EPS 050 or AST 010G or AST 010L or AST 010S or AST 025); (MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); (PHY 007A or PHY 009A or PHY 009HA); (PHY 007B or PHY 009B or PHY 009HB); (PHY 007C or PHY 009C or PHY 009HC).

165.title: AI & Machine Learning for Earth & Environmental Sciences
165.description: Theory and application of machine learning and artificial intelligence to problems in Earth and Environmental Sciences. Model fitting and regression. Feature extraction and classification from remote sensing observations. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Applications to datasets including earthquakes, streamflow, water quality, geochemistry, and petrology.
165.prereq_text: ECS 032A or PHY 040; or equivalent python programming course; or consent of instructor.

186.title: Facilitating Learning in STEM Classrooms
186.description: STEM Learning Assistant Seminar. Theoretical and practical issues of effective teaching in discussion/labs: student-centered, active, cooperative learning environments, responsive teaching, and differentiated classroom instruction.
186.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GEL 186

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Group study focused on topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences.

200BN.title: Principles & Applications of Ecology
200BN.description: Provides a broad background in the principles and applications of ecology, and serves as a foundation for advanced ecology courses. Topics include ecophysiology, behavioral ecology, population ecology, genetics and evolution. Emphasis on historical developments, current understanding, and real world applications.
200BN.prereq_text: STA 102; MAT 016A; MAT 016B; or consent of instructor; first course in Ecology (e.g., ESP 100).

231.title: Mathematical Methods in Population Biology
231.description: Mathematical methods used in population biology. Linear and nonlinear difference equation and differential equation models are studied, using stability analysis and qualitative methods. Partial differential equation models are introduced. Applications to population biology models are stressed.
231.prereq_text: MAT 016C or MAT 021C; or the equivalent.

243.title: Ecological Genomics
243.description: Genomics concepts, technologies, and analyses for ecology research. Mixture of lecture, discussion of recent literature, hands-on training in data analysis and experimental design, and research proposal preparation and evaluation. One all-day field trip is required.
243.prereq_text: ECL 242; or equivalent training in ecology and genetics according to the discretion of the instructors.

290.title: Seminar in Ecology
290.description: Topics in ecology. Students are expected to present an oral seminar on a particular aspect of the general topic under consideration.

296.title: Topics in Ecology & Evolution
296.description: Seminars presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis faculty, and graduate students.

297T.title: Tutoring in Ecology
297T.description: Teaching ecology including conducting discussion groups for regular departmental courses under direct guidance of staff.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing in ecology.

001A.title: Principles of Microeconomics
001A.description: ECN 001A & ECN 001B may be taken in either order. Analysis of the allocation of resources and the distribution of income through a price system; competition and monopoly; the role of public policy; comparative economic systems.

001AV.title: Principles of Microeconomics
001AV.description: Analysis of the allocation of resources and the distribution of income through a price system; competition and monopoly; the role of public policy; comparative economic systems.
001AV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ECN 001A.

001B.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
001B.description: ECN 001A & ECN 001B may be taken in either order. Analysis of the economy as a whole; determinants of the level of income, employment and prices; money and banking, economic fluctuations, international trade, economic development; the role of public policy.

092.title: Internship & Field Work
092.description: Intensive study of practical application of concepts in economics, stressing research methods and empirical analysis.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

100A.title: Intermediate Micro Theory: Consumer & Producer Theory
100A.description: Consumer and producer theory. Equilibrium and welfare analysis. Topics include competitive markets, consumer and producer surplus at an intermediate level.
100A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students that have taken ARE 100A
100A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better)).

100B.title: Intermediate Micro Theory: Imperfect Competition & Market Failure
100B.description: Imperfect competition and market failure. Topics include exchange, monopoly, game theory, uncertainty, asymmetric information, and public goods.
100B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students that have taken ARE 100B.

101.title: Intermediate Macro Theory
101.description: Theory of income, employment and prices under static and dynamic conditions, and long term growth.
101.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (ECN 001B C- or better or ECN 001BV C- or better); ((MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better)).

102.title: Analysis of Economic Data
102.description: Analysis of economic data to investigate key relationships emphasized in introductory micro and macro economics. Obtaining, transforming, displaying data; statistical analysis of economic data; basic univariate and multivariate regression analysis.
102.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032); ((MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C) or (MAT 017A, MAT 017B) or (MAT 019A, MAT 019B, MAT 019C) or (MAT 021A or MAT 021B)); or consent of instructor.

111B.title: Economics History
111B.description: Survey of economic change in the United States from 1865 to the post World War II era.
111B.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); or consent of instructor.

115A.title: Economic Development
115A.description:
Major issues encountered in emerging from international poverty, including problems of growth and structural change, human welfare,
population growth and health, labor markets and internal migration. Important issues of policy concerning international trade and industrialization.
115A.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

117.title: Economics of International Immigration
117.description: Introduction to research on the economics of immigration. Immigrant demographics and reasons for migrating. Immigrant success and effects on native populations. Influence of immigrants on those left behind. Discussion of migration policy in the US and other countries.
117.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in international immigration.
117.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV).

122.title: Theory of Games & Strategic Behavior
122.description: Introduction to game theory. Explanation of the behavior of rational individuals with interacting and often conflicting interests. Non-cooperative and cooperative theory. Applications to economics, political science and other fields.
122.prereq_text: (MAT 016A C- or better, MAT 016B C- or better, MAT 016C C- or better) or (MAT 017A C- or better, MAT 017B C- or better) or (MAT 019A C- or better, MAT 019B C- or better, MAT 019C C- or better) or (MAT 021A C- or better, MAT 021B C- or better); or consent of instructor.

134.title: Financial Economics
134.description: General background and rationale of corporation; finance as resource allocation over time; decision making under uncertainty and the role of information; capital market and interest rate structure; financial decisions.
134.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ARE 171.
134.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100AY or ARE 100A); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y); (ECN 100B or ARE 100B).

135.title: Money, Banks, & Financial Institutions
135.description: Banks and the banking system. Uncertainty and asymmetric information in the lending process; efficiency of competitive equilibrium in lending markets. Regulation and the conduct of monetary policy.
135.prereq_text: (ECN 101 or ECN 101Y or ECN 101V); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032).

138.title: Public Economics in International Perspective
138.description: Social problems and government responses in developed and developing countries; health, unemployment, informal insurance, poverty, corruption, and public service delivery; emphasis on quantitative and data analysis skills; applications to real world policy problems.
138.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in international public economics.
138.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100 or ARE 100A); ECN 102.

140.title: Econometrics
140.description: Problems of observation, estimation and hypotheses testing in economics through the study of the theory and application of linear regression models. Critical evaluation of selected examples of empirical research and exercises in applied economics.
140.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ECN 100AY or ARE 100A); (ECN 102 or STA 108); or consent of instructor.

142.title: Economics & Business Data Analytics
142.description: Introduction to economics and business data analytics. Statistical learning methods to analyze big data in economics and business data analysis. Statistical learning, linear regression, classification, resampling methods, and linear model selection and regularization.
142.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have previously completed an upper division economics course in economics and business data analytics.
142.prereq_text: (ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or ARE 100A); (ECN 102 B or better or ECN 140 B or better); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y).

160A.title: International Microeconomics
160A.description: International trade theory: impact of trade on the domestic and world economies; public policy toward external trade.
160A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed ECN 162.

160B.title: International Macroeconomics
160B.description: Macroeconomic theory of an open economy. Balance of payments adjustment mechanism, international monetary economics issues; international financial institutions and their policies.
160B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed ECN 162.

171.title: Economy of East Asia
171.description: Intensive reading, discussion and research on selected topics from the economies of the countries of East Asia. Consult department for course scheduling.
171.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (ECN 001B or ECN 001BV); or consent of instructor.

190.title: Topics in Economics
190.description: Selected topics in economic analysis and public policy. Variable content.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

200C.title: Microeconomic Theory
200C.description: Uncertainty and information economics. Individual decision making under uncertainty. Introduction to game theory, with emphasis on applications to markets with firms that are imperfect competitors or consumers that are imperfectly informed.

200E.title: Macroeconomic Theory
200E.description: Macrodynamic theory of income, employment, and prices.

215B.title: Open Macroeconomics of Development
215B.description: Models and policy approaches regarding trade, monetary and fiscal issues, capital flows and debt are discussed in the macroeconomic framework of an open developing country. Basic analytical focus is real exchange rate and its impact on sectoral allocation of resources.
215B.prereq_text: (ARE 200A or ECN 200A); (ARE 204 or ECN 204); (ECN 214 or ECN 215A); ECN 200D or ECN 205.

221B.title: Empirical Analysis in Industrial Organization
221B.description: Recent empirical work in industrial organization.  Topics include empirical analysis of cartels, product differentiation, innovation and technological change, and imperfect competition in international markets.

230B.title: Public Economics
230B.description: Effects of government policies on economic behavior; labor supply, program participation, investment, consumption and savings.

240A.title: Econometric Methods
240A.description: Least squares, instrumental variables, and maximum likelihood estimation and inference for single equation linear regression model; linear restrictions; heteroskedasticity; autocorrelation; lagged dependent variables.

240C.title: Time Series Econometrics
240C.description: Probability theory; estimation, inference and forecasting of time series models; trends and non-standard asymptotic theory; vector time series methods and cointegration; time series models for higher order moments and transition data; state-space modeling and the Kalman filter.

240F.title: Topics in Cross Section Econometrics
240F.description: Modern econometrics techniques for cross-section data. Expand on topics covered in ECN 240A, ECN 240B, ECN 240D. Content may differ year to year.

250A.title: Labor Economics
250A.description: Philosophy, theory and history of American and foreign labor movements; union structure, organization and collective bargaining under changing labor market conditions; current labor market issues.

260B.title: International Economics
260B.description: Balance of payments adjustment mechanisms; foreign exchange markets theories of balance of payments policy and international monetary mechanisms.

260E.title: Topics in International Trade
260E.description: Current literature in international trade theory.

001.title: Cracking the Education Code
