001.description: Forces shaping the U.S. educational system and how education intersects with various dimensions of people’s lives. How education influences and is impacted by: law and politics, capital and financial resources, social opportunities, and technological advancements.

050.title: Education, Leadership, & Community Non-Profits
050.description: Educational non-profit and community-based organizations and their role in addressing the opportunity gap and school discipline. Skills required to navigate diverse community and organizational structures.

081.title: Learning in Science & Mathematics
081.description: Exploration of how students learn and develop understanding in science and mathematics classrooms. Introduction to case studies and interview techniques and their use in K-6 classrooms to illuminate factors that affect student learning.

100.title: Introduction to Schools
100.description: Study of both traditional classroom and out of school/classroom settings; skills for observing educational activities; school and educational organization and finance; school reform movement; observing, aiding, and tutoring in schools and out of school spaces.

110.title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
110.description: Learning processes in diverse environments across the lifespan, cognitive development, individual differences, and designing equitable learning environments.

115.title: Educating All Learners: Inclusion & Disability
115.description: Theories, topics, and frameworks related to disability, neurodiversity and inclusive education. Complex learning needs of neurodiverse students within mainstream, general education classrooms.

119.title: Use & Misuse of Standardized Tests
119.description: Principles underlying educational and psychological testing. Purposes of testing for individual achievement and evaluation of school programs. Interpretation and misinterpretations of outcomes. Analysis of SAT, GRE and other common tests. Experience in test administration and outcome interpretation.

120.title: Philosophical & Social Foundations of Education
120.description: Philosophical and sociological foundations of education and schools in contemporary societies.

122.title: Children, Learning & Material Culture
122.description: How material artifacts shape what and how children learn in school, at home, and in the community. Artifacts examined include books, computers, household appliances, toys and games, entertainment media, collectibles, sports equipment, clothing, folk arts and crafts, and neighborhood space.

130.title: Issues in Higher Education
130.description: Analysis of current issues in higher education and of some practical implications of varying philosophical approaches to the role of the university.

150.title: Cultural Diversity & Education in a Sociopolitical Context
150.description: Critical examination of cultural diversity in U.S. schools in light of long-standing inequalities in education and the identity-affirming pedagogies intended to address them.

155.title: Ethnic Studies in K-12 Schools
155.description: Brief historical genealogy of Ethnic Studies as an interdisciplinary field, content and pedagogical knowledge of Ethnic Studies approaches in K-12 school settings and grassroots communities, and reviews the existing research of Ethnic Studies literacies in US public schools.

181.title: Teaching in Science & Mathematics
181.description: Exploration of effective teaching practices based on examination of how middle school students learn math and science. Selected readings, discussion and field experience in middle school classrooms.
181.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus.

183.title: Teaching High School Mathematics & Science
183.description: Exploration and creation of effective teaching practices based on examination of how high school students learn mathematics and science. Field experience in high school classrooms.
183.prereq_text: Major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus and consent of the instructor.

201.title: Qualitative Research in Education
201.description: Examines the design and conduct of educational research using non-numerical data (e.g., text, discourse, imagery and artifacts). Focuses on issues (e.g., validity, reliability, generalizability, ethics) and reporting genres (e.g., narrative accounts, case studies, and arguments).
201.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

204A.title: Quantitative Methods in Educational Research:  Analysis of Correlational Designs
204A.description: Methods for analysis of correlational data in educational research. Topics include multiple correlation and regression, discriminant analysis, logistic regression, and canonical correlation. Emphasis on conceptual understanding of the techniques and use of statistical software.
204A.prereq_text: Introductory statistics or consent of instructor.

220.title: Concepts & Methods of Policy Analysis
220.description: Introduction to concepts and methods of policy analysis. Emphasis on the relationship between educational issues and problems; policy development; constructing persuasive policy analyses; issues related to policy process.

237.title: Survey Research Methods
237.description: Theories, principles and application of survey research methodology. Students develop, validate, and administer survey instruments; select representative samples; conduct focus groups; and collect, organize, and analyze survey data. Familiarity with introductory concepts in descriptive and inferential statistics is assumed.

247.title: Research on Response to Culturally Diverse Literature, K-12
247.description: Research on response to culturally diverse literature in classrooms and other K-12 settings. Topics include reader response theories, values in expanding the literary canon, problems of cultural authenticity, resistance to multicultural literature, and instruction for diverse texts and learners.

294.title: Special Topics in Science, Agriculture & Mathematics Education
294.description: Critical study of special topics of research relevant to science, agricultural and mathematics education. Students and faculty present work-in-progress on a major research project, and critically analyze and discuss one another's developing scholarly work.

295.title: Special Topics in Learning & Mind Science
295.description: Critical study of selected issues in the learning sciences, neurodevelopmental disorders, and psychometrics and measurement, as they relate to education.

297B.title: Preparing for the Preliminary Writing Exam Paper, Part II

192.title: Internship in Education Abroad
192.description: Internship with Education Abroad program, potentially either at university or taught abroad.
192.prereq_text: Participation in a study abroad program.

007.title: Introduction to Programming & Microcontrollers
007.description: Programming computers using C/C++ languages. Software engineering and object-oriented design. Programming for hardware devices.
007.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECS 036A or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV..

018.title: Digital Systems I
018.description: Introduction to digital system design including combinational logic design, sequential and asynchronous circuits, computer arithmetic, memory systems and algorithmic state machine design; computer aided design (CAD) methodologies and tools.
018.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have previously completed EEC 180A.

100.title: Circuits II
100.description: Theory, application, and design of analog circuits. Methods of analysis including frequency response, SPICE simulation, and Laplace transform. Operational amplifiers and design of active filters.
100.credit_limit_text: Students who have completed ENG 100 may receive 3.5 units of credit.
100.prereq_text: (ENG 017 C- or better or ENG 017V C- or better); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B); EEC 010; or consent of instructor.

110A.title: Electronic Circuits I
110A.description: Use and modeling of nonlinear solid-state electronic devices in basic analog and digital circuits. Introduction to the design of transistor amplifiers and logic gates.
110A.prereq_text: EEC 100; (EEC 140A (can be concurrent) or EEC 140AV (can be concurrent) or EEC 111 (can be concurrent)).

112.title: Communication Electronics
112.description: Electronic circuits for analog and digital communication, including oscillators, mixers, tuned amplifiers, modulators, demodulators, and phase-locked loops. Circuits for amplitude modulation (AM) and frequency modulation (FM) are emphasized.

130B.title: Introductory Electromagnetics II
130B.description: Plane wave propagation in lossy media, reflections, guided waves, simple modulated waves and dispersion, and basic antennas.

134A.title: RF/Microwave Systems Design
134A.description: Board-level RF design, fabrication, and characterization of an RF/microwave system, including the antenna, RF front-end, baseband, mix-signal circuits, and digital signal processing models.

136A.title: Electronic Design Project
136A.description: Optical, electronic and communication-engineering design of an opto-electronic system operating under performance and economic constraints. Measurement techniques will be designed and implemented, and the system will be characterized.
136A.prereq_text: (ECS 036B or EEC 007); EEC 018; EEC 100; (EEC 110B or EEC 180 or EEC 157A (can be concurrent) or EEC 157AV (can be concurrent)).

146A.title: Integrated Circuits Fabrication
146A.description: Theoretical and experimental study of basic fabrication processes for metal oxide semiconductor integrated circuits, including oxidation, photolithography, impurity diffusion, metallization, wet chemical etching, and characterization.

150.title: Introduction to Signals & Systems
150.description: Characterization and analysis of continuous-time linear systems. Fourier series and transforms with applications. Introduction to communication systems. Transfer functions and block diagrams. Elements of feedback systems. Stability of linear systems.

157AV.title: Control Systems
157AV.description: Analysis and design of feedback control systems. Examples drawn from electrical and mechanical systems as well as other engineering fields. Mathematical modeling of systems, stability criteria, root-locus and frequency domain design methods.

161.title: Applied Probability for Electrical & Computer Engineers
161.description: Axioms of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, expectation and moments. Transformation of random variables. Joint and conditional densities. Limit theorems, Markov and Poisson processes. Applications in Electrical and Computer Engineering.

172.title: Embedded Systems
172.description: Introduction to embedded-system hardware and software. Topics include: embedded processor and memory architecture; input/output hardware and software, including interrupts and direct memory access; interfacing with sensors and actuators; wired and wireless embedded networking.

173A.title: Computer Networks
173A.description: Overview of computer networks, TCP/IP protocol suite, computer-networking applications and protocols, transport-layer protocols, network architectures, Internet Protocol (IP), routing, link-layer protocols, local area and wireless networks, medium access control, physical aspects of data transmission, and network-performance analysis.
173A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have taken ECS 157.
173A.prereq_text: (ECS 032B or ECS 036C); (ECS 132 or EEC 161 or MAT 135A or STA 131A or STA 100 or STA 032, STA 035B).

180.title: Digital Systems II
180.description: Computer-aided design of digital systems with emphasis on hardware description languages (VHDL), logic synthesis, and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGA). May cover advanced topics in digital system design such as static timing analysis, pipelining, memory system design, testing digital circuits.
180.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have previously completed EEC 180B.

193A.title: Senior Design Project
193A.description: Team design project for seniors in Electrical or Computer Engineering. Project involves analysis, design, implementation and evaluation of an Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering system. Project is supervised by a faculty member.
193A.prereq_text: EEC 196 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

195A.title: Autonomous Vehicle Design Project
195A.description: Design and construct an autonomous race car. Work in groups to design, build and test speed control circuits, track sensing circuits, and a steering control loop.
195A.prereq_text: (ECS 036A or EEC 007); EEC 018; (EEC 110B or EEC 157A (can be concurrent) or EEC 157AV (can be concurrent) or ECS 036B).

201.title: Digital Signal Processing
201.description: Theory and design of digital filters. Classification of digital filters, linear phase systems, all-pass functions, FIR and IIR filter design methods and optimality measures, numerically robust structures for digital filters.
201.prereq_text: EEC 150B; STA 120 or MAT 131 or MAT 167 recommended.

212.title: Analog MOS IC Design for Signal Processing
212.description: Analysis and design of analog MOS integrated circuits. Passive components, Single-ended and fully differential op amps, Sampled-data and continuous-time filters.

230.title: Electromagnetics
230.description: Maxwell's equations, plane waves, reflection and refraction, complex waves, waveguides, resonant cavities, and basic antennas.

235.title: Photonics
235.description: Optical propagation of electromagnetic waves and beams in photonic components and the design of such devices using numerical techniques.

243.title: Optical Imaging & Microscopy
243.description: Theory and techniques of optical imaging & microscopy. Fourier optics; light propagation & light detection; imaging contrast mechanisms; optical & microscopy techniques.

244.title: Introduction to Neuroengineering
244.description: Survey of neuroengineering field from engineering and biological perspectives; micro-/nano-fabrication technology; optical and electrical techniques to monitor and modulate neural activity; computational tools and control systems; prosthetics and human machine interfaces; human performance and rehabilitation; cognitive neuroengineering; neuroethics; extensive proposal development to merge aforementioned themes into a multidisciplinary project.
244.prereq_text: Graduate standing; or consent of instructor.

264.title: Estimation & Detection of Signals in Noise
264.description: Introduction to parameter estimation and detections of signals in noise. Bayes and Neyman-Pearson likelihood-ratio tests for signal detection. Maximum-likelihood parameter estimation. Detection of known and Gaussian signals in white or colored noise.  Applications to communications, radar, signal processing.

270.title: Computer Architecture
270.description: Introduction to modern techniques for high-performance single and multiple processor systems. Topics include advanced pipeline design, advanced memory hierarchy design, optimizing pipeline and memory use, and memory sharing among multiprocessors. Case studies of recent single and multiple processor systems.

273.title: Networking Architecture & Resource Management
273.description: Design & implementation principles of networking architecture and protocols. Internet, data center, and telephony case studies. Topics: Internet data & control planes; application & services; resource management; Quality of Service (QoS) provisioning; traffic engineering; performance evaluation, software-defined networks, & future research issues.

281.title: VLSI Digital Signal Processing
281.description: Digital signal processors, building blocks, and algorithms. Design and implementation of processor algorithms, architectures, control, functional units, and circuit topologies for increased performance and reduced circuit size and power dissipation.
281.prereq_text: EEC 150B; EEC 170; (EEC 180 or EEC 180B); or consent of instructor.

283.title: Advanced Design Verification of Digital Systems
283.description: Design verification techniques for digital systems; simulation-based design verification techniques; formal verification techniques, including equivalence checking, model checking, and theorem proving; timing analysis and verification; application of design certification techniques to microprocessors.

289A.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: Computer Science

289K.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: High Frequency Phenomena & Devices
289K.description: Special topics in High Frequency Phenomena & Devices.

289O.title: Special Topics in Electrical & Computer Engineering: Integrated Circuits

290.title: Seminar in Electrical & Computer Engineering
290.description: Discussion and presentation of current research and development in Electrical & Computer Engineering.

192.title: Emergency Medicine Clinical Research Internship
192.description: Intended to give the upper division undergraduate student an opportunity to conduct "hands-on" clinical research in the Emergency Department. Through the lecture/discussion, students learn the basics of conducting and developing clinical research studies.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; undergraduate student in good academic standing at UC Davis.

192.title: Internship in Endocrinology
192.description: Supervised work experience in endocrinology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

201.title: Life Cycle Assessment for Sustainable Engineering
201.description: Life cycle assessment methodology. Emphasis on applications to infrastructure and energy systems. Life cycle design, life cycle cost methods, other tools from industrial ecology, and links to policy.
201.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken ECI 244.

298A.title: Group Study
298A.description: Directed reading and discussion on select topics

003Y.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
003Y.description: Introduction to the engineering design process that incorporates the development of oral and written communication skills  integral to the design process. Conducted in workshop format with hands-on engagement in the design process.
003Y.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

004.title: Engineering Graphics in Design
004.description: Engineering design, descriptive geometry, pictorial sketching, computer-aided graphics, and their application in the solution of engineering problems.

006.title: Engineering Problem Solving with Applied AI
006.description: Problem-solving methodology, engineering computing, and visualization, emphasizing the responsible application of generative AI to enhance coding, testing, and algorithmic thinking. Foundational programming skills for data analysis and future-ready engineering workflows.
006.prereq_text: (MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better); (MAT 016B C- or better (can be concurrent) or MAT 017B C- or better (can be concurrent) or MAT 019B C- or better (can be concurrent) or MAT 021B C- or better (can be concurrent)).

008.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
008.description: Students from all majors will learn the processes involved in modern entrepreneurship and identify an opportunity for innovation. The 3 C's of the entrepreneurial mindset (developed by KEEN) will be covered: Curiosity, Connections, and Creating Values.

009.title: Technology Startup Speaker Series
009.description: Presentations from successful entrepreneurs about the challenges of building a technology company, leadership, barriers faced by underrepresented founders, and professional resources to support student entrepreneurship.

017.title: Circuits I
017.description: Basic electric circuit analysis techniques, including electrical quantities and elements, resistive circuits, transient and steady-state responses of RLC circuits, sinusoidal excitation and phasors, and complex frequency and network functions.

035.title: Statics
035.description: Force systems and equilibrium conditions with emphasis on engineering problems.
035.prereq_text: (PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better); MAT 021D C- or better (can be concurrent).

102.title: Dynamics
102.description: Kinematics and kinetics of particles, systems of particles, and of rigid bodies; application of these topics are applied to engineering problems.
102.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have previously taken ENG 036.
102.prereq_text: ENG 035 C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

103.title: Fluid Mechanics
103.description: Fluid properties, fluid statics, continuity and linear momentum equations for control volumes, flow of incompressible fluids in pipes, dimensional analysis and boundary-layer flows.
103.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECH 150A.
103.prereq_text: ENG 035 C- or better; PHY 009B C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

104.title: Mechanics of Materials
104.description: Uniaxial loading and deformation. General concepts of stress-strain-temperature relations and yield criteria. Torsion of shafts. Bending of beams. Deflections due to bending. Introduction to stability and buckling.
104.prereq_text: ENG 035 C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

104L.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
104L.description: Experiments which illustrate the basic principles and verify the analysis procedures used in the mechanics of materials are performed using the basic tools and techniques of experimental stress analysis.

105.title: Thermodynamics
105.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics: heat energy and work, properties of pure substances, First and Second Law for closed and open systems, reversibility, entropy, thermodynamic temperature scales. Applications of thermodynamics to engineering systems.
105.prereq_text: PHY 009B C- or better; (MAT 022B C- or better or MAT 027B C- or better).

106.title: Engineering Economics
106.description: Analysis of problems in engineering economy; the selection of alternatives; replacement decisions. Compounding, tax, origins and cost of capital, economic life, and risk and uncertainty are applied to methods of selecting most economic alternatives.

108.title: Launching a Company
108.description: Technological innovation and product development. Working as a team to turn ideas into companies through customer development.
108.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have previously completed ENG 002 or ENG 080.

190.title: Professional Responsibilities of Engineers
190.description: Organization of the engineering profession; introduction to contracts, specifications, business law, patents, and liability; discussion of professional, ethical, societal, and political issues related to engineering.

003.title: Introduction to Literature
003.description: Introductory study of several genres of English literature, emphasizing both analysis of particular works and the range of forms and styles in English prose and poetry. Frequent writing assignments.
003.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); or concurrent enrollment in ENL 003A.

003A.title: Writers' Workshop
003A.description: Focuses on the development of writing and revision strategies, exploring ways to understand a writing task; to develop appropriate content for a writing task; to revise content to reflect competence as a communicator.
003A.prereq_text: Has not yet completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement and concurrent enrollment in ENL 003 or ENL 003V

003V.title: Introduction to Literature
003V.description: Introductory study of several genres of English literature, emphasizing both analysis of particular works and the range of forms and styles in English prose and poetry. Frequent writing assignments will be made.
003V.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR); or concurrent enrollment in ENL 003A or ENL 003AV.

005F.title: Introduction to Creative Writing: Fiction
005F.description: Elementary principles of writing fiction. Write both in prescribed forms and in experimental forms of their own choosing. No final examination.
005F.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005NF.title: Introduction to Creative Writing: Non-Fiction
005NF.description: Elementary principles of writing creative non-fiction. Work in prescribed literary forms (such as essay, meditation, biography, memoir, book review, documentary, or experimental non-fiction forms) and forms of students' choosing. No final examination.
005NF.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005P.title: Introduction to Creative Writing: Poetry
005P.description: Elementary principles of writing poetry. Write both in prescribed forms and in experimental forms of their own choosing. No final examination.
005P.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

010A.title: Literatures in English I: To 1700
010A.description: Historical introduction to English language and literature from 800-1700. Linguistic borrowing, innovation, and change. Emergence of key literary genres. Colonial America as a new site of English literary production and consumption.
010A.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or equivalent.

040.title: Introductory Topics in Literature
040.description: Study of a special topic. Literature written in English in any period or place or genre.  Thematic, formal, or temporal focus.
040.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or equivalent.

041.title: Introductory Topics in Literature & Media
041.description: Study of a topic centered on the relationships between literature and moving-image media.
041.prereq_text: (ENL 003 or ENL 003V) or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y); or equivalent.

045.title: Introductory Topics in Poetry
045.description: Topical study and close reading of selections from English and American poetry.
045.prereq_text: (ENL 003 or ENL 003V) or (UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y); or equivalent.

053.title: Youth in Revolt
053.description: American literary and cultural representations of adolescence as a time of rebellious refusals and wild behaviors in relation to questions of gender and sexuality, psychological states, economic pressures, racial inequality, and methods of discipline and punishment.

054.title: Literature, Health, &  Medicine
054.description: Literary and cultural representations of health and medicine in relation to issues of race, gender, sexuality, and disability. Narratives and reading practices that provide complex accounts of the social determinants of health, contested understandings of illness, and critical perspectives on biomedicine.

072.title: Introduction to Games
072.description: Introduction to the history, theory, and practice of play.  Survey of both analog and digital games. Overview of gaming cultures, aesthetics, industries, and technologies.

100F.title: Creative Writing: Fiction
100F.description: Writing of fiction. No final examination.
100F.prereq_text: ENL 005F or ENL 005P; ENL 005NF; and consent of instructor.

100FA.title: Creative Writing Advanced Fiction
100FA.description: Development and evaluation of students' work in prose, primarily in the workshop format. Some reading and discussion of published novels and short stories. Conferences with individual students once per quarter.

100P.title: Creative Writing: Poetry
100P.prereq_text: ENL 005F or ENL 005P or ENL 005NF; and consent of instructor.

100PA.title: Creative Writing Advanced Poetry
100PA.description: Development and evaluation of students' work in poetry, primarily in the workshop format. Some reading and discussion of published works of poetry. Conferences with individual students once per quarter.

106.title: English Grammar
106.description: Survey of present-day English grammar as informed by contemporary linguistic theories. The major syntactic structures of English; their variation across dialects, styles, and registers; their development; and their usefulness in describing the conventions of English.
106.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or consent of instructor.

110B.title: Introduction to Modern Literary & Critical Theory
110B.description: History of literary criticism in the modern era, with emphasis on the ties with the past and the special problems presented by modern literary theory.
110B.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

113B.title: Chaucer: The Canterbury Tales
113B.description: Literary analysis of the complete "Canterbury Tales."  Courtly love, literary forms, medieval science and astrology, theology and dogma as they inform the reading of Chaucer's work.
113B.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

117.title: Shakespeare
117.description: Historically, generically, or thematically focused study of Shakespeare's works.
117.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or equivalent.

133.title: 19th-Century British Literature
133.description: Historically or thematically focused study of works of 19th-century English literature.
133.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

140.title: Topics in Postcolonial Literatures & Cultures
140.description: Study of postcolonial literature of Anglophone colonies. Specific emphases may include literature from and about Anglophone India, the Caribbean, the Middle East, South Asia, Africa, and/or South America.
140.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

144.title: Post-Civil War American Literature
144.description: Historically or thematically focused study of works of post-Civil War American literature.
144.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

149.title: Topics in Literature
149.description: Intensive examination of literature considered in topical terms, not necessarily historically.
149.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

157.title: Detective Fiction
157.description: Historically, formally, and thematically focused study of novels and short stories in the detective fiction genre.
157.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

170.title: Narrative Game Design
170.description: Narrative game design. Character, dialogue, environmental storytelling, procedurally-generated text, play as narrative. Workshop, critique, and publish narrative and text-based games.
170.prereq_text: ENL 072 or CDM 072 or ENL 172 or CDM 172 or STS 172; or consent of instructor.

172.title: Video Games & Culture
172.description: Critical approaches to the study of video games, focusing on formal, historical, and cultural modes of analysis. History of software and hardware in North American and global contexts. Relations of games to society, politics, economics, media, etc.
172.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CTS 172 (former course CTS 172).

177.title: Study of an Individual Author
177.description: In-depth study of an author's works; historical context; relation to predecessors and contemporaries; critical reception; influence.

179.title: Topics in Comparative Racial & Ethnic Literary Studies
179.description: Writings by Black, Indigenous, and/or People-of-Color authors responding to specific American contexts of racialization such as slavery, imperial warfare, international and internal migration, naturalization law, religion, mass incarceration, and environmental injustice.
179.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or COM 001 or COM 002 or COM 003 or COM 004 or NAS 005 or NAS 005V; Or standing above freshman level.

182.title: Literature of California
182.description: Focus is on the diverse contributions to the rise of California literature from the 19th century to today. Reading of poetry, fiction, and essays. Includes Native American, Latino/a, and other Californian writers.
182.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

185B.title: Literature by Women from 1800-1900
185B.description: Women's Writing in English from 1800 to 1900; organized by period, place, genre, or theme.
185B.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or COM 001 or COM 002 or COM 003 or COM 004 or NAS 005.

186.title: Literature, Sexuality, & Gender
186.description: Historically or thematically focused intensive examinations of gender and sexuality in British and American literature.
186.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or the equivalent.

187A.title: Topics in Literature & Media
187A.description: Group study of a topic centered on the relationships between literature and film or other moving-image media.
187A.prereq_text: ENL 110A or ENL 110B; and consent of instructor.

188A.title: Topics in Literary & Critical Theory
188A.description: Intensive examination of theories addressing a particular problem, topic, or question.
188A.prereq_text: ENL 110A or ENL 110B; and consent of instructor.

189.title: Seminar in Literary Studies
189.description: Intensive, focused study of literature at an advanced level. May be organized by topic, author, period, movement, or genre. High participation.

192.title: Internship in English
192.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills. A maximum of 4 units is allowed toward the major in English.
192.prereq_text: ENL 003 or ENL 003V or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y.

194H.title: Seminar for Honors Students
194H.description: Preparation for writing an honors thesis in ENL 195H. High level of participation expected.
194H.prereq_text: ENL 110A or ENL 110B; One advanced study course; admission to English Department Senior Honors Program in Literature, Criticism, and Theory.

195H.title: Honors Thesis
195H.description: Preparation of a thesis, under the supervision of an instructor. Students satisfying requirements for the general major or the teaching emphasis write on a scholarly or critical subject; creative writing students submit a volume of poems or fiction.

197TC.title: Community Tutoring in English
197TC.description: Field experience, with individuals or in classroom in instruction of English language, literature, and composition. Does not fulfill requirement for major.
197TC.prereq_text: Upper division standing and a major in English; consent of Chairperson.

230.title: Study of a Major Writer
230.description: Artistic development of one major writer and his intellectual and literary milieu.

237.title: Seminar for Writers
237.description: Varied topics in the study of literature and literary culture craft and poetics from the perspective of the writer/practitioner.

288.title: Prospectus Workshop
288.description: Training in writing the dissertation prospectus. Participation in group discussions of preparatory assignments and final proposal.

290NF.title: Creative Writing: Non-Fiction
290NF.description: Writing of literary non-fiction, with emphasis on autobiography, biography, memoir, the occasional or nature essay, or other non-fiction prose narratives.
290NF.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing; with preference given to those enrolled in the master's program in Creative Writing.

299D.title: Special Study for the Doctoral Dissertation
299D.description: Special study for the doctoral dissertation.

010.title: Natural History of Insects
010.description: Introduction to the insects detailing their great variety, structures and functions, habits, and their significance in relation to plants and animals including man. Designed for students not specializing in entomology.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have had ENT 100, but students who have taken this course may take ENT 100 for credit.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work-learn experience on and off campus in all subject areas offered by the department, supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

102.title: Insect Physiology
102.description: Processes by which insects maintain themselves, reproduce, and adapt to environment. Insects as models for basic/applied research through detailed analysis of metabolic, physiological, and behavioral processes. Emphasis on analysis of methodology, fact, and theory.
102.prereq_text: ENT 100; or course in physiology or invertebrate zoology.

153.title: Medical Entomology
153.description: Basic biology and classification of medically important arthropods with special emphasis on the ecology of arthropodborne diseases and principles of their control. Relationships of arthropods to human health.
153.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)); or consent of instructor; upper division standing in one of the biological sciences.

158.title: Forensic Entomology
158.description: Arthropods, their general biology, succession, developmental cycles and population biology in matters of criminal prosecution and civil litigation. Emphasis on basic arthropod biology, ecological and developmental concepts and methods, development of reasoning abilities, implication, development of opinions and evidence.
158.prereq_text: ENT 100; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

180A.title: Experimental Ecology & Evolution in the Field
180A.description: Experimental design in field ecology. Examination of primary literature, experimental design, independent and collaborative research, analysis of data, development of original research paper based on field experiments.
180A.prereq_text: EVE 100 (can be concurrent); (ENT 105 (can be concurrent) or ESP 100 (can be concurrent) or EVE 101 (can be concurrent)); consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Laboratory experience or fieldwork off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Entomology. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

197T.title: Tutoring in Entomology
197T.description: Leading small discussion groups. Preview assignments and prepare guidelines for discussion.

290.title: Exploratory Topics in Entomology
290.description: Interdisciplinary topics in entomology, including innovative applications of entomological concepts to other fields of research and human endeavor (e.g. medicine, technology, art, criminology).

125.title: Greenhouse & Protected Cultivation Systems
125.description: Principles and techniques for the cultivation of crops in protected environments, including nursery, greenhouse and Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) systems. Technologies, climate control, lighting, irrigation, and substrate management to optimize plant growth and development.

133.title: Woody Plants in the Landscape: Growth, Ecology & Management
133.description: Principles and practices of managing trees and shrubs in the urban landscape and other managed environments. Topics include woody plant form; growth response and adaptation; tree management in relation to soil, moisture, climate; plant problems.
133.prereq_text: PLS 002 (can be concurrent); BIS 002B; or consent of instructor.

200.title: Interdisciplinary Readings in the Environmental Humanities
200.description: Classic and contemporary readings in environmental history, ecocriticism, environmental philosophy and ethics, geography, design, cultural anthropology, cultural studies, ecoarts, and other fields that make up the environmental humanities.

200CN.title: Environmental Governance
200CN.description: Theories of environmental governance and their practical applications in solving modern environmental problems. Application of governance theory to choice of real-world case studies of environmental problems

201.title: Environmental Law
201.description: Roles of legislatures, agencies, and courts in creating and interpreting law; legal strategies for addressing environmental problems; major environmental statutes; and the relationship between federal and state/local legal authority.

203A.title: Environmental Policy Clinic
203A.description: Teams analyze environmental policy problems and natural resources issues from scientific, legal, and economic perspectives. Hands-on learning partnering with a client organization.

297.title: Professional Development Seminar
297.description: Weekly seminar focused on the development of professional skills needed for environmental careers. May feature guest speakers working in environmental or policy careers to discuss pathways and day-to-day job tasks and skills required.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in resource sciences. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

120.title: Global Environmental Interactions
120.description: Relationships among climate, hydrology, biogeochemical cycles, soils and vegetation distribution in diverse landscapes and biomes. Emphasis on physical, chemical, and biological processes affecting ecosystems from the poles to the equator, and human impacts on the environment.
120.prereq_text: One college level chemistry course; one college level biology course.

125.title: River Conservation
125.description: Law, policy, science, and practice used in managing rivers with the aim of balancing human societal needs and those of riparian and aquatic species.
125.prereq_text: ESM 100 or ESM 108 or ESM 120 or ESM 121 or GEL 001 or GEL 050 or HYD 010 or HYD 141 or HYD 143 or SSC 100 or EVE 101 or ESP 100 or ESP 001 or ESP 110 or WFC 010 or WFC 051 or ECI 040 or ECI 100.

131.title: Air as a Resource
131.description: Degradation of the atmospheric resource, historical aspects and effects of air pollution examined. Evaluation of primary gaseous and particulate pollutants and discussion of their impact.

141.title: Role of Fire in Natural Ecosystems
141.description: Fire regimes and roles in major North American vegetation types, especially in the west. Physics of fire, fire effects on organisms and ecosystem functioning, reconstructing fire histories, fire in resource management, and fire use by indigenous people.
141.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or PLS 002); (BIS 002B or BIS 002C); basic biological, ecology/evolution concepts.

186.title: Environmental Remote Sensing
186.description: Overview of satellite, airborne, and ground-based remote sensing, building on properties of electromagnetic radiation. Applications include hydrologic processes, weather and climate, ecology and land use, soils, geology, forestry, and agriculture. Computer based analysis and visualization of images and processing techniques.
186.prereq_text: MAT 016B; (PHY 007C or PHY 009B); upper division standing; LDA 150 recommended.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in resource sciences. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194H.title: Senior Honor Thesis
194H.description: Independent study, guided research on an environmentally related subject of special interest to the student.
194H.prereq_text: Senior standing, overall GPA of 3.50 or higher and consent of master advisor.

010.title: Current Issues in the Environment
010.description: Science behind environmental issues, and policies affecting our ability to solve domestic and international environmental problems. Resources, environmental quality, regulation, environmental perception and conservation. Integrative case studies.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ESP 001.

041.title: Careers in Environmental Science & Policy: Alumni Seminar
041.description: Environmentally focused career paths through presentations and discussions with alumni of the Environmental Science and Management and Environmental Policy Analysis and Planning majors. Each offering will feature a unique set of alumni speakers.

100.title: General Ecology
100.description: Theoretical & experimental analysis of the distribution, growth & regulation of species populations; predator-prey & competitive interactions; and the organization of natural communities. Application of evolutionary & ecological principles to selected environmental problems.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken EVE 101.
100.prereq_text: (BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C); (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); STA 013 recommended.

106.title: Environmental Data Science
106.description: Programming with environmental data using R. Understanding data types, loops, branching and functions. Reproducible workflows and version control to import, organize, explore, analyze and visualize environmental data. Data science terminology and approaches. Common data sources used in environmental science and policy.
106.prereq_text: STA 013 (can be concurrent) or STA 013V (can be concurrent) or STA 013 (can be concurrent) or STA 032 (can be concurrent) or STA 100 (can be concurrent).

110.title: Principles of Environmental Science
110.description: Application of physical and chemical principles, ecological concepts, and systems approach to policy analysis of atmospheric environments, freshwater and marine environments, land use, energy supplies and technology, and other resources.
110.prereq_text: (PHY 001A or PHY 007A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); BIS 002A or BIS 010 recommended; upper division standing.

111.title: Marine Environmental Issues
111.description: Examination of critical environmental issues occurring in coastal waters including the effects of climate change, overfishing, and other human impacts. Through readings and group discussions, students will develop an integrative understanding of the oceanographic and ecological processes.

121.title: Population Ecology
121.description: Development of exponential and logistic growth models for plant and animal populations, analysis of age structure, analysis of competition and predator-prey systems, and analysis of disease dynamics. Developing mathematical models and using them to make predictions and solve problems.
121.prereq_text: BIS 002B; (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 019C or MAT 021B or MAT 021BH).

162.title: Environmental Policy
162.description: Compares economic with socio-cultural approaches to understanding the causes of environmental problems and strategies for addressing them.  Includes different approaches to the policy process, policy instruments, and environmental behavior. Applies these principles to several problems.

167.title: Energy Policy
167.description: Survey of primary energy resources (fossil, renewable, nuclear), energy conversion methods, future energy demand scenarios, and environmental impacts of energy. Overview of energy policy in the U.S. Analysis of policy alternatives for addressing energy-related environmental and national security issues.
167.prereq_text: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); or consent of instructor.

176.title: Community Analysis for Environmental Justice
176.description: Community-engaged research on a local or regional environmental justice issue. Emphasis on skill development for applied projects.
176.prereq_text: ESP 001 or equivalent recommended; or consent of instructor.

178.title: Applied Research Methods
178.description: Research methods for analysis of urban and regional land use, transportation, and environmental problems. Survey research and other data collection techniques; demographic analysis; basic forecasting, air quality, and transportation models. Collection, interpretation, and critical evaluation of data.
178.prereq_text: STA 103 or STA 100 or STA 108 or SOC 106 or ARE 106; or the equivalent.

179.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
179.description: Introduction to the information resources and methods typically used in environmental impact analysis. Emphasis on how environmental information is applied to planning, environmental regulation, and public policymaking, with case studies from California land use and natural resource policy.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

010.title: Introduction to Environmental Toxicology
010.description: Hazardous substances, their effects on humans and their actions and movement in the environment. Emphasis on substances of current concern.

020.title: Introduction to Forensic Science
020.description: Basic principles of forensic science, types of information on which investigations focus, how information is obtained and used in criminal investigations, types of scientific skills required to practice forensic science, guidance on training. Real cases discussed; demonstrations of methods provided.

030.title: Chemical & Drug Use & Abuse
030.description: Overview of chemical use and abuse in our society. Effects of chemicals (therapeutic drugs, pesticides, food additives, herbal remedies, environmental contaminants, and recreational drugs) on humans and other living systems.

040.title: Contaminants in Our Environment
040.description: Contaminants in the environment (air, water, and soil) that influence the health of the environment, wildlife, and humans. An emphasis on contaminant properties, sources, and movement, public policy, and applying quantitative reasoning.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the College of Agricultural & Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

102A.title: Environmental Fate of Toxicants
102A.description: Properties of toxic chemicals influencing their distribution and transformations; action of environmental forces affecting toxicant breakdown, movement, and accumulation; sources and occurrence of major classes of environmental toxicants.
102A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ETX 112A.
102A.prereq_text: CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B; or consent of instructor.

103A.title: Biological Effects of Toxicants
103A.description: Biological effects of toxic substances in living organisms.  Metabolism, cellular and tissue targets, mechanisms of action, and pathological effects.
103A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ETX 114A.
103A.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; NPB 101 & ETX 101 recommended.

111.title: Introduction to Mass Spectrometry
111.description: Introduction to mass spectrometry, including ionization techniques, mass analyzers, interpretation of mass spectra, and applications of mass spectrometry. Emphasis on fundamental concepts of mass spectrometry necessary to identify and quantify organic molecules.

120.title: Perspectives in Aquatic Toxicology
120.description: Toxic substances, their fate in marine and freshwater systems, and their effects on aquatic organisms, populations, and ecosystems. Emphasis on substances and issues of current concern.
120.prereq_text: BIS 002A; CHE 002C; or consent of instructor.

130.title: Role & Applications of Toxicology in Modern Industry
130.description: Role of toxicology in industry research and development, human health and environmental protection, hazard and risk evaluations, risk management and communications, product stewardship, and regulatory compliance. Scientific principles and methods of toxicology in chemical, energy, pharmaceutical, pesticide, biotechnology industries.

190.title: Seminar
190.description: Selected topics presented by students, faculty, or outside speakers covering current research and instructional activities within environmental toxicology. Reports and discussion concerning oral and written presentations, literature sources, and career opportunities.

190C.title: Research Group Conference
190C.description: Weekly conference of advanced research methods and the interpretation of research results.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194HA.title: Honors Research
194HA.description: Specific research project conducted under the supervision of a faculty sponsor. Experience to include experimental design, learning new techniques, data analysis and interpretation of findings.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing; minimum GPA of 3.250.

194HB.title: Honors Research
194HB.description: Specific research project conducted under the supervision of a faculty sponsor. Experience to include experimental design, learning new techniques, data analysis and interpretation of findings.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing; minimum GPA of 3.250.

194HC.title: Honors Research
194HC.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing, minimum GPA of 3.250.

197T.title: Tutoring in Environmental Toxicology
197T.description: Teaching toxicology including conducting discussion groups for regular departmental courses under direct guidance of staff.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advanced standing in Environmental Toxicology, a related major, or the equivalent experience.

278.title: Molecular Techniques
278.description: Recombinant DNA technology and its applications.
278.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Current topics in environmental toxicology.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of advanced research methods and interpretation of research results. Designed primarily for graduate students.

297T.title: Tutoring in Environmental Toxicology
297T.description: Teaching toxicology including conducting discussion groups for regular departmental courses under direct guidance of staff.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing in Environmental Toxicology, a related major, or the equivalent experience.

203.title: Quantitative Epidemiology II: Statistical Inference
203.description: Provides the mathematical statistics foundation for statistical models, methods, and data analysis.
203.prereq_text: STA 108; (EPI 202 or STA 130A or STA 131A); (EPI 205 or MPM 205 or MPM 205V); ((MAT 017A B or better, MAT 017B B or better) or (MAT 021A B or better, MAT 021B B or better)); MAT 017C or MAT 021C or MAT 167 recommended.

206.title: Epidemiologic Study Design
206.description: Builds on concepts presented in EPI 205. Concepts of epidemiologic study design—clinical trials, observational cohort studies, case control studies—introduced in EPI 205A are covered in more depth, using a problem-based format. Discussion of published epidemiologic studies.

210.title: Implementation Research in Health
210.description: Introduction to concepts and methods in implementation science, including theories, models and frameworks, qualitative and mixed methods, adaptations, and common study designs in implementation research.

212.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
212.description: Basic and advanced level of conceptual and methodological foundations in infectious disease epidemiology necessary to develop and evaluate programs for the detection, prevention, and control of infectious diseases in domestic animals, wildlife, and human populations.

280.title: Introduction to SAS Programming
280.description: Introduction to SAS, an integrated software system for data retrieval and management, data manipulation and programming.
280.prereq_text: Introductory statistics course; e.g., MPM 402, STA 102.

290.title: Seminars in Epidemiology
290.description: Faculty and students will present and lead discussion of ongoing or published epidemiologic research.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Group study in selected areas of epidemiology.

299.title: Research
299.description: Research in selected areas of epidemiology.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Evolution & Ecology. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

100.title: Introduction to Evolution
100.description: General survey of the origins of biological diversity and evolutionary mechanisms.
100.prereq_text: (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 019B or MAT 021B); ((BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C) or (BIO 001, BIO 002,  BIO 003)); STA 100 recommended.

101.title: Introduction to Ecology
101.description: General survey of the principles of ecology.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ESP 100.
101.prereq_text: ((BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C) or (BIO 001, BIO 002, BIO 003)); (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 019B or MAT 021B); or the equivalent.

111.title: Marine Environmental Issues
111.description: Examination of critical environmental issues occurring in coastal waters including the effects of climate change, overfishing, and other human impacts. Through readings and group discussions, students will develop an integrative understanding of the oceanographic and ecological processes.

115.title: Marine Ecology
115.description: Processes affecting the distribution, abundance, and diversity of plant and animal life in the sea.  Introduction to marine habitat diversity and human impacts on marine ecosystems.
115.prereq_text: EVE 101 or ESP 100 or BIS 002B or BIO 001; or consent of instructor.

161.title: Microbial Phylogenomics; Genomic Perspectives on the Diversity & Diversification of Microbes
161.description: Use of DNA and genomic sequencing in studies of the diversity of microorganisms. Diversity of microbes, phylogenetics, genome sequencing, comparative genomics, phylogenomics, lateral gene transfer, molecular ecology, metagenomics, and studies of the human microbiome.
161.prereq_text: (BIS 002A, BIS 002B, BIS 002C) or (BIO 001, BIO 002, BIO 003); or equivalent.

180A.title: Experimental Ecology & Evolution in the Field
180A.description: Experimental design in field ecology. Examination of primary literature, experimental design, independent and collaborative research, analysis of data, development of original research paper based on field experiments.
180A.prereq_text: EVE 100 (can be concurrent); (EVE 101 (can be concurrent) or ESP 100 (can be concurrent) or ENT 105 (can be concurrent)); consent of instructor.

189.title: Introduction to Biological Research
189.description:
Introduction to research methods in biology. Presentation and discussion
of research by faculty, graduate, and undergraduate students.
189.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Evolution & Ecology or related biological science.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Evolution & Ecology. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194HA.title: Research Honors
194HA.description: Students pursue intensive research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Students are expected to complete the full three-quarter sequence culminating in the writing of an honors thesis.
194HA.prereq_text: Students who have completed 135 units and qualify for the Honors Program (as defined by the current catalog).

194HB.title: Research Honors
194HB.description: Students pursue intensive research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Students are expected to complete the full three-quarter sequence culminating in the writing of an honors thesis.
194HB.prereq_text: Students who have completed 135 units and qualify for the Honors Program (as defined by the current catalog).

194HC.title: Research Honors
194HC.description: Students pursue intensive research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Students are expected to complete the full three-quarter sequence culminating in the writing of an honors thesis.
194HC.prereq_text: Students who have completed 135 units and qualify for the Honors Program (as defined by the current catalog).

197T.title: Tutoring in Biological Sciences 2B
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in a Biological Sciences 2B laboratory. Tutoring is voluntary and is supervised by a Laboratory Teaching Assistant and the Laboratory Coordinator.
197T.prereq_text: BIS 001B B or better.

225.title: Linear Mixed Modeling in Ecology & Evolution
225.description: Analysis of clustered data requires hierarchical or mixed statistical models. Conceptual basis and practical application of linear (mixed) models. Examples drawn from evolutionary and behavioral ecology. Hands-on manipulation and analysis of data in R.
225.prereq_text: PLS 205 or equivalent coursework or experience with basic linear modelling is strongly recommended.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate student research in biology.

390.title: Methods of Teaching
390.description: Practical experience in the methods and problems of teaching. Includes analyses of texts and supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques and preparing and conducting of laboratory and discussion sections.

090C.title: Research Conference
090C.description: Research findings and methods in exercise biology.  Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
090C.prereq_text: EXB 099 (can be concurrent); Lower division standing in Exercise Biology or related biological science and consent of instructor; EXB 099 required concurrently.

092.title: Exercise Biology Internship
092.description: Work experience in the application of physical activity programs to teaching, recreational, clinical or research situations under department faculty supervision.
092.credit_limit_text: No internship units will be counted towards the Exercise Biology major.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment dependent on availability of intern positions.

097T.title: Tutoring in Exercise Biology
097T.description: Assisting the professor by tutoring students in exercise biology course-related projects.
097T.credit_limit_text: No tutorial units will be counted towards the Exercise Biology major.
097T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

097TC.title: Tutoring Exercise Biology in the Community
097TC.description: Tutoring in the community in exercise biology related projects under the guidance of the faculty.

101.title: Exercise Physiology
101.description: Physiology of Exercise; acute responses and adaptations to training.  Neuromuscular function; bioenergetics; metabolic responses to acute exercise; adaptation to trainings; cardiorespiratory; and, applications to environmental physiology, and human health.
101.prereq_text: NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C; or consent of instructor.

106.title: Human Gross Anatomy
106.description: Detailed study of the gross anatomical structure of the human body, with emphasis on function and clinical relevance to students entering health care professions.
106.prereq_text: BIS 002A; concurrent enrollment in EXB 106L or CHA 101L strongly recommended.

106L.title: Human Gross Anatomy Laboratory
106L.description: Detailed study of prosected human cadavers in small group format with extensive hands-on experience.
106L.prereq_text: BIS 002A; EXB 106 (can be concurrent) or CHA 101 (can be concurrent); must have completed EXB 106 or CHA 101 or required concurrently.

116.title: Nutrition for Physically Active Persons
116.description: The role of nutrition and exercise in modifying metabolism, body composition, performance and health of humans.

190C.title: Research Conference
190C.description: Research findings and methods in exercise biology. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: EXB 099 (can be concurrent); upper division standing in Exercise Biology or related biological science and consent of instructor; EXB 199 required concurrently.

192.title: Exercise Biology Internship
192.description: Work experience in the application of physical activity programs to teaching, recreational, clinical or research situations under program faculty supervision. Written report required.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment dependent on availability of intern positions.

197T.title: Tutoring in Exercise Biology
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in exercise biology course-related projects.
197T.credit_limit_text: No tutorial units will be counted towards the Exercise Biology major.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

197TC.title: Tutoring Exercise Biology in the Community
197TC.description: Tutoring in the community in exercise biology related projects under the guidance of the faculty.

092C.title: Primary Care Clinic
092C.description: Students must apply and interview with the Board of Clinica Tepati or Imani Clinic. Field experience exposes lower division students to health care delivery, patient histories, physical examinations, health promotion, disease prevention, diagnosis; treatment of episodic, acute, chronic illness; appropriate referral and follow-up.
092C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment at the UC Davis campus, for freshman and sophomore students.

192C.title: Primary Care Clinics
192C.description: Students must apply and interview with the Board of Clinica Tepati or Imani Clinic. Field experience introduces students to health care delivery, patient histories and physical examinations, health promotions and disease prevention, diagnosis and treatment of episodic, acute and chronic illness, basic laboratory testing and appropriate referral and follow-up.
192C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment at the UC Davis campus; upper division standing.

195.title: Health Care to Underserved Populations
195.description: Discusses sociocultural perspectives of underserved populations in California impacting their health; roles of family/interpersonal relationships in making health care decisions; and clinician's perspectives in treating people of cultures which are unfamiliar and/or uncomfortable with Western medicine.
195.prereq_text: Sociology, political science, or applied behavioral science background recommended, or registration in medical school.

192.title: Internship in Fiber & Polymer Science
192.description: Work experience off campus in a fiber and polymer science related area. Supervision by a member of the Textiles and Clothing faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Fiber & Polymer Science
197T.description: Tutoring of students in Fiber & Polymer Science courses. Assistance with discussion groups and laboratory sections under supervision of instructor.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division fiber and polymer science related major.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

142.title: New German Cinema
142.description: German filmmakers of the 1960s-1980s such as Fassbinder, Herzog, Syberberg, Brückner, Schlöndorf, Kluge, Wenders.  Knowledge of German is not required.

003V.title: Introduction to Brewing & Beer
003V.description: Basic description of brewing and associated processes, from raw materials to final product; history of brewing and brewing science; types of beer worldwide; world beer markets; basics of beer quality, including wholesomeness; role of scientist in brewing.
003V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken FST 003.

010.title: Food Science, Folklore & Health
010.description: Ancient and modern food folklore in relation to health and well-being. Food safety, organic food, herbalism, food preservation, and nutritional enhancement.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed FST 002.

100B.title: Food Properties
100B.description: Sensory quality, chemical and microbial safety, and nutritional properties of foods. Effects of food processing and preparation on these properties. Selected properties of food commodities.
100B.prereq_text: FST 100A; CHE 008B; and consent of instructor.

100C.title: Food Physical Chemistry
100C.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics and kinetics related to food physical chemistry. Phase behavior, crystallization, water activity and food stability, solubility, aroma volatility, formation of glasses, gels and dispersions, biopolymers and rheology.

101B.title: Food Properties Laboratory
101B.description: Properties of food sensory quality, chemical and nutritional properties of foods. Effects of food processing and preparation on these properties

102B.title: Practical Malting & Brewing
102B.description: Provides practical working knowledge of analytical methods used in malting and brewing and experience with brewing materials and processes, by analysis of samples that illustrate the range of values experienced in practice and pilot scale brewing.

103.title: Physical & Chemical Methods for Food Analysis
103.description: Theory and application of physical and chemical methods for determining the constituents of foods. Modern separation and instrumental analysis techniques are stressed.
103.prereq_text: CHE 002C; CHE 118B; BIS 103; FST 101A; FST 101B; FST 100C (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

104.title: Food Microbiology
104.description: Microorganisms in food safety, spoilage, and production. Food-borne disease agents and their control. Growth parameters of food spoilage agents. Destruction of microbes in food. Food fermentations. The development of microbes as a resource for the food industry.

113.title: Food Law & Regulations
113.description: Food law and regulatory landscape of the food industry. Regulatory aspects of food safety. Major U.S. food laws and regulations including labeling, standards, misbranding, adulteration, food fraud, environmental policies, as well as international law. Laws pertaining to specific food categories including milk, dairy, meat, poultry, eggs, seafood, produce, packaged foods, and alcohol.

127.title: Sensory Evaluation of Foods
127.description: Critical examination of methods of sensory measurement applied to food and beverage systems; descriptive analysis and consumer tests and their application to quality assurance, product development and optimization.

159.title: New Food Product Ideas
159.description: Create, refine, test and present viable ideas for new food products. Activities include trend monitoring, consumer research, idea generation, concept screening, and new product concept presentations.
159.prereq_text: FST 050; BIS 002A; PHY 007A; PHY 007B; PHY 007C; CHE 002A; CHE 002B; CHE 002C.

192.title: Internship for Advanced Undergraduates
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in the practical application of food science.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

203.title: Food Processing
203.description: Principles of food engineering applied to food processing. Relationship of Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluid properties to heat and momentum transfer. Application of mass transfer in controlling kinetics and quality changes of foods.
203.prereq_text: FST 100C; FST 110; PHY 007C; or consent of instructor.

227.title: Food Perception & the Chemical Senses
227.description: Examination of the anatomy and physiology of the chemical senses (taste, smell, and the trigeminal senses) and how they are involved in the perception of food and food intake.
227.prereq_text: FST 107B (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

228.title: Sustainable Food Systems
228.description: Environmental impacts of food systems. Methods for quantifying resource use and managing waste for food production and processing. Influence of policies, technologies, and consumer demand on advancing sustainable food systems.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Critical presentation and evaluation of original research by graduate students. Planning of research programs and proposals. Discussion led by individual major instructors for their research group.

291.title: Advanced Food Science Seminar
291.description: Oral presentation of student's original research, discussion, and critical evaluation.
291.prereq_text: FST 290; completion of at least one quarter of FST 290.

122.title: Food Service Systems Management
122.description: Principles of quantity food production management: production schedules, portion control, financial management, layout and equipment planning, evaluation of alternative systems, and computer applications.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in practical aspects of food service management, supervised by a faculty member.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; one upper division course in Food Service Management (FSM).

197T.title: Tutoring in Food Service Management
197T.description: Tutoring of students in food service management, assistance with discussion groups or laboratory sections; weekly conference with instructor in charge of course; written evaluations.
197T.prereq_text: Dietetics or related major; completion of the Food Service Management (FSM) course in which tutoring is done.

201B.title: Forensic Science Fundamentals-B
201B.description: Forensic biology and DNA, microscopy and materials analysis and pattern evidence as practiced in the forensic sciences. Second in a series of three courses which covers the curriculum requirements of the Forensic Education Program Accreditation Committee (FEPAC).
201B.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrolled in the Forensic Science Graduate Program.

208.title: Forensic Toxicology
208.description: Forensic toxicology as related to driving under the influence of drugs (DUID) investigations, detection, and evaluation through the use of standardized field sobriety tests and drug recognition protocols.

268.title: Statistics in Forensic Science
268.description: Statistics that are used by the forensic scientist, their limitations/applications in presenting evidential results in such areas as DNA-STR results, trace evidence correlation, fingerprint statistics, population sampling and the Bayes method.

276.title: Population Genetics
276.description: Principles, theories, and models of population genetics as they apply to forensic science.
276.prereq_text: FOR 280; FOR 281; or consent of instructor.

278.title: Molecular Techniques
278.description: Recombinant DNA technology and its applications.
278.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar in Forensic Science
290.description: Students will be exposed to topical areas in Forensic Science by presentations conducted by expert guest speakers.  The seminar will also serve as a medium whereby the exiting students will present the research conducted as part of their thesis requirement.

290C.title: Graduate Research Conference in Forensic Science
290C.description: Individual and/or group conference on problems, progress and techniques in forensic science and research.

001Y.title: Elementary French
001Y.description: Introduction to French grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent courses FRE 001 or FRE 001S; students who have completed two or more years of French in high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

021Y.title: Intermediate French
021Y.description: Review of grammar and vocabulary acquired in the elementary sequence, as well as the study of new grammatical structures and a continuing enrichment of vocabulary through oral work in class, written exercises, readings and compositions.
021Y.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have completed FRE 021 or FRE 021S.

022Y.title: Intermediate French
022Y.description: Continuation of FRE 021 or FRE 021S. Review of grammar and vocabulary, as well as the study of new grammatical structures and a continuing enrichment of vocabulary.

023Y.title: Intermediate French
023Y.description: Continuation of  FRE 022 or FRE 022S. Review of grammar and vocabulary, as well as the study of new grammatical structures and a continuing enrichment of vocabulary.

055.title: Fashion & French Society
055.description: French cultural history through fashion. How artists, writers, photographers, and filmmakers depict a world where clothing reflects social transformations, including urbanization, changing political and class structures, evolving gender roles, global and colonial relationships, and concerns about ethics, including environmental and social justice. Fashion Icons and designers whose work shaped France such as Marie Antoinette, Louis XIV, Coco Chanel, Dior, Saint-Laurent.

105.title: Advanced French Grammar
105.description: Understanding of, and extensive practice with, various grammatical structures in French. Lexical-semantic, morphological, and syntactic analysis.

128.title: Topics in French & Francophone Culture
128.description: In-depth study of topics in French and Francophone culture. Topics may include the Court of Louis XIV, the French Revolution, immigration, ​decolonization, rap, fashion, comics, environmental movements.

141.title: Selected Topics in French & Francophone Literature
141.description: Subjects and themes such as autobiography, literature and film, immigration and displacement, postcolonial rewritings/restagings of "canonical" texts, epistolary fictions.

390B.title: The Teaching of French in College
390B.description: Designed for graduate teaching assistants with emphasis on problems and procedures encountered by teachers of lower division classes at the university.
390B.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

001.title: First-Year Seminar
001.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.
