002.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

003.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

004.description: Investigation of a special topic through shared readings, discussions, written assignments, term papers, and special activities (such as fieldwork, site visits, laboratory work, etc.). Emphasis placed upon student participation in learning. Students may take more than one First-Year Seminar, but may not take more than one in any given quarter.

391.title: Scholarship of Teaching & Learning Seminar
391.description: Research articles on the scholarship of teaching and learning. Current trends in undergraduate level pedagogical research methods and results.

392.title: Teaching Practicum in the Sciences
392.description: Teaching practicum in a college-level science course. Planning and facilitation of class sessions in a college-level setting. Assessment of student learning under the guidance of a science faculty mentor. Teaching assignments must be approved by the instructor of record and the students' thesis advisor.

192.title: Internship in Gastroenterology
192.description: Supervised work experience in gastroenterology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

025.title: Gender & Global Cinema
025.description: Application of transnational feminist and queer/trans critique for the study of film and media histories/cultures across geopolitical contexts and in aspects of contemporary globalization. Analyses of films as well as study of film theory from a range of national and transnational contexts.
025.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken WMS 025.

050.title: Introduction to Critical Gender Studies
050.description: Introduction to interdisciplinary, critical gender studies. Emergence of women’s, gender and feminist studies internationally, its links to women’s movements, and its influence within the various arts, humanities, and social science disciplines.

070.title: Sexualities
070.description: Key issues in the social construction, organization, and reproduction of sexualities such as the intersection of sexual identity with gender, race, ethnicity, and class, and the relation between movements for sexual liberation and the regulation of the body.
070.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken former course WMS 070.

103.title: Introduction to Feminist Theory
103.description: Introduction to the emergence of feminist theory and to key concepts in feminist theorizing. Examination of past and current debates over sexuality, race, identity politics, and the social construction of women's experience.

140.title: Gender & Law
140.description: Women's legal rights in historical and contemporary contexts. Legal issues and applicable feminist theories. Constitutional equal protection, discrimination in employment and education, sexual orientation discrimination, and the regulation of abortion.
140.credit_limit_text: No credit if student has taken WMS 140

187.title: Gender & Public Policy
187.description: Role of gender in the creation of social policies, especially with respect to issues brought into the policy arena by contemporary feminism.
187.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken WMS 187.

194HA.title: Senior Honors Project in Gender, Sexuality, & Women's Studies
194HA.description: In consultation with an advisor, students complete a substantial research paper or significant creative project on a GSW topic.
194HA.prereq_text: Senior standing; GSW major; advisor's approval; consent of instructor.

194HB.title: Senior Honors Project in Gender, Sexuality, & Women's Studies
194HB.description: In consultation with an advisor, students complete a substantial research paper or significant creative project on a GSW topic.
194HB.prereq_text: Senior standing; GSW major; advisor's approval; consent of instructor.

200A.title: Current Issues in Feminist Theory
200A.description: Current issues in feminist theory; techniques employed to build feminist theory in various fields.
200A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken former course WMS 200A.

192.title: Internship in General Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in general medicine.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

201B.title: Genomics
201B.description: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic genomes. Experimental strategies and analytical challenges of modern genomics research and the theory and mechanics of data analysis. Structural, functional, and comparative genomics. Related issues in bioinformatics.
201B.prereq_text: GGG 201A; GGG 201C; or equivalents that provide a basic understanding of genetics and molecular biology.

205.title: Molecular Genetics Laboratory
205.description: Students will conduct experiments in molecular genetics laboratories. Individual research problems will emphasize experimental design, experience with methodologies, and data interpretation.
205.prereq_text: BIS 101 (can be concurrent) or BIS 101V (can be concurrent); or the equivalent course; enrolled in Genetics Graduate Group.

297.title: Seminar in Plant Genetics
297.description: Current topics in plant genetics examined in student-conducted seminars and discussion format. Integration of molecular, organismal and population genetics to address questions in plant biology will be emphasized.

298.title: Group Study
298.description: Group study of selected topics in genetics.

300.title: Methods in Teaching Genetics
300.description: Practical experience in the methods and problems of teaching genetics. Includes analysis of texts and supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques, preparing for and conducting discussion or laboratory sections, formulating examinations under supervision of instructor.

200BN.title: Theory & Practice of Geography
200BN.description: Development, application, and philosophical background of theory in discipline of geography and geographical knowledge production. Similarities and differences in theories employed in physical and human geography and cartography. Geographic contributions to interdisciplinary theory bridging biophysical sciences, social sciences, and humanities.

200E.title: Advanced Research Design in Geography
200E.description: Helps Ph.D. students develop their research question, design their research plan and complete a full dissertation research proposal.
200E.prereq_text: GEO 200AN; GEO 200BN; GEO 200CN; GEO 200DN; graduate standing.

201.title: Sources & General Literature of Geography
201.description: Designed for students preparing for higher degrees in geography.
201.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing in geography.

236.title: Transportation Policy
236.description: Application of policy concepts to the transportation context. Overview of the transportation policy landscape. Critical challenges in transportation including sustainability and mobility justice.

298.title: Group Study
298.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

081.title: Learning in Science & Mathematics
081.description: Exploration of how students learn and develop understanding in science and mathematics classrooms. Introduction to case studies and interview techniques and their use in K-6 classrooms to illuminate factors that affect student learning.

181.title: Teaching in Science & Mathematics
181.description: Exploration of effective teaching practices based on examination of how middle school students learn math and science. Selected readings, discussion and field experience in middle school classrooms.
181.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus.

183.title: Teaching High School Mathematics & Science
183.description: Exploration and creation of effective teaching practices based on examination of how high school students learn mathematics and science. Field experience in high school classrooms.
183.prereq_text: Major in mathematics, science, or engineering; or completion of a one-year sequence of science or calculus and consent of the instructor.

217.title: Topics in Geophysics
217.description: Discussion and evaluation of current research in a given area of geophysics. Topic will change from year to year. Offered in alternate years.

290.title: Seminar in Geology
290.description: Presentation and discussion of current topics in geology by visiting lecturers, staff, and students.

390.title: Methods of Teaching & Research
390.description: Introduction to academia at UC Davis. Introduction to graduate-level research, professional development skills, and methods for undergraduate-level teaching. Includes methods in scientific communication (written, oral and poster presentations); literature review and synthesis; professional development; discussions on campus teaching resources, presenting information, managing classroom dynamics, and assessing student’s work.

002Y.title: Elementary German
002Y.description: Continuation of GER 001 in areas of grammar and basic language skills.
002Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken GER 001A.

021.title: Intermediate German
021.description: Review of grammatical principles by means of written exercises; expanding of vocabulary through readings of modern texts; addresses social relations and cultural practices in Germany; discusses history of Germany.

116.title: Readings in Jewish Writing & Thought in German Culture
116.description: Historical tradition of Jewish thought in the German cultural context; unique contributions of Jewish writers to culture of the German-speaking world; what it means to be "other" in the mainstream culture.
116.credit_limit_text: No credit will be given to students who have completed HUM 121.

127.title: Major Writers in German
127.description: Examination of representative works by a major writer, set in the broader cultural context of the relevant period or movement.

142.title: New German Cinema
142.description: Knowledge of German not required.  German filmmakers of the 1960s-1980s such as Fassbinder, Herzog, Syberberg, Brückner, Schlöndorf, Kluge, Wenders.

090.title: Introduction to Global Disease Biology
090.description: Introduction to the Global Disease Biology major, research and internship opportunities, and potential career paths in human, animal, and plant health. Communication, ethics and the nature of science.
090.prereq_text: Open to GDB majors only, or consent of instructor.

101.title: Epidemiology
101.description: Principles and practice of epidemiology as applied to human, animal, and plant populations and the environment in which these populations co-exist. Quantitative analysis of both infectious and non-infectious disease. Inter-dependence between epidemiological analysis, decision-making and policy formulation will be highlighted.
101.prereq_text: SAS 013; (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)), (BIS 002C or BIO 003), ((STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y) or (STA 100 or PLS 120)).

103.title: Microbiome of People, Animals, & Plants
103.description: Examination of the structure and function of microbial communities that live inside and on host organisms. Introduction to general concepts of the microbiome and microbiota, and their relationship to host health and disease.
103.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)), (BIS 002C or BIO 003); or consent of instructor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Preparation of undergraduate students in identified graduate school pipeline programs (e.g. McNair scholars) for graduate education. Emphasis on educating and training undergraduates on key skills and competencies needed for the development of a successful graduate school applicant and future graduate scholar. Topics will vary.

002.title: Elementary Greek
002.description: Continuation of GRK 001.

002NT.title: Elementary New Testament Greek
002NT.description: Supplementary study of New Testament Greek.
002NT.prereq_text: GRK 002 (can be concurrent); concurrent attendance required.

101.title: Plato
101.description: Study of Plato and his works.

202.title: Computer-Based Patient Records
202.description: Introduction and overview of computer-based clinical record systems. Topics include data modeling, health system standards and terminologies; security, privacy and confidentiality; workflow modeling; data visualization; legal; decision support; public health; and evidence-based practice.
202.prereq_text: Current enrollment within the Health Informatics Graduate Program or consent of instructor.

289E.title: Clinical Knowledge for the Health Informaticist
289E.description: Basic clinical knowledge for health informatics students. Human systems, disease states and conditions, treatments and prognosis.

289F.title: Database & Knowledge Management
289F.description: Objectives include understanding the informatics techniques for data capture, information management, and knowledge generation that a student will use throughout their career.

289H.title: Modeling Biological Systems
289H.description: Create awareness of how modern computer graphics have led to VR-Sim-Rob applications, and how they are modifying the teaching of medicine and in some cases the diagnosis and treatment of patients.

290.title: Seminar in Medical Informatics
290.description: Discussion of current graduate research and topics in Medical Informatics. Oral presentations of individual study.

002.title: Elementary Hebrew
002.description: Speaking, listening, comprehension, reading and writing fundamentals of modern Hebrew.

022.title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew II
022.description: Continued development and refinement of grammar, composition, and language skills required for reading literary texts and conversing about contemporary topics at an advanced level. History of the Hebrew language.
022.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken HEB 101 or HEB 100B.

199.title: Research in Hematology-Oncology
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

298.title: Topics in Hematology
298.description:
Basic concepts of the physiology of the hematopoietic organ, the pathophysiology of hematopoietic disease, and concepts of therapeutics
will be offered for study. The specific topics to be dictated by the interest and background of the students.
298.prereq_text: One year of graduate work and/or consent of instructor.

299.title: Research
299.description:
Laboratory investigation contributing to the dissertation for a graduate
degree.

002.title: Elementary Hindi
002.description: Introduction to conversation, vocabulary, and sentence structure in the Hindi form of Hindi/Urdu using the Devanagari script in the context of the shared culture of Hindi/Urdu.
002.credit_limit_text: Not credit if student has taken HIN 002.

022.title: Intermediate Hindi/Urdu
022.description: Intermediate skills in reading and composition in the Hindi form in the Devanagari script and the Urdu form in the Nastaʿliq script and discussion of social and cultural issues in Hindi/Urdu.

007B.title: History of Latin America, 1700-1900
007B.description: Latin America from colony to republic. The nature of Iberian colonialism, the causes for independence, the creation of nation states, the difficulties in consolidating these nations, and the rise of Liberalism and export economies in the 19th century.

008.title: History of Indian Civilization
008.description: Survey of Indian civilization from the rise of cities (ca. 2000 B.C.) to the present, emphasizing themes in religion, social and political organization, and art and literature that reflect cultural interaction and change.

010C.title: World History III
010C.description: Major topics from world history of the 19th and 20th centuries, emphasizing the rise and fall of Western colonial empires; Cold War and the superpowers; the spread of the nation-states; and process of globalization.

012.title: Food & History
012.description: Survey of the ways humans have fed themselves from the dawn of humanity to the present. Transformation of plants and animals into food, cooking into cuisine, and ceremony into etiquette.

016.title: Sex, Science, & Society
016.description: Survey of the relationship between sex, science, and society in the history of the modern world. Emphasis on the development of scientific ideas about the human body against broader social, cultural, and political trends and from a global viewpoint.

017B.title: History of the United States
017B.description: The experience of the American people from the Civil War to the end of the Cold War.
017B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed HIS 017C.

072A.title: Women & Gender in America, to 1865
072A.description: History of women and gender in America through 1865, emphasizing intersections of gender, race, class, and sexuality.  Topics include interracial marriage, slavery, witchcraft, meanings of motherhood, war, domestic labor, moral reform, women’s rights, migrations, the effects of commercialization and industrialization.

080.title: The History of the United States in the Middle East
080.description: History of the United States in the Middle East from 1900 to the present. Examination of U.S. foreign relations toward the Middle East, their regional ramifications and domestic repercussions.

090.title: Research in History
090.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. Emphasis on primary sources and archival research.

100.title: Selected Topics in History
100.description: Selected Topics in History may be organized around a particular geography (e.g., the Balkans), a chronological framework (e.g., the 1960s around the world) or a thematic approach (e.g., the rise of ethnic or racial identities in a particular region).

102D.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: Modern Europe to 1815
102D.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. Modern Europe to 1815.

102M.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: United States Since 1896
102M.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. United States since 1896.

102Q.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: India
102Q.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. India.

102X.title: Undergraduate Proseminar in History: Comparative History
102X.description: Designed primarily for history majors. Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in the various fields of history. Comparative History, selected topics in cultural, political, economic, and social history that deal comparatively with more than one geographic field. May be taught abroad.

103.title: Topics in Historical Research
103.description: Individual research resulting in a research paper on a specific topic in one of various fields of history.

113.title: History of Modern Palestine/Israel
113.description: Cultural, social, and political histories of Palestine and Israel from the Ottoman Empire to the present. Topics include Zionist and Palestinian national movements; colonialism and the British Mandate; immigration, settlement, and refugees; the development of modern Israeli cultures; questions of statehood and multiculturalism; conflict and regional minority populations.

132.title: Crime & Punishment in Early Modern Europe
132.description: Deviance and crime in early modern Europe, contrasting imaginary crimes, e.g. witchcraft, with "real" crimes such as highway robbery and infanticide. Examines impact of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, and class in processes of criminalization.

136.title: Scientific Revolution
136.description: Rise of modern science in Europe, 1500–1750. Transformation of ideas about nature, knowledge, medicine, and technology in the age of Copernicus, Vesalius, Galileo, Descartes, and Newton.

142A.title: History of the Holocaust
142A.description: Topics include comparative genocide, medieval and modern antisemitism, modern German history, the rise of Nazism, Jewish life in Europe before the Nazi period, and the fate of the Jewish communities and other persecuted groups in Europe from 1933-1945.

146B.title: Europe in the 20th Century
146B.description: Survey of the history of Europe since 1939.

147A.title: European Intellectual History: 1800-1870
147A.description: European thought in the early industrial era. Shifting cultural frameworks, from romanticism to scientism; liberal and socialist reactions to social change. Focus on the work of Goethe, Hegel, J.S. Mill, Marx, Darwin and Flaubert.

166B.title: History of Mexico since 1848
166B.description: History of Mexico from 1848 to the present.

173.title: Becoming an American: Immigration & American Culture
173.description: Introduction to the wide range of immigrant experiences and cycles of nativism that have shaped American culture in the 20th century. From novels, memoirs and films, students will explore how external and internal immigration has created a multicultural society.

177B.title: History of Black People & American Race Relations: 1860-Present
177B.description: History of black people and race relations from 1860-present. Emphasis on Civil War, Reconstruction, Segregation, Age of Accommodation, black nationalism, urbanization, civil rights, and changing ideology of race relations.

179.title: Asian American History, 1850-Present
179.description: Historical experience of people of Asian ancestry in the United States from the mid-19th century to the present. Migration, labor, community formation, race relations, women and gender, popular culture.

184.title: History of Sexuality in America
184.description: History of sexuality in America from pre-European through the late-20th century. Topics include birth control, marriage, sexual violence, prostitution, inter-racial relationships, heterosexuality and homosexuality, the feminist, gay, and lesbian liberation movements, AIDS, commercialization of sexuality.

192.title: Internship in History
192.description: Supervised internship and study as historian, archivist, curator, or in another history-related capacity, in an approved organization or institution.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; enrollment dependent on availability of intern positions, with priority to History majors.

194A.title: Aristocratic & Feudal Japan
194A.description: Broad survey of the cultural, social, religious, and political aspects of Japanese history from mythological times through the 16th century emphasizing comparison of the organizations, values, and beliefs associated with the aristocratic and feudal periods.

197T.title: Tutoring in History
197T.description: Tutoring of students in lower division courses. Weekly meeting with instructors in charge of courses. Written reports on methods and materials required. No final examination.
197T.prereq_text: Enrolled as a History major with senior standing and consent of department chairperson.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

200A.title: First Year Research Seminar
200A.description: Preparation for higher degrees in History. Individual research and analysis resulting in a substantial research paper of publishable quality. Completion required of all Ph.D. candidates. HIS 200A and HIS 200B must be taken in continuous sequence, ordinarily during the first year.

202C.title: Major Issues in Historical Interpretation: Modern Europe
202C.description: Fundamental issues and debates in the study of history. Modern Europe. Readings, papers, and class reports.

202H.title: Major Issues in Historical Interpretation: United States
202H.description: Fundamental issues and debates in the study of history. United States. Readings, papers, and class reports.

203B.title: Second-Year Research Seminar
203B.description: Prepare for higher degrees in history. Individual research and analysis resulting in substantial research paper of publishable quality. Completion required of all Ph.D. candidates. HIS 203A & HIS 203B must be taken in continuous sequence, ordinarily during second year.

389.title: Introductory Seminar for Teaching Assistants
389.description: An introduction to the broad comparative and theoretical issues of teaching methods and techniques in history.

390.title: Teaching History in College
390.description: Designed for teaching assistants with emphasis on problems and procedures encountered by teachers of lower division classes at the university.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to students in the Davis Honors Challenge.

203.title: Research Perspectives in Horticulture
203.description: Following lectures/discussions of scientific methodology, students develop research proposals aided by classroom discussions and individual interactions with instructors. Lectures and critiques of classical papers provide a sense of the evolution of the current concepts in perennial plant biology.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship, off campus and on campus, in community and institutional setting. Involves progressively greater (supervised) participation in program delivery or assessment.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; field work experience or at least one course related to fieldwork assignment (e.g. HDE 100A, HDE 100B, HDE 140 or HDE 140L).

100A.title: Infancy & Early Childhood
100A.description: Biological, social, and cultural influences in the psychological growth and development of children, prenatal through age six. Two observations of preschool children required.
100A.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (BIS 002A or BIS 010 or BIS 001A or BIS 010V) or MCB 010 or NPB 010 or NPB 012 or MIC 010.

100B.title: Middle Childhood & Adolescence
100B.description: Interplay of biological and social-cultural factors in the emotional, cognitive and social development from middle childhood through adolescence.
100B.prereq_text: (HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V); (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y).

104.title: Children in Families, Schools, Communities
104.description: Children's social contexts (e.g., family, peers, school, neighborhood, community culture), development, and environmental challenges (e.g., poverty, maltreatment) from birth through adolescence.
104.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V.

112.title: Social Relationships Across the Lifespan
112.description: Spectrum of relationships across the lifespan; e.g., families, friends, members from the broader social network. Major theories and research among social relationships and development.
112.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

120.title: Research Methods in Human Development
120.description: Scientific process, research designs, and experimental controls; APA manuscript style and scientific writing; statistical analysis and interpretation of results. Laboratory exercises to collect data, analyze and interpret results, and write scientific papers.
120.prereq_text: STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 013V or STA 100 or EDU 114 or PSC 041 or PSC 041V or (SOC 046A,  SOC 046B).

130.title: Developmental Psychopathology
130.description: Foundational principles and current issues in developmental psychopathology, the study of mental health problems and disorders that originate in childhood and adolescence (e.g., disruptive behavior, mood and anxiety disorders).
130.prereq_text: ((HDE 100A or HDE 100AV); HDE 100B or HDE 100BV) or (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V); consent of instructor.

131.title: Thriving Across the Lifespan
131.description: Positive developmental trajectories from womb to tomb. Developmental process of thriving (e.g., happiness, life satisfaction, wisdom) and the factors that support thriving.
131.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

133.title: Stress, Adversity & Resilience
133.description: Short and long term biobehavioral responses to stress and adversity. The biological, psychological, social, and cultural factors of resilience. Interventions promoting resilience. Developmental perspective of stress and resilience across the lifespan.
133.prereq_text: HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

135V.title: Health Behaviors Across the Lifespan
135V.description: Development of health-related behaviors and physical and mental health outcomes across the lifespan. Coping strategies and behaviors such as nutrition, physical activity, technology, substance use/abuse, and social and cognitive engagement, as related to developmental stage.
135V.prereq_text: NPB 011 or NUT 010 or NUT 010V or NUT 010Y or SAS 013 or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100C.

140.title: Field Study in Early Childhood
140.description: Application of theories of learning and development to interaction with infants, toddlers, and preschoolers at Early Childhood Laboratory School. Applied skills in communication, guidance, and curriculum.

142.title: Field Study with Emotionally Distressed Children & Adolescents
142.description: Field study with children who are identified as emotionally distressed, including those with internalizing and externalizing behavioral problems.
142.prereq_text: HDE 130 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

143.title: Field Studies of the Elderly
143.description: Apply theory and research on adult development and aging, work with older adults in a variety of settings, and develop skills relevant to that application. Develop a small research project.
143.prereq_text: HDE 100C or HDE 160 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.

180.title: Special Topics in Human Development
180.description: In-depth examination into selected topics in the field of human development (e.g., brain development, parenting, nutrition).  Content varies from quarter to quarter.
180.prereq_text: Four upper division courses in Human Development (HDE).

190C.title: Introductory Research Conference
190C.description: Instructors lead discussions with undergraduate students who involve themselves in a research project. Research papers are reviewed and aspects of project proposals developed out of class are presented and evaluated.
190C.prereq_text: Involvement in ongoing research; consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Supervised internship off and on campus, in community, and institutional
settings.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

200B.title: Middle Childhood & Adolescence
200B.description: Theory and research on biological, cognitive, social, and cultural influences on behavioral development from age five years until late adolescence.
200B.prereq_text: Graduate standing; basic biology or physiology; at least two upper division or graduate level courses in psychology or related fields.

205.title: Longitudinal Data Analysis
205.description: Introduction to longitudinal data manipulation, organization, description, and modeling in the multilevel modeling and structural equation modeling frameworks.
205.prereq_text: PSC 204B; or equivalent graduate courses in statistics or consent of instructor; familiarity with multiple regression and the basics of matrix algebra.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Supervising instructors lead research discussions with their graduate students. Research papers are reviewed and project proposals are presented and evaluated.

292.title: Graduate Internship
292.description: Individually designed supervised internship, off campus, in community or institutional setting. Developed with advice of faculty mentor.
292.prereq_text: Consent of faculty (internship sponsor) and satisfactory completion of placement relevant course work, for example: EDU 213, EDU 216; HDE 222, HDE 242; LAW 272, LAW 273.

192.title: Internship in Human Physiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in physiology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed reading, discussion and/or laboratory experience on selected topics.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Senior standing in biology, chemistry, physics, psychology, or engineering.

298.title: Group Study
298.description:
For graduate students desiring to explore particular topics in depth.
Lectures and conferences may be involved.

497T.title: Tutoring in Human Physiology
497T.description: Assist instructor by tutoring medical students in preparation for one of the departmental courses that is a component of the required curriculum of the School of Medicine.
497T.prereq_text: Advanced standing or consent of instructor.

498.title: Directed Reading & Group Study
498.description: Directed reading and discussion on selected topics in human physiology.

131.title: Genocide
131.description: Comparative and critical study of the modern phenomenon of genocide from religious, ethical and historical perspectives.

136.title: Human Rights in the Middle East
136.description: Study of the experience of Human Rights in the modern Middle East, with special attention to the Human Rights issues raised by events of Arab Spring; Palestine-Israel conflict; history of genocide, mass killing and totalitarianism in the region.

138.title: Human Rights, Gender, & Sexuality
138.description: Gender and sexuality in the context of human rights. Topics include women's participation in the public sphere, the right to change gender, the right for family privacy, and the right to marriage.

200B.title: Memory, Culture, & Human Rights
200B.description: Explores the multiple convergences among memory, culture, and human rights. Discusses diverse approaches to how societal actors in different historical, cultural, and national settings, construct meanings of past political violence, inter-group conflicts, and human rights struggles.
200B.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

013.title: Witches: Myth & Historical Reality
013.description: Examines the historical construction of the witch. Four areas covered are: European pagan religions and the spread of Christianity; the "Burning' Times" in early modern Europe; 17th-century New England and the Salem witch trials; and fairy tales.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.

299.title: Individual Research
299.description: Individual research in the humanities resulting in a formal written research report.

010.title: Water, Power, Society
010.description: Water resources issues. How water has been used to gain and wield socio-political power. Water resources development in California as related to current and future sustainability of water quantity and quality. Roles of science and policy in solving water problems.

092.title: Hydrologic Science Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in Hydrologic Science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division student.

150.title: Water Law
150.description: Principles and issues of California Water Law. Types of water rights, groundwater rights and management, and protection of instream uses. Water projects, role of federal government and federal/state relations. Basic water quality acts, endangered species act, water transfers and current water issues.
150.prereq_text: Consent of instructor or upper division standing.

192.title: Hydrologic Science Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in water science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

201B.title: Hydrologic Sciences Core Seminar
201B.description: Exposure to research underway in the Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group as well as provide opportunities to present and refine research through interaction with other students in the Graduate Group. One main goal of this core course is to build cohesiveness among the HSGG students and to create an opportunity for them to hear about each other's work.

290.title: Seminar in Hydrologic Science
290.description: Seminars and critical review of problems, issues, and research in hydrologic sciences. Oral presentations of research. Topics vary.
290.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing and background in Hydrologic Science.

293.title: Current Concepts in Immunology
293.description: Innate and acquired immunity as defense mechanisms against disease. Mechanisms regulating the distinct cell types driving these responses and current concepts in the literature.

192.title: Research Internship in Internal Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in the division of Infectious Diseases. Undergraduates will have an opportunity to acquire research experience in clinical settings.

199.title: Infectious Diseases Research
199.description: Discrete problem requiring reading and actual manual effort in solution will be assigned to each student. Progress and results will be reviewed at intervals with instructor and via seminar presentation.
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; chemistry through organic chemistry (in addition, physical and biochemistry preferred), biology through basic bacteriology (in addition, microbiology and immunology preferred).

299.title: Research in Infectious Diseases
299.description:
Laboratory investigation contributing to the dissertation for a graduate
degree.

499.title: Research Topics in Infectious Disease
499.description:
Discrete problem requiring reading and actual manual effort in solution will be assigned to each student. Progress and results to be reviewed at
intervals with instructor and via seminar presentation.
499.prereq_text: Successful completion of the first-year of study in School of Medicine; graduate students (approved for graduate credit); and/or consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Integrated Studies
197T.description: Tutoring in Integrated Studies  courses, usually in small discussion groups. Weekly discussions with the instructor on the subject matter of the course being tutored and on the art and craft of teaching.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of Director of Integrated Studies.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship in internal medicine and related fields.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Directed group study in medicine and related fields.
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Undergraduate Research in Medicine: Molecular & Cell Biology
099.description: Undergraduate research in medicine, focusing on molecular & cellular biology.

192.title: Internship in Internal Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in internal medicine and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

194.title: Practicum in Community Health Clinics
194.description: The undergraduate student, through active participation in the medical aspects of community health clinics, gains knowledge of the organization, administration, and problem-solving capabilities of these primary care facilities.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study in medicine and related fields.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

458Y.title: Climate Change: Implications for Clinical Practice & Population Health
458Y.description: Climate change and its associated environmental and social disruptions are and will increasingly lead to clinical and population health consequences for which clinicians, and health systems, will need to be prepared to best care for their patients and the populations they serve. Draws from the Global Consortium on Climate and Health Education’s set of Core Climate and Health Competencies for Health Professionals and places an emphasis on climate change and clinical practice.

496.title: Integrative Geriatric Medicine
496.description: Provides a two-week clinical experience for fourth-year medical students. Introduces medical students to the care elements for older adults in the inpatient and outpatient settings.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

103.title: Social Change & Agricultural Development
103.description: How social and cultural factors influence technological change in agriculture; theories of diffusion of innovations; social impact analysis and technology assessment.
103.prereq_text: Introductory social science course (Anthropology (ANT), Sociology (SOC), Economics (ECN), International Agricultural Development (IAD)).

170.title: Program Development for International Agriculture
170.description: Principles of leadership and management for international agricultural development. Organizations and organizational behavior, and the implications for planning and administering organizations involved in the global development effort.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Supervised internship, off and on campus, in community and institutional settings. May be taught abroad.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

290.title: Seminar in International Agricultural Development
290.description: Discussion and critical evaluation of advanced topics and issues in international agricultural development.

291.title: Topics in International Agricultural Development
291.description: Selected topics dealing with current issues in agricultural development in lesser developed nations. Variable content.

292.title: Graduate Internship
292.description: Individually designed supervised internship, off or on campus, in community, business or institutional setting. Developed with advice of faculty mentor and Humphrey Coordinator.
292.prereq_text: Participation in H. Humphrey Fellow Program or consent of instructor.

192.title: International Relations Internship
192.description: Work experience in international relations, with term paper summarizing the practical experience of the student.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

002Y.title: Elementary Italian
002Y.description: Continuation of ITA 001, ITA 001Y or ITA 001S. Review of grammar and vocabulary, and practice of all language skills through cultural texts.
002Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken ITA 001A or ITA 002S.
002Y.prereq_text: ITA 001 or ITA 001Y or ITA 001S; or consent of Instructor.

022Y.title: Intermediate Italian
022Y.description: Continued development of grammatical structures and vocabulary. Emphasis on reading and writing in Italian.

112.title: Medieval & Renaissance Poetry: St. Francis to Petrarch
112.description: Study of the origins of Italian religious and secular poetry of the 13th and 14th centuries. Diversified poetry is illustrated in works of St. Francis, Dante, Cavalcanti, Petrarch, the Sicilian School, the Sweet New Style Poets, and other authors.
112.prereq_text: ITA 009 or ITA 009S or ITA 023 or ITA 023S; consent of instructor, or the equivalent.

114.title: Boccaccio, Decameron, & the Renaissance Novella
114.description: Study of the development of the short story in Italy, as exemplified in Giovanni Boccaccio's Decameron, in his predecessors and Renaissance followers.
114.prereq_text: ITA 009 or ITA 009S or ITA 023 or ITA 023S; consent of instructor, or the equivalent course.

002.title: Elementary Japanese
002.description: Continuation of training in basic Japanese spoken and written skills.
002.prereq_text: JPN 001 C- or better; or the equivalent language proficiency.

005.title: Intermediate Japanese
005.description: Intermediate-level training in spoken and written Japanese in cultural context, based on language skills developed in JPN 004.
005.prereq_text: JPN 004 C- or better; or the equivalent language proficiency.

102.title: Japanese Literature in Translation: The Middle Period
102.description: Study of the major literary genres from the 12th century to the second half of the 19th century including poetry, linked-verse, military chronicles, no drama, Buddhist literature, haiku, haibun, kabuki, bunraku, plays and Edo prose narratives.

112.title: Modern Japanese: Reading & Discussion
112.prereq_text: JPN 111 C- or better; or the equivalent language proficiency.

122.title: Advanced Japanese II
122.description: Second of three courses in a series of fourth-year Advanced Japanese which focuses on the levels of formality or politeness in conversation as well as socio-cultural aspects and topics in Japanese society.
122.prereq_text: JPN 121 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

151.title: Japanese Linguistics
151.description: Introduction to Japanese linguistics, featuring key aspects of the Japanese language. Analysis of Japanese from the perspectives of phonology, syntax, discourse analysis, sociolinguistics and psycholinguistics.

156.title: Japanese Literature on Film
156.description: Survey of films based on works of Japanese literature, emphasis on pre-modern and early modern texts. Introduction to major directors of Japan, with a focus on cinematic adaptation. Lectures and readings in English. Films in Japanese with English subtitles.

192.title: Japanese Internship
192.description: Work experience in Japanese language, with analytical term paper on a topic approved by instructor.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Japanese
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the Program's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of Department Chairperson.

116.title: Readings in Jewish Writing & Thought in German Culture
116.description: Historical tradition of Jewish thought in the German cultural context; unique contributions of Jewish writers to culture of the German speaking world; what it means to be "other" in the mainstream culture.
116.credit_limit_text: No credit will be given to students who have completed HUM 121.

002.title: Place, Culture & Community
002.description: Social dimensions of landscapes and everyday environments, including concepts of place, culture and community. Urban and rural environments including wilderness, parks, sacred space, agricultural sites, workplaces, transportation networks, housing, recreation, and military sites. Application of course concepts and methods for interpreting cultural landscapes through archival and field research.

030.title: History of Environmental Design
030.description: History of environmental design across disciplines, including landscape architecture, architecture, planning, and urban design.
030.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 030.

070.title: Introduction to Spacemaking
070.description: Introduction to basic principles of design towards the creation of space. Design methodologies and skills to define, manipulate, and represent the built environment. Workshops in 3D physical modeling for spacemaking.
070.prereq_text: LED 021 or LDA 021; or consent of instructor.

092.title: Internship in Environmental Design
092.description: Supervised internship, off or on campus, in community, professional and institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of Instructor.

102.title: Methods in Environmental Design Research
102.description: Research, design, and planning methods employed in various disciplines of environmental design, including architecture, landscape architecture, planning, and urban design. Historical overview of research methodology. Designing independent environmental design research.
102.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 102
102.prereq_text: LED 050 or LDA 050; or consent of instructor..

119.title: Landscape & Environmental Design Representation II
119.description: Methods to explore and communicate environmental design intentions through digital media.
119.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 023.
119.prereq_text: LED 021 or LDA 021; or consent of instructor.

120.title: Landscape & Environmental Design Representation III
120.description: Studio to explore advanced representation and modeling skills. Digital drawing applied as an analytical research method, generative design technique and presentation tool.
120.prereq_text: LED 0119 or LDA 119; or consent of instructor.

130.title: Plants in the City
130.description: Benefits of plants in the urban environment. Plant selection and usage to create multifunctional urban green networks. Emphasis on the environmental, social, and economic value of plants in cities.
130.credit_limit_text: No repeat credit for students who have taken LDA 130
130.prereq_text: (LED 050 or LDA 050); (LED 070 or LDA 070); or consent of instructor.

141.title: Community Participation in Design & Planning
141.description: Introduction to community participation in design and planning. Histories, theories, policies and practices of participation, including social, cultural and political factors, and incorporating diverse perspectives within the design and planning process. Contemporary methods are applied through real-world projects undertaken in collaboration with community partners.
141.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 141.
141.prereq_text: (LED 030 or LDA 030); (LED 070 or LDA 070); or consent of instructor.

150.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
150.description: Basic concepts, principles, and methods of GIS are presented. Data structures, database design, GIS data creation, GPS, and spatial analysis. May be taught abroad.
150.credit_limit_text: Not open to credit for students who have completed ABT 180, PLS 180, ABT 181N.

170.title: Site Planning & Design Studio
170.description: Application of place-making and problem-solving skills to local landscape sites. Analysis of social and environmental conditions in the field. Lectures link design projects to contemporary theories and practices.
170.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 170.
170.prereq_text: LED 160 or LDA 160; or consent of instructor.

183.title: Advanced Landscape Architecture Studio II
183.description: Landscape architecture studio featuring advanced studies and applications of creative work, design, technology and/or theory. One day-long field trip required.
183.prereq_text: LED 171 or LDA 171; or consent of instructor.

202.title: Research Methods in Environmental Design
202.description: Research methods used in environmental design. Conceptual frameworks, research design, ethics, proposals, data collection, analysis and dissemination. Methods examined may include visual observation, surveys, interviews, workshops, material studies, experimental design, participatory design, mapping, prototyping, and post-occupancy evaluation.
202.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LDA 202.

298.title: Group Study in Landscape & Environmental Design
298.description: Group Study. May be taught abroad.

002.title: Elementary Latin
002.description: Continuation of LAT 001.

002R.title: Elementary Latin
002R.description: Continuation of LAT 001 with special emphasis on review of basic grammar and vocabulary.
002R.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed LAT 002.

118.title: Roman Historians
118.description: Readings in Latin from one or more of the major Roman historians and biographers. Authors may include Sallust, Nepos, Livy, Tacitus, Suetonius, and Ammianus Marcellinus.

001.title: Introduction to Linguistics
001.description: Introduction to the study of language; its nature, diversity, and structure.

001Y.title: Introduction to Linguistics
001Y.description: Introduction to the study of language; its nature, diversity, and structure.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Students may not take both LIN 001 and LIN 001Y for credit.

002V.title: Language, the Mind, & Computers
002V.description: Analysis of human language and language processing by humans and machines. How language is represented and processed in the human mind, how computers process language, and similarities and differences between human and computer processing of language. Human-media interaction for language and society.

096.title: Directed Group Study in English as a Second Language
096.description: Directed group study of topic in English as a Second Language (ESL).

105.title: Topics in Language & Linguistics
105.description: Detailed examination of a major contemporary linguistic theory, a major contemporary issue or related set of issues in linguistics, or the structure of a particular language or language family.

106.title: English Grammar
106.description: Survey of present-day English grammar as informed by contemporary linguistic theories. The major syntactic structures of English; their variation across dialects, styles, and registers; their development; and their usefulness in describing the conventions of English.
106.prereq_text: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or ENG 003 or UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y; or consent of instructor.

127.title: Text Processing & Corpus Linguistics
127.description: Investigation of the lexical organization of human languages through corpus linguistics. Application of principles of linguistic analysis, automatic text processing, and statistical research to solving problems of textual evaluation and classification, as well as information retrieval and extraction.
127.prereq_text: LIN 001, LIN 005, LIN 006, or ANT 004 recommended.

131.title: Introduction to Syntactic Theory
131.description: Introduction to syntactic theory, primarily through the examination of a major theory of syntax, emphasizing theoretical reasoning, argumentation, and problems of theory building in syntax.

150.title: Languages of the World
150.description: Survey of the world's languages, their geographical distribution and classification, both genetic and typological.  Illustrative descriptions of several major languages from different geographical areas; pidgins and creoles, lingua francas and other languages of widespread use.
150.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 050.

166.title: The Spanish Language in the United States
166.description: Linguistic features of the varieties of the Spanish language spoken throughout the United States; phonology, morphology, syntax, vocabulary. Focus on the relationship between United States Spanish and other world varieties of Spanish, within a historical framework.
166.prereq_text: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or SPA 111N; SPA 023; or equivalent to SPA 023 recommended.

171.title: Introduction to Psycholinguistics
171.description:
Introduction to psychological issues relating to the implementation
of language and linguistic structure during speech production and comprehension and to the implications of research in psychology and related fields for linguistic theory.

175.title: Biological Basis of Language
175.description: Overview of issues in the field of neurolinguistics and techniques used to explore representation of language in the human brain.

177.title: Computational Linguistics
177.description: Understanding the nature of language through computer modeling of linguistic abilities.  Relationships between human cognition and computer representations of cognitive processing.
177.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 007.
177.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; LIN 001 or LIN 001Y recommended.

192.title: Internship in Linguistics
192.description: Internship applying linguistic-related skills to a fieldwork project in areas such as media, law, or industry, in approved organizations or institutions. Maximum of 4 units applicable toward major.
192.prereq_text: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y; or equivalent course; consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Linguistics
197T.description: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing and consent of department chairperson.

201.title: Proseminar
201.description: Introduction to research activity of faculty in the Graduate Group in Linguistics and guest speakers.

205A.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
205A.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

205C.title: Topics in Linguistic Theory & Methods
205C.description: Advanced study of current problems in linguistic theory and methodology.

297T.title: English as a Second Language Teaching/Tutoring
297T.description: Teaching classes for ESL graduate students. Aiding the ESL undergraduate composition classes; tutoring foreign graduate student Teaching Assistants in pronunciation. Does not fulfill requirement toward the M.A. degree.
297T.prereq_text: LIN 300 or LIN 301 or LIN 302 (can be concurrent); consent of instructor.

011A.title: Elementary Financial Accounting
011A.description: Basic concepts of accounting; interpreting and using financial statements; understanding accounting principles.

011AY.title: Elementary Financial Accounting
011AY.description: Basic concepts of accounting; interpreting and using financial statements; understanding accounting principles.

011B.title: Elementary Managerial Accounting
011B.description: Theory of product costing. Analyzing the role and impact of accounting information on decision making; planning and performance evaluation.

012Y.title: Navigating Life’s Financial Decisions
012Y.description: Survey of major life financial decisions (e.g., career choice, consumption v. saving, investments, mortgages, insurance) and how decision-making biases (e.g., overconfidence, present bias, limited attention) can lead to suboptimal choice. Draws on research from economics, psychology, and sociology.

101.title: Sources & Uses of Accounting Information
101.description: Develops an understanding of the supply and demand of accounting information. Topics include the generation and processing of accounting information, the examination of accounting information by auditors, and the use of accounting information by capital markets and tax authorities.
101.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better; must have C- or better in all prerequisite courses.

103.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
103.description: Begin to develop expertise in the accounting for assets and introduce analysis of financial statements.
103.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better

105.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
105.description: Continue to develop expertise in the preparation of financial statements by studying the accounting for liabilities and stockholders’ equity. Examines the accounting for contracts that can have significant effects on firms’ financial statements.

107.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting III
107.description: Finishes the Intermediate Financial Accounting series by examining in depth the accounting for contracts related to pensions and leases. Preparation of the statement of cash flows and footnote disclosures.

114.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurial Marketing
114.description: Frameworks, concepts, and tools for marketing new products and services for startups and established, large firms: defining market opportunities, testing concepts, competitive landscapes, critical product features, marketing channels, and launch strategies.
114.credit_limit_text: Only two units of credit for students who have taken ARE 113.

116.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurial Finance
116.description: Theories and methodologies for determining, evaluating, and structuring financial aspects in an entrepreneurial context in new ventures and established companies. Building and evaluating business and revenue models, developing and using pro-forma financial statements (income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow), valuing a business, and financing through various sources of capital. How financial aspects of new ventures and projects help define, value, and fund early-stage projects.
116.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 160 or ARE 171.
116.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better).

120.title: Introduction to Information Systems
120.description: Develop an analytical framework to manage and monitor business systems concerned with operational, human, and organizational interactions. Introduction to computer hardware, systems software, and fundamental principles of database management systems. Concepts of data visualization.

140.title: Introduction to Marketing & Data Analytics
140.description: Strategic analysis and solutions to marketing decision problems. Enduring concepts and emerging issues of marketing; analytics tools to address modern marketing challenges.
140.prereq_text: (ECN 001A C- or better or ECN 001AY C- or better or ECN 001AV C- or better); (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better).

150.title: Introduction to Management
150.description: Management of firms in a variety of industries, including high technology industries such as software development and biotechnology. Motivating and managing workers, organizing for innovation, and making decisions. Enable the development of skills to analyze and address management challenges and opportunities.

151.title: Management of Innovation & Entrepreneurship
151.description: Innovation and entrepreneurship in established companies or new ventures. Knowledge, skills, and hands-on experiences in creative problem-solving, decision-making, building new ventures, and innovation strategy.

170.title: Management Accounting & Control
170.description: Covers the design of cost accounting systems, the preparation of financial budgets and forecasts, cost analysis, and the use of cost and other financial data to motivate and evaluate the performance of business units and managers.
170.prereq_text: (MGT 011A C- or better or MGT 011AV C- or better or MGT 011AY C- or better); MGT 011B C- or better.

180.title: Introduction to Operations Management
180.description: Delivery of goods and services to customers, focusing on effectiveness and efficiency of processes. Key concepts and relationships between supply chain design and business models and strategies.
180.prereq_text: (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better).

224.title: Managing People in High-Performance Organizations
224.description: Strategic approach to the management of people within organization. Analyze employment systems' fit with firms' environments and strategies. Explore consequences of choices firms make in managing people—decisions as to selection, performance evaluation, compensation, and other management policies and practices.
224.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken MGB 224 or MGP 224.

241.title: New Product Development
241.description: State-of-the-art concepts and methods to enhance the effectiveness of new product development activities. Focuses on the understanding of managerial issues and acquiring the ability to solve problems.

290.title: Topics in General Management
290.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in MGT 201A and MGT 201B, or current business interest topics in fields of business writing, business communications, development, or workplace processes.
290.prereq_text: Completion of all first-year graduate courses at the Graduate School of Management or the equivalent.

293.title: Topics in Marketing
293.description: Advanced topics in marketing, which may include marketing research, new product development, brand management, pricing, distribution management, service marketing, hitech marketing, advertising, sales promotions, marketing through the Web.
293.prereq_text: Completion of all first-year graduate courses at the Graduate School of Management or the equivalent.

402A.title: Markets & the Firm
402A.description: Examines the interaction of consumers, firms and government, and the effect this interaction has on the use of resources and firm profitability. Fundamental economic concepts such as marginal analysis, opportunity cost, pricing, and externalities are introduced and applied.
402A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 202A, MGP 202A, MGB 202A or MGV 202AV.

404.title: Marketing Management
404.description: Analysis of market opportunities, elements of market research, development of marketing strategies, market planning and implementations, and control systems. Consumer and industrial markets, market segmentation, pricing strategies, distribution channels, promotion, and sales.
404.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 204, MGP 204, MGB 204 or MGV 204V.

423.title: Leader as Coach: An Introduction to Coaching Skills for Leaders
423.description: Introduces the fundamental coaching skills and coaching models that leaders can apply in everyday interactions with their team and colleagues in order to build trust, overcome challenges and help others discover their own full potential.

444.title: Strategic Branding
444.description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of branding strategies and implementation.

450.title: Technology Competition & Strategy
450.description: Provides a framework for thinking about technology competition and strategy.
450.prereq_text: (MGT 402A or MGP 402A or MGB 402A); (MGT 403A or MGP 403A or MGB 403A).

456.title: Personal Branding
456.description: Learn how to use the cornerstone principles of corporate branding and content marketing to define and create a personal brand in four phases using E.P.I.C. Framework: Establish: Discovery and Vision; Package: Content and Packaging; Inform: Dissemination; and Cultivate: Growth and Management.

465.title: Technology Finance & Valuation
465.description: Venture capital finance and the related practice of research and development finance. Application of finance tools and framework to the world of venture capital and financing of projects in high-growth industries.

468.title: Articulation & Critical Thinking
468.description: Public speaking, business writing, efficient and critical thinking about business challenges, and defining a personal code of ethics to shape actions and decisions.
468.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 268, MGP 268, MGB 268 or MGV 268V.

468A.title: Articulation & Critical Thinking
468A.description: Public speaking, business writing, efficient and critical thinking about business challenges, and defining a personal code of ethics to shape actions and decisions.
468A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 468.

473.title: Managerial Cost Accounting
473.description: Covers in-depth the cost and management accounting concepts enabling students to make decisions, including interpreting business situations, identifying available options, interpreting impacts on financial statements and stakeholders, and clearly and articulately recommending a course of action.

474.title: Managerial Budgeting
474.description: Covers in-depth the management accounting budgeting concepts enabling students to make decisions, including interpreting business situations, identifying available options, interpreting impacts on financial statements and stakeholders, and clearly and articulately recommending a course of action.

490B.title: Topics in General Management-Extended
490B.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in the MBA core such business writing, management, organizational behavior, business communications, development, finance and workplace processes.

490BV.title: Topics in Management
490BV.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in the MBA core such business writing, management, organizational behavior, business communications, development, and workplace processes.

200BV.title: Managerial Accounting
200BV.description: Information managers should know to be effective, including: product costing, motivating people, and differential analysis for decision making. Includes team projects and written and oral presentations.
200BV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 200B, MGP 200B, or MGB 200B.

201AV.title: The Individual & Group Dynamics
201AV.description: Examines basic psychological and social psychological processes shaping human behavior and applies knowledge of these processes to the following organizational problems: motivation, job design, commitment, socialization, culture, individual and group decision making, and team building.
201AV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 201A, MGP 201A or MGB 201A.

201BV.title: Organizational Strategy & Structure
201BV.description: Strategic management of organizations, including analysis of industries, firm resources and capabilities and corporate strategy. Strategy formulation, implementation and strategic decision-making. Firm and industry life cycles and change. Analysis of organizational design and structure including differentiation and integration.
201BV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 201B, MGP 201B, or MGB 201B.

202AV.title: Markets & the Firm
202AV.description: Examines the interaction of consumers, firms and government, and the effect this interaction has on the use of resources and firm profitability. Fundamental economic concepts such as marginal analysis, opportunity cost, pricing, and externalities are introduced and applied.
202AV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 202A, MGP 202A or MGB 202A.

203BV.title: Forecasting & Managerial Research Methods
203BV.description: Influence of government and international factors on business. Distribution of income, business cycles, inflation and interest rates, the federal debt, monetary policy and international trade and finance.
203BV.credit_limit_text: Not open for students who have taken  MGT 203B, MGP 203B, or MGB 203B.

204V.title: Marketing Management
204V.description: Analysis of market opportunities, elements of market research, development of marketing strategies, market planning and implementations, and control systems. Consumer and industrial markets, market segmentation, pricing strategies, distribution channels, promotion, and sales.
204V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 204, MGP 204, or MGB 204.

205V.title: Financial Theory & Policy
205V.description: Corporate financial policy and investment management. Covers capital budgeting, optimal financial structure, cost-of-capital determination, risk measurement. Develops basic valuation principles for investments with long-lived and risky cash-flows, and extends these to derivative securities, asset portfolios, investment management and hedging.
205V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 205, MGP 205, or MGB 205.

224V.title: Managing People in High-Performance Organizations
224V.description: Explore choices firms make in managing workers–decisions as to wages, benefits, working conditions, and other management policies and practices. Analyze employment systems' fit with firms' environments and strategies, and the consequences of choices managers make regarding policies and practices.
224V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 224, MGP 224, or MGB 224.

239V.title: Digital Marketing
239V.description: Equips students for a career in digital marketing and social media. Topics include online advertising, search engine optimization, interactive marketing, online privacy issues, e-commerce, social influence, social network theory, measurement of social influence and integrating social and traditional media.
239V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 239, MGP 239 or MGB 239.

246V.title: Negotiations in Organizations
246V.description: Basic theory of negotiation; applies theory to process of building teams to achieve business purposes. Covers integrative and distributive strategies of claiming value, how to recognize bargaining tricks, uncovering hidden agendas, brainstorming to extend Pareto frontier.
246V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 246, MGP 246, or MGB 246.

251V.title: Management of Innovation
251V.description: Managing innovative enterprise in changing and uncertain environments. Covers technology forecasting and assessment, program selection and control, financial management, regulation, and ethics.
251V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 251, MGP 251 or MGB 251.

252V.title: Managing for Operational Excellence
252V.description: Explore the management of operations as applied to manufacturing, as well as services provided both inside & outside the organization. Develop an understanding of how uncertainty affects planning & delivery by looking at fundamental models of operations.
252V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 252, MGP 252, or MGB 252.

261V.title: Investment Analysis
261V.description: Examines asset pricing theories and relevant evidence, including the investment performance of stocks and bonds. Topics include the efficiency of markets, domestic and international portfolio diversification, factors influencing the value of stocks and other investments, and portfolio management and performance.
261V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 261, MGP 261, or MGB 261.

264V.title: Business Taxation
264V.description: Analysis of the impact of business taxation on investment, production, and finance decisions. Relationship between business organization and tax liability. Not intended for tax specialists.
264V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 264, MGP 264 or MGB 264.

265V.title: Technology Finance & Valuation
265V.description: Examines venture capital finance and the related practice of R&D finance. Goal is to apply finance tools and framework to the world of venture capital and financing of projects in high-growth industries.
265V.credit_limit_text: Not open for students who have previously taken MGT 265, MGB 265, or MGP 265.

268V.title: Articulation & Critical Thinking
268V.description: Public speaking, business writing, efficient and critical thinking about business challenges, and defining a personal code of ethics to shape actions and decisions.
268V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 268, MGP 268, or MGB 268.

400AV.title: Financial Accounting
400AV.description: Introduction to the concepts and objectives underlying the preparation of financial statements. Topics include understanding the accounting cycle, measurement and valuation problems associated with financial statement components, consideration of the usefulness of financial statements in the analysis of a corporation’s operations.

403AV.title: Data Analysis for Managers
403AV.description: Introduction to statistics and data analysis for managerial decision making. Descriptive statistics, principles of data collection, sampling, quality control, statistical inference. Application of data analytic methods to problems in marketing, finance, accounting, production, operations, and public policy.

438V.title: Quantitative Tools for Business
438V.description: Quantitative analysis and business storytelling through practical quantitative frameworks, descriptive procedures and real life case studies.

440V.title: Integrated Management Project
440V.description: Examines the scope of missions, objectives strategies, policies, structures, measurements and incentives which bear on the management of an organization. Simulated organizations in the private and public sectors, are assigned to student teams as the subjects of study.
440V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 240, MGP 240, MGB 240 or MGT 440, MGP 440, MGB 440.
440V.prereq_text: First-year core courses of online MBA program.

445V.title: Product Management
445V.description: Overview of the requirements, issues, and tools involved in marketing of products and services via lectures, case studies, and a hands-on, quarter-long competitive simulation.

452AV.title: Managing for Operational Excellence
452AV.description: Explore the management of operations as applied to manufacturing, as well as services provided both inside & outside the organization. Develop an understanding of how uncertainty affects planning & delivery by looking at fundamental models of operations.
452AV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGV 452V or MGV 252V

475V.title: R & SQL for Business Analytics
475V.description: Introduces programming concepts and how they can be applied to derive insights from data and make management decisions.

241.title: New Product Development
