241.description: State-of-the-art concepts and methods to enhance the effectiveness of new product development activities. Focuses on the understanding of managerial issues and acquiring the ability to solve problems.

400AY.title: Financial Accounting
400AY.description: Introduction to the concepts and objectives underlying the preparation of financial statements. Topics include understanding the accounting cycle, measurement and valuation problems associated with financial statement components, consideration of the usefulness of financial statements in the analysis of a corporation’s operations.
400AY.credit_limit_text: Not available for credit for students who have taken MGT 200A, MGP 200A, MGB 200A, MGV 200AV, MGV 400AV, MGT 400A, MGP 400A or MGB 400A.

402AY.title: Markets & the Firm
402AY.description: Examines the interaction of consumers, firms and government, and the effect this interaction has on the use of resources and firm profitability. Fundamental economic concepts such as marginal analysis, opportunity cost, pricing, and externalities are introduced and applied.
402AY.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGT 202A, MGP 202A, MGB 202A, MGV 202AV, MGT 402A, MGP 402A or MGB 402A.

415V.title: Business Law
415V.description: Introduction to law and legal process in the United States. Sources of law. Structure and operation of courts, federal-state relationships, fundamentals of administrative law, fundamentals of business law.
415V.credit_limit_text: Not available for credit for students who have taken MGT 215, MGP 215, MGB 215.

419V.title: Business Strategy Consulting Skills
419V.description: Students will learn practical business consulting skills which will help apply strategy theories in the workplace. Students will learn and practice tools to frame and analyze problems, conduct research, communicate findings and navigate client relationships.
419V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 419, MGP 419, or MGB 419.

423.title: Leader as Coach: An Introduction to Coaching Skills for Leaders
423.description: Introduces the fundamental coaching skills and coaching models that leaders can apply in everyday interactions with their team and colleagues in order to build trust, overcome challenges and help others discover their own full potential.

428.title: Negotiations in Organizations
428.description: Basic theory of negotiation; applies theory to process of building teams to achieve business purposes. Covers integrative and distributive strategies of claiming value, how to recognize bargaining tricks, uncovering hidden agendas, brainstorming to extend Pareto frontier.

450V.title: Technology Competition & Strategy
450V.description: Provides a framework for thinking about technology competition and strategy.
450V.prereq_text: (MGT 402A or MGP 402A or MGB 402A); (MGT 403A or MGP 403A or MGB 403A).

456.title: Personal Branding
456.description: Learn how to use the cornerstone principles of corporate branding and content marketing to define and create a personal brand in four phases using E.P.I.C. Framework: Establish: Discovery and Vision; Package: Content and Packaging; Inform: Dissemination; and Cultivate: Growth and Management.

473V.title: Managerial Cost Accounting
473V.description: Covers in-depth the cost and management accounting concepts enabling students to make decisions, including interpreting business situations, identifying available options, interpreting impacts on financial statements and stakeholders, and clearly and articulately recommending a course of action.

474V.title: Managerial Budgeting
474V.description: Covers in-depth the management accounting budgeting concepts that enables students to make decisions, including interpreting business situations, identifying available options, interpreting impacts on financial statements and stakeholders, and clearly and articulately recommending a course of action.

480V.title: Professional English for Multilingual Business Students
480V.description: Workshop-style course hones English writing and presentation skills. Learn techniques to improve professional communication, and practice with weekly assignments.

490BV.title: Topics in Management
490BV.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in the MBA core such business writing, management, organizational behavior, business communications, development, and workplace processes.

496.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in the MBA core such as business writing, management, organizational behavior, business communications, development, and workplace processes.

Application of data analytic methods to problems in marketing, finance, accounting, production, operations, and public policy.
403AY.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have taken MGT 203A, MGP 203A, MGB 203A, MGV 403AV, MGT 403A, MGP 403A or MGB 403A.

406A.title: Decision Modeling & Optimization
406A.description: Learn linear, network, integer, and nonlinear optimization methods, along with decision tree approaches for managerial decision-making. Develops AI literacy by having students critique AI-generated optimization models for correctness, interpretability, and business relevance across applications in marketing, operations, finance, and strategy.
406A.credit_limit_text: Not available for credit for students who have taken MGT 206, MGP 206, MGB 206 or MGV 206V.

407.title: Storytelling for Leadership
407.description: Internalize the fundamental principles behind stories that educate, influence, motivate, inspire, persuade and connect.

412V.title: International Marketing
412V.description: Basic concepts of international marketing. Understanding and managing heterogeneous, dynamic, and interdependent environments across countries. How to develop and implement an international marketing strategy: where and how to compete, how to adapt your marketing mix.

415V.description: Introduction to law and legal process in the United States. Sources of law. Structure and operation of courts, federal-state relationships, fundamentals of administrative law, fundamentals of business law.
415V.credit_limit_text: Not available for credit for students who have taken MGT 215, MGP 215, MGB 215.

423V.description: Introduces the fundamental coaching skills and coaching models that leaders can apply in everyday interactions with their team and colleagues in order to build trust, overcome challenges and help others discover their own full potential.

440.title: Integrated Management Project
440.description: Applies classroom learning to solve complex business challenges for real-world clients. Students learn practical consulting skills while their clients benefit from the student’s experience, insights, and work product.
440.prereq_text: First-year core courses of MBA program.

440DV.title: Integrated Management Project
440DV.description: Examines the scope of missions, objectives, strategies, policies, structures, measurements and incentives which bear on the management of an organization. Simulated organizations in the private and public sectors, are assigned to student teams as the subjects of study.

450V.description: Provides a framework for thinking about technology competition and strategy.

480V.description: Workshop-style course hones English writing and presentation skills. Learn techniques to improve professional communication, and practice with weekly assignments.

490.title: Topics in Business
490.description: Provides opportunity for students to gain experience in applying business methodologies previously acquired in other GSM courses.
490.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Sponsorship of a GSM Academic Senate faculty member; approval of graduate advisor.

490B.title: Topics in General Management-Extended
490B.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in the MBA core such business writing, management, organizational behavior, business communications, development, finance and workplace processes.

490BV.title: Topics in Management
490BV.description: Advanced topics in general management. Varied topics to cover more extensively issues discussed in the MBA core such business writing, management, organizational behavior, business communications, development, and workplace processes.

206.title: Epidemiologic Study Design
206.description: Builds on concepts presented in MPM 205. Concepts of epidemiologic study design—clinical trials, observational cohort studies, case control studies—introduced in MPM 205A are covered in more depth, using a problem-based format. Discussion of published epidemiologic studies.
206.prereq_text: MPM 205 or MPM 205V; or consent of instructor.

207.title: Applied Epidemiologic Problem Solving
207.description: Integration of epidemiologic and statistical methodology in a problem-solving approach to contemporary animal population health issues. Data validation and manipulation.

209.title: Research Planning & Reporting II
209.description: Concepts and skills in effective scientific writing for publication in a peer-reviewed journal in animal health or biomedicine. Includes developing an argument, organizing and writing a manuscript, improving readability, and responding to peer review.

212.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
212.description: Basic and advanced level of conceptual and methodological foundations in infectious disease epidemiology necessary to develop and evaluate programs for the detection, prevention, and control of infectious diseases in domestic animals, wildlife, and human populations.

002.title: Materials Marvels
002.description: Introduction to science and technology of materials as key engineering ingredients. Analysis of engineering marvels hidden in plain sight, including butterfly wings, bicycle frames, and computer chips. Relationships between materials, art, and nature, and how common items are both products and sources of ideas for new materials technologies.

162.title: Structure & Characterization of Engineering Materials
162.description: Description of the structure of engineering materials on the atomic scale by exploring the fundamentals of crystallography. Importance of this structure to materials’ properties. Description of experimental determination using x-ray diffraction techniques.
162.prereq_text: (ENG 045 C- or better or ENG 045Y C- or better); MAT 022A C- or better; PHY 009B C- or better.

162L.title: Structure & Characterization of Materials Laboratory
162L.description: Experimental investigations of structure of solid materials are combined with techniques for characterization of materials. Laboratory exercises emphasize methods used to study structure of solids at the atomic and microstructural levels. Methods focus on optical, x-ray and electron techniques.
162L.prereq_text: EMS 162 (can be concurrent); concurrent enrollment in EMS 162 recommended.

164.title: Kinetics of Materials
164.description: Basic kinetic laws and the principles governing phase transformations. Applications in diffusion, oxidation, nucleation, growth and spinodal transformations.
164.prereq_text: (ENG 045 C- or better or ENG 045Y C- or better); EMS 160; (ECH 060 or ECH 060V or ENG 006 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV).

181.title: Manufacturing of 3D & Composite Materials
181.description: Fundamental physical and chemical principles underlying various processing techniques, used in manufacturing processes for bulk (3D) and composite structural and functional materials. Effects of processing variables on structure-property relationships.
181.prereq_text: (ENG 045 C- or better or ENG 045Y C- or better); (ENG 105 or ECH 152B or EEC 140A or EEC 140AV or EMS 164).

183.title: Processing of 2D & Nanomaterials
183.description: Fundamentals of processing methods for two-dimensional materials, including thin films and graphene-like materials; as well as nanomaterials, including nanoparticles, nanowires, and quantum dots.
183.prereq_text: (ENG 045 C- or better or ENG 045Y C- or better); (ENG 105 or ECH 152B or EEC 140A or EEC 140AV or EMS 164).

186B.title: Materials Design Project
186B.description: Advanced materials design including examination of materials synthesis, processing, fabrication, and their practical applications. Rigorous evaluation of economic, manufacturing, and ethical limitations. Incorporation of diverse principles from the field of materials science into a collaborative design project.

197T.title: Tutoring in Materials Science & Engineering
197T.description: Tutoring of students in courses taught by instructors in the Department of Materials Science & Engineering. Tutor responsibilities may include attending class, assisting an instructor or TA in laboratory sections or group discussions, or providing non-graded feedback on assignments. Weekly meeting with the instructor.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

272.title: Advanced Functional Properties of Materials
272.description: Fundamental physical properties of solid materials important to solid state devices, including electronic, magnetic, dielectric, and optical properties. Fundamental principles underlying these properties, how these properties change at nanoscale dimensions and the implementation of these properties into devices.
272.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics, Chemistry, and Engineering.

274.title: Advanced Mechanical Properties of Materials
274.description: Comprehensive study of mechanical properties of materials, with special attention to dislocations and deformation and fracture control mechanisms. Mechanical properties of conventional engineering materials as well as advanced materials such as nanocrystalline solids and thin films are considered.

288.title: Living Matter: Physical Biology of the Cell
288.description: Introduction to the origin, maintenance, and regulation of the dynamic architecture of the cell, including cellular modes of organization, dynamics and energy dissipation, molecular transport, motility, regulation, and adaptability.

290.title: Materials Science & Engineering Seminar
290.description: Selected topics of current interest in Materials Science & Engineering. Subjects covered vary from year to year and are announced at the beginning of each quarter.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

261.title: Lactation & Infant Nutrition
261.description: Overview of the physiological and biochemical processes underlying human lactation and nutritional needs of both mother and infant. Development of skills in assessment, nutrition counseling, education and support of new mothers and their families.

263.title: Applied Research Methods in Maternal & Child Nutrition
263.description: Application of epidemiological principles to the study of maternal and child nutrition. Topics include quantitative & qualitative study procedures, including study design, data collection, and related analytical techniques.

264B.title: Current Topics in Maternal & Child Nutrition: Epidemiology & Evidence-Based Practice
264B.description: Current scientific literature related to Maternal & Child Nutrition. Topics include epidemiology, evidence-based practice, breastfeeding promotion, and nutritional assessment of populations.

012.title: Precalculus
012.description: Topics selected for their use in calculus, including functions and their graphs, slope, zeroes of polynomials, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions, sketching surfaces and solids.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed any of MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 017A, MAT 017B, MAT 017C, MAT 021A, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C with a C- or better.
012.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry; obtaining required score on the Precalculus Diagnostic Examination also known as the Math Readiness Assessment.

017A.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
017A.description: Introduction to differential calculus via applications in biology and medicine. Limits, derivatives of polynomials, trigonometric, and exponential functions, graphing, applications of the derivative to biology and medicine.
017A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 021A, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016A.
017A.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and analytical geometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

017B.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
017B.description: Introduction to integral calculus and elementary differential equations via applications to biology and medicine. Fundamental theorem of calculus, techniques of integration including integral tables and numerical methods, improper integrals, elementary first order differential equations, applications in biology and medicine.
017B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016C, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit for students who have completed MAT 016B.
017B.prereq_text: MAT 016A C- or better or MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better or MAT 021AH C- or better.

017C.title: Calculus for Biology & Medicine
017C.description: Matrix algebra, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, systems of differential equations, and applications to biology and medicine.
017C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016C.

019A.title: Calculus for Data-Driven Applications
019A.description: Calculus and other mathematical methods necessary in data driven analysis in the sciences, technology and the humanities.
019A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016A, 016B, 016C, MAT 017B, MAT 017C, MAT 021A, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 017A.
019A.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

019B.title: Calculus for Data-Driven Applications
019B.description: Calculus and other mathematical methods necessary in data driven analysis in the sciences, technology and the humanities.
019B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, 016C, MAT 017C, MAT 021B, or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 017B.
019B.prereq_text: MAT 017A C- or better or MAT 021A C- or better or MAT 021AH C- or better or MAT 019A C- or better.

019C.title: Calculus for Data-Driven Applications
019C.description: Calculus and other mathematical methods necessary in data-driven analysis in the sciences, technology and the humanities. Multivariable calculus, differential equations, partial derivatives.
019C.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016C or MAT 021C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 017C.
019C.prereq_text: MAT 019B C- or better or MAT 017B C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better or MAT 021BH C- or better.

021A.title: Calculus
021A.description: Functions, limits, continuity. Slope and derivative. Differentiation of algebraic and transcendental functions. Applications to motion, natural growth, graphing, extrema of a function. Differentials. L'Hopital's rule.
021A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 017B, or MAT 017C; only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016A or MAT 017A.
021A.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra, plane geometry, plane trigonometry, and analytical geometry, and satisfying the Mathematics Placement Requirement.

021B.title: Calculus
021B.description: Continuation of MAT 021A. Definition of definite integral, fundamental theorem of calculus, techniques of integration. Application to area, volume, arc length, average of a function, improper integral, surface of revolution.
021B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit to students who have completed MAT 016B, MAT 016C, MAT 017B, or MAT 017C.
021B.prereq_text: (MAT 021A C- or better or MAT 021AH C- or better) or MAT 017A B or better or MAT 019A B or better.

021C.title: Calculus
021C.description: Continuation of MAT 021B. Sequences, series, tests for convergence, Taylor expansions. Vector algebra, vector calculus, scalar and vector fields. Partial derivatives, total differentials. Applications to maximum and minimum problems in two or more variables. Applications to physical systems.
021C.prereq_text: MAT 016C C- or better or MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 017B B or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better or MAT 021BH C- or better.

021D.title: Vector Analysis
021D.description: Continuation of MAT 021C. Definite integrals over plane and solid regions in various coordinate systems. Line and surface integrals. Green's theorem, Stoke's theorem, divergence theorem.
021D.prereq_text: (MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better) or MAT 017C B or better.

022A.title: Linear Algebra
022A.description: Matrices and linear transformations, determinants, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization, factorization.
022A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 067.
022A.prereq_text: MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better.

022AL.title: Linear Algebra Computer Laboratory
022AL.description: Introduction to MATLAB and its use in linear algebra.
022AL.prereq_text: MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 021C or MAT 021CH.

022B.title: Differential Equations
022B.prereq_text: (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or BIS 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better).

027A.title: Linear Algebra with Applications to Biology
027A.description: Introduction to linear algebra with biological, medical, and bioengineering applications. Matrix algebra, vector spaces, orthogonality, determinants, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, principal component analysis, singular value decomposition, and linear transformations. Computer labs cover mathematical and computational techniques for modeling biological systems.
027A.credit_limit_text: Only 1 unit of credit for students who have completed MAT 022A.
027A.prereq_text: MAT 017C C- or better or or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better.

108.title: Introduction to Abstract Mathematics
108.description: Rigorous treatment of mathematical concepts with emphasis on developing the ability to understand abstract mathematical ideas, to read and write mathematical concepts, and to prove theorems. Designed to serve as preparation for the more rigorous upper division courses.

111.title: History of Mathematics
111.description: History of mathematics from ancient times through the development of calculus. Mathematics from Arab, Hindu, Chinese and other cultures. Selected topics from the history of modern mathematics.
111.prereq_text: MAT 127A or MAT 067 or MAT 108 or MAT 108V or MAT 114 or MAT 115A or MAT 141 or MAT 145; 8 units of upper division Mathematics.

115B.title: Number Theory
115B.description: Euler function, Moebius function, congruences, primitive roots, quadratic reciprocity law.
115B.prereq_text: MAT 115A; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A).

119A.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
119A.description: Scalar and planar autonomous systems; nonlinear systems and linearization; existence and uniqueness of solutions; matrix solution of linear systems; phase plane analysis; stability analysis; bifurcation theory; Liapunov's method; limit cycles; Poincare Bendixon theory.
119A.prereq_text: MAT 021D; (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A); (MAT 022B or MAT 027B or BIS 027B).

127A.title: Real Analysis
127A.description: Real numbers, sequences, series, and continuous functions.
127A.prereq_text: (MAT 021C or MAT 021CH); (MAT 067 or MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A); (MAT 108 or MAT 108V).

127B.title: Real Analysis
127B.description: Derivatives, integrals, sequences of functions, and power series.

128A.title: Numerical Analysis
128A.description: Error analysis, approximation, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration.
128A.prereq_text: MAT 021C; (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ENG 006); programming in languages such as MATLAB or Python will be used.

128B.title: Numerical Analysis in Solution of Equations
128B.description: Solution of nonlinear equations and nonlinear systems. Minimization of functions of several variables. Simultaneous linear equations. Eigenvalue problems. Linear programming.
128B.prereq_text: (ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ENG 006); (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A); methods of programming in languages such as MATLAB or Python for numerical analysis will be used.

135A.title: Probability
135A.description: Probability space; discrete probability, combinatorial analysis; independence, conditional probability; random variables, discrete and continuous distributions, probability mass function, joint and marginal density functions; expectation, moments, variance, Chebyshev inequality; sums of random variables, random walk, large number law, central limit theorem.
135A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former MAT 131.

135B.title: Stochastic Processes
135B.description: Generating functions, branching processes, characteristic function; Markov chains; convergence of random variables, law of iterated logarithm; random processes, Brownian motion, stationary processes, renewal processes, queueing theory, martingales.
135B.prereq_text: MAT 135A; (MAT 022A  or MAT 027A or MAT 067 or BIS 027A).

145.title: Combinatorics
145.description: Combinatorial methods using basic graph theory, counting methods, generating functions, and recurrence relations. Designed to serve as preparation for the more rigorous upper division courses.

150A.title: Modern Algebra
150A.description: Basic concepts of groups, symmetries of the plane. Emphasis on the techniques used in the proof of the ideas (Lemmas, Theorems, etc.) developing these concepts. Precise thinking, proof writing, and the ability to deal with abstraction.
150A.prereq_text: MAT 067 or (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A, (MAT 108 or MAT 108V)).

167.title: Applied Linear Algebra
167.description: Applications of linear algebra; LU and QR matrix factorizations, eigenvalue and singular value matrix decompositions.
167.prereq_text: MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A or MAT 067.

168.title: Optimization
168.description: Linear programming, simplex method. Basic properties of unconstrained nonlinear problems, descent methods, conjugate direction method. Constrained minimization. Programming language required.
168.prereq_text: MAT 021C; (((MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A), (MAT 108 or MAT 108V)) or MAT 067).

180.title: Special Topics
180.description: Special topics from various fields of modern, pure, and applied mathematics.  Some recent topics include Knot Theory, General Relativity, and Fuzzy Sets.
180.prereq_text: (MAT 067 or (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A, MAT 108)), MAT 127A.

185A.title: Complex Analysis
185A.description: Complex number system, analyticity and the Cauchy-Riemann equations, elementary functions, complex integration, power and Laurent series expansions, residue theory.
185A.prereq_text: (MAT 067 or (MAT 022A or MAT 027A or BIS 027A, MAT 108)), MAT 127B.

192.title: Internship in Applied Mathematics
192.description: Supervised work experience in applied mathematics. Final report.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

194.title: Undergraduate Thesis
194.description: Independent research under supervision of a faculty member. Student will submit written report in thesis form.

197TC.title: Tutoring Mathematics in the Community
197TC.description: Special projects in mathematical education developing techniques for mathematics instruction and tutoring on an individual or small group basis.

201B.title: Analysis
201B.description: Metric and normed spaces. Continuous functions. Topological, Hilbert, and Banach spaces. Fourier series. Spectrum of bounded and compact linear operators. Linear differential operators and Green's functions. Distributions. Fourier transform. Measure theory. Lp and Sobolev spaces. Differential calculus and variational methods.
201B.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Mathematics or Applied Mathematics, or consent of instructor.

202.title: Functional Analysis
202.description: Hahn-Banach, Open mapping, Closed graph, Banach-Steinhaus, and Krein-Milman. Subspaces and quotient spaces. Projections. Weak and weak-star topologies. Compact and adjoint operators in Banach spaces. Fredholm theory. Functions of operators. Spectral theory of self-adjoint operators.

205A.title: Complex Analysis
205A.description: Cauchy's theorem, Cauchy's integral formulas, meromorphic functions, complex logarithm, entire functions, Weierstrass infinite product formula, the gamma and zeta functions, and prime number theorem.
205A.credit_limit_text: No credit given to students who have completed MAT 205.
205A.prereq_text: MAT 185A; or equivalent to MAT 185A; or consent of instructor.

207B.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
207B.description: Ordinary differential equations and dynamical systems. Variational principles. Eigenfunctions, integral equations and Green's functions. Complex analysis and contour integration. Laplace's equation.  Diffusion equations. Wave phenomena. Dimensional analysis and scaling. Asymptotic expansions and perturbation theory. Stochastic processes and Brownian motion.
207B.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

215B.title: Topology
215B.description: Fundamental group and covering space theory. Homology and cohomology. Manifolds and duality. CW complexes. Fixed point theorems.
215B.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

228B.title: Numerical Solution of Differential Equations
228B.description: Numerical solutions of initial-value, eigenvalue and boundary-value problems for ordinary differential equations. Numerical solution of parabolic and hyperbolic partial differential equations.

235B.title: Probability Theory
235B.description: Measure-theoretic foundations, abstract integration, independence, laws of large numbers, characteristic functions, central limit theorems. Weak convergence in metric spaces, Brownian motion, invariance principle. Conditional expectation. Topics selected from: martingales, Markov chains, ergodic theory.
235B.prereq_text: MAT 235A or STA 235A; or consent of instructor.

240A.title: Differential Geometry
240A.description: Riemannian metrics, connections, geodesics, Gauss lemma, convex neighborhoods, curvature tensor, Ricci and scalar curvature, connections and curvature on vector bundles.
240A.prereq_text: MAT 201A; MAT 239; MAT 250A & MAT 250B highly recommended; intended primarily for second-year graduate students.

250A.title: Algebra
250A.description: Group and rings. Sylow theorems, abelian groups, Jordan-Holder theorem. Rings, unique factorization. Algebras, and modules. Fields and vector spaces over fields. Field extensions. Commutative rings. Representation theory and its applications.
250A.prereq_text: Graduate standing in mathematics or consent of instructor.

267.title: Quantum Information Theory
267.description: Axioms of quantum information, quantum states and observables, Bell non-locality, quantum channels, quantum entropy, quantum error correction, quantum circuits, examples of quantum algorithms
267.prereq_text: MAT 201B or MAT 250B; or consent of instructor.

280.title: Topics in Pure & Applied Mathematics
280.description: Special topics in various fields of pure and applied mathematics. Topics selected based on the mutual interests of students and faculty.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Advanced study in various fields of mathematics, including analysis, applied mathematics, discrete mathematics, geometry, mathematical biology, mathematical physics, optimization, partial differential equations, probability, and topology.

399.title: Individual Study
399.description: Individual study of some aspect of mathematics education or a focused work on a curriculum design project under supervision of a faculty member in mathematics.

217.title: Combustion
217.description: Review of chemical thermodynamics and chemical kinetics. Discussion of reacting flows, their governing equations and transport phenomena; detonations; laminar flame structure and turbulent combustion.

222.title: Advanced Dynamics
222.description: Dynamics of particles, rigid bodies and distributed systems with engineering applications; generalized coordinates; Hamilton's principle; Lagrange's equations; Hamilton-Jacobi theory; modal dynamics orthogonality; wave dynamics; dispersion.

239.title: Advanced Finite Elements & Optimization
239.description: Introduction to advanced finite elements and design optimization methods, with application to modeling of complex mechanical, aerospace and biomedical systems. Application of states of the art in finite elements in optimum design of components under realistic loading conditions and constraints.

271.title: Advanced Modeling & Simulation of Mechatronic Systems
271.description: Multiport models of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and thermal devices; bond graphs, block diagrams and state space equations; modeling of multiple energy domain systems; three-dimensional mechanics; digital simulation laboratory.

272.title: Theory & Design of Control Systems
272.description: Mathematical representations of linear dynamical systems. Feedback principles; benefits and cost of feedback. Analysis and design of control systems based on classical and modern approaches, with emphasis on applications to mechanical and aeronautical systems.

297.title: SEMINAR
297.description: Current topics in engineering including developments in mechanical and aeronautical engineering with presentations by students, faculty, and visitors.

050.title: Manufacturing Processes
050.description: Modern manufacturing methods, safety, manufacturing instructions, computer-aided manufacturing and their role in the engineering design and development process.
050.prereq_text: ENG 004 C- or better; PHY 009A C- or better.

092.title: Internship in Mechanical Engineering
092.description: Supervised work-study experience in engineering.
092.prereq_text: Lower division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing.

106.title: Thermo-Fluid Dynamics
106.description: Inviscid incompressible flow, compressible flow, ideal gas mixtures, psychrometrics, reacting mixtures and combustion.
106.prereq_text: ENG 103 C- or better; ENG 105 C- or better.

108.title: Measurement Systems
108.description: Experiments to illustrate principles of mechanical systems. Signal analysis; demonstration of basic sensors for mechanical systems; experimental project design; experiments involving voltage measurement; strain gauges, dynamic systems of 1st order.
108.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have previously taken BIM 111; 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken EBS 165; 1 unit of credit allowed for students who have completed EME 107B (former version of EME 108).
108.prereq_text: ENG 100 C- or better; ENG 102 C- or better; ENG 104 recommended.

109.title: Experimental Methods for Thermal Fluids
109.description: Experiments illustrating principles of thermal-fluid systems and related measurement devices. Statistical design of experiments and uncertainty analysis of data; thermodynamic cycles, combustion, compressible and incompressible flows.
109.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECH 155A; 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECH 155B; 3 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECI 141L; 1 unit of credit for students who have already completed EME 107A (former version of EME 109).

154.title: Mechatronics
154.description: Overview of mechatronics system and control system design concepts, control software architecture, control hardware architecture, microcontroller and interface technology for mechatronics control, sensor for mechatronics systems, actuator drives.
154.prereq_text: ENG 100 C- or better; ENG 102 C- or better; EME 050 C- or better.

164.title: Introduction to Heating, Ventilation & Air Conditioning Systems
164.description: Introduction to basic mechanisms and processes associated with heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), including equipment and systems used for HVAC in residential and commercial buildings.
164.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units for students who have completed ECI 125.
164.prereq_text: EME 106 C- or better; EME 165 C- or better.

165.title: Heat Transfer
165.description: Conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. Computational modeling of heat transfer in engineering. Applications to engineering equipment with the use of digital computers.
165.prereq_text: (ENG 006 C- or better or EME 005 C- or better or ECS 030 C- or better); ENG 103 C- or better; ENG 105 C- or better.

171.title: Analysis, Simulation & Design of Mechatronic Systems
171.description: Modeling of dynamic engineering systems in various energy domains. Analysis and design of dynamic systems. Response of linear systems. Digital computer simulation and physical experiments.
171.prereq_text: ENG 100 C- or better; ENG 102 C- or better.

172.title: Automatic Control of Engineering Systems
172.description: Classical feedback control systems; block diagrams; performance specifications; steady state errors; rise and settling times; root locus; PID controllers; Bode and Nyquist plots; stability; phase and gain margins; advanced topics as time allows.
172.prereq_text: ENG 100 C- or better; ENG 102 C- or better.

185A.title: Mechanical Engineering Systems Design Project
185A.description: Major mechanical engineering design experience; the mechanical engineering design process and its use in the design of engineering systems incorporating appropriate engineering standards and multiple realistic constraints.
185A.prereq_text: EME 050 C- or better; EME 150A C- or better; EME 165 C- or better (can be concurrent); ENG 003, CMN 001 or CMN 003 recommended; upper division composition recommended.

192.title: Internship in Engineering
192.description: Supervised work experience in mechanical engineering.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

402.title: Advanced Product Development
402.description: Concept selection, design, prototype manufacturing, initial testing, iteration, and product and process verification and validation activities.  Reducing risk throughout the product development stages. US and OUS regulatory options and the design of clinical trials including treatment groups, control groups, and sample sizes.

412.title: Business Leadership for Engineers II
412.description: Managing innovative enterprise in changing and uncertain environments. Technology forecasting and assessment, program selection and control, financial management, regulation, and ethics. Strategic management of organizations, including analysis of industries, firm resources and capabilities and corporate strategy. Strategy formulation, implementation and strategic decision-making. Firm and industry life cycles and change.

422.title: Engineering Skills II: Electronics, Microcontrollers, & Coding
422.description: Electronic circuit design, analysis, and prototyping. Programming of commonly used microcontrollers or single board computers (SBCs) for use in medical device applications. Artificial intelligence and machine learning in the medical device and healthcare industries. CAD tools and PCB prototyping to realize simple designs.
422.prereq_text: MDD 421; introductory course on engineering circuits or electronics required; introduction to coding recommended (Python preferred)

432.title: Capstone Project II: Product Concept Development
432.description: Teams apply product development, business leadership and engineering content to propose, implement, and verify a concept solution for their capstone project. Application of business and engineering principles and design theory to deliver initial prototypes that could meet client needs under operational constraints.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Group Study in Medical Microbiology and Immunology; primarily for lower division students. Directed reading and discussion on selected topics.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

177.title: Human Virology
177.description: Covers viruses that cause diseases in humans, the structure and classification of medically-important viruses, methods of transmission and replication strategies. Viruses that are important human pathogens and epidemiology, immune response, detection, diagnosis and treatment of human viral infections. Discussion of clinical cases, cellular pathology, cancer and emerging and reemerging human viral diseases including Coronaviruses, vaccines, antivirals, and use of viruses in medicine.
177.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 101 or BIS 101V or BIS 103 or BIS 104 or BIS 105.

192.title: Internship in Medical Microbiology
192.description: Supervised work experience in medical microbiology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

194H.title: Senior Honors Project in Medical Microbiology & Immunology
194H.description: Project in research related to immunology of medically important viruses. Development of a hypothesis-driven project, performance of experimental protocols and preparation of graphical representation of original data. Requires oral and written presentation of research results.

198.title: Group Study in Medical Microbiology
198.description: Directed reading and discussion and/or laboratory investigation on selected topics.
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Research in Medical Microbiology
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing.

200D.title: Mechanisms for Microbial Interactions with Hosts
200D.description:
Study of mechanisms involved in microbial interactions within a host
environment. The following principles are basic to understanding these interactions: host recognition, invasion, competition and growth, and host defense.

210A.title: Critical Analysis of Contemporary Research on Animal Models of Human Infectious Disease
210A.description: Topics will include diverse vertebrate and invertebrate models of human infectious diseases.
210A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; students funded by the Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Training Grant.

291.title: Seminar in Microbiology & Immunology
291.description: Research seminars on current topics in microbiology and immunology.

298.title: Group Study in Medical Microbiology & Immunology
298.description: Directed reading and discussion and/or laboratory investigation on selected topics. Sections 1, 2, 4, 5 are S/U grading only.
298.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to graduate students.

299.title: Research
299.description: Laboratory investigation contributing to the dissertation for a graduate degree.
299.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to graduate students.

497T.title: Tutoring in Medical Microbiology
497T.description: Assist instructor by tutoring medical students in one of the departmental courses that is a component of the required curriculum of the School of Medicine.
497T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; appropriate preparation in subject matter.

498.title: Group Study in Medical Microbiology & Immunology
498.description: Directed reading and discussion and/or laboratory investigation on selected topics.
498.prereq_text: Medical students with consent of instructor.

499.title: Research
499.prereq_text: Medical students with consent of instructor.

092.title: Internship in Pharmacology
092.description: Supervised work experience in pharmacology and related fields.
092.prereq_text: Lower division student with good academic standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

192.title: Internship in Pharmacology
192.description: Supervised work experience in pharmacology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

205.title: Problem Solving in Pharmacology
205.description: Introduction to a current biomedical problem that would benefit from a developing drug and will develop an experimental strategy for addressing the issue. Develop model systems for testing various classic and recent pharmacological approaches.

207.title: Drug Discovery & Development
207.description: Survey of the process by which a drug is discovered, developed and made available to the public. Topics include drug identification and optimization, safety testing, clinical evaluation, regulatory issues, intellectual property, formulation, and the global pharmaceutical industry.
207.prereq_text: An equivalent course in general pharmacology, or knowledge of basic pharmacology.

099.title: Special Study in Medicine for Undergraduates
099.description: Participate in research projects relating to medicine with faculty in the School of Medicine.

192.title: Medical Education Internship for Advanced Undergraduates
192.description:
Participate in projects related to curriculum development in support of curriculum for M.D. degree. Gain work experience and appreciation
for innovative approaches to learning in basic and clinical sciences of medical education.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; competency with computers.

416.title: ACE-PC Advanced Clinical Skills
416.description: Longitudinal clinic component of the second year of the ACE-PC Program. Start with a four-week immersion experience and then 12 additional half-days over the course of the year, working one-on-one with a primary care preceptor.

442.title: Enhancing Quality Improvement & Patient Safety ASC
442.description: Participate in a project contributing to healthcare improvement by partnering with a faculty member to identify, design, implement, and evaluate a quality improvement/patient safety initiative or synthesizing and interpreting existing evidence in quality improvement/patient safety by preparing a narrative review of the literature, commentary, or perspective paper. Share work at the UC Davis Health Quality Forum, or as a publication.

443.title: Global Health ASC
443.description: Aimed at furthering student experience with global health. An important step toward addressing global health is to drive learning toward consistent One Health core competencies in medical education and other health sciences.

446.title: Medical Education ASC
446.description: Acquire advanced knowledge in Medical Education through understanding of psychological safety, and effective learning and teaching strategies.

447.title: Health Policy & Advocacy ASC
447.description: Develop, implement, and evaluate a scholarly project contributing to Health Policy & Advocacy under the guidance of faculty knowledgeable in the field

448.title: Research ASC
448.description: Acquire advanced knowledge in research methodology and be able to demonstrate advanced knowledge in research methodology. Culminates in the creation of a manuscript for publication based on research under the guidance of faculty knowledgeable in the field.

468C.title: International Clinical Preceptorship
468C.description: Multidisciplinary preceptorship in a foreign country. Clinical credit will be awarded using this course, once approval has been received from the appropriate governing committee.

474.title: Cardiovascular, Pulmonary, & Renal Systems
474.description: Fourth course of the pre-clerkship phase curriculum of the I-EXPLORE. Runs 19 weeks from January-May.

479.title: Clerkship Intersession Course
479.description: Longitudinal experience to supplement and support the clerkships in their efforts to facilitate students’ acquisition of the graduation competencies; to ensure biomedical science and health systems science are taught and learned in the context of the clinical science-focused clerkship year; to support students’ professional identity formation and wellness, and provide time for enrichment activities and scholarly work.

488.title: Community Health Scholars ASC
488.description: Regularly present work-in-progress and receive peer and faculty feedback throughout medical school, with a final capstone project presentation at the end of their fourth year prior to graduation. Submit a final written summary of their project and outcomes prior to graduation.

490.title: Reimagining Education to Advance Central California Health (REACH) Selective
490.description: Third-year REACH students participate in the clinical care of patients at Kaiser Central Valley and associated partners in Central California within specialties of internal medicine, family medicine, pediatrics, surgery, or obstetrics/gynecology. Rotate through outpatient clinics, inpatient wards, and consult services, and may be introduced organizations that provide health education, patient navigation services, and other resources who care for the same people.

491.title: TEACH-MS Pediatric Advocacy & Community Health Elective
491.description: Through this elective, third- or fourth- year students gain understanding in the importance of community partnerships by directly engaging with community organizations that provide health education, patient navigation services, and other resources that they may refer their patients to. Students who complete this elective will develop key skills necessary for educating the public and lobbying key decision-makers in government.

495.title: Medicine Literature Review
495.description: Independent study: topics for selection include, but are not restricted to, medical ethics, economics and jurisprudence, culture and medicine, ethnicity and medicine, gender and medicine, history of medicine, health manpower, and medical education. A prepared paper on the selected topic will be required.
495.prereq_text: Medical student in good academic standing and permission of the Associate Dean of Curricular Affairs.

496.title: California Oregon Medical Partnership to Address Disparities in Rural Education & Health (COMPADRE) Elective
496.description: Third- or fourth-year students enrolled in COMPADRE participate in the clinical care of patients from rural, underserved, or indigenous communities. Students may rotate through outpatient clinics, inpatient wards, and consult services, and may also be introduced to local community organizations that provide health education, patient navigation services, and other resources that they may refer their patients to.

158.title: Infectious Disease in Ecology & Conservation
158.description: Introduction to the dynamics and control of infectious disease in wildlife, including zoonotic diseases and those threatening endangered species. Basic epidemiological models and application to field data. Scientists' role in developing disease control policies.

190.title: Senior Thesis
190.description: Preparation of a research paper dealing with a selected aspect of remodern (from Late Antique to Early Modern) culture, under supervision with a designated Supervisor and second reader.
190.prereq_text: Senior standing and major in Medieval & Early Modern Studies.

197T.title: Tutoring in Medieval Studies
197T.description: Tutoring in MST 020A & MST 020B, including leadership in small discussion groups affiliated with the course.
197T.prereq_text: MST 020A; MST 020B; upper division standing; consent of instructor and chairperson of curriculum committee.

091.title: Introduction to Research
091.description: Discussion of faculty research focusing on the biochemistry, genetics, and cell biology of microorganisms, along with ways undergraduates can participate in research projects of faculty members.

102.title: Introductory Microbiology
102.description: Essentials of microbial biology, emphasizing phylogeny, physiology, genetics, ecology, and pathogenesis. Interactions with other microbes, humans, and the biosphere. Uses of microbes in agriculture and biotechnology. May be taught abroad.
102.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MIC 101, MIC 102, or MIC 104.
102.prereq_text: (BIS 001A or BIS 002A or BIO 002); CHE 002B (can be concurrent).

103L.title: Introductory Microbiology Laboratory
103L.description: Introduction to principles and laboratory methods employed in working with microorganisms. Designed for students requiring microbiology for professional school admission. May be taught abroad.
103L.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who completed MIC 101 before spring 2016, or who have completed MIC 102L, or MIC 104L.
103L.prereq_text: (MIC 102 C- or better or MMG 102 C- or better (can be concurrent) or MMG 102V C- or better (can be concurrent)); CHE 002B.

107L.title: General Microbiology Laboratory
107L.description: Principles and laboratory methods employed in working with microorganisms. Designed for students continuing in microbiology, genetics, or biochemistry.
107L.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who completed MIC 101 before spring 2016, or who have completed MIC 103L or MMG 103L; not open to students who have completed MIC 102L or MIC 104L.
107L.prereq_text: (MIC 102 C- or better (can be concurrent) or MMG 102 C- or better (can be concurrent)); (CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 129A); consent of instructor.

162.title: General Virology
162.description: Integrated presentation of the nature of animal, bacterial, and plant viruses, including their structure, replication and genetics.
162.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have taken PMI 128 or MMI 177; no credit if student has taken MIC 162.
162.prereq_text: (BIS 101 C- or better or BIS 101V C- or better); BIS 102 or BIS 105 recommended.

180.title: Microbial Diversity
180.description: Survey of the major groups of microorganisms emphasizing diversity of energy metabolism, morphology, evolution, and natural history.
180.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MIC 105.
180.prereq_text: (MIC 102 or MMG 102); (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); BIS 103 or BIS 105 strongly recommended.

181L.title: Microbial Diversity Laboratory
181L.description: Classical enrichments for the isolation of metabolically diverse microbes; modern molecular methods for the identification of isolates; cultivation independent analysis of microbial communities from local environmental samples.
181L.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MIC 105L.
181L.prereq_text: (MIC 102 or MIC 104 or MMG 102); (MIC 102L or MIC 104L or MMG 107L); (MIC 105 or MMG 180 (can be concurrent)).

190C.title: Undergraduates Research Conference
190C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of staff research activities; designed for advanced undergraduate students.
190C.prereq_text: MIC 199 (required concurrently) or MMG 199 (required concurrently); and consent of instructor; upper division standing.

191.title: Introduction to Research for Advanced Undergraduates
191.description: Discussion of faculty research focusing on the biochemistry, genetics, and cell biology of microorganisms, along with ways undergraduates can participate in research projects of faculty members.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Technical and/or professional experience on or off campus. Supervised by a member of the Department of Microbiology & Molecular Genetics faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Microbiology
197T.description: Assist instructor in one of the section's regular courses by tutoring individual or small groups of students in a laboratory, in voluntary discussion groups, or other voluntary course activities.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

291.title: Selected Topics in Microbiology
291.description: Current progress in microbiology and cellular and molecular biology.

201L.title: Advanced Microbiology Laboratory Rotations
201L.description: Two five-week assignments in microbiology research laboratories. Individual research problems with emphasis on methodological/procedural experience and experimental design.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of staff research activities. Designed for advanced graduate students.
290C.prereq_text: Graduate standing and/or consent of instructor.

299.title: Research
299.description: Research under the guidance of dissertation committee.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation and critical discussion of staff research activities. Designed for advanced graduate students.
290C.prereq_text: Graduate standing and/or consent of instructor.

002Y.title: World Coffee Cultures
002Y.description: Coffee cultural traditions and practices from around the world. Historical perspectives and analysis of future trends. Corresponding experiments testing distinct cultural influences on the sensory qualities and nutritional aspects of coffee beverages.

100.title: Middle East & South Asia: Comparative Perspectives
100.description: Ethnographic and historical points of intersection and divergence in various aspects of the Middle East and South Asia in precolonial, colonial, and postcolonial societies.  Anthropological, historical, and theoretical debates surrounding the region.

121C.title: A Story for a Life: The Arabian Nights
121C.description: In-depth exploration of The Arabian Nights, the best-known work of pre-modern Arabic literature and a major work of world literature. Analysis of the work in its historical context and in comparison to other frame tales in world literature.

151A.title: Iranian Society & Culture
151A.description: In-depth investigation of modern Iranian society and culture. Exploration of structures of Iranian society: family, gender, religion, minorities, economy, politics, and state. Iran’s role in the globalizing world, and the role of Iranian diasporas.

181B.title: Topics in Regional ME/SA Studies
181B.description: Indian/South Asia topics for students specializing in region-specific Middle East & South Asia Studies.

012.title: Introduction to Tactical Military Leadership
012.description: Military leadership fundamentals to include setting direction, problem-solving, presenting briefs, and using effective writing skills. Basic military tactics, orienteering and land navigation. Dimensions of leadership values, attributes, skills, and actions.

014B.title: Introduction to Military Leadership Skills
014B.description: Continuation of development of leadership and military skills introduced in MSC 014A. Emphasis on the role of the individual, the basic organizational element of the Army, the squad. Supervisory controls reduced as students gain capabilities.
014B.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

022B.title: Foundations of Tactical Leadership
022B.description: Leadership of tactical teams in complex operating environment. Self-assessment of leadership style. Basic military skills: terrain analysis, patrolling and operations orders. Dynamics of adaptive leadership in the context of military operations.

024B.title: Individual Military Leadership Skills
024B.description: Development and practice of personal military leadership skills in extensive supervised leadership labs. Performance of basic military skills, improvement on troop-leading procedures, leadership of subordinates in tactical situations.
024B.prereq_text: MSC 014A; MSC 014B; MSC 014C; MSC 022B (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor. MSC 022B required concurrently.

132B.title: Applied Leadership
132B.description: Military small unit tactical theory and application as basis for leadership development.  Application of leadership styles and skills to complete problem-solving exercises and the development of an adaptable framework applicable to a variety of shifting environments and situations.
132B.prereq_text: MSC 132A; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

134B.title: Adaptive Tactical Leadership
134B.description: Small unit tactical operations as the basis for enhancement of leadership performance through tactical application.  Assessment of leadership attributes, skills, and actions through participation in a variety of leadership roles in problem-solving exercises.
134B.prereq_text: MSC 132A; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

142.title: Military Law
142.description: The United States Constitution and the Military Justice System. Basic law of war, with an emphasis on issues that might arise on the battlefield or during a national emergency.
142.prereq_text: MSC 141; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

144B.title: Military Training Leadership Skills
144B.description: Enhancement of student leadership performance through practical application.  Small unit military tactical operations serve as the basis for student exploration and development.
144B.prereq_text: MSC 142; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

010.title: Introduction to Human Heredity
010.description: Topics in human heredity and human gene structure and function, including the genetic basis of human development, causes of birth defects, mental retardation, genetic diseases, sexual determination, development, and behavior.

120.title: Molecular Biology & Biochemistry Laboratory Associated Lecture
120.description: Introduction to laboratory methods and procedures employed in studying molecular biology and biochemical processes. Lecture component for MCB 120L.
120.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; or consent of instructor.

120L.title: Molecular Biology & Biochemistry Laboratory
120L.description: Introduction to laboratory methods and procedures employed in studying molecular biology and biochemical processes. Designed for students who need experience in use of molecular biology and biochemical techniques as research and analytical tools.
120L.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; or consent of instructor; must be taken concurrently with MCB 120.

121.title: Advanced Molecular Biology
121.description: Structure, expression, and regulation of eukaryotic genes. Chromosome structure and replication; gene structure, transcription, and RNA processing; protein synthesis and translation control; development, immune system, and oncogenes.
121.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MCB 161.
121.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 (can be concurrent) or BIS 102V (can be concurrent) or BIS 105 (can be concurrent) or ABI 102 (can be concurrent)); BIS 102 or BIS 105 or ABI 102 can be concurrent, although prior completion is recommended.

123.title: Behavior & Analysis of Enzyme & Receptor Systems
123.description: Introduction to the principles of enzyme kinetics and receptor-ligand interactions with emphasis on metabolic regulation and data analysis. Topics include simultaneous equilibria, chemical and steady-state kinetics, allosteric enzymes, mulitreactant systems, enzyme assays, membrane transport and computer-assisted simulations and analyses.

126.title: Plant Biochemistry
126.description: The biochemistry of important plant processes and metabolic pathways. Discussion of methods used to understand plant processes, including use of transgenic plants.

140L.title: Cell Biology Laboratory
140L.description: Exercises illustrating the principles of cell biology with emphasis on light microscopy.

148.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Cell Biology
148.description: Student reports on current topics in cell biology with emphasis on integration of concepts, synthesis, and state-of-the-art research approaches. Reviews of literature and reports of undergraduate research may be included.
148.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 105).

150.title: Developmental Biology
150.description: Analysis of the mechanistic basis for animal development with a focus on experimental evidence and the relevant fundamental experimental strategies. Fertilization and early development, morphogenesis and patterning, cell differentiation, regulation of cell proliferation and tissue growth.

160L.title: Principles of Genetics Laboratory
160L.description: Laboratory work in basic and molecular genetics including gene mapping, isolation and characterization of mutants in eukaryotic model systems, reverse genetics, gel electrophoresis, recombinant DNA techniques, and PCR.

162.title: Human Genetics & Genomics
162.description:
Human genome and genetic variation in human populations, molecular and genomic approaches in the practice of human genetics, epigenetic gene regulation, personal genetics and genomic medicine.

BIS 101V added to prereqs effective 202501. 9/13/24 DV

185.title: Computer Programming for Biologists
185.description: Introduction to computer programming specifically for biology majors. Programming projects have molecular biology and bioinformatic themes.
185.credit_limit_text: Only two units of credit for students who have previously taken ECS 012 or ECS 032A or ECS 032AV or ENG 006.
185.prereq_text: BIS 101 C- or better or BIS 101V C- or better.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Technical and/or practical experience on and off campus, supervised by a member of the Section of Molecular and Cellular Biology faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

193.title: Advanced Research
193.description: Research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty sponsor. Discussion and analysis of results and proposed experiments on a weekly basis with faculty sponsor. May include presentation of a seminar to a research group.
193.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; completion of an upper division Molecular & Cellular Biology (MCB) laboratory course.

194H.title: Research Honors
194H.description: Honors project. Continuation of an intensive, individual laboratory research project in biochemistry, genetics, or cell biology culminating with the presentation of the work in a written thesis and in a seminar.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; 6 units of MCB 193 and/or MCB 199 with faculty director; senior standing; GPA of at least 3.250.

197T.title: Tutoring in Molecular & Cellular Biology
197T.description: Assisting the instructor in one of the section's regular courses by tutoring individual or small groups of students in a laboratory, in voluntary discussion groups, or other voluntary course activities. May be taught abroad.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing, completion of course to be tutored.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Presentations and critical discussions of faculty and graduate student research in molecular and cellular biology including biochemistry, genetics, and cell biology.

291.title: Current Progress in Molecular & Cellular Biology
291.description: Seminars presented by guest lecturers on subject of their own research activities.
291.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

390.title: Methods of Teaching
390.description:
Practical experience in the methods and problems of teaching biochemistry/genetics/cell biology. Includes analysis of texts and
supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques, preparing for and conducting discussion and laboratory sections, formulating examinations under supervision of instructor. Participating in the teaching program required for Ph.D.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Molecular Biosciences.  Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered by the Department of Molecular Biosciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

220.title: Oxidative Stress & Free Radical Signaling
220.description: Nature of nitrogen and oxygen radicals, their role in health, disease, medicine, toxicology, pharmacology, and related disciplines. Free radicals, antioxidants, and biological pathways. Clinical cases of increased oxidative stress.
220.prereq_text: Advanced undergraduates, graduates, and professional students with a solid background in biochemistry and physiology.

253.title: Metabolism of Toxicants & Drugs
253.description: Significance/chemical pathways of toxicants and drug metabolism, enzymology and molecular aspects of P450 and flavin monooxygenases, hydrolases and phase 2 transferases and experimental approaches for metabolism studies.
253.prereq_text: PTX 201; PTX 202; PTX 203; general biochemistry or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Topics in nutrition, pharmacology/toxicology, and biochemistry.

297T.title: Tutoring in Graduate Molecular Biosciences
297T.description: Assist in preparation and teaching of courses in Nutrition, Pharmacology and Toxicology, or other courses offered by the department under direct supervision of the instructor. Designed for graduate or professional students who desire teaching experience in graduate courses.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate or professional student standing.

397T.title: Tutoring in Molecular Biosciences
397T.description: Experience in professional curriculum for graduate or professional students, not teaching assistants, under direct supervision of instructor.
397T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate or professional student standing.

210B.title: Advanced Physiology
210B.description: Advanced course in general principles of physiology, surveying homeostasis, cellular and selected topics, and neurophysiology.
210B.prereq_text: Physiology Ph.D. program, or consent of instructor.

211B.title: Animal Models in Physiology Research
211B.description: Use of animal models in research, types of models available, selection criteria and limitations, alternative approaches. Principles of basic and systemic physiology. Student presentations promote critical independent thinking, public speaking skills, conception of a scientific hypothesis, and scientific rigor in developed experimental plans.

261B.title: Topics in Vision: Systems, Psychophysics, Computational Models
261B.description: Functions of the central visual pathways and their underlying mechanisms. Recent research on aspects of anatomy, biochemistry, electrophysiology, psychophysics, development, and genetics of the visual system.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Discussion and critical evaluation of advanced topics and current trends in research.

390.title: The Teaching of Physiology
390.description: Practical experience in methods and problems of teaching physiology lecture courses. May include analyses of texts and supporting material, discussion of teaching techniques, preparing for and conducting discussion sessions, and formulation of topics and questions for examinations under supervision of instructor.
390.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; Teaching Assistant assignment to a physiology lecture course.

002A.title: Keyboard Competence, Part 1
002A.description: Training to meet the minimum piano requirements for the major in music. Scales and simple harmonic progressions in twelve keys, both major and minor.

002B.title: Keyboard Competence, Part 2
002B.description: Training to meet the minimum piano requirements for the major in music. Harmonic progressions, modulations and score reading at the piano.
002B.prereq_text: MUS 002A; consent of instructor; completion of MUS 002A or demonstration of required keyboard proficiency level on diagnostic exam.

003A.title: Introduction to Music Theory, Part 1
003A.description: Fundamentals of music theory, ear-training, harmony, counterpoint, and analysis directed toward the development of listening and writing techniques. Intended for the general student.

006A.title: Elementary Theory, Part 1
006A.description: Development of music writing and listening skills through the study of music fundamentals, species counterpoint, harmony, analysis of repertory. Intended primarily for music majors.

007B.title: Intermediate Theory, Part 2
007B.description: Harmony and voice of the 19th century leading through the music of the Romantic era. Focus on analysis of music by Chopin, Schumann, Brahms, Wagner, and Wolf. Composition of character pieces and songs. Intended for Music majors.

011.title: Musics of the World
011.description: Survey of selected art, folk, and popular music cultures from different parts of the world. Emphasis on understanding relationship of musical style, aesthetic principles, and performance practice to wider cultural contexts.

016A.title: Elementary Musicianship, Part 1
016A.description: Melodic, rhythmic, and harmonic materials of Western music. Includes sight singing, explanations, drills, melodic/rhythmic/harmonic dictations, and listening analysis.

017B.title: Intermediate Musicianship, Part 2
017B.description: Melodic, rhythmic, and harmonic materials of Western music. Includes sight singing, explanations, drills, melodic/rhythmic/harmonic dictations, and listening analysis.
017B.prereq_text: MUS 017A; (MUS 007B (can be concurrent); MUS 007B required concurrently. Completion of MUS 017A or demonstration of required proficiency level on diagnostic exam.

024A.title: History of Western Music: Baroque & Classic Eras
024A.description: History of western music in the baroque and classic eras, roughly 1600-1800. Intended primarily for majors in music.

028.title: Introduction to African American Music
028.description: Survey of African American music, such as spirituals, blues, ragtime, jazz, theater, gospel, R&B, rap, and art music. Emphasis on historical and sociocultural contexts, as well as African roots.

101B.title: Advanced Theory, Part 2
101B.description: Music from 1950 to the present and the analytical tools pertaining to it. Works of Babbit, Carter, Dallapiccola, Ligeti, Messiaen, Reich and others. Composition of small pieces for ensemble.

103.title: Workshop in Composition
103.description: Workshop in musical composition for undergraduates who are interested in pursuing serious compositional studies and intending to follow the composition track of the major. Explores the techniques and materials of musical composition.

105.title: History & Analysis of Jazz
105.description: Jazz and the evolution of jazz styles in historical and cultural context. For non-majors.
105.prereq_text: MUS 003A or MUS 006A or MUS 010 or MUS 010V or MUS 011 or MUS 011V or MUS 028; or consent of instructor.

107C.title: Computer Music
107C.description: Making electronic music in an open source programming environment. Intermediate synthesis, physical controllers, and algorithmic music. Overview of history, aesthetics, and techniques of digital sonic art. Three composition projects.

113.title: Introduction to Conducting
113.description: Principles and techniques of conducting as they apply to both choral and instrumental ensembles.

117.title: The Broadway Musical
117.description: Exploration of a variety of Broadway and film musicals from different time periods, and how musicals reflect and help create social reality, and the different aspects of the creative process as manifested through music, dance, scenery, and acting.

124C.title: History of Western Music: 20th Century to the Present
124C.description: History of Western Music from 1900 to the present. Intended primarily for music majors.

131A.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual)
131A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131C.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Harpsichord
131C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131E.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Violin
131E.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131F.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Viola
131F.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to Music majors only; admission by audition.

131G.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Cello
131G.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131H.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Double Bass
131H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131I.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Flute
131I.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131J.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Oboe
131J.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131K.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Clarinet
131K.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131L.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Bassoon
131L.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131M.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); French Horn
131M.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131N.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Trumpet
131N.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131P.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Tuba
131P.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131Q.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Percussion
131Q.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131R.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Classical Guitar
131R.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

131U.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Saxophone

131W.title: Applied Study of Music: Advanced (Individual); Harp
131W.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admitted by audition.

135.title: Recital Preparatory Practice
135.description: Practice and preparation for recital performances. Introduction to techniques for managing performance anxiety, working with accompanists, gaining experience performing on stage. Helps students gain practice and experience performing on the concert stage. Learn and perform different repertoire from one quarter to the next. Continually practice instrument, improving, and learning new pieces. Continue to learn each quarter to gain a deeper and more embodied understanding of music and performance.

140.title: University Jazz Band
140.description: Rehearsal, study, and performance of jazz band music and a full variety of jazz band styles, including swing, be-bob, and contemporary jazz styles.
140.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

141.title: University Symphony
