141.description: Open to any student in the University whose proficiency meets the requirements of concert performance. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of music from the orchestral literature.
141.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

142.title: University Chamber Singers
142.description: Rehearsal and performance of works for small choral group.
142.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

143.title: University Concert Band
143.description: Rehearsal and performance of music for band.
143.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

144.title: University Chorus
144.description: Rehearsal and performance of choral music.
144.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

146.title: Chamber Music Ensemble
146.description: Open to any student in the University whose proficiency meets the requirements of concert performance. Study, rehearsal, and performance of ensemble music for strings, winds, voice, piano, harpsichord, and organ.
146.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

148.title: Hindustani Vocal Ensemble
148.description: Basics of Hindustani music through theory and practice. Fundamentals of raga (mode) and tala (rhythms) with special emphasis on improvisation, a central feature of khyal (singing style). Five ragas each quarter.

149.title: Indonesian Gamelan Ensemble
149.description:
Indonesian music practice. Basic instrumental technique and repertory.
Focus on two styles of Sundanese gamelan (tuned percussion orchestras): 
salendro and degung.

152.title: Afro-Cuban Ensemble
152.description: Performance of African derived folkloric music of Cuba. Basic instrumental technique and repertory. Focus on percussion and song traditions from Havana, Matazas and Santiago, Cuba.

153.title: Brazilian Capoeira Ensemble
153.description: Basic instrumental techniques, songs, and dance movements of Capoeira Angola. Protocols of a Capoeira Angola performance and the meanings of Capoeira in Brazil with its connections to Afro-Brazilian culture.

155.title: Percussion Ensemble
155.description: Study and rehearsal of percussion chamber music from the 20th and 21st centuries. Study of standard and extended techniques for a broad range of percussion instruments. Public performance of significant works for percussion ensemble.
155.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; admission by audition.

156.title: Mariachi Ensemble
156.description: Rehearsal and performance of traditional and contemporary mariachi repertoire.

157.title: Bluegrass & Old Time String Band
157.description: Performance of bluegrass and Appalachian old time music. Practice of instrumental and vocal techniques and repertory in vernacular American string band idioms.

192.title: Internship in Music
192.description: Internship outside the university related to music.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor or academic advisor.

194HA.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HA.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of music.

194HB.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194HB.description: Preparation and presentation of a culminating project, under the supervision of an instructor, in one of the creative or scholarly areas of music.

195.title: Senior Project
195.description: Preparation of a senior project in music composition (public presentation of a new work), in music performance (a public recital), or in music history and theory (public presentation of research results).

203.title: Music Composition
203.description: Technical projects that explore compositional problems, the skill and techniques with which to solve them, and free composition.

221.title: Topics in Music History
221.description: Studies in selected areas of music history and theory.

222.title: Techniques of Analysis
222.description: Analysis and analytical techniques as applied to music of all historical style periods.

001.title: Introduction to Native American Studies
001.description: Introduction to Native American Studies with emphasis upon basic concepts relating to Native American historical and political development.

005.title: Introduction to Native American Literature
005.description: Focus on the development of writing skills through close readings and analysis of Native American literary texts, with scaffolded writing assignments to develop critical thinking and composition skills.
005.prereq_text: NAS 005A (can be concurrent) or UWP 001A (can be concurrent); or completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

005V.title: Introduction to Native American Literature
005V.description: Focus on the development of writing skills through close readings and analysis of Native American literary texts, with scaffolded writing assignments to develop critical thinking and composition skills.
005V.prereq_text: NAS 005A (can be concurrent) or UWP 001A (can be concurrent); or completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

010.title: Native American Experience
010.description: Introduction to the diverse cultures of Native American peoples from North, Central, and South America. Emphasis on Native American voices in the expression of cultural views and in the experience of conflicting values.

109.title: Native American Language Spotlight
109.description: In-depth examination of the history, structure, and sociolinguistics of a particular Native American language or language family. Different language studied each time the course is offered. Oral proficiency component included in some years.

110B.title: Quechua Language & Society: Beginning Level 2
110B.description: Second Level of the teaching of Quechua language and society.  Emphasis on development of conversational and reading skills.  Continuation of the study of aspects of contemporary Andean society and the status of Quechua language today.

161.title: California Indian Environmental Policy I
161.description: Contemporary California Indian environmental policy issues, with a focus on water, minerals, contamination, and alliance-building. Issues will be placed within historical and political context, drawing on theories of Native environmental ethics, environmental justice, and Federal Indian law.

165.title: Keepers of the Flame: Native American Cultural Burning & Land Stewardship in California
165.description: Use of fire by California Indian tribes to maintain ecosystems that sustain their economic, cultural, and spiritual well being. Guests include Native American cultural practitioners and prescribed fire professionals.
165.prereq_text: consent of instructor; course involves regular field days working with cultural burn practitioners.

175V.title: Hemispheric Indigenous Connections
175V.description: Indigenous worlds in motion in the Americas, 1491-present. Comparative Indigenous experiences of colonialism and neocolonialism, plus histories of resistance, cultural survival, and transnational grassroots organizing with an emphasis on environmental justice movements.

189.title: Powwow Internship
189.description: Supervised internship for the annual UC Davis Powwow.

191.title: Topics in Native American Studies
191.description: Selected topics in Native American Studies related to indigenous knowledges and worldviews from a historical, cultural, hemispheric perspective.

193.title: Leadership Training in Native American & Indigenous Organizations
193.description: Supervised leadership training in Native American department, campus, and community settings, including the Native American Academic Student Success Center (NAASSC; aka, the Native "Nest").

194HA.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of faculty advisor.

194HB.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HB.description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of faculty advisor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

208.title: Advanced Study of Native American Languages
208.description: Advanced study of Native American languages. Development of proficiency in a particular language in order to incorporate language into Native American Studies research and argumentation. Engagement with theoretical perspectives on social, cultural, and structural dimensions of language to guide language study.
208.prereq_text: NAS 107 or equivalent background with a Native American language.

224.title: Performance in the Americas
224.description: Ethnomusicological and anthropological approaches to study of public performance in the Americas. New ways of looking at music, dance, rituals and other forms of public expressive forms normally called "folklore" or "popular culture."
224.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MUS 224. (Former MUS 224.).

237.title: Native American Art Collections & Museums
237.description: Research and examination of regional Native American art held in museums and other public institutions, as well as privately-held collections. Includes onsite viewing and research of museum collections and archives.

246.title: Native American/Indigenous Research Methodologies
246.description: Introduction to advanced methodologies currently influencing research in Native American Studies and among Indigenous communities. Develop an original project and course assignments will guide them through the process of research design and implementation.

257.title: Indigenous Religious Traditions in the Americas
257.description: Religious/spiritual traditions, belief-systems, and world-views of Native American/indigenous peoples in the Americas.  Land, ecological knowledge, sacred sites, the role of tricksters, language (revitalization), gender, ethics of representation, cultural revitalization, renewed ancient knowledge and practices, ceremonial (and daily) performance of the sacred, music, the arts, the worlds of the sacred, the rules of the sacred, freedom of religion.

110.title: Introduction to Nematology
110.description: Relationship of nematodes to the human environment. Classification, morphology, ecology, distribution, and importance of nematodes occurring in water and soil as parasites of plants and animals.
110.prereq_text: BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L); or consent of instructor.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Planning and results of research programs, proposals, and experiments. Discussion and critical evaluation of original research being conducted by the group. Discussion led by individual research instructors for research group.
290C.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship in Nephrology
192.description: Supervised work experience in nephrology.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

010.title: Elementary Human Physiology
010.description: Introduction to physiology for non-science majors. Includes basic cell physiology and survey of major organ systems and how they function in homeostasis and human health.
010.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 101.

012.title: The Human Brain & Disease
012.description: Normal function and diseases of the human brain and nervous system. Diseases discussed include Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, leprosy, amnesia and schizophrenia. Intended for non-science majors.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed NPB 100, NPB 101, NPB 112, or PSC 121.

014.title: Illusions: Fooling the Brain
014.description: Introduction to perceptual processing in the human nervous system; illusions.

091C.title: Research Conference
091C.description: Research findings and methods in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
091C.prereq_text: NPB 099 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; lower division standing in Neurobiology, Physiology and Behavior or related biological science; NPB 099 required concurrently.

092.title: Internship
092.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
Department of Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing.

100.title: Neurobiology
100.description: Brains and nervous systems, neurons and neural circuits. Coordination of movement. Development of nervous systems. Vision, hearing, and feature extraction by the central nervous system. The cell biology of learning and memory. Perception, cognition, and disorders of the brain.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110B, NPB 112, NPB 160, NPB 161 or NPB 162, or NSC 221 or NSC 222.
100.prereq_text: BIS 002A; PHY 009A, PHY 009B or PHY 007A, PHY 007B recommended.

101.title: Systemic Physiology
101.description: Systemic physiology with emphasis on aspects of human physiology. Functions of major organ systems, with the structure of those systems described as a basis for understanding the functions.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110C.
101.prereq_text: (BIO 002 or BIS 002A); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH); or consent of instructor; PHY 001B or PHY 007C strongly recommended.

101L.title: Systemic Physiology Laboratory
101L.description: Selected experiments to illustrate functional characteristics of organ systems discussed in NPB 101.
101L.prereq_text: ANS 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C.

107.title: Cell Signaling in Health & Disease
107.description: Basics of cell signaling pathways, their disruption in disease, and their current utility and future potential as therapeutic targets. Focus is on signaling pathways specific to nervous, endocrine and immune systems, and those fundamental to all cells.

110A.title: Foundations 1: From Molecules to Individuals
110A.description: Major concepts in cell biology with special emphasis on connections between cell biology and behavior. Includes: cellular metabolism, cellular sensing and signaling, membrane structure-function, molecular switches, electrical and chemical signaling, endocrine signaling, cell cycle and differentiation, cytoskeleton, and integrative examples.
110A.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 3 units for students who have taken BIS 104.
110A.prereq_text: ((BIS 002A, BIS 002B) or (BIO 001, BIO 002)); (CHE 002B or CHE 003A); PHY 007A and PHY 007B recommended; BIS 002C recommended.

110B.title: Foundations 2: Neurobiology
110B.description: Core concepts of neurobiology including single-neuron biophysics, synapses and transmitters, neuronal development, motor systems, central pattern generation, neuronal circuits, intracellular signal transduction, sensory processing, multisensory integration, autonomic nervous system, neuromodulation, learning and memory, and higher cognition and disease.
110B.credit_limit_text: Credit limited to 2 units for students who have taken NPB 100.
110B.prereq_text: NPB 110A C- or better; PHY 007A and PHY 007B recommended.

110C.title: Foundations 3: Physiology
110C.description: Focuses on the structure, function, and interactions of human and other animal organ systems in homeostasis and reproduction, and the response to perturbations of homeostasis; neural and endocrine signaling; skeletal muscle and movement; cardiovascular and respiratory systems; renal, digestive, immune, and reproductive physiology.
110C.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units for students who have taken NPB 101.
110C.prereq_text: NPB 110A C- or better; PHY 007A; PHY 007B and PHY 007C recommended.

143.title: Neurobiology & Psychopharmacology of Mental Illness
143.description: Neurobiology and psychopharmacology of mental illness. Mechanisms and pharmacodynamics of psychotropic drugs used in the treatment of schizophrenia, mood disorders, anxiety, sleep disorders, and ADHD.
143.prereq_text: NPB 100 C- or better; or NPB 110B C- or better; or consent of instructor.

152.title: Hormones & Behavior
152.description: Endocrine physiology with an emphasis on the principles of behavior. Fundamental relationships between hormones and various behaviors engaged in by the organism during its lifetime. Role of hormones in behavioral homeostasis, social behavior, reproductive behavior, parental behavior, adaptation to stress.
152.prereq_text: (NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C); (NPB 102 or PSC 101).

154.title: Diabetes: Physiology & Management
154.description: Normal regulation of blood glucose contrasted with dysfunction in diabetes. Types of diabetes, physiological consequences of diabetes, as well as current and future medications and treatments.

168.title: Neurobiology of Addictive Drugs
168.description: Neurobiological basis for the effects and mechanisms of action of drugs with addictive potential, including opiates (morphine, heroin, methadone), amphetamines, cocaine, nicotine, marijuana (cannabinoids), alcohol, caffeine, and mind-altering drugs such as LSD and antidepressants.
168.prereq_text: NPB 100 or NPB 110B or NPB 110C or NPB 101 or NPB 101V; or equivalents.

190C.title: Research Conference
190C.description: Research findings and methods in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: NPB 199 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; upper division standing in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior or related biological science; NPB 199 required concurrently.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in neurobiology, physiology, & behavior.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194HA.title: Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior: Honors
194HA.description: Honors project in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Laboratory research on a specific question. Project is developed with the sponsoring faculty member and approved by the student’s Honors Thesis Committee. Honors thesis to be submitted upon completion of the project.
194HA.prereq_text: Senior standing; minimum 3.500 GPA in courses counted toward major; approval by the master advisor.

194HB.title: Neurobiology, Physiology & Behavior: Honors
194HB.description: Honors project in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Laboratory research on a specific question. Project is developed with the sponsoring faculty member and approved by the student’s Honors Thesis Committee. Honors thesis to be submitted upon completion of the project.
194HB.prereq_text: Senior standing; minimum 3.500 GPA in courses counted toward major; approval by the master advisor.

194HC.title: Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior: Honors
194HC.description: Honors project in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Laboratory research on a specific question. Project is developed with the sponsoring faculty member and approved by the student’s Honors Thesis Committee. Honors thesis to be submitted upon completion of the project.
194HC.prereq_text: Senior standing; minimum 3.500 GPA in courses counted toward major; approval by the master advisor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in one of the Department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

261B.title: Topics in Vision: Systems, Psychophysics, Computational Models
261B.description: Functions of the central visual pathways and their underlying mechanisms.  Recent research on aspects of anatomy, biochemistry, electrophysiology, psychophysics, development, and genetics of the visual system.

271B.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
271B.description: Core concepts and detailed survey methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity, from the cellular and molecular level to the level of neural circuits. Areas of learning, memory, and plasticity research where recent progress has been made in linking across these levels of analysis.

199.title: Individual Special Study & Research
199.description: Individual special study in neurophysiology and biomedical engineering is offered to qualified students. Studies on psychophysics, single-unit electrophysiology and instrumentation are offered in Davis.

450.title: Clinical Neurology Clerkship
450.description: Critical elements of neurological clinical skills (history & exam) and basic and clinical neurological concepts expected for general residency preparation. Active, didactic, experiential and independent learning to encourage maturation of general professional competencies.
450.prereq_text: Open to all fourth-year medical students; third-year medical students with consent of instructor.

452.title: Advanced Clinical Neurology
452.description: Teaches the principles and skills necessary to recognize and manage the neurologic diseases a general medical practitioner is most likely to encounter in practice. Gain clinical experience in both inpatient and outpatient settings, and learn how to interview patients and their caregivers to obtain a complete and reliable neurologic history and perform a reliable neurologic examination.
452.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of four-week Neurology selective.

455.title: Child Neurology
455.description: Exposure to children with disorders of the nervous system, both in outpatient and inpatient services. Cases presented to a member of full-time faculty who will discuss clinical findings, differential diagnosis, management and therapy. Satisfies fourth-year neuroscience requirement.
455.prereq_text: IMD 430; OBG 430; PED 430; consent of instructor.

499.title: Research
499.description: Approved for graduate degree credit. Laboratory investigation on selected topics.

200LB.title: Laboratory Methods in Neurobiology
200LB.description: Individual research in the laboratory of a faculty member. Research problems emphasize the use of contemporary methods and good experimental design.
200LB.prereq_text: Graduate standing in the Neuroscience Graduate Group.

201.title: Neuroanatomy
201.description: Mix of lectures, demonstrations, and dissections, emphasizing functional significance of neuroanatomy from a biological perspective, with comparisons between human and non-human brains. Emphasis placed on functional anatomy of the nervous system, integrated with cellular, molecular, cognitive, and developmental concepts.

219.title: Design to Data: Statistics for Modern Neuroscience
219.description: Statistical methods and applications for neuroscience. Quantitative foundations covering key concepts, methods, and applications, from descriptive analysis through data science. Statistical considerations in experimental design, analysis and statistical testing in hypothesis and data-driven contexts, and responsible conduct of research in the acquisition, storage, analysis, and presentation of scientific data.
219.prereq_text: Graduate student standing in neuroscience or related discipline or consent of instructor.

271B.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
271B.description: Core concepts and detailed survey methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity, from the cellular and molecular level to the level of neural circuits. Areas of learning, memory, and plasticity research where recent progress has been made in linking across these levels of analysis.

290C.title: Research Conference in Neurobiology
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate student research in neurobiology.
290C.prereq_text: NSC 299 required concurrently; graduate standing in Neuroscience or consent of instructor.

207BY.title: Intermediate Qualitative Research Methods in Nursing & Healthcare
207BY.description: Ways to frame qualitative research questions. Data to address important knowledge gaps in the health sciences. Interactive exercises for considering independent research.
207BY.prereq_text: NRS 207AY B- or better; or consent of instructor.

208BY.title: Logic & Scientific Inference
208BY.description: Concepts used in scientific research, critical thinking skills to examine the association between concepts and empirical evidence. Identifying new concepts that can be the analytic foundations of new research questions.

282EY.title: Clinical E
282EY.description: Advanced health assessment skills to manage common patient-reported problems or conditions. Integrating health maintenance and promotion along with assessment, diagnosis, and management of frequently encountered acute and chronic conditions in primary care. Varies by quarter to prepare family nurse practitioners (FNPs) to deliver primary care services to individuals and families and across the lifespan.
282EY.prereq_text: NRS 281DV C or better; NRS 282DY C or better; NRS 283DV C or better; or consent of instructor.

299.title: Research & Writing
299.description: Conduct research and writing under the supervision of a faculty member.

299D.title: Dissertation Research & Writing
299D.description: Conduct dissertation research and writing under the supervision of a faculty member.

307.title: Family Centered Communication & Shared Decision Making
307.description: Incorporates shared decision-making principles and group communication to address family centered care planning and challenging clinical discussions. Targets competencies needed by health professionals to partner effectively to enhance the caregiving experience and reduce negative sequelae over the caregiving trajectory.

323BV.title: Psychotherapeutic Interventions Across the Lifespan II
323BV.description: Group therapies, family systems, attachment and developmental approaches to psychotherapeutic intervention. Clinical case materials for assessment, engagement, and evaluation of psychotherapeutic interventions within the context of PMHNP practice.
323BV.prereq_text: NRS 323AV C+ or better; or consent of instructor.

415Y.title: PMHNP Clinical Residency
415Y.description: Integrate scientific knowledge and clinical practice to develop diagnostic, clinical decision-making, and direct care of individuals, groups, and families across the lifespan. Application/ integration of research, consultation, and clinical leadership as appropriate. Offered every quarter; course taken for four consecutive quarters to meet their clinical rotation requirement hours.

429B.title: Collaborative Practice B
429B.description: Series focuses on the art of nursing and collaborative practice. Each course in the series uses a variety of experiential learning activities to integrate and extend key concepts, applied through the lens of caring for a specific population.

010.title: Discoveries & Concepts in Nutrition
010.description: Nutrition as a science; historical development of nutrition concepts; properties of nutrients and foods.
010.credit_limit_text: No credit will be granted to students who have completed NUT 010Y or NUT 010V or an upper division Nutrition (NUT) course.

010V.title: Discoveries & Concepts in Nutrition
010V.description: Nutrition as a science; historical development of nutrition concepts; properties of nutrients and foods.
010V.credit_limit_text: No credit will be granted to students who have completed NUT 010 or NUT 010Y or an upper division Nutrition (NUT) course.

011.title: Current Topics & Controversies in Nutrition
011.description: Exploration of current applications and controversies in nutrition. Read scientific journal articles and write summaries, as well as give brief oral presentations. Topics change to reflect current interests and issues.

108.title: Metabolic Regulation &  Precision Nutrition
108.description: Role of metabolic transformations on the bioavailability and health effects of dietary and environmental compounds. Key metabolic pathways involved in the metabolism and health effects of dietary and environmental compounds. Contribution of individual variations in these pathways to diverse responses to diet and environmental exposures.
108.prereq_text: CHE 118B or CHE 128B or CHE 008B or ABI 102 or BIS 102 or BIS 102V; or consent of instructor.

111AY.title: Introduction to Nutrition & Metabolism
111AY.description: Introduction to metabolism of protein, fat and carbohydrate: the biological role of vitamins and minerals; nutrient requirements during the life cycle; assessment of dietary intake and nutritional status.
111AY.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed NUT 101 or NUT 111AV.
111AY.prereq_text: CHE 008B; NPB 101; or equivalent of NPB 101.

114.title: Developmental Nutrition
114.description: Role of nutritional factors in embryonic and postnatal development.
114.prereq_text: (ABI 102 or BIS 102 or BIS 102V); (ABI 103 or BIS 103); NUT 111AY; NUT 111B.

115.title: Animal Nutrition
115.description: Comparative differences among animals in digestion and metabolism of nutrients. Nutrient composition of feeds, digestive systems, digestion, absorption, feeding strategies.
115.prereq_text: CHE 008B or CHE 118B; or consent of instructor.

116BL.title: Clinical Nutrition Practicum
116BL.description: Fundamental principles of planning and evaluating therapeutic diets and patient education for pathological conditions covered in NUT 116B. Continuation of NUT 116AL.
116BL.prereq_text: NUT 116AL;(NUT 116B (can be concurrent) or NUT 116BY(can be concurrent)).

116BY.title: Clinical Nutrition
116BY.description: Biochemical and physiological bases for therapeutic diets. Problems in planning diets for normal and pathological conditions.
116BY.prereq_text: NUT 111AY; NUT 111B; NUT 112; NUT 116A; (NPB 101 or NPB 101V; or the equivalent to NPB 101).

118.title: Community Nutrition
118.description: Nutrition problems in contemporary communities and of selected target groups in the United States and in developing countries. Nutrition programs and policy, principles of nutrition education.

130.title: Experiments in Nutrition: Design & Execution
130.description: Experiments in current nutritional problems. Experimental design: students choose project and, independently or in groups of two-three, design a protocol, complete the project, and report findings.
130.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; NUT 111AV, NUT 111AY, NUT 111B or NUT 114 recommended.

190C.title: Nutrition Research Conference
190C.description: Introduction to research findings and methods in nutrition. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Nutrition or related biological science.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in practical application of nutrition, supervised by a faculty member.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; one upper division course in nutrition.

197T.title: Tutoring in Nutrition
197T.description: Tutoring of students in nutrition courses, assistance with discussion groups or laboratory sections, weekly conference with instructor in charge of course: written evaluations.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; Nutrition Science, Clinical Nutrition or related major.

219A.title: International Nutrition
219A.description: Epidemiology, etiology, and consequences of undernutrition, with particular focus on the nutritional problems of children and women in low income populations.
219A.prereq_text: NUT 111AV; NUT 111AY; graduate standing; undergraduates only admitted with consent of instructor.

230.title: Experiments in Nutrition: Design & Execution
230.description: Student-selected projects to enhance laboratory skills. Independently, or in groups of two-three students, design a protocol, carry out the project, analyze the results and report the findings.
230.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; NUT 201, NUT 202, NUT 203, NUT 204, or the equivalent recommended.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description:
Major professors lead research discussions with their graduate students.
Research papers are reviewed and project proposals presented and evaluated. Format will combine seminar and discussion style.

291.title: Advanced Nutrition Seminar
291.description: Advanced topics in nutrition research. Multiple sections may be taken concurrently for credit.

297T.title: Supervised Teaching in Nutrition
297T.description: Practical experience in teaching nutrition at the university level; curriculum design and evaluation; preparation and presentation of material. Assistance in laboratories, discussion sections, and evaluation of student work.
297T.prereq_text: Graduate standing in nutrition or consent of instructor.

210B.title: Advanced Nutrition II: Nutrition & Cell Biology, Micronutrients
210B.description: Effects of nutrients at the cellular level. Principles of cell signaling and signaling modulation by nutrients. Advanced concepts of mineral and vitamin metabolism. Mineral and vitamin deviencies and associated pathologies.
210B.prereq_text: Admission to the Nutritional Biology Graduate Group or consent of instructor.

290C.title: Research Group Conference
290C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in animal sciences.

194.title: Shifa Clinic Student Volunteer
194.description: Attend clinic every third Sunday performing duties of receptionist, intake, translation, monitor. Students attend a meeting immediately after end of clinic.  There is a mandatory Monday meeting with Clinic co-directors. Students are expected to participate on various committees.
194.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; applications will be available for students; selection of students will be made by selection committee of medical students coordinators and the instructor of record.

290.title: Current Topics in Research
290.description: Selected topics in reproductive biology.

430.title: Obstetrics & Gynecology Clerkship
430.description: Obstetrics, gynecologic and gynecological oncology experience in the delivery room, operating room, clinics and wards at UCDMC and affiliated sites. Rounds, conferences, interactive student presentations and seminars ongoing.
430.prereq_text: Approval by School of Medicine Committee on Student Progress.

192.title: Research Internship
192.description: Supervised work experience in ophthalmology research. Research staff in Ophthalmology have programs in cell biology, electron microscopy, biochemistry, immunology and visual psychophysics.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

498.title: Group Study
498.prereq_text: Medical students with consent of instructor.

099.title: Special Studies for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

192.title: Internship in Human Pathology
192.description: Supervised work experience in pathology and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

199.title: Special Study in Pathology for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study in Pathology for advanced undergraduates.

298.title: Advanced Group Study
298.description: Group Study provides the opportunity for a faculty member to work with students in a focused manner.

126.title: Fundamentals of Immunology
126.description: Fundamental concepts of immunology including components of the immune system, initiation and regulation of the immune response, infection and immunity, allergy and hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, and transplantation.
126.prereq_text: BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 105 or ABI 102; or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

129Y.title: One Health: Human, Animal & Environment Interfaces
129Y.description: Introduction to fundamentals, challenges, and opportunities in One Health  using local and global health case studies. Animal, human, and environmental health problems, along with tools and transdisciplinary approaches, will be introduced to foster innovative thinking that addresses complex issues.

201.title: Integrative Pathobiology Core I
201.description: Overview of molecular biology techniques, tissue structure and function, cell membrane pathology and cellular mechanisms of disease including cellular responses and adaptations to stress, cell cycle, cell death, cell biomechanics, vascular disturbances, and mechanisms of neoplasia and tumorigenesis.

221.title: Topics in Virus  Research
221.description: Discussion-based seminar covering graduate student virology research. Informal presentations and discussion of technical problems in research design and experimentation are encouraged. Current stage of the research project is not important.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Topics in pathology, microbiology or immunology.

199.title: Special Study in Pediatric Research
199.prereq_text: Undergraduate student with consent of instructor based upon adequate preparation as determined by instructor.

299.title: Pediatric Research
299.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate students who are candidates for a degree in some area of biology or behavioral sciences.

460B.title: Acting Internship: Outpatient Pediatrics
460B.description: Supervised experience in pediatric care on outpatient service at UCDMC. Student functions as Acting Intern with appropriate supervision by residents and attending faculty.
460B.prereq_text: PED 430 B or better; and consent of instructor; letter of recommendation from Pediatrics faculty member.

467.title: Elective in Pulmonary Medicine
467.description: Inpatient and outpatient management of pediatric patients with pulmonary diseases. These will include but will not be limited to cystic fibrosis, asthma, and other forms of chronic pulmonary diseases as well as congenital abnormalities.

471.title: Elective in Pediatric Gastroenterology
471.description: Inpatient and outpatient experience in diagnosis and management of gastroenterology disorders in children. Laboratory experience and participation in clinical investigation may be arranged.
471.prereq_text: PED 430; consent of instructor; satisfactory completed.

474.title: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
474.description: The UC Davis Children's Hospital Pediatric ICU is a 24-bed ICU on Davis 10 providing care for critically ill pediatric patients. Patients are usually younger than 18 years of age and can have either primary medical or surgical issues.

477.title: Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
477.description: Evaluation and support of critically ill infants and children. In general, expected to take night call every third night during rotation.

499.title: Research Topics in Pediatrics
499.description: Individual research project in pediatric subspecialty areas (cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, metabolism, newborn physiology and others) may be arranged with faculty member. Independent research by student will be emphasized and long-term projects are possible.
499.prereq_text: Student in Medical School with consent of instructor.

265C.title: Performance Studies: Performance & Society
265C.description: Introduction to the role of performance (broadly defined), in everyday life, sociopolitical negotiation, identity, social movements, the media, and the state.

270A.title: Individually Guided Research in Performance Studies
270A.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Performance Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270A.prereq_text: PFS 200; (PFS 265A or PFS 265B or PFS 265C or PFS 265D); and consent of instructor.

270B.title: Individually Guided Research in Performance Studies
270B.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Performance Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project, to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270B.prereq_text: PFS 200; (PFS 265A or PFS 265B or PFS 265C or PFS 265D); and consent of instructor.

270C.title: Individually Guided Research in Performance Studies
270C.description: Individually guided research, under the supervision of a faculty member, on a Performance Studies topic related to the student's proposed dissertation project to produce a dissertation prospectus.
270C.prereq_text: PFS 200; (PFS 265A or PFS 265B or PFS 265C or PFS 265D); and consent of instructor.

290.title: Colloquia in Performance Studies
290.description: Designed to provide cohort identity and faculty exchange. Opportunity to present papers, hear guest   lecturers, and see faculty presentations, gather for organizational and administrative new, exchange of information and make announcements. Must be taken every year that a Performance Studies graduate is registered, prior to taking the Qualifying Examination.
290.prereq_text: Registration in Performance Studies Graduate Group and prior to Qualifying Examination.

299D.title: Dissertation Research
299D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advancement to Candidacy.

002.title: Elementary Persian
002.description: Continuation of PER 001. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in Persian and to Persian culture.

022.title: Intermediate Persian
022.description: Integrated presentation of listening, speaking, reading and writing as well as cultural topics in Intermediate Persian.

202.title: Principles of Pharmacology & Toxicology II
202.description: Second of three courses presenting fundamental principles of pharmacology and toxicology. Principles of pharmacodynamics and mechanisms of drug/toxicant actions.

230.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacology & Toxicology
230.description: In-depth coverage of selected topics for graduate students in Pharmacology-Toxicology and related disciplines. Topics determined by instructor in charge for each quarter.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Current topics in pharmacology and toxicology.

001.title: Introduction to Philosophy
001.description: Problems of philosophy through major writings from various periods. Problems are drawn from political, aesthetic, religious, metaphysical, and epistemological concerns of philosophy.

005.title: Critical Reasoning
005.description: Criteria of good reasoning in everyday life and in science. Topics to be covered may include basic principles of deduction and induction; fallacies in reasoning; techniques and aids to reasoning; principles of scientific investigation; aids to clarity.
005.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PHI 006.

010.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
010.description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary cognitive scientific approach to the study of mind, drawing concepts and methods from psychology, philosophy, linguistics, artificial intelligence, and other disciplines.

012.title: Introduction to Symbolic Logic
012.description: Syntax and semantics of the symbolic language sentence logic. Symbols of sentence logic. Translation between sentence logic and English. Truth table interpretation of sentence logic. Proof techniques.  Application of truth tables and proof techniques to arguments in English.
012.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken PHI 112, PHI 113, PHI 134, or PHI 135 and passed with a grade of C or better.

013.title: Minds, Brains, & Computers
013.description: Computational theories of the nature of the mind. Mind as a computer process. Possibility of machine intelligence, consciousness, and mentality.
013.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed PHI 013G.

013D.title: Minds, Brains, & Computers, Discussion
013D.description: Small group discussion and preparation of papers related to the content of PHI 013. Computational theories of the nature of the mind. Mind as a computer process. Possibility of machine intelligence, consciousness, and mentality.
013D.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken PHI 013G.
013D.prereq_text: PHI 013 (can be concurrent); Concurrent enrollment in PHI 013 strongly recommended.

015.title: Introduction to Bioethics
015.description: Critical analysis of normative issues raised by contemporary medicine and biology. Possible topics include euthanasia, reproductive technologies, genetic engineering, informed consent and patient autonomy, experimentation on human subjects and non-human animals.

030.title: Introduction to Philosophy of Science
030.description: Basic problems in the philosophy of science, common to the physical, biological, and social sciences. Analysis of explanation, confirmation theory, observational and theoretical terms, the nature of theories, operationalism and behaviorism, realism, reduction.

103.title: Philosophy on Mind
103.description: The relation between mind and body, our knowledge of other minds, and the explanation of mental acts. Discussion of such concepts as action, intention, and causation.

105.title: Philosophy of Religion
105.description: Logical, metaphysical, epistemological, and existential aspects of selected religious concepts and problems.

108.title: Philosophy of the Biological Sciences
108.description: Scientific method in biology. Nature of biological theories, explanations, and models. Problems of evolutionary theory, ecology, genetics, and sociobiology. Science and human values.
108.prereq_text: One course in Biology or one course in Philosophy recommended.

112.title: Intermediate Symbolic Logic
112.description: Predicate logic syntax and semantics. Transcription between predicate logic and English. Models, truth-trees, and derivations. Identity, functions, and definite descriptions. Introduction to concepts of metatheory.
112.prereq_text: PHI 012 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

116.title: Ethical Theories
116.description: Study of fundamental concepts and problems in ethical theory through an examination of classical and contemporary philosophical theories of ethics. Among the theories that may be discussed are utilitarianism, virtue theory, theories of natural rights, Kantian ethical theory, and contractarianism.

119.title: Philosophy of Law
119.description: Philosophical theories of the nature of law, legal obligation, the relation of law and morals. Problems for law involving liberty and justice: freedom of expression, privacy, rights, discrimination and fairness, responsibility, and punishment.
119.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; one course in Philosophy recommended.

122.title: Philosophy of Race
122.description: Core issues in the philosophy of race, including investigation of the nature and reality of race, use of race in science and medicine, nature of racial identity, and ethical responses to racial injustice.
122.prereq_text: One previous course in Philosophy recommended.

131.title: Philosophy of Logic & Mathematics
131.description: Nature of formal systems and mathematical theories. Selected topics include logical and semantical paradoxes; foundations of mathematics; set theory, type theory, and intuitionistic theory; philosophy of geometry; philosophical implications of Gödels incompleteness results.
131.prereq_text: PHI 012 or one course for credit in mathematics.

189A.title: Special Topics in Philosophy: History of Philosophy
189A.description: Special topics in History of Philosophy.
189A.prereq_text: One course in the area of the special topic recommended.

194HA.title: Honors Research Project
194HA.description: Completion of honors research project under direction of an instructor. Consult departmental major advisor for list of instructors available in a given quarter.
194HA.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to students who are members of the honors program in Philosophy.

194HB.title: Research Project
194HB.description: Completion of honors research project under direction of an instructor. Consult departmental major advisor for list of instructors available in a given quarter.
194HB.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open to students who are members of the honors program in Philosophy.

200B.title: Proseminar II
200B.description: Intensive study of core works in a selected area of philosophy. Intensive experience in philosophical writing, discussion, and presentation of written work.

214.title: Ethics
214.description: Topics may include morality and motivation, objectivity in ethics, the relationship between the factual and the moral. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
214.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

290.title: History of Philosophy
290.description: Topics in the history of philosophy. Topics vary according to instructor from quarter to quarter.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

463.title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine: Caring for Developmental Disabilities
463.description: Clerkship. Participate in the outpatient clinical care of children with a wide variety of medical conditions at Shriner's Hospitals for Children. Rotate through a variety of different outpatient clinics including cerebral palsy, neuromuscular disease, limb difference, spinal cord injury, spina bifida, brachial plexus, and sports medicine.

499.title: Research for Medical Students
499.description: Research on any of a variety of topics in physical medicine and rehabilitation.

001A.title: Principles of Physics
001A.description: Mechanics. Introduction to general principles and analytical methods used in physics with emphasis on applications in applied agricultural and biological sciences and in physical education.
001A.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have received credit for PHY 007B or PHY 009A.

001B.title: Principles of Physics
001B.description: Continuation of PHY 001A. Heat, optics, electricity, modern physics.
001B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have received credit for PHY 007A, PHY 007B, PHY 007C, PHY 009B, PHY 009C, or PHY 009D.

007A.title: General Physics
007A.description: Introduction to general principles and analytical methods used in physics for students majoring in a biological science.
007A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed PHY 001B or PHY 009B.
007A.prereq_text: MAT 016B (can be concurrent) or MAT 017B (can be concurrent) or MAT 021B (can be concurrent); completion or concurrent enrollment in MAT 017B or MAT 021B.

007B.title: General Physics
007B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed PHY 001A or PHY 009A.

007C.title: General Physics
007C.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed PHY 009C or PHY 005C.

009A.title: Classical Physics
009A.description: Introduction to general principles and analytical methods used in physics for physical science and engineering majors. Classical mechanics.
009A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 001A or PHY 007B; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009HA.
009A.prereq_text: MAT 021B C- or better or MAT 021BH C- or better or MAT 021M C- or better or MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 017B B or better.

009B.title: Classical Physics
009B.description: Continuation of PHY 009A. Fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, wave phenomena, optics.
009B.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 007A; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009HB, PHY 009HC, or ENG 105.
009B.prereq_text: (PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better); (MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better or MAT 021CH C- or better).

009C.title: Classical Physics
009C.description: Electricity and magnetism including circuits and Maxwell's equations.
009C.credit_limit_text: Only 3 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 007C; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009HD.
009C.prereq_text: PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better; PHY 009B C- or better; MAT 021D C- or better.

009HB.title: Honors Physics
009HB.description: Special relativity, thermal physics. Continuation of PHY 009HA.
009HB.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have completed PHY 007A; not open for credit to students who have completed PHY 009B or PHY 009D.
009HB.prereq_text: PHY 009HA C- or better or PHY 009A B- or better; MAT 021C (can be concurrent) or MAT 021CH (can be concurrent).

010.title: Topics in Physics for Nonscientists
010.description: Emphasis varies: survey of basic principles or a deeper exploration of some particular branch. Past topics included black holes, space time, and relativity; physics of music; history and philosophy; energy and the environment; and natural phenomena.
010.credit_limit_text: No units of credit allowed if taken after any other PHY course.

045.title: Computational Physics
045.description: Algorithms and programming techniques of computational physics with applications from introductory physics.
045.credit_limit_text: No credit if PHY 104B was taken prior to Fall 2022; 2 units of credit if student has taken PHY 102.

080.title: Experimental Techniques
080.description: Experimental techniques. Design of circuits. Data analysis, sources of noise,  statistical and systematic uncertainties. Light sources, detection, and measurement in basic optical systems.
080.prereq_text: PHY 009C C- or better or PHY 009HD C- or better.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Primary for lower division students.

105A.title: Classical Mechanics
105A.description: Principles and applications of Newtonian mechanics. Introduction to Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics.
105A.prereq_text: (PHY 009A C- or better or PHY 009HA C- or better); (PHY 009C C- or better or PHY 009HD C- or better); (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better); (MAT 022B (can be concurrent) or MAT 027B (can be concurrent)); or consent of instructor.

110A.title: Electricity & Magnetism
110A.description: Theory of electrostatics, electromagnetism, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves.
110A.prereq_text: (PHY 009C C- or better or PHY 009HD C- or better); PHY 104A C- or better; or consent of instructor.

115B.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
115B.description: Angular momentum and spin; hydrogen atom and atomic spectra; perturbation theory; scattering theory.
115B.prereq_text: PHY 104A C- or better; PHY 115A C- or better; or consent of instructor.

118.title: Physics Instrumentation for Data Acquisition
118.description: Experimental application of modern high-density integrated circuits. Automated data acquisition, microprocessors, field programmable gate arrays.
118.credit_limit_text: 2 units of credit if student has taken PHY 116B. No credit if student has taken PHY 116C.

122B.title: Advanced Laboratory in Particle Physics
122B.description: Experimental techniques and measurements in nuclear and particle physics. Perform three to six experiments depending on difficulty. Individual work is stressed. Thorough write-ups of the experiments are required.
122B.prereq_text: PHY 080 C- or better; PHY 110A C- or better; PHY 115A C- or better; PHY 110B C- or better (can be concurrent); PHY 112 C- or better (can be concurrent); PHY 115B recommended (can be concurrent).

129A.title: Introduction to Nuclear Physics
129A.description:
Survey of basic nuclear properties and concepts requiring introductory
knowledge of quantum mechanics: nuclear models and forces, radioactive decay and detecting nuclear radiation and nuclear reaction products,
alpha, beta and gamma decay.
129A.prereq_text: PHY 115A C- or better; or consent of instructor.

130A.title: Elementary Particle Physics
130A.description: Properties and classification of elementary particles and their interactions. Experimental techniques. Conservation laws and symmetries. Strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions. Introduction to Feynman calculus.
130A.prereq_text: PHY 104A C- or better; PHY 115A C- or better; PHY 115B (can be concurrent);or consent of instructor.

140A.title: Introduction to Solid State Physics
140A.description: Survey of fundamental ideas in the physics of solids, with selected device applications. Crystal structure, x-ray and neutron diffraction, phonons, simple metals, energy bands and Fermi surfaces, semiconductors, optical properties, magnetism, superconductivity.
140A.prereq_text: (PHY 009D B or better or PHY 009HC B or better or PHY 115A C- or better); PHY 104A C- or better; or consent of instructor.

155.title: General Relativity
155.description: Definition of the mathematical frame work for the description of the gravitational field, introduction of the dynamical equations of Einstein governing its evolution and review of the key solutions, including black holes and expanding universes.
155.prereq_text: PHY 104A; PHY 105A; PHY 105B; PHY 110A; PHY 105B and PHY 110A or consent of instructor.

156.title: Introduction to Cosmology
156.description: Contemporary knowledge regarding the origin of the universe, including the Big Bang and nucleosynthesis, microwave background radiation, formation of cosmic structure, cosmic inflation, cosmic acceleration and dark energy.
156.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have completed PHY 126.
156.prereq_text: ((PHY 009A, PHY 009B, PHY 009C, PHY 009D) or (PHY 009HA, PHY 009HB, PHY 009HC, PHY 009HD, PHY 009HE)); PHY 105A (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.

200C.title: Theory of Mechanics & Electromagnetics
200C.description: Theoretical approaches in electromagnetics including static electromagnetic fields; Maxwell's equations; plane waves in various media; magnetohydrodynamics; diffraction theory; radiating systems; and special relativity.
200C.prereq_text: PHY 200B B- or better; or consent of instructor.

215B.title: Quantum Mechanics
215B.description: Formal development and interpretation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics; its application to atomic, nuclear, molecular, and solid-state problems; brief introduction to relativistic quantum mechanics and the Dirac equation.

219A.title: Statistical Mechanics
219A.description: Foundations of thermodynamics and classical and quantum statistical mechanics with simple applications to properties of solids, real gases, nuclear matter, etc. and a brief introduction to phase transitions.

240C.title: Condensed Matter Physics
240C.description: Review of second quantization.  Interacting electron gas, electron-phonon interaction and effects, including instabilities of electronic systems.  Topics in the theory of superconductivity and magnetism.

245B.title: High-Energy Physics
245B.description: Electroweak interactions; phenomenology of the Standard Model of SU(2)LxU(1); weak interaction experiments; properties of and experiments with W and Z vector bosons; Glashow-Weinberg-Salam model and the Higgs boson; introduction to supersymmetry and other speculations.

269.title: Stellar Structure & Evolution
269.description: Underlying physics of stars as the building blocks of the Universe. Reasons for their existence, mechanisms behind their function, their evolution and ultimate fate. Structure of self-gravitating objects, energy transport in stars, nuclear fusion in stars, stellar evolution, and the birth of compact objects.
269.prereq_text: PHY 200A, PHY 200B, and PHY 215A recommended; graduate standing in Physics; or consent of instructor.

270.title: Current Topics in Physics Research
270.description: Reading and discussion to help physics graduate students develop and maintain familiarity with the current and past literature in their immediate field of research and related areas.
270.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar in Physics
290.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in physics. Topics will vary weekly and will cover a broad spectrum of the active fields of physics research at a level accessible to all physics graduate students.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

292A.title: Seminar in Elementary Particle Physics
292A.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in elementary particle physics.
292A.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

292B.title: High Energy Frontier Initiative & Cosmology Theory Seminar
292B.description: Weekly seminar on current issues in Particle physics and Cosmology.

293.title: Seminar in Condensed Matter Physics
293.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in condensed matter physics.
293.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

294.title: Seminar in Cosmology
294.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in Cosmology.
294.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Physics or consent of instructor.

296.title: Field, Strings, & Gravity Seminar
296.description: Presentation and discussion of topics of current research interest in the areas of quantum field theory, string theory and gravity.

200B.title: PBGG Core Course Series–Winter quarter
200B.description: The second of three PBGG graduate core courses. Coverage includes (1) embryo development, (2) cytoskeleton and vesicle trafficking, (3) cell walls, (4) cell growth, (5) secondary metabolism, (6) plastids and (7) senescence.

210.title: Plant Ecophysiology
210.description: Study of the mechanisms of physiological adaptation of plants to their environment.

290A.title: Faculty Seminar
290A.description: Discussion of research area of seminar speakers in Plant Biology Graduate Group Seminar Series.

290B.title: Seminar
290B.description: Seminars presented by visiting scientists on research topics of current interest.

291.title: Graduate Student Seminar in Plant Biology
291.description: Student-given seminars on topics in plant biology, with critiques by instructor and peers. How to give a seminar, including preparation of visual and other teaching aids. Topic determined by instructor in charge.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Technical and/or professional experience on or off campus. Supervised by a member of the Plant Biology faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

112.title: Plant Growth & Development
112.description: Introduction to the mechanisms and control systems that govern plant growth and development and the responses of plants to the environment. Strong emphasis on vegetative development of flowering plants.
112.prereq_text: ((BIO 001, BIO 002, BIO 003) or (BIS 002A, BIS 002B, BIS 002C)); (CHE 008B or CHE 118B); (BIS 101 or BIS 101V).

116.title: Plant Morphology & Evolution
116.description: Structure and evolution of terrestrial plants. Evolutionary and developmental origins and adaptive significance of both reproductive and vegetative structures, in the context of current understanding of phylogenetic relationships.
116.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLS 116.
116.prereq_text: Introductory Plant Biology; e.g., BIS 002C, PLS 002.

126.title: Plant Biochemistry
126.description: The biochemistry of important plant processes and metabolic pathways. Discussion of methods used to understand plant processes, including use of transgenic plants.

189.title: Experiments in Plant Biology: Design & Execution
189.description: Provides an opportunity for undergraduate students to formulate experimental approaches to current questions in plant biology and to carry out their proposed experiments.
189.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)), (BIS 002C or BIO 003); or the equivalent courses in Plant Sciences; consent of instructor.

190C.title: Research Conference in Plant Biology
190C.description: Introduction to research methods in plant biology. Design of field or laboratory research projects, survey of appropriate literature, and discussion of research by faculty and students.
190C.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Plant Biology or related discipline.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Technical and/or professional experience on or off campus.  Supervised by a member of the Plant Biology Department faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

194H.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194H.description:
Independent study of selected topics under the direction of a member or members of the staff. Completion will involve the writing of a senior
thesis.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; open only to majors of senior standing on honors list.

197T.title: Tutoring in Plant Biology
197T.description: Assisting the instructor by tutoring students in one of the Department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

100.title: Biology of Plant Pathogens
100.description: Behavior, pathology, ecology, and evolution of plant pathogens with global impact on food security and environmental health. Bacteria, fungi, viruses, and other pathogens that infect plants.
100.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or (BIO 002, BIO 002L)), (BIS 002B or (BIO 001, BIO 001L)), (BIS 002C or BIO 003),

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience off and on campus, supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

201B.title: Impacts, Mechanisms & Control of Plant Disease
201B.description: Case-studies approach to analysis of plant diseases, including emerging diseases, caused by bacteria, fungi, nematodes, and oomycetes: impacts, etiology, pathogen taxonomy, epidemiology, biochemical and genetic aspects of pathogen-host interactions, virulence, resistance, disease control and statistical analysis.
201B.prereq_text: PLP 120; PLP 201A; graduate student status in the Plant Pathology Graduate Program or consent of instructor.

210.title: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology of Plant-Microbe Interaction
210.description: Discussion of plantmicrobe interactions, focused on the underlying cellular, biochemical, and molecular events that determine the diseased state.
210.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (BIS 102 or BIS 102V); BIS 103; BIS 104; or the equivalent.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Review and evaluation of current research in plant pathology.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Presentation, evaluation, and critical discussions of research activities in the area of advanced plant pathology; primarily designed for graduate students.

291.title: Seminar in Molecular Plant Pathology
291.description: Review and evaluation of current literature and research in biochemistry and molecular biology of plant microbe interactions.

006V.title: Flower Power; Art & Science of Flowers & Their Uses
006V.description: Introduction to the art and science of using and growing flowers to harness the power that is represented by their aesthetic beauty. Handling, production, arranging, breeding and marketing of flowers. Emphasis on potted plants and cut-flowers.

007V.title: Just Coffee: The Biology, Ecology & Socioeconomic Impacts of the World's Favorite Drink
007V.description: Coffee used as a case study to examine biological, ecological and social factors influencing sustainability of farming systems and how food production systems impact human well-being.

021.title: Computer & Technology Skills for the Classroom & Workplace
021.description: Application of computer software commonly used in the classroom and workplace to build digital fluency: spreadsheets, word processing, databases, web design, presentation software, photo/video editing, computer programming basics. Selection of software tools, cloud computing, digital information protection, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to boost productivity.

021V.title: Computer & Technology Skills for the Classroom & Workplace
021V.description: Application of computer software commonly used in the classroom and workplace to build digital fluency: spreadsheets, word processing, databases, web design, presentation software, photo/video editing, computer programming basics. Selection of software tools, cloud computing, digital information protection, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to boost productivity.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Work experience on or off campus in subject areas pertaining to plant and environmental sciences.  Internship supervised by a faculty member.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; primarily for lower division students.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; primarily for lower division students.

100A.title: Metabolic Processes of Cultivated Plants
100A.description: Principles of energy capture and photosynthesis, water use, and nutrient cycling. Conversion of these resources into products (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and other chemicals) by plants. Emphasis on the relationships between environmental resources, plant metabolism and plant growth.
100A.prereq_text: PLS 002 or BIS 002C; or consent of instructor.

100AL.title: Metabolic Processes of Cultivated Plants Laboratory
100AL.description: Techniques and instruments used to study plant metabolic processes, including water relations, respiration, photosynthesis, enzyme kinetics, microscopy, immunochemistry, and nitrogen fixation. Quantitative methods, problem solving, and practical applications are emphasized.
100AL.prereq_text: PLS 100A (can be concurrent); or the equivalent.

101.title: Agriculture & the Environment
101.description: Focus on the interaction between agriculture and the environment to address the principles required to analyze conflict and develop solutions to complex problems facing society. May be taught abroad.
101.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed AMR 101. (Former AMR 101.)

112.title: Forage Crop Production
112.description: Forages as a world resource in food production. Ecological principles governing the adaptation, establishment, growth and management of perennial and annual forages, including pastures, rangelands and hay; aspects of forage quality which affect feeding value to livestock.
112.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed AMR 112. (Former AMR 112.)
112.prereq_text: PLS 002 or BIS 001C or BIS 002C; or consent of instructor.

116.title: Plant Morphology & Evolution
116.description: Structure and evolution of terrestrial plants. Evolutionary and developmental origins and adaptive significance of both reproductive and vegetative structures, in the context of current understanding of phylogenetic relationships.
116.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 116.
116.prereq_text: Introductory Plant Biology; e.g., BIS 002C, PLS 002.

123.title: Introduction to Plant & Crop Systems Modeling
123.description: Modeling approaches commonly used in plant and crop applications. Fundamentals of how plant/crop models are developed and considerations regarding their limitations. Example model applications include degree-day and radiation-use-efficiency models of growth and yield, phenological models, and crop coefficients.

130.title: Grassland Ecology
130.description: Comprehensive survey of grassland ecology including distributions of major grassland types; systematics; morphology, physiology, and diversity of grassland species; population, community, and ecosystem processes occurring in grasslands; the role of grazing, fire, and drought in grasslands; management and conservation.
130.prereq_text: PLS 002 or BIS 002B or BIS 002C; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

141.title: Ethnobotany
141.description: Relationships and interactions between plants and people, including human perceptions, management, and uses of plants, influences of plants on human cultures, and effects of human activity on plant ecology and evolution. Concepts, questions, methods, and ethical considerations in ethnobotanical research.
141.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 141. (Former PLB 141.)

154.title: Introduction to Plant Breeding
154.description: Principles, methods and applications of plant breeding and genetics to the improvement of crop plants. Illustration of how plant breeding is a dynamic, multidisciplinary, constantly-evolving science. Laboratory emphasizes hands-on experience in the basics of breeding through experiments.
154.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 154. (Former PLB 154.)
154.prereq_text: PLS 152 or BIS 101 or BIS 101V; or consent of instructor.

162.title: Urban Ecology
162.description: Application of fundamental concepts and approaches in landscape and ecosystem ecology to urban ecosystems. Ecological and social drivers and responses. Landscape heterogeneity, nutrient dynamics, invasive species, altered hydrology and climate, and pollution. Discussion of primary literature.
162.prereq_text: ESP 100 C- or better or ESP 110 C- or better or BIS 002B C- or better or PLS 100C C- or better; or consent of instructor.

163.title: Ecosystem & Landscape Ecology
163.description: Integration of concepts to understand and manage ecosystems in a complex and changing world. Emphasis on interactions among biotic, abiotic & human factors and changes over space/time. Local to global controls over water, carbon and nutrients across ecosystems/landscapes.
163.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECL 201.
163.prereq_text: ENH 160 C- or better or ESM 144 C- or better or ESP 100 C- or better or ESP 155 C- or better or EVE 101 C- or better or EVE 117 C- or better or PLB 117 C- or better or PLS 130 C- or better or PLS 144 C- or better or PLS 147 C- or better or PLS 150 C- or better or PLS 162 C- or better or SSC 100 C- or better or SSC 102 C- or better or SSC 109 C- or better or SSC 112 C- or better or HYD 124 C- or better or ECL 200AN C- or better or ECL 200BN (can be concurrent); or similar class with consent of instructor.

176.title: Introduction to Weed Science
176.description: Weed biology and ecology, methods of weed management, biological control, herbicides and herbicide resistance. Weed control in managed and natural ecosystems; invasive species. Laws and regulations. Application of herbicides. Sight and software-assisted identification of common weeds.
176.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PLB 176. (Former PLB 176.)

190.title: Seminar on Alternatives in Agriculture
190.description: Seminar on topics related to alternative theories, practices and systems of agriculture and the relationship of agriculture to the environment and society. Scientific, technological, social, political and economic perspectives.
190.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

190C.title: Research Group Conference
190C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in the plant sciences.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience on or off campus in subject areas pertaining to plant and environmental sciences. Internship supervised by a faculty member.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

193.title: Garden & Farm-Based Experiential Education Methods
193.description: Methods of teaching children and youth about fruit and vegetable production and consumption. Lesson and activity planning for garden and farm field trips. Basic biology, ecology, plant science, and crop management practices. Mentorship in experiential learning. Preparation of garden site.
193.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

194H.title: Senior Honors Thesis
194H.description: Independent study of selected topics under the direction of a member or members of the staff. Completion will involve the writing of a senior thesis.
194H.prereq_text: Senior standing; overall GPA of 3.250 or higher and consent of master advisor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Plant Sciences
197T.description: Leading small voluntary discussion or lab groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing, completion of course being tutored or the equivalent.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

199FA.title: Student Facilitated Course Development
199FA.description: Under the supervision of a faculty member, an undergraduate student plans and develops the course they will teach under 098F/198F.

205.title: Experimental Design & Analysis
205.description: Introduction to the research process and statistical methods to plan, conduct and interpret experiments.
205.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed AGR 205. (Former AGR 205.)

225.title: Quantitative Genetics
225.description: Introduction to the principles of quantitative genetics including the study and analysis of quantitative variation, concepts of heritability and genetic gain from artificial selection, and application of classic and genome-informed approaches in breeding.
225.prereq_text: PLS 205; GGG 201D; or consent of instructor; graduate standing.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Topics of current interest related to Plant Sciences.

290C.title: Research Conference
290C.description: Research conference.

297T.title: Tutoring in Plant Sciences
297T.description: Designed for graduate students who desire teaching experience but are not teaching assistants.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; graduate standing; completion of course to be tutored or the equivalent.

460.title: Clinical Plastic Surgery Elective
460.description: Total involvement in patient care involving surgical preparation, treatment, operative care, and follow-up. Developing and understanding reconstruction and aesthetic plastic surgery. Microvascular surgery included. Student rotation.
460.prereq_text: SUR 430; and consent of instructor; third- or fourth-year medical students.

001Y.title: American National Government
001Y.description: Survey of American national government, including the constitutional system, political culture, parties, elections, the presidency, Congress, and the courts.

003.title: International Relations
003.description: International conflict and cooperation, including the Cold War, nuclear weapons, and new techniques for understanding international politics.

004.title: Basic Concepts in Political Theory
004.description: Analysis of such concepts as the individual, community, liberty, equality, justice, and natural law as developed in the works of the major political philosophers.

011C.title: Politics & Film
011C.description: Survey of portrayals of politics and policy issues in moving pictures. Analysis of political processes, policy development, social mores, and historical periods as highlighted in Hollywood movies, television, and/or documentary films.

012A.title: Politics & Sports
012A.description: Core issues in American and world politics through the lens of sports and the athletes who play them. Introduction of American civil rights movement, the Cold War, Middle East Tensions, and democratization.
