012Y.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
012Y.description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

051.title: Scientific Study of Politics
051.description: Introduction to the basic principles of the scientific study of politics. Research design and empirical analysis of data with applications to different methodological approaches and different substantive areas in political science.

100.title: Local Government & Politics
100.description: Politics and government of local communities in the United States, including cities, counties and special districts. Emphasizes sources and varieties of community conflict, legislative and executive patterns, expertise, decision making and the politics of structure. Observation of local governing boards.

113.title: American Political Thought
113.description: Origins and nature of American political thought. Principles of American thought as they emerge from the founding period to the present.

118C.title: History of Political Theory:  Late Modern
118C.description: Critical analyses of the works of late modern political philosophers such as Rousseau, Kant, Hegel, Tocqueville, Mill, Marx and Nietzsche.

119.title: Contemporary Political Thought
119.description: Contemporary political thought from the end of the 19th century to the present. Emphasis upon an individual philosopher, concept, or philosophical movement; e.g., Nietzsche, Continental political thought, Rawls and critics, theories of distributive justice, feminist theory.

122.title: International Law
122.description:
Selected topics in international law; territory, sovereign immunity,
responsibility, the peaceful settlement or nonsettlement of international disputes.

124.title: The Politics of Global Inequality
124.description: Analysis of current economic and political international relations resulting from a long standing division of the global system into rich and poor regions. May be taught abroad.

130.title: Recent U.S. Foreign Policy
130.description: Broad survey of the development of U.S. foreign policy in 20th century with emphasis on transformation of policy during and after World War II, and the introduction to analytic tools and concepts useful for understanding of current foreign policy issues.

142C.title: Comparative Political Development: Democracy & Democratization
142C.description: Examination of conditions promoting democratization and democratic stability.

150.title: Judicial Politics & Constitutional Interpretation
150.description: Politics of judicial policy making, issues surrounding constitutional interpretation and decision making, prerequisite for courses on the politics of constitutional law.

159.title: Voting Rights Politics, Policy, & the Law in the United States
159.description: Examination of recent issues, political battles, policy, and legal decisions on voting rights in the United States.

164.title: Public Opinion
164.description: Nature of public opinion in America as it is supposed to be and as it is. Distribution of opinions among different publics and the significance of that distribution for system stability and institutions. Opinion polling and its problems.

165V.title: Mass Media & Politics
165V.description: Organization of and decision making within the media; media audiences and the effect of the media on attitudes and behavior; the relationship of the government to the media (censorship, secrecy, freedom of the press, government regulation);the media in election campaigns

166.title: Women in Politics
166.description: Role of women in American politics. Historical experiences; contemporary organizations and strategies; areas of legislative concern; the impact of differences in social class, race, and ethnicity upon the involvement of women in politics.

167.title: Politics at Intersection of Identities: Race, Gender, & Other Intersecting Groups in U.S. Politics
167.description: Examination of political attitudes and behaviors of groups at the intersection of multiple marginalized identities.

170.title: Political Psychology
170.description: Overview to the growing literature on political psychology. Introduction to how psychological concepts (personality, attitudes, stereotypes, heuristics, affect, identity, group dynamics) help us understand how citizens think about politics.

176.title: Racial Politics
176.description: Race, racial attitudes and racial policies in the United States with a specific emphasis on African Americans.

179.title: Special Studies in Comparative Politics
179.description: Intensive examination of one or more special problems appropriate to comparative politics. Coverage is given to formal and informal political institutions, economically developing and developed countries, and non-democratic, democratic, and democratizing countries.

193W.title: Washington Center Research Seminar
193W.description: Core academic component of Washington Program offered every quarter. Topics coordinated with internships. Research draws on resources uniquely available in Washington, DC. Supervised preparation of extensive paper.

196A.title: Seminar in American Politics
196A.description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing in American politics. Topics may include Congress, the Presidency, the Supreme Court, federalism, voting behavior, interest groups, ethnic groups or other topics with a more specialized content than normal course offerings.
196A.prereq_text: Upper division Political Science majors or consent of instructor.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of Instructor; upper division standing.

209.title: The American Political System
209.description: Analysis of selected theoretical and empirical issues posed by contemporary research in American government and politics.

212.title: Quantitative Analysis in Political Science I
212.description: Seminar provides an introduction to the linear regression model. Will obtain a working knowledge of basic regression techniques and problems.

214B.title: Research in Political Science
214B.description: Research seminar sequence required of all PhD students. Design, execution, and defense of an original piece of research in political science, culminating in a paper of publishable quality.

220.title: Seminar in Political Theory
220.description: Introduction to political theory and current debates over its study. Readings from and textual interpretations of political theory including the Federalist Papers and major works by thinkers such as Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, and Rawls. Other readings addressing issues of textual interpretation.

224.title: International Security
224.description: Contemporary scholarship on issues related to international conﬂict and political violence, with particular emphasis on how current trends in globalization and governance affect global security.

285.title: Statistics of Causal Inference in Political Science
285.description: Approaches to causal inference using the potential outcomes framework, with political science applications using observational and experimental data. Covers several prominent causal research designs used for studying politics.

290A.title: Research in American Government & Public Policy
290A.description: Special research seminar on problems and issues in the study of American government and public policy.

290D.title: Research in Judicial Politics
290D.description: Contemporary research on judicial politics, judicial institutions, jurisprudence, and judicial behavior.
290D.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Political Science or consent of instructor.

290G.title: Research in Methodology
290G.description: Special research seminar on selected problems and issues in methods in political science.

202.title: Principles of Population Biology
202.description: Principles of multi-species ecology and evolution. Ecological and evolutionary processes underlying the formation and maintenance of biodiversity. Natural history, modeling, experimental, and molecular approaches to community ecology and evolutionary biology.
202.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken PBG 200B or PBG 200C.

231.title: Mathematical Methods in Population Biology
231.description: Mathematical methods used in population biology. Linear and nonlinear difference equation and differential equation models are studied, using stability analysis and qualitative methods. Partial differential equation models are introduced. Applications to population biology models are stressed.
231.prereq_text: MAT 016C or MAT 021C; or the equivalent.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminars presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis graduate students and faculty.

290C.title: Research Conference in Population Biology
290C.description: Presentation and discussion of faculty and graduate student research in population biology.
290C.prereq_text: PBG 299 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor. Graduate standing; PBG 299 required concurrently.

292.title: Topics in Ecology & Evolution
292.description: Seminar presented by visiting lecturers, UC Davis faculty and graduate students.

092.title: Internship in Veterinary Science
092.description: Supervised work experience in reproduction.
092.prereq_text: Approval of project prior to period of internship by faculty sponsor.

192.title: Internship in Veterinary Science
192.description: Supervised work experience in Reproduction.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship.

243.title: Advanced Topics in Conservation Genetics
243.description: In-depth study of topics related to the application of genetic tools to wildlife conservation. Topics vary annually; may include use of non-invasive methods of genetic assessment and monitoring of wildlife populations. Student-led discussions on assigned readings.
243.prereq_text: Undergraduate genetics and ecology or consent of instructor.

002.title: Elementary Portuguese
002.description: Continuation of POR 001 in the areas of grammar and development of all basic language skills in cultural context with special emphasis on communication.

031.title: Intermediate Portuguese for Spanish Speakers
031.description: Development of linguistic and learning skills required for Spanish-speaking students in upper division courses in Portuguese.

203.title: Intermediate Financial Reporting
203.description: Focuses on the preparation of complex financial statements. Topics include accounting recognition, measurement, and disclosure, as well as the theoretical foundations of and motivations for financial reporting choices.
203.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken MGB 200A or MGP 200A or MGT 200A.
203.prereq_text: ACC 201 or (MGB 200A or MGP 200A or MGT 200A).

211.title: Tax Reporting & Analysis
211.description: Introduction to the taxation of business entities and their related transactions, with an emphasis on the details of tax law and tax reporting requirements. Topics include individual, partnership, and corporate taxation, as well as tax theory.
211.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MGB 264 or MGP 264 or MGT 264.

243.title: Auditing & Attestation Services
243.description: Advanced treatment of the audit process and environment. Topics include audit planning and performance, evidence, internal controls, professional standards, and audit reports. Reviews, compilations and attestation services are examined, as are governmental agency audits.

455.title: Audit Data Analytics
455.description: Analytical techniques and methods as related to the practice of financial statement auditing. Combines theory and the application of auditing professional standards including diagnosing problems and issues, analyzing relevant information, and reporting decision results and recommendations.

298.title: Directed Group Study for Graduate Students
298.description: Directed group study for graduate students.

001.title: General Psychology
001.description: Introduction to empirical approaches. Focus on perception, cognition, personality and social psychology, and biological aspects of behavior.

012Y.title: Data Visualization in the Social Sciences
012Y.description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

041.title: Research Methods in Psychology
041.description: Introduction to experimental design, interviews, questionnaires, field and observational methods, reliability, and statistical inference.
041.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 013V or STA 100 strongly recommended.

099.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
099.description: Special study for lower division students.

100.title: Introduction to Cognitive Psychology
100.description: Introduction to human information processing, mental representation and transformation, imagery, attention, memory, language processing, concept formation, problem solving, and computer simulation.
100.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

101.title: Introduction to Biological Psychology
101.description: Survey and integration of the relationships between behavior and biological processes, including physiology, genes, development, ecology, and evolution.
101.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for those students who have completed NPB 100.

103A.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Data
103A.description: Design and statistical analysis of psychological investigations and the interpretation of quantitative data in psychology.
103A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 103.
103A.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

103B.title: Statistical Analysis of Psychological Data
103B.description: Probability theory, sampling distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing using standard parametric and correlational approaches. Simple regression analysis, multiple regression analysis, non-parametric statistics, introduction to multivariate statistics, with applications in psychology.
103B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 105.

104.title: Applied Psychometrics: An Introduction to Measurement Theory
104.description: Examination of the basic principles and applications of classical and modern test theory. Topics include test construction, reliability theory, validity theory, factor analysis and latent trait theory.
104.prereq_text: (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 103A; (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y); upper division standing in Psychology.

106.title: Network Analysis of Psychological Data
106.description: Fundamental principles of Graph Theory and applications of Network Analysis to psychological data. Community detection, network control, and modeling of cascading failures.
106.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 103A.

120.title: Agent-Based Modeling
120.description: Introduction to agent-based computer simulation and analysis with emphasis on learning how to model animals, including humans, to achieve insight into social and group behavior.

123.title: Hormones & Behavior
123.description: Endocrine physiology with an emphasis on the principles of behavior. Fundamental relationships between hormones and various behaviors engaged in by the organism during its lifetime. Role of hormones in behavioral homeostasis, social behavior, reproductive behavior, parental behavior, adaptation to stress.
123.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 152.

125.title: Behavioral Epigenetics
125.description: Review of basic principles in genetics and epigenetics with emphasis on behavior. Introduction to the use of modern molecular methods in understanding the complex relationships between genes, environment, and behavior.

126.title: Health Psychology
126.description: Psychological factors influencing health and illness. Topics include stress and coping, personality and health, symptom perception and reporting, heart disease, cancer, compliance, and health maintenance and promotion.
126.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 160.
126.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 101 recommended.

130.title: Human Learning and Memory
130.description: Consideration of major theories of human learning and memory with critical examination of relevant experimental data.
130.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100); or consent of instructor.

131.title: Perception
131.description: Cognitive organizations related to measurable physical energy changes mediated through sensory channels. Perception of objects, space, motion, events.
131.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135).

135.title: Cognitive Neuroscience: The Biological Foundations of the Mind
135.description: Neuroscientific foundations of higher mental processes including attention, memory, language, higher-level perceptual and motor processes, and consciousness. Emphasis on the neural mechanisms which form the substrates of human cognition and the relationship of mind to brain. May be taught abroad.
135.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); or consent of instructor; PSC 101 or PSC 121 recommended.

137.title: Neurobiology of Learning & Memory
137.description: Overview of the neural basis of learning and memory focusing on modern behavioral  neuroscience research with animals. Topics include consolidation, neural plasticity, cellular competition for memory storage, and the role of neurogenesis in learning.
137.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 101.

140.title: Developmental Psychology
140.description: An ontogenetic account of human behavior through adolescence with emphasis on motor skills, mental abilities, motivation, and social interaction.
140.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B; not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 112. (Former PSC 112.)
140.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

141.title: Cognitive Development
141.description: Theories, methods, evidence, and debates in the field of cognitive development, such as nature/nurture, constraints on learning, and the role of plasticity. Topics include attention, memory, concepts about the physical and social world, and language.
141.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken HDE 101.
141.prereq_text: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100B or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV.

142.title: Social & Personality Development
142.description: Social and personality development of children, infancy through adolescence. Topics include the development of personality, achievement motivation, self-understanding, sex-role identity, and antisocial behavior. Emphasis on the interface between biological and social factors.
142.prereq_text: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV.

143.title: Infant Development
143.description: Psychological development in infancy. Topics include physical and motor development, sensory and nervous system development, and memory and cognitive development. Emphasis will be  on evaluating theories, empirical research, and experimental methods for understanding infant development.
143.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV).

146.title: The Development of Memory
146.description: Theory and research on memory development with focus on infancy and childhood.
146.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 133.
146.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or PSC 141 or PSC 142 or PSC 100 or PSC 130).

150V.title: Relationship Science: Lust, Love, & Evolution
150V.description: Evolutionary perspectives on attraction and close relationships. Integrating social psychological and evolutionary theories with empirical evidence pertaining to human mating.
150V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 051
150V.prereq_text: PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V; PSC 041 recommended.

151V.title: Social Psychology
151V.description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
151V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 145.
151V.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 041 recommended.

152.title: Social Cognition
152.description: Examines how social factors influence how we attend to, encode, and process information and how these mental processes affect subsequent judgments and behavior.
152.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

154.title: Psychology of Emotion
154.description: Introduction to current theories and research on emotion and bodily feelings with special reference to self-knowledge.
154.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

155.title: The Psychology of Cultural Appropriation
155.description: Social psychological approach to study of cultural appropriation; integration of social psychological theories with empirical evidence and examples from popular press and digital media; development of critical and integrative ways of thinking about theory and research on intergroup relations, identity, and social inequality; examines routes to cultural appreciation.
155.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

162.title: Introduction to Personality Psychology
162.description: Scientific study of personality. Methods of personality research. Overview of current research and theory in the field of personality psychology.
162.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed former PSC 147.
162.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

165.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
165.description: Major theoretical formulations in the history of clinical psychology, from classical psychoanalysis to contemporary existentialism and behavior modification. Survey based on lectures, films, and tapes, of what clinical psychologists do, including methods of appraisal, professional roles, and approaches to treatment.
165.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

168.title: Mental Health, Mental Illness, & Problems in Living
168.description: Overview of psychological disorders and psychological conditions that lead to problems in daily living, with consideration of causes, classification systems, and treatment.
168.prereq_text: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V).

180C.title: Research in Personality & Social Psychology
180C.description: Empirical research on selected topics in personality and social psychology (personality, social psychology, organizational psychology, etc.). Content will vary from quarter to quarter.
180C.prereq_text: PSC 041 or PSC 041V; four upper division Psychology courses and consent of instructor.

182.title: Methods in Laboratory Research
182.description: Training in specific lab-based research methods coupled with hands-on experience in a research lab. Students assessed on their ability report and interpret research findings. Content varies from quarter to quarter.

190.title: Seminar in Psychology
190.description: Intensive treatment of a special topic or problem of psychological interest.
190.prereq_text: Junior or senior standing; major in Psychology or consent of instructor.

192.title: Fieldwork in Psychology
192.description: Supervised internship off and on campus, in community and institutional settings. Maximum of 6 units may be used towards satisfaction of upper division major requirement.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in Psychology.

197T.title: Tutoring in Psychology
197T.description: Intended for advanced undergraduate students who will lead discussion sections in Psychology courses.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

202.title: Research Seminar
202.description: Presentation of graduate research to program faculty and graduate students.

204B.title: Causal Modeling of Correlational Data
204B.description: Examination of how to make causal inferences from correlational data in the behavioral sciences. Emphasis is on testing rival causal models using correlations among observed variables. Beginning with multiple regression analysis, discussion advances to path analysis and related techniques.
204B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed PSC 207A.
204B.prereq_text: PSC 204A; or the equivalent course and graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

205G.title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
205G.description: Modeling and understanding of intraindividual change and interindividual differences in change. Reviews conventional methods and introduces contemporary techniques for modeling intraindividual change.
205G.prereq_text: PSC 204A; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

212A.title: Developmental Psychology: Cognitive & Perceptual Development
212A.description: Theories and empirical findings concerning human cognitive and perceptual development. Development of perception, memory, concepts (e.g., theory of mind, concepts about number), problem solving, and language from infancy to adolescence.
212A.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; completion of an undergraduate or graduate course on developmental psychology or human development.

218B.title: Fundamentals of Animal Behavior
218B.description:
Survey of the phenomena and theory of animal behavior from the 
perspectives of multiple biological disciplines, including evolution, ecology, psychology, genetics, neurobiology, endocrinology, and animal science.

244.title: Stereotyping, Prejudice, & Stigma
244.description: Examines the social psychological underpinnings of stereotyping, prejudice, and stigma, including sociocultural, motivational, and cognitive factors.

263.title: Topics in Cognitive Psychology
263.description: Selected topics in language processing, memory, perception, problem solving, and thinking, with an emphasis on the common underlying cognitive processes.
263.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

271B.title: Core Concepts & Methods in Learning, Memory, & Plasticity
271B.description: Core concepts and detailed survey methods used in studies of learning, memory and plasticity, from the cellular and molecular level to the level of neural circuits. Areas of learning, memory, and plasticity research where recent progress has been made in linking across these levels of analysis.

289A.title: Current Research in Psychology
289A.description: Contemporary theory and empirical research in specialized topics in psychology. Topics include developmental attachment, social neuroscience, mental health, emotion, sexual orientation and identity.
289A.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

289B.title: Current Research in Psychology
289B.description: Intensive examination of contemporary theory and empirical research on a specialized topic in psychology. Sample topics include developmental attachment, social neuroscience, culture and mental health, electrophysiology and cognitive neuroscience, emotion, implicit cognitive processes, sexual orientation and identity, and attention.
289B.prereq_text: PSC 289A; graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar devoted to a highly specific research topic in any area of basic psychology. Special topic selected for a quarter will vary depending on interests of instructor and students.
290.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Psychology or consent of instructor.

391.title: Teaching of Psychology Practicum
391.description: Supervised teaching in undergraduate classrooms. Techniques for delivering content through lectures, discussions, or labs; course administration; communications; assessment of student learning; solving ethical problems; instructional technology.

102.title: Introduction to Human Epidemiology
102.description: Practice of epidemiology as it relates to human populations. Content is fundamental to the Public Health minor and a required core course.

109.title: History of Epidemiology in Public Health
109.description: Historic events in public health and the epidemiology that paved the way for disease control and prevention.

113.title: Health Disparities in the U.S.
113.description: Introduction to the principles and practice of health disparities research.

121.title: Health Informatics Systems
121.description: Health Informatics with a focus on Information Technology. Data gathering, manipulating, storing, retrieving, and classifying.
121.prereq_text: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

132.title: Health Issues Confronting Asian Americans & Pacific Islanders
132.description: Health issues confronting Asian Americans & Pacific Islanders.

190.title: Topics in Public Health
190.description: Seminar on key issues and current topics in public health.

217V.title: Scientific Communication for Public Health Researchers
217V.description: Scientific communication for public health researchers. Oral and written communication for professional and lay audiences. Peer review, seeking grant funding, writing manuscripts, presenting, applying for academic jobs, and disseminating findings to the general public.

233.title: Persuasive Technologies for Health
233.description: Theorizing, designing and evaluating ethical technology-based health communication interventions. Uses of social media, mobile communication apps, wearable devices, computer-generated tailored messages, educational games, and computational approaches in health promotion and healthcare delivery.

280.title: Introduction to SAS Programming
280.description: Introduction to SAS, an integrated software system for data retrieval and management, data manipulation and programming.
280.prereq_text: Introductory statistics course; e.g., MPM 402, STA 102.

192.title: Internship in Pulmonary Medicine
192.description: Supervised work experience in pulmonary medicine.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

299.title: Pulmonary Disease Research
299.description: Pulmonary disease research activity with focus in inhalation toxicity, oxidants or lung biochemistry, and cell and molecular biology.
299.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; by arrangement only.

462.title: Pulmonary Consult Clerkship
462.description: Similar to PUL 460. Rotation designed for students interested in learning pulmonary medicine, but who desire more variety in their clerkships, and do not desire the comprehensive experience offered by a four-week pulmonary rotation.
462.prereq_text: Completion of second year of medical school and/or consent of instructor; completion of Internal Medicine Clerkship.

002.title: Elementary Punjabi
002.description: Continuation of PUN 001. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.
002.prereq_text: PUN 001 or PUN 001V; or consent of instructor.

002V.title: Elementary Punjabi
002V.description: Continuation of PUN 001V. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.
002V.prereq_text: PUN 001 or PUN 001V; or consent of instructor.

022.title: Intermediate Punjabi
022.description: Integrated listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in formal and informal contexts in Intermediate Punjabi.  Continuation of  fluency acquisition in grammar, vocabulary, and meaningful verbal and written expression in Punjabi. Short final essay about topics in Punjabi literature and culture.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates: Research in Radiation Biology
199.description: Radiation Oncology is a unique discipline combining elements of clinical practice linked to complex physics based dosimetry and treatment planning. Included within this clinical environment is a strong basis in biology that underpins the clinical effectiveness of radiation treatment.

299.title: Independent Study & Research
299.description: Research under supervision of Radiation Oncology faculty. Work must be appropriate to fulfill the requirements for the Ph.D. degree.
299.prereq_text: Enrollment with a graduate group for Ph.D. candidacy and consent of group advisor and sponsor.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

299.title: Research: Special Study for Graduate Students

463.title: Clinical Clerkship in Nuclear Medicine
463.description: Clerkship correlates radioisotopic methods with clinical, pathophysiological, and other diagnostic aspects of the patients care. Each patient reviewed with student by faculty member. Reading assignments, informal projects, and research techniques available.
463.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; satisfactory completion of second-year medical school; RDI 461 recommended.

001.title: Survey of Religion
001.description: Basic concepts introduced through readings of the primary religious literature. Discussion of central ideas (creation, history, law, prophecy, suffering, mysticism, asceticism, karma, reincarnation, moksha, etc.); readings from the Bible, Bhagavad Gita, the Koran, selections from Plato and early Buddhist writings.

032.title: History of Yoga
032.description: History of yoga from antiquity to its most recent formulation in American popular and consumer culture.

040.title: New Testament
040.description: New Testament literature from critical, historical, and theological perspectives.

069.title: Introduction to Hindu Mythology
069.description: Survey of the major narrative traditions within Hinduism, including epic literature and local stories in oral, textual, visual and performative forms.

115.title: Mysticism
115.description: Historical and descriptive analysis of selected key figures in mystical traditions and readings of representative mystical texts. Analytic term paper.
115.prereq_text: One lower division Religious Studies course.

154.title: The Hindu Temple
154.description: Comparative history of architecture and symbolism of the Hindu Temple in India, Southeast Asia and the United States. Attention to the temple as expression of religious knowledge, political authority, and cultural heritage through the lens of colonialism and postcolonialism.

158.title: The Ramayana
158.description: Exploration of the Indian epic, Ramayana, through the lens of literature, performance, and visual art. Emphasis on the text's diversity and its contemporary global relevance. Topics include Ramayanas in Southeast Asia, and in various South Asian diaspora communities.

165.title: Islam in Asia
165.description: Islam as a lived religion in the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, China, and Southeast Asia. Emphasis is on primary sources studied comparatively and historically.

099.title: Directed Research Immunology
099.description: Independent research will be encouraged in basic immunology, including the role of the cellular immune system in oncogenesis.

192.title: Internship in Rheumatology-Allergy
192.description: Supervised work experience in rheumatology-allergy.
192.prereq_text: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.

199.title: Directed Research in Immunology
199.description: Independent research will be encouraged in basic immunology, including the role of the cellular immune system in oncogenesis.

209.title: Current Topics in Immunology: From Presentations to Grants
209.description: Current developments in various aspects of immunology and their interrelationships. Focus on areas of immunology not currently covered in the basic and advanced immunology courses. Oral presentation, written review and grant preparation.

298.title: Topics in Rheumatology & Clinical Immunology
298.description: Library and/or laboratory work as required.

299.title: Research in Autoimmune Disease
299.description:
Independent research will be encouraged in both animal models of human disease (including congenitally athymic [nude], asplenic, and New Zealand mice) and the cellular immune system of patients with systemic
lupus erythematosus, Sjögrens syndrome, polymyositis and drug hypersensitivity.

002.title: Elementary Russian
002.description: Continuation of grammar and language skills developed in RUS 001.

005.title: Intermediate Russian
005.description: Grammar review. Introduction to literature in its sociopolitical context. Conversational practice.

101B.title: Advanced Russian
101B.description: Continuation of RUS 101A. Topics in Russian grammar for the advanced student. Reading and discussion of journalistic texts and classic and contemporary literature. Conversational exercises utilizing literary and colloquial variants of current Russian speech.

103.title: Literary Translation
103.description: Translation of Russian literary texts into stylistically equivalent idiomatic English.

134.title: Humor & Comedy in Russian Culture
134.description: Survey of humor, comedy and satire in Russian culture, from the nineteenth-century to the present day. Includes literature, film, drama, and contemporary media. All works are situated in the historical and political context of Imperial Russia, the Soviet Union, and contemporary Russian society.

002.title: Feeding the World: Influences on the Global Food Supply
002.description: Scientific principles and dynamic interactions involved in food production, food processing, nutrition, and agribusiness.  Physical, biological and social science issues influencing the availability and safety of the food supply worldwide.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken SAS 002V.

009.title: Crisis in the Environment
009.description: Exploration of contemporary environmental issues, including causes, effects, and solutions to a wide range of environmental problems facing the global ecosystem. Political, societal, and economic dimensions of these issues. Topics covered include climate change, air pollution, ocean exploitation, forest management and wildfire, and food and water insecurity.

010.title: Water, Power, Society
010.description: Water resources issues. How water has been used to gain and wield socio-political power. Water resources development in California  related to current and future sustainability of water quantity and quality. Roles of science and policy in solving water problems.

013.title: Disease & Society
013.description: Introduction to the concept of disease, the societal and personal impacts of past, present and future diseases, and the science behind disease discoveries, causes, evolution, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

014.title: Forests & Society
014.description: Sociology, natural history and current issues of the world's forests. Application of scientific principles in outdoor laboratories and on-campus field trips.

025.title: Global Climate Change: Convergence of Biological, Geophysical, & Social Sciences
025.description: Causes of global climate change and the biological, geophysical, and social consequences of such change. Methods used by different scientists for predicting future events. Complexity of global affairs. Decision making under uncertainty.
025.credit_limit_text: Students cannot take both SAS 025 & SAS 025V for credit.

025V.title: Global Climate Change: Convergence of Biological, Geophysical, & Social Sciences
025V.description: Causes of global climate change and the biological, geophysical, and social consequences of such change. Methods used by different scientists for predicting future events. Complexity of global affairs. Decision making under uncertainty.
025V.credit_limit_text: Students cannot take both SAS 025 & SAS 025V for credit.

040.title: Photography: Bridging Art & Science
040.description: Photography is used to explore the common ground between art and science. Photographic processes, creativity and aesthetics, chaos and order, principles of space, time and light. Photographic interpretation and documentation of the natural world. Camera required.

043.title: Energy, Materials, & Design Over Time
043.description: Global history of design across time, viewed through the lens of the effects of the creation and discovery of new energy sources, processes, and materials on design.

092.title: Internship in Science & Society
092.description: Supervised internship on and off campus, in the community, or in institutional settings.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

120.title: Science & Contemporary Societal Issues
120.description: Study of a contemporary societal issue/problem emphasizing critical thinking with information drawn from several disciplines. Multiple instructors illustrate the necessity of an interdisciplinary and cooperative approach in solving important issues. Topics will vary.

192.title: Internship in Science & Society
192.description: Supervised internship on or off campus, in the community, or in institutional settings.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.

199.title: Special Study in Science & Society
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

390.title: Teaching Methods in Science & Society
390.description: Practical experience in methods and problems related to teaching Science & Society courses. Discussion of critical pedagogies specific to teaching of science-societal issues, preparing for and conducting discussion sessions, analyses of texts and supporting material, formulation of assignments, exams.

016.title: Sex, Science, & Society
016.description: Survey of the relationship between sex, science, and society in the history of the modern world. Emphasis on the development of scientific ideas about the human body against broader social, cultural, and political trends and from a global viewpoint.

040B.title: Media History 2: 1945-Present
040B.description: History of media from 1945 to present, with particular focus on the development of the computer, digital network and internet technologies in the context of other media infrastructures like radio, television and satellite networks.

100.title: Methods in Science, Technology, & Medicine Studies
100.description: Methodological approaches for studying science, technology, and medicine in social context. Detailed case studies illustrate different historical, philosophical, sociological, ethical, rhetorical, and political methods of analysis.
100.credit_limit_text: Only two units of credit for students who have previously taken STS 020.

101.title: Data & Society
101.description: Basic concepts in data science from a socio-cultural perspective. Identifying data stakeholders and their biases, reading and evaluating data documentation, exploring data through analysis and visualization, identifying knowledge gaps, and assessing data ethics.

102.title: Artificial Intelligence in Society
102.description: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in social context. Implications of AI for scientific, legal, educational, economic, and political systems. History of AI research and development. Debates about privacy, security, authenticity, and public policy in the era of AI, with focus on diversity, social justice, and ethical decision-making. Hands-on exercises and projects using AI that generates text and images.

115.title: Data Sense & Exploration: Critical Storytelling with Analysis
115.description: Data science and the communication of data insights through critical storytelling. Attention to the historical and social contexts of data analysis, emphasizing narrative, visualization, and exploration. Introduction to the R computing environment for data analysis.

129.title: Health & Medicine in a Global Context
129.description: Recent works in medical anthropology and the science studies of medicine dealing with social and cultural aspects of global health issues such as AIDS, pandemics, clinical trials, cultural differences in illnesses, diabetes, organ trafficking, medical technologies, illness narratives, and others.

136.title: Scientific Revolution
136.description: Rise of modern science in Europe, 1500–1750. Transformation of ideas about nature, knowledge, medicine, and technology in the age of Copernicus, Vesalius, Galileo, Descartes, and Newton.

160.title: Ghosts of the Machine: How Technology Rewires our Senses
160.description: Historical, aesthetic and critical approaches to how information technologies produced ghost effects or a sense of terror in response to new media like the photograph, gramophone, film, typewriter, computer, Turing Machine. Focus on technological media transforms sense perception.

162.title: Surveillance Media
162.description: Surveillance technologies and media surveillance in daily life. Topics include CCTV, facial recognition, tracking systems, biosensors, data mining, encryption, and AI. Analysis of laws, security measures, and counter-surveillance practices.

172.title: Video Games & Culture
172.description: Critical approaches to the study of video games, focusing on formal, historical, and cultural modes of analysis. History of software and hardware in North American and global contexts. Relations of games to society, politics, economics, media, etc.
172.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken CTS 172 (former course CTS 172).

176.title: Sociology of Science
176.description: Social, cultural, and historical dimensions of science. Problems, methods, and theories in the sociology of scientific knowledge. Laboratories and field sites as social spaces. Scientific and technical knowledge in institutional and organizational contexts.

194A.title: Research in Science & Technology Studies
194A.description: Directed reading and research in preparation for a thesis project.
194A.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing & faculty approval recommended.

205.title: Contemporary Issues in Science & Technology Studies
205.description: Recent topics, debates, and innovative methods in Science & Technology Studies. Issues may include the governance of technoscience, science and media, data studies, indigenous knowledge, science and globalization, citizen science, new and emerging technologies.

001.title: Introduction to Sociology
001.description: Principles and basic concepts of sociology. The study of groups, culture, collective behavior, classes and caste, community and ecology, role, status, and personality.

001V.title: Introduction to Sociology
001V.description: Principles and basic concepts of sociology. The study of groups, culture, collective behavior, classes and caste, community and ecology, role, status, and personality.

002.title: Self & Society
002.description: Exploration of how self and identity are formed and transformed by socialization and social interaction in relation to roles, groups, institutions, power, and social change. Consideration of how people make decisions, fall in love, and come to blows.

003.title: Social Problems
003.description: General sociological consideration of contemporary social problems in relation to sociocultural change and programs for improvement.

005.title: Global Social Change: An Introduction to Macrosociology
005.description: Introduction to change and diversity in world history, including the United States. Examines population and family, technological change and economic development, power and status, culture and identity.

006.title: Health & Illness
006.description: Introduction to the sociology of health and illness, including social determinants of health, social inequalities in health/health disparities, social construction of health, the organization of health care, and the politics of health care reform.

007.title: Race & Ethnicity
007.description: Introduction to the sociology of race and ethnicity in the U.S., including historical changes in racial and ethnic categories, mechanisms of racism, anti-racist social movements, the role of social policy in shaping patterns of racial inequality.

046.title: Introduction to Social Research Methods
046.description: Examination of logic and methods of sociological research. Selection and definition of problems of investigation, data-gathering techniques, and sampling.
046.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken SOC 046A.

056.title: Introduction to Social Statistics
056.description: Data-analysis techniques, measurement, scaling, multivariate analysis, and quantitative measures of association.
056.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken SOC 046B.

100.title: Origins of Modern Sociological Theory
100.description: Origins of modern sociological thought. Special emphasis on three major theorists from the classical tradition of 19th-century European social thought: Karl Marx, Max Weber, and Emile Durkheim.

120.title: Deviance
120.description:
Social structural sources, institutional practices and microprocesses
associated with illegality, evil, disease, immorality, disability, racial and class differences, citizenship, and the body. Special emphasis on expert knowledge and the production and management of social difference.

125.title: Sociology of Culture
125.description: Sociological approaches to study of historical and contemporary culture and mass media, and their structuring in relation to social actors, institutions, stratification, power, the production of culture, audiences, and the significance of culture in processes of change.

126.title: Social Interaction
126.description: Everyday interaction in natural settings; ethnographic approaches to the understanding of social meanings, situations, personal identity and human relationships. Particular attention to the work of Erving Goffman and to principles of field observation and qualitative analysis.

130.title: Race Relations
130.description: Functions of the social definitions of race and racial groups. Analysis of racial conflict, oppression, and other forms of ethnic stratification. Models of ethnic interaction and social change. Emphasis on racial relationships within the U.S.

132.title: The Sociology of Gender
132.description: Analysis of biological, psychological, cultural and structural conditions underlying the status and roles of men and women in contemporary society, drawing on a historical and comparative perspective.

133.title: Sexual Stratification & Politics
133.description: Analysis of origins, dynamics, and social implications of sexual stratification. Examination of classical and contemporary theorists such as Engels, Freud, J.S. Mill, de Beauvoir, Juliet Mitchell, D. Dinnerstein. Attention to selected issues in social movements for and against sexual equality.
133.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; SOC 001, SOC 002, or SOC 003 recommended.

135.title: Social Relationships
135.description: Social and cultural factors influencing friendships and intimate relationships. Topics include relationship development, relationship maintenance, and relationship loss.

137.title: African American Society & Culture 1790 to 1990
137.description: Political and social transformations of African American communities between 1790 and 1990, as seen through film, literature, and music. Topics include: Black consciousness, Afro-Slave culture, The Harlem Renaissance, and contemporary Hip Hop.

138.title: Economic Sociology
138.description: Overview of the rapidly growing field of economic sociology. Focus on variations in the ways that markets are organized. The relationship between individual and collective rationality will also be emphasized.

140.title: Social Stratification
140.description: Systems of social ranking, theories of stratification; power, prestige, culture, and styles of life of various social classes; social mobility and its consequences for social structure.

143A.title: Urban Society
143A.description: Theories of city origins. Analysis of the historic process of urbanization and of varying city types. Comparison of American and European experience of metropolitanization, counterurbanization, and neighborhood change. Consideration of competing theories of urban growth and change and competing visions of the urban future.

148.title: Collective Behavior
148.description: Study of behavior of human crowds and masses in extraordinary circumstances, including crowd panics, mass scares, collective protests, riots, revolutionary situations, ecstatic and revivalist gatherings, crazes, fads, and fashions.

150.title: Criminology
150.description: Sociological analysis of criminal behavior in relation to social structure and the criminalization process.

153.title: The Sociology of Childhood
153.description: Contemporary childhood in historical, cross-cultural, and global perspectives. Examine changes in understanding of the nature of childhood and "best interests of the child" by class, race, gender, geographic region, and historical period.

155.title: Sociology of Law
155.description: Law as a social institution. Theories and research on the relationships between legal systems and other aspects of society. How social inequalities can be reproduced, lessened, or exacerbated by law and its enforcement.

157.title: Social Conflict
157.description: Analysis of the causes, dynamics, and regulation of social conflict within and between various kinds of social groupings with particular reference to nonviolent methods of waging and regulating conflict.

162.title: Society, Culture, & Health
162.description: Analysis of how socio-cultural factors shape illness experience. Evaluation of how certain conditions come to be understood as health conditions; illness identities and biographies; doctor-patient interactions; biomedical cultures; how race, ethnicity, and gender shape health practices.
162.prereq_text: SOC 001, SOC 002, SOC 003, or SOC 006 recommended.

172.title: Intersections of Race, Gender & Class
172.description: Sociological approaches to the intersections of race, class, gender and other forms of social difference. Theories of racism and racial identities. Application of intersectional analyses to historical and contemporary social problems and social movements.

176.title: Sociology of Science
176.description: Social, cultural, and historical dimensions of science. Problems, methods, and theories in the sociology of scientific knowledge. Laboratories and field sites as social spaces. Scientific and technical knowledge in institutional and organizational contexts.

180A.title: Complex Organizations
180A.description:
Develops a sociological approach to organizations theory. Designed to
introduce sociological concepts, address the alternative psychological and economic models, and involve students in the practice of organizational analysis.

195.title: Special Topics in Sociological Analysis
195.description: In-depth examination of topics in sociology. Emphasis on student research and writing.

215.title: Economy, Polity, & Society
215.description: Introduces topics and selected issues in the related fields of economic and political sociology and political economy.

233.title: Gender, Culture, & Local/Global Transformation
233.description: Focus on critical approach to women and development; analyze local transformations with global connections within specific cultural contexts. Covers theory, methodological issues, and relationship between theory and practice.

092.title: Soil Science Internship
092.description:
Work experience off and on campus in soil science. Internship supervised
by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

102.title: Environmental Soil Chemistry
102.description: Soil chemistry processes related to the fate and transport of contaminants in soil. Soil minerals, natural organic matter, surface charge, soil solution chemistry, redox reactions in soil, and sorption of inorganic and organic contaminants.
102.prereq_text: General chemistry; SSC 100 or equivalent recommended.

111.title: Soil Microbiology
111.description: Major groups of microorganisms in soil, their interrelationships, and their responses to environmental variables. Role of microorganisms in cycling of nutrients. Plant-microbe relationships. Transformations of organic and inorganic pollutants.

192.title: Soil Science Internship
192.description:
Work experience off and on campus in soil science. Internship supervised
by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

229Y.title: Soil Minerals in the Environment
229Y.description: Describing and identifying soil minerals commonly found in the Critical Zone; Origin, occurrence, and properties of soil minerals in relation to chemical, pedologic, and environmental conditions. Research applications of mineral identification techniques including X-ray diffraction, electron microprobe analysis, and electron microscopy.

290.title: Special Topics in Soil Science
290.description: Seminars and critical review of problems, issues, and research in soil science.

001.title: Elementary Spanish
001.description: Introduction to Spanish grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent SPA 001S, SPA 001V, or SPA 001Y; students who have successfully completed SPA 002 or SPA 003 in the 10th or higher grade of high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP grading basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

001V.title: Elementary Spanish
001V.description: Introduction to Spanish grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent SPA 001S, SPA 001Y, or SPA 001; students who have successfully completed SPA 002 or SPA 003 in the 10th or higher grade of high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP grading basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

001Y.title: Elementary Spanish
001Y.description: Introduction to Spanish grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent courses SPA 001, SPA 001V, or SPA 001S; students who have completed SPA 002 or SPA 003 in the 10th grade of high school may receive unit credit for this course on a P/NP basis only; although a passing grade will be charged to the student's P/NP option, no petition is required; all other students will receive a letter grade unless a P/NP petition is filed.

002.title: Elementary Spanish
002.description: Continuation of SPA 001 and SPA 001S in the areas of grammar and basic language skills.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent SPA 002S, SPA 002V or SPA 002Y.
002.prereq_text: SPA 001 or SPA 001S or SPA 001V or SPA 001Y.

002V.title: Elementary Spanish
002V.description: Continuation of SPA 001, SPA 001S, or previous high school experience in the areas of grammar and basic language skills. Online format combining synchronous chatting with technologically based materials.
002V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken equivalent SPA 002, SPA 002S, SPA 002Y, or higher.
002V.prereq_text: SPA 001 or SPA 001S or SPA 001V or SPA 001Y.

002Y.title: Elementary Spanish
002Y.description: Continuation of SPA 001 or SPA 001S in the areas of grammar and basic language skills. Hybrid format combining classroom instruction with technologically based materials.
002Y.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken equivalent SPA 002, SPA 002S, or SPA 002V.
002Y.prereq_text: SPA 001 or SPA 001Y or SPA 001V or SPA 001S.

003.title: Elementary Spanish
003.description: Completion of grammar sequence and continuing practice of all language skills using cultural texts.
003.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent SPA 003S, SPA 003V or SPA 003Y.
003.prereq_text: SPA 002 or SPA 002S or SPA 002V or SPA 002Y.

003V.title: Elementary Spanish
003V.description: Continuation of SPA 002, SPA 002S, SPA 002V or SPA 002Y. Online format combining synchronous chatting with technologically based materials.
003V.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken equivalent SPA 003, SPA 003S, SPA 003Y, or higher.
003V.prereq_text: SPA 002 or SPA 002S or SPA 002V or SPA 002Y.

003Y.title: Elementary Spanish
003Y.description: Completion of grammar sequence and continuing practice of all language skills using cultural texts. Hybrid format combining classroom instruction with technologically based materials.
003Y.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken equivalent SPA 003, SPA 003S, or SPA 003V.
003Y.prereq_text: SPA 002 or SPA 002S or SPA 002V or SPA 002Y.

021.title: Intermediate Spanish
021.description: Review and development of grammar, vocabulary and composition acquired in the first year through exercises and reading of modern texts.
021.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent SPA 021S, SPA 021V or SPA 021Y.
021.prereq_text: SPA 003 or SPA 003S or SPA 003V or SPA 003Y.

021V.title: Intermediate Spanish
021V.description: Continuation of SPA 003, SPA 003V, SPA 003Y, SPA 003S, or previous high school experience in the areas of grammar and intermediate language skills. Online format combining synchronous chatting with technologically based materials.
021V.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken equivalent SPA 021, SPA 021Y or SPA 021S.
021V.prereq_text: SPA 003 or SPA 003Y or SPA 003V; or the equivalent from previous high school language experience.

022Y.title: Intermediate Spanish
022Y.description: Continuation of SPA 021, SPA 021S, or SPA 021V in the areas of grammar and basic language skills. Online format combining synchronous chatting with technologically based materials.
022Y.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken equivalent SPA 022, SPA 022S or SPA 022V.
022Y.prereq_text: SPA 021 or SPA 021S or SPA 021V or SPA 021Y.

023.title: Spanish Composition I
023.description: Development of writing skills by way of reading, discussion, and analysis of authentic materials, literary texts, and videos. Selective review of grammar. Composition, journals, individual and group projects.
023.credit_limit_text: Not open for students who have completed equivalent SPA 023S.
023.prereq_text: SPA 022 or SPA 022S or SPA 022V or SPA 022Y.

024.title: Spanish Composition II
024.description: Development of advanced level writing skills, with emphasis on how to write argumentative prose, essays, and research papers. Introduction to the analysis of literary genres. Compositions, journals, individual and group projects.
024.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed equivalent SPA 024S.

032.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers II
032.description: Course two of a three quarter series providing bilingual students whose heritage language is Spanish with the linguistic and learning skills required for successfully completing upper division courses in Spanish. Oral presentations and compositions on themes relevant to the Latinx/Chicanx experience in the U.S.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chairperson.

100.title: Principles of Hispanic Literature & Criticism
100.description: Principles of literary criticism applied to the study of fiction, drama, poetry, and essay of major literary writers of the Hispanic world.
100.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken SPA 100S.
100.prereq_text: SPA 024 or SPA 024S or SPA 033 or SPA 033V.

139.title: Modern Spanish Theater
139.description: Study of the main dramatic trends and playwrights of modern Spanish theater. Selected works by Valle Inclán, García-Lorca, Mihura, Buero-Vallejo, Arrabal and others. Offered in alternate years.
139.prereq_text: SPA 100 or SPA 100S or SPA 141 or SPA 141S or SPA 168 or SPA 170 or SPA 170S.

142.title: Special Topics in Spanish Cultural & Literary Studies
142.description: Special topics in the study of Spanish literature and culture. May be taught abroad.
142.prereq_text: SPA 100 or SPA 100S or SPA 141 or SPA 141S or SPA 168 or SPA 170 or SPA 170S.

153.title: Latin American Short Story
153.description: Evolution of the Latin American short story from the 19th century to the present. Emphasis on the contemporary period.
153.prereq_text: SPA 100 or SPA 100S or SPA 141 or SPA 141S or SPA 168 or SPA 170 or SPA 170S.

155.title: Mexican Novel
155.description: Evolution of the Mexican novel from the 19th century to the present. Emphasis on the narrative of the Revolution and significant contemporary works.
155.prereq_text: SPA 100 or SPA 100S or SPA 141 or SPA 141S or SPA 168 or SPA 170 or SPA 170S.

164.title: Race & Culture in Latin America
164.description: How race is constructed through literature, music, visual culture, and media culture in Latin America, including transatlantic contexts. Slavery, Afro-Latinidad, diaspora, mestizaje, indigeneity, intersectionality, and limpieza de sangre.
164.prereq_text: SPA 024 or SPA 024S or SPA 033 or SPA 033V; or consent of instructor.

178A.title: Spanish for the Professions
178A.description: For students with an advanced level of Spanish interested in the use of Spanish in the health care, legal and law enforcement and marketing and business professions.  Field trips documenting the use of Spanish in the public context.

192I.title: Internship in Spanish
192I.description: Internships in fields where Spanish language skills can be used and perfected (teaching, counseling, translating-interpreting).
192I.prereq_text: SPA 023; consent of instructor; junior standing; major in Spanish or a related field.

194H.title: Special Study for Honors Students
194H.description: Guided research, under the direction of a faculty member, leading to a senior honors thesis on a topic in Spanish literature, civilization, or language studies.
194H.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; senior standing; qualification for the Spanish honors program.

197T.title: Tutoring in Spanish
197T.description: Tutoring in undergraduate courses including leadership in small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with departmental courses.
197T.prereq_text: Upper division standing and permission of the chairperson.

197TC.title: Tutoring in the Community
197TC.description: Tutoring in public schools under the guidance of a regular teacher and supervision by a departmental faculty member.
197TC.prereq_text: Upper division standing and permission of the chairperson.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chairperson.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study of a topic or an author to be determined in consultation with an individual faculty member. May be taught abroad.

206.title: Spanish Syntax
206.description:
An examination of Spanish word order within the framework of general linguistic theory. The student will investigate how to write a grammar
of Spanish with particular attention to the structure of noun and verb clauses.

013.title: Elementary Statistics
013.description: Descriptive statistics; basic probability concepts; binomial, normal, Student's t, and chi-square distributions. Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals for one and two means and proportions. Regression.
013.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit for students who have completed STA 013V/Y, or higher.
013.prereq_text: Two years of high school algebra or Mathematics D.

032.title: Gateway to Statistical Data Science
032.description: Probability concepts; programming in R; exploratory data analysis; sampling distribution; estimation and inference; linear regression; simulations; resampling methods. Alternative to STA 013 for students with a background in calculus and programming.
032.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have taken STA 013; not open for credit to students who have taken STA 100.
032.prereq_text: MAT 016B C- or better or MAT 017B C- or better or MAT 019B C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better.

035A.title: Statistical Data Science I
035A.description: Principles of descriptive statistics; basic R programming; probability models; sampling variability; hypothesis tests; confidence intervals; statistical simulation.
035A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken STA 032 or STA 100; only 2 units of credit for students who have taken STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y.
035A.prereq_text: MAT 016A (can be concurrent) or MAT 017A (can be concurrent) or MAT 019A (can be concurrent) or MAT 021A (can be concurrent).

035B.title: Statistical Data Science II
035B.description: Advanced programming and data manipulation in R. Principles of data visualization. Concepts of correlation, regression, analysis of variance, nonparametrics.
035B.prereq_text: (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better; ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better) or STA 032 C- or better or STA 035A C- or better or STA 100 C- or better; MAT 016B or MAT 017B (can be concurrent) or MAT 019B (can be concurrent) or MAT 021B (can be concurrent).

100.title: Applied Statistics for Biological Sciences
100.description: Descriptive statistics, probability, sampling distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, contingency tables, ANOVA, regression; implementation of statistical methods using computer package.
100.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit allowed to students who have taken STA 013, STA 032 or 103; not open for credit to students who have taken STA 102.
100.prereq_text: MAT 016B C- or better or MAT 017B C- or better or MAT 019B C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better.

103.title: Applied Statistics for Business & Economics
103.description: Descriptive statistics; probability; random variables; expectation; binomial, normal, Poisson, other univariate distributions; joint distributions; sampling distributions, central limit theorem; properties of estimators; linear combinations of random variables; testing and estimation; Minitab computing package.
103.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit to students who have completed STA 100.
103.prereq_text: (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better or STA 035B C- or better or STA 100 C- or better); (MAT 016B C- or better or MAT 017B C- or better or MAT 019B C- or better or MAT 021B C- or better).

104.title: Applied Statistical Methods: Nonparametric Statistics
104.description: Sign and Wilcoxon tests, Walsh averages. Two-sample procedures. Inferences concerning scale. Kruskal-Wallis test. Measures of association. Chi square and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests.
104.prereq_text: STA 013 C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better or STA 035B C- or better or STA 100 C- or better.

106.title: Applied Statistical Methods: Analysis of Variance
106.description: Basics of experimental design. One-way and two-way fixed effects analysis of variance models. Randomized complete and incomplete block design. Multiple comparisons procedures. One-way random effects model.
106.prereq_text: STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better or STA 035B C- or better or STA 100 C- or better.

108.title: Applied Statistical Methods: Regression Analysis
108.description: Simple linear regression, variable selection techniques, stepwise regression, analysis of covariance, influence measures, computing packages.
108.prereq_text: STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better or STA 035B C- or better or STA 100 C- or better.

130A.title: Mathematical Statistics: Brief Course
130A.description: Basic probability, densities and distributions, mean, variance, covariance, Chebyshev's inequality, some special distributions, sampling distributions, central limit theorem and law of large numbers, point estimation, some methods of estimation, interval estimation, confidence intervals for certain quantities, computing sample sizes.
130A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have taken STA 131A.
130A.prereq_text: (MAT 016C C- or better or MAT 017C C- or better or MAT 019C C- or better or MAT 021C C- or better); (STA 013 C- or better or STA 013V C- or better or STA 013Y C- or better or STA 032 C- or better or STA 035B C- or better or STA 100 C- or better).

130B.title: Mathematical Statistics: Brief Course
130B.description: Transformed random variables, large sample properties of estimates. Basic ideas of hypotheses testing, likelihood ratio tests, goodness-of-fit tests. General linear model, least squares estimates, Gauss-Markov theorem. Analysis of variance, F-test. Regression and correlation, multiple regression. Selected topics.
130B.prereq_text: STA 130A C- or better or STA 131A C- or better or MAT 135A C- or better.

131A.title: Introduction to Probability Theory
131A.description: Fundamental concepts of probability theory, discrete and continuous random variables, standard distributions, moments and moment-generating functions, laws of large numbers and the central limit theorem.
131A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed MAT 135A.
131A.prereq_text: MAT 021C C- or better; (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better); MAT 021D strongly recommended.

131B.title: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics
131B.description: Sampling, methods of estimation, bias-variance decomposition, sampling distributions, Fisher information, confidence intervals, and some elements of hypothesis testing.
131B.prereq_text: STA 131A C- or better or MAT 135A C- or better; consent of instructor.

135.title: Multivariate Data Analysis
135.description: Multivariate normal distribution; Mahalanobis distance; sampling distributions of the mean vector and covariance matrix; Hotellings T2; simultaneous inference; one-way MANOVA; discriminant analysis; principal components; canonical correlation; factor analysis. Intensive use of computer analyses and real data sets.
135.prereq_text: (STA 130B C- or better or STA 131B C- or better); (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better); MAT 167 recommended.

137.title: Applied Time Series Analysis
137.description: Time series relationships; univariate time series models: trend, seasonality, correlated errors; regression with correlated errors; autoregressive models; autoregressive moving average models; spectral analysis: cyclical behavior and periodicity, measures of periodicity, periodogram; linear filtering; prediction of time series; transfer function models.
137.prereq_text: STA 108 C- or better; (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better).

138.title: Analysis of Categorical Data
138.description:
Varieties of categorical data, cross-classifications, contingency tables, tests for independence. Multidimensional tables and log-linear models, maximum likelihood estimation; tests of goodness-of-fit. Logit
models, linear logistic models. Analysis of incomplete tables. Packaged computer programs, analysis of real data.

141A.title: Fundamentals of Statistical Data Science
141A.description: Introduction to computing for data analysis & visualization, and simulation, using a high-level language (e.g., R). Computational reasoning, computationally intensive statistical methods, reading tabular & non-standard data.
141A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken STA 141 or STA 242.
141A.prereq_text: STA 108 C- or better or STA 106 C- or better.

141B.title: Data & Web Technologies for Data Analysis
141B.description: Essentials of using relational databases and SQL. Processing data in blocks. Scraping Web pages and using Web services/APIs. Basics of text mining. Interactive data visualization with Web technologies. Computational data workflow and best practices. Statistical methods.

141C.title: Big Data & High Performance Statistical Computing
141C.description: High-performance computing in high-level data analysis languages; different computational approaches and paradigms for efficient analysis of big data; interfaces to compiled languages; R and Python programming languages; high-level parallel computing; MapReduce; parallel algorithms and reasoning.
141C.prereq_text: STA 141B C- or better or (STA 141A C- or better,  (ECS 010 C- or better or ECS 032A C- or better or ECS 032AV C- or better)).

142A.title: Statistical Learning I
142A.description: Fundamental concepts and methods in statistical learning with emphasis on supervised learning. Principles, methodologies and applications of parametric and nonparametric regression, classification, resampling and model selection techniques.
142A.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units of credit for students who have previously taken ECS 171.
142A.prereq_text: STA 141A C- or better; (STA 130A C- or better or STA 131A C- or better or MAT 135A C- or better); (MAT 022A C- or better or MAT 027A C- or better or MAT 067 C- or better); STA 131A or MAT 135A preferred; MAT 167 recommended.

145.title: Bayesian Statistical Inference
145.description: Subjective probability, Bayes Theorem, conjugate priors, non-informative priors, estimation, testing, prediction, empirical Bayes methods, properties of Bayesian procedures, comparisons with classical procedures, approximation techniques, Gibbs sampling, hierarchical Bayesian analysis, applications, computer implemented data analysis.
145.prereq_text: STA 130A C- or better or STA 131A C- or better or MAT 135A C- or better.
