160.title: Practice in Statistical Data Science
160.description: Principles and practice of interdisciplinary, collaborative data analysis; complete case study review and team data analysis project.

192.title: Internship in Statistics
192.description: Work experience in statistics.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

194HA.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HA.description: Directed reading, research and writing, culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of a faculty advisor.

194HB.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
194HB.description: Directed reading, research and writing, culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of a faculty advisor.

200B.title: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics I
200B.description: Sampling, methods of estimation, bias-variance decomposition, sampling distributions, Fisher information, confidence intervals, and some elements of hypothesis testing.

207.title: Statistical Methods for Research II
207.description: Linear and nonlinear statistical models emphasis on concepts, methods/data analysis using professional level software. Topics include linear mixed models, repeated measures, generalized linear models, model selection, analysis of missing data, and multiple testing procedures.
207.prereq_text: STA 206; knowledge of vectors and matrices.

220.title: Data & Web Technologies for Data Analysis
220.description: Essentials of using relational databases and SQL. Processing data in blocks. Scraping Web pages and using Web services/APIs. Basics of text mining. Interactive data visualization with Web technologies. Computational data workflow and best practices. Statistical Methods.

223.title: Biostatistics: Generalized Linear Models
223.description: Likelihood and linear regression; generalized linear model; Binomial regression; case-control studies; dose-response and bioassay; Poisson regression; Gamma regression; quasi-likelihood models; estimating equations; multivariate GLMs.

231B.title: Mathematical Statistics II
231B.description: Second part of a three-quarter sequence on mathematical statistics. Emphasizes hypothesis testing (including multiple testing), as well as theory for linear models.

232B.title: Applied Statistics II
232B.description: Alternative approaches to regression, model selection, nonparametric methods amenable to linear model framework and their applications.
232B.prereq_text: STA 106; STA 108; STA 131A; STA 131B; STA 131C; STA 232A; MAT 167.

235B.title: Probability Theory
235B.description: Measure-theoretic foundations, abstract integration, independence, laws of large numbers, characteristic functions, central limit theorems. Weak convergence in metric spaces, Brownian motion, invariance principle. Conditional expectation. Topics selected from: martingales, Markov chains, ergodic theory.
235B.prereq_text: STA 235A or MAT 235A; or consent of instructor.

250.title: Topics in Applied & Computational Statistics
250.description: Resampling, nonparametric and semiparametric methods, incomplete data analysis, diagnostics, multivariate and time series analysis, applied Bayesian methods, sequential analysis and quality control, categorical data analysis, spatial and image analysis, computational biology, functional data analysis, models for correlated data, learning theory.

260.title: Statistical Practice & Data Analysis
260.description: Principles and practice of interdisciplinary collaboration in statistics, statistical consulting, ethical aspects, and basics of data analysis and study design. Emphasis on practical consulting and collaboration of statisticians with clients and scientists under instructor supervision.
260.prereq_text: STA 207 or STA 232B; working knowledge of advanced statistical software and the equivalent of STA 207 or STA 232B.

290.title: Seminar in Statistics
290.description: Seminar on advanced topics in probability and statistics.

298.title: Directed Group Study
298.description: Special topics in Statistics appropriate for study at the graduate level.

299D.title: Dissertation Research
299D.description: Research in Statistics under the supervision of major professor.
299D.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; advancement to candidacy for Ph.D.

200B.title: Foundational Theories of Religion
200B.description: Survey of classical 19th and 20th century approaches to the study of religion.
200B.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

210B.title: Special Topics in Asian Religious Cultures
210B.description: Comparative, interpretive study of the treatment of specific topics in Asian religious cultures.
210B.prereq_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

297.title: Directed Independent Study: Thematic & Regional Area of Specialization or Area of Competence
297.description: Directed Independent Study in the Thematic Area of Specialization (TAOS), Regional Area of Specialization (RAOS), or Area of Competence (AOC) culminating in a term paper.

192.title: Internship in General Surgery
192.description: Supervised work experience in general surgery and related fields.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Upper division standing; approval of project prior to period of internship by preceptor.

199.title: Special Study in General Surgery for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study in general surgery for advanced undergraduates.
199.prereq_text: Advanced undergraduate student with consent of instructor.

430.title: Surgery Clerkship
430.description: Eight week general surgery clerkship includes GI, Burn, Oncology, Plastics, Vascular Cardiothoracic, consult, transplant and trauma.  Clerkship assignments are at UCDMC. Daily core material presentations and reading assignments.  Student involvement includes work-up and care of surgical patients.
430.prereq_text: Approval by School of Medicine Committee on Student Progress.

461.title: Surgery Burn Unit Clerkship
461.description: Rotation through Surgery Specialty Clinics: Vascular, GI, GU, Thoracic, Plastic, Radiotherapy. Work up one new and two return visit patients. Presents consult to on-site faculty. Weekly review with preceptor and course director. Reading assignments to add perspective for in-depth discussions.
461.prereq_text: SUR 430; and consent of instructor; fourth-year medical student or third-year medical student.

462.title: Surgery Trauma Service Clerkship
462.description: Work as an extern on one of the two general surgery trauma teams. Participate in resuscitation and management of critically injured patients. Team hours consist of 24 hours on, and 24 hours off.
462.prereq_text: SUR 430; consent of instructor; fourth-year medical student, or third-year medical student.

465.title: Surgery Intensive Care Unit
465.description: Focuses on single family, attached, detached, multi-family, and light commercial development. Study factors which make up successful real estate developments. Consider financial aspects involved in land acquisition, land development, construction, and project lending.

467.title: Surgical Oncology
467.description: Students actively participate in management of patients requiring surgery for cancer, endocrine disease and selected general surgical problems. Cases include malignant melanoma, sarcomas, gastrointestinal cancer, head and neck pathology, and metastatic malignancies. Attending rounds daily. Four teaching conferences weekly.
467.prereq_text: SUR 430; and consent of instructor; fourth-year medical student, or third-year medical student.

468.title: Cardiothoracic Surgery Clerkship
468.description: Student works as an extern on the Cardiothoracic Surgical Service, participating in perioperative management and operations on the heart, lungs, mediastinum, and other thoracic structures. Regularly scheduled teaching conferences are conducted.
468.prereq_text: SUR 430; and consent of instructor; fourth-year medical student, or third-year medical student.

471.title: Gastrointestinal Surgery
471.description: Student participates on the GI Surgery Service, working under the immediate supervision of the faculty and surgical housestaff, involving the full spectrum of gastrointestinal diseases performed by the medical student.
471.prereq_text: SUR 430; IMD 430; PED 430; and consent of instructor. Fourth-year medical student or third-year medical student.

472.title: Vascular Surgery
472.description: Student participates on the vascular surgery service and in the management and operations of arterial and venous system, exclusive of diseases that require cardiopulmonary bypass for treatment. Includes patient care responsibilities with appropriate supervision.
472.prereq_text: SUR 430; IMD 430; PED 430; and consent of instructor; fourth-year medical student or third-year medical student.

475.title: Pediatric Surgery
475.description: Care of patients with neonatal congenital surgical problems. Fluid and electrolyte management in infants. General experience with acquired surgical diseases in children.
475.prereq_text: SUR 430; and consent of instructor; fourth-year medical student or third-year medical student.

476.title: Surgical Consult
476.description: Function as acting intern working in parallel with interns on the service. Consult on all non-trauma patients in the emergency room, on the wards, and also participate in the operating room.
476.prereq_text: SUR 430; consent of instructor; successful completion of acting internship in any specialty

477.title: Clinically Oriented Anatomy
477.description: Anatomy of selected regions of the body using cadaver dissection, prosections and interactive CD ROMs. Anatomical relationships relevant to common surgical procedures. Surgical and interventional radiology procedures.
477.prereq_text: Completion of three years of medical school.

480.title: Insights in Surgery
480.description: Individualized activities, including ward rounds, subspecialty clinics and conferences, grand rounds, and observation of a variety of surgical procedures.
480.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; medical student in good academic standing.

484.title: Multidisciplinary Experience in Endocrine Neoplasia
484.description: Consists predominately of multidisciplinary clinical experiences focusing on the diagnosis and management of patients with benign and malignant thyroid disease, parathyroid disorders, benign and malignant adrenal disease, pituitary neoplasia, and multiple endocrine neoplasia syndromes.

498.title: Group Study
498.description: Directed reading and discussion and/or laboratory investigation on selected topics.

499.title: Laboratory Research
499.description: Laboratory research on surgically related problems. Participation in projects to include the following: burn, nutrition, oncology, transplant and others.
499.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of second year of medical school.

092.title: Internship
092.description: Lower-division internship for students enrolled in the Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems program of study.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.

098.title: Directed Group Study
098.description: Group study on focused topics in Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems. Varies according to instructor. Course plan is adapted to student need and interest in conjunction with the expertise of the instructor.

099.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
099.description: Under faculty supervision, students pursue a special or individualized course of study related to Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems.

191A.title: Workshop on Food System Sustainability
191A.description: First in a two-quarter senior capstone course sequence. Identify projects addressing specific problems and opportunities of sustainable agriculture and food systems, form multidisciplinary teams, and identify and consult with key stakeholders to understand their needs and concerns.
191A.credit_limit_text: No credit to students who have taken ESP 191A.
191A.prereq_text: PLS 015; CRD 020; ARE 121; PLS 150; or consent of instructor; upper division standing.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Upper-division internship for students enrolled in the Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems program of study.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

197T.title: Tutoring in Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems
197T.description: Undergraduates assist the instructor by tutoring students in regularly scheduled courses that fulfill SA&FS major requirements.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

197TC.title: SA&FS Tutoring in the Community
197TC.description: Undergraduates assist the instructor by tutoring in the community in settings related to Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems.
197TC.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Group study on focused topics in Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems. Varies according to instructor. Course plan is adapted to student need and interest in conjunction with the expertise of the instructor.
198.prereq_text: Consent of instructor;  upper division standing.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Under faculty supervision, advanced students pursue a special or individualized course of study related to Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems.
199.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

134.title: Systems Biology: From Biological Circuits to Biological Systems
134.description: Application of systems theory to understanding the properties of biological networks in a variety of model organisms. Local biological circuits and genome-scale biological networks. Network motifs, robustness, modeling, emergent properties and integration of networks.
134.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit if student has taken BIS 134.
134.prereq_text: (BIS 101 or BIS 101V); (MCB 121 or PLB 113); (MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 019C or MAT 021B or MAT 021BH); or consent of instructor; BIS 015L recommended.

160.title: Ghosts of the Machine: How Technology Rewires our Senses
160.description: Historical, aesthetic and critical approaches to how information technologies produced ghost effects or a sense of terror in response to new media like the photograph, gramophone, film, typewriter, computer, Turing Machine. Focus on technological media transforms sense perception.

211.title: Energy & Transportation Modeling for Policy Analysis
211.description: Development of energy and transportation models for policy analysis. Methods for modeling transportation, electricity, fuels, resources, and infrastructure systems.

220.title: Transportation Policy
220.description: Application of policy concepts to the transportation context. Overview of the transportation policy landscape. Critical challenges in transportation including sustainability and mobility justice.

224.title: Transportation Equity & Justice
224.description: Topics in transportation equity and justice. Theories of mobility justice, review of historical planning and policy, evaluation of equity analyses, and investigation of equity across mode and domain specific topics in transportation.

225.title: Bicycle & Pedestrian Planning & Design
225.description: Principles of bicycle and pedestrian planning and design. Safety, behavior, and performance metrics in planning and design. City-scale planning in the US in the context of regional, state, and national policy. Lessons learned from outside the US. Weekend field trips are required.

281.title: ITS Transportation Seminar Series
281.description: Transportation seminars by guest speakers, on varied topics.

193.title: Washington Center Research Seminar
193.description: Core academic component of Washington Program offered every quarter. Topics coordinated with internships. Research draws on resources uniquely available in Washington, DC. Supervised preparation of extensive paper.

001.title: Introduction to Academic Literacies
001.description: Introduction to reading and composing processes and key rhetorical concepts for academic literacies. Multiple drafts of composing projects in a variety of genres and modes with feedback from peers and the instructor.
001.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 001Y or UWP 001V.
001.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

001A.title: Writers’ Workshop
001A.description: Writing course focuses on the development of writing and revision strategies, exploring ways to understand a writing task; to develop appropriate content for a writing task; to revise content to reflect competence as a communicator.
001A.prereq_text: Has not yet completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR) required and concurrent enrollment in (UWP 001 (can be concurrent) or UWP 001V (can be concurrent) or UWP 001Y (can be concurrent));

001V.title: Introduction to Academic Literacies: Online
001V.description: Introduction to reading and composing processes and key rhetorical concepts for academic literacies. Multiple drafts of composing projects in a variety of genres and modes with feedback from peers and the instructor.
001V.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken UWP 001 or UWP 001Y.
001V.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

001Y.title: Introduction to Academic Literacies
001Y.description: Introduction to reading and composing processes and key rhetorical concepts for academic literacies. Multiple drafts of composing projects in a variety of genres and modes with feedback from peers and the instructor.
001Y.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have taken UWP 001 or UWP 001V.
001Y.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

007.title: Practices in College Reading & Writing
007.description: Development of skills required for success in college-level writing across genres and disciplines. Integrates reading, critical thinking, and written communication, using texts from across the curriculum. Course is equivalent to UWP  007Y/V/M/MY.
007.credit_limit_text: Students who do not earn a grade that fulfills ELWR but that confers unit credit (a grade of C-, D+, D, or D-) can repeat the course to complete the ELWR and to replace their previous grade, but will not receive additional unit credit. Students who fail the course (receive a grade of F) can repeat the course to complete the ELWR, to replace their previous grade, and to receive the unit credit for the course. Not open for credit to students who have completed the ELWR.

007M.title: Practices in College Reading & Writing for Multilingual Writers
007M.description: Development of multilingual writers' composition and English language skills across genres and disciplines. Integrates college-level reading, critical thinking, and written communication, using texts from across the curriculum. Equivalent to UWP 007/Y/V/MY.
007M.credit_limit_text: No credit for students who have completed UWP 007, UWP 023, or WLD 057.
007M.prereq_text: Enrollment via campus placement (using the English Language Placement Exam or Analytical Writing Placement Exam) or after successful completion of UWP 022.

007V.title: Practices in College Reading & Writing
007V.description: Development of skills required for success in college-level writing across genres and disciplines. Integrates reading, critical thinking, and written communication, using texts from across the curriculum. Course is equivalent to UWP  007/Y/M/MY.
007V.credit_limit_text: Students who do not earn a grade that fulfills ELWR but that confers unit credit (a grade of C-, D+, D, or D-) can repeat the course to complete the ELWR and to replace their previous grade, but will not receive additional unit credit. Students who fail the course (receive a grade of F) can repeat the course to complete the ELWR, to replace their previous grade, and to receive the unit credit for the course. Not open for credit to students who have completed the ELWR.

007Y.title: Practices in College Reading & Writing
007Y.description: Development of skills required for success in college-level writing across genres and disciplines. Integrates reading, critical thinking, and written communication, using texts from across the curriculum. Course is equivalent to UWP  007/V/M/MY.
007Y.credit_limit_text: Students who do not earn a grade that fulfills ELWR but that confers unit credit (a grade of C-, D+, D, or D-) can repeat the course to complete the ELWR and to replace their previous grade, but will not receive additional unit credit. Students who fail the course (receive a grade of F) can repeat the course to complete the ELWR, to replace their previous grade, and to receive the unit credit for the course. Not open for credit to students who have completed the ELWR.

011.title: Popular Science & Technology Writing
011.description: Positioning of science and technology in society as reflected and constructed in popular texts. Topics include genre theory, demarcation, rhetorical figures, forms of qualitative and quantitative reasoning, and the epistemic role of popularization in science.

012.title: Writing & Visual Rhetoric
012.description: Introduction to writing needs, conventions, and genres in design contexts. Emphasis on applying critical reading, analysis, and writing skills to designed products, such as graphics, visual communications, and clothes, and designed spaces, such as exhibitions and interior architecture.

016.title: Writing with Artificial Intelligence
016.description: Composing with artificial intelligence (AI) tools; prompting, editing, and refining AI-generated content. Critical evaluation and integration of AI tools into writing processes. Development of professional and academic writing through hands-on projects; emphasis on voice, integrity, and effective AI use in research and drafting.
016.prereq_text: Completion of Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR).

022.title: Intermediate Academic Reading & Writing for Multilingual Students
022.description: Reading and writing short multi-paragraph texts for academic purposes. Suitable for students whose primary home language was not English.

101.title: Advanced Composition
101.description: Instruction for students in all disciplines in advanced principles of academic and professional writing. Focus on writing tasks both within and beyond the academy. May be taught abroad.
101.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

101V.title: Advanced Composition
101V.description: Instruction for students in all disciplines in advanced principles of academic and professional writing. Focus on writing tasks both within and beyond the academy.
101V.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better; upper division standing.

101Y.title: Advanced Composition
101Y.description: Instruction for students in all disciplines in advanced principles of academic and professional writing.  Focus on writing tasks both within and beyond the academy.
101Y.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

102B.title: Writing in the Disciplines: Biology
102B.description: Advanced instruction in writing in biology.
102B.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ENL 102B.
102B.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

102E.title: Writing in the Disciplines: Engineering
102E.description: Advanced instruction in writing in engineering.
102E.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

102H.title: Writing in the Disciplines: Human Development & Psychology
102H.description: Advanced instruction in writing and practice in effective styles of communication in Human Development & Psychology.
102H.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed UWP 102A in the same academic field.
102H.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

102J.title: Writing in the Disciplines: Fine Arts
102J.description: Advanced instruction in writing about the arts and practice in effective styles of communication.
102J.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have completed UWP 102A in the same academic field.
102J.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104A.title: Writing in the Professions: Business Writing
104A.description: Effective communication in and for organizations, including corporations, government agencies, and non-profit. Suitable for students entering careers such as management, public relations, and grant writing.
104A.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104AY or UWP 104AV.
104A.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104AV.title: Writing in the Professions: Business Writing
104AV.description: Effective communication in and for organizations, including corporations, government agencies, and nonprofit. Suitable for students entering careers such as management, public relations, and grant writing.
104AV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104A or 104AY.
104AV.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104AY.title: Writing in the Professions: Business Writing
104AY.description: Effective communication in and for organizations, including corporations, government agencies, and nonprofit. Suitable for students entering careers such as management, public relations, and grant writing.
104AY.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104A or UWP 104AV.
104AY.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104B.title: Writing in the Professions: Law
104B.description: Advanced principles of critical thinking, argumentation, and style, with special emphasis on their application in the legal profession. Suitable for students planning careers in law, business, administration, or management.
104B.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104C.title: Writing in the Professions: Journalism
104C.description: Non-fiction for magazines and newspapers, with attention to style and language. Emphasis on research, interviewing, market analysis, and query letters. May be taught abroad.
104C.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104D.title: Writing in the Professions: Elementary & Secondary Education
104D.description: Advanced expository writing in the contemporary American classroom. Strongly recommended for teaching credential candidates.
104D.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104E.title: Writing in the Professions: Science
104E.description: Writing abstracts, research proposals, scientific papers, other forms of scientific communication. Presenting data graphically. Primarily for students engaged in or planning careers in basic or applied research.
104E.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing or enrollment in a graduate science curriculum.

104F.title: Writing in the Professions: Health
104F.description: Advanced expository writing common in the health professions, emphasizing effective communication between the writer and different audiences. Topics relate to health, disability, and disease. Suitable for students planning careers in professions such as medicine, dentistry, physical therapy, optometry.
104F.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104FY or UWP 104FV.
104F.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104FV.title: Writing in the Professions: Health
104FV.description: Advanced expository writing common in the health professions, emphasizing effective communication between the writer and different audiences. Topics relate to health, disability, and disease. Suitable for students planning careers in professions such as medicine, dentistry, physical therapy, optometry.
104FV.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104F or UWP 104FY.
104FV.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104FY.title: Writing in the Professions: Health
104FY.description: Advanced expository writing common in the health professions, emphasizing effective communication between the writer and different audiences. Topics relate to health, disability, and disease. Suitable for students planning careers in professions such as medicine, dentistry, physical therapy, optometry.
104FY.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104F or UWP 104FV.
104FY.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better; UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

104J.title: Writing in the Professions: Writing for Social Justice
104J.description: Advanced instruction in writing for Social Justice, using an interdisciplinary approach combining feminist, critical race, ethnic, cultural, and transnational studies; practice in techniques of research and styles of communication for diverse audiences. Suitable for activists in community organizing, non-profits, politics. May be taught abroad.
104J.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better; and upper division standing.

104T.title: Writing in the Professions: Technical Writing
104T.description: Communicating effectively about technology and other technical subjects to varied audiences for varied purposes. Suitable for students entering professions that require communicating technical information to subject matter experts, managers, technicians, and non-specialists.
104T.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken UWP 104A prior to fall 2012.
104T.prereq_text: UWP 001 C- or better or UWP 001V C- or better or UWP 001Y C- or better or ENL 003 C- or better or ENL 003V C- or better or COM 001 C- or better or COM 002 C- or better or COM 003 C- or better or COM 004 C- or better or NAS 005 C- or better or NAS 005V C- or better; and upper division standing.

106.title: English Grammar
106.description: Survey of present-day English grammar as informed by contemporary linguistic theories. The major syntactic structures of English; their variation across dialects, styles, and registers; their development; and their usefulness in describing the conventions of English.
106.prereq_text: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or ENL 003 or ENL 003V or LIN 001 or LIN 001Y; or consent of instructor.

110B.title: Report Writing
110B.description: Communication skills needed to excel in report writing. Extensive practice in writing successful reports, emphasizing the role of reports in decision-making processes and the rhetorical work that particular genre moves, conventions, and elements do.
110B.prereq_text: (UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y); or the equivalent.

112A.title: Introduction to Professional Editing
112A.description: Introduction to general editing practices and principles, with an emphasis on professional editing in organizational contexts, including academia and the workplace. Extensive practice in copy, comprehensive, and collaborative editing.
112A.prereq_text: satisfaction of the upper division writing requirement.

197T.title: Tutoring in Writing
197T.description: Tutoring one-on-one or leading small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with a writing course.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

197TC.title: Community Tutoring in Writing
197TC.description: Field experience, with individuals or in K-12 classroom instruction, focusing on reading- and writing-to-learn strategies in any subject area.
197TC.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.

198.title: Directed Group Study
198.description: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
198.prereq_text: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or ENL 003 or ENL 003V or equivalent course; consent of instructor.

225.title: English for International/ESL Graduate Students
225.description: Multi-skills ESL course designed to help international/ESL students improve their English language skills for successful academic study. Emphasis on writing, speaking, listening, reading, and academic culture.
225.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 025.

226.title: Writing for International Graduate Students
226.description: Focuses on writing needed for academic work, including summaries, critiques, research & grant proposals, memos, resumes, and research papers. Includes a review of grammar needed for writing and some focus on reading skills and American vocabulary and idioms.
226.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 026.

002.title: Elementary Urdu
002.description: Introduction to conversation, vocabulary, and sentence structure in the Urdu form of Hindi/Urdu using the Nastaʿliq script in the context of the shared culture of Hindi/Urdu. Emphasis on conversation, vocabulary, and sentence structure.
002.credit_limit_text: Not open for credit to students who have taken HIN 002.

197T.title: Tutoring in Urdu
197T.description: Tutoring in undergraduate courses, including leadership in small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with departmental courses.
197T.prereq_text: (HIN 023 B or better; or consent of instructor); consent of Program Director required.

003.title: Introduction to Winemaking
003.description: Overview of the history of wine, viticulture, fermentation, winery operations, the physiology of wine consumption, wines produced in California and other major wine-producing regions and the sensory evaluation of wine.

101B.title: Viticultural Practices
101B.description: Theory, principles, and practices of pruning and grapevine propagation.  Plant materials and the certification process, weed control and weed identification, wood diseases, and frost protection. One field trip required.

103.title: Commercial Winemaking
103.description: Materials, processes, equipment, and quality control in commercial winemaking. Production stages, timelines, and styles across wine types. Risk assessment and control measures. Basic sensory techniques for understanding wine characteristics.
103.prereq_text: VEN 003 C- or better; or consent of instructor.

110.title: Grapevine Growth & Physiology
110.description: Botanical aspects including morphology and domestication will precede lectures covering flower development and energy budget concepts. Impact of physiological variables such as photosynthesis translocation, mineral nutrition, and water relations on fruit ripening and composition will be covered.

125.title: Wine Types & Sensory Evaluation
125.description: Principles of sensory evaluation and application to wines. Factors influencing wine flavor, data from sensory analysis of model solutions.

125L.title: Sensory Evaluation of Wine Laboratory
125L.description: Sensory evaluation of wines and model systems using discrimination tests, ranking, descriptive analysis and time-intensity analysis. Data will be analyzed by appropriate statistical tests and the results interpreted in extensive weekly lab reports.

128.title: Wine Microbiology
128.description: Nature, development, physiology, biochemistry and control of yeasts and bacteria involved in the making, aging and spoilage of wine.
128.prereq_text: (VEN 123,  VEN 124,  MIC 102,  MIC 103L); VEN 125, VEN 126 recommended.

128L.title: Wine Microbiology Laboratory
128L.description: Nature, development, physiology, biochemistry and control of yeasts and bacteria involved in the making, aging and spoilage of wine.
128L.prereq_text: VEN 123; VEN 124; VEN 128 (can be concurrent); MIC 103L.

140.title: Distilled Beverage Technology
140.description:
Distillation principles and practices; production technology of brandy,
whiskey, rum, vodka, gin, and other distilled beverages; characteristics of raw materials, fermentation, distillation, and aging.

192.title: Internship
192.description: Work experience related to Fermentation Science (Enology) or Plant Science (Viticulture) majors. Internships must be approved and supervised by a member of the department or major faculty, but are arranged by the student.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.

199.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
199.description: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.

270.title: Critical Evaluation of Scientific Literature
270.description: Contemporary research topics in biological sciences. Discussion of recent research articles in a special topic area chosen by instructor. Intended to develop skills in critical evaluation of scientific publications.

290C.title: Advanced Research Conference
290C.description: Planning and results of research programs, proposals, and experiments. Discussion and critical evaluation of original research being conducted by the group. Discussion led by individual research instructors for research group.

297T.title: Tutoring in Viticulture & Enology
297T.description: Designed for graduate students who desire teaching experience, but are not teaching assistants. Student contact primarily in laboratory or discussion sections, and under direction of a faculty member.

050.title: Natural History of California's Wild Vertebrates
050.description: Examination of the natural history of California's wild vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals), including their biogeography, systematics, ecology and conservation status.

092.title: Internship
092.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
department. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
092.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.

103.title: Applied Statistics for Wildlife Research
103.description: Introduction to basic statistical concepts and methods as tools for fish and wildlife research. Application of general guiding principles of developing research questions and projects, basic probability theory, statistical estimation (correlation, regression, ANOVA, Chi-square test) and hypothesis testing. Introduction of some specialized analytical techniques, such as population dynamics modeling and time series analysis.
103.credit_limit_text: Only 2 units credit allowed to students who have completed STA 013, STA 100, or PLS 120.
103.prereq_text: (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B) or equivalent course; or consent of instructor.

130.title: Physiological Ecology of Wildlife
130.description: Principles of physiological ecology, emphasizing vertebrates. Ecological, evolutionary, and behavioral perspectives on physiological mechanisms used by animals to adapt to their environment, including consideration of climate-change and other threats to biodiversity. Tropical, temperate, and polar ecosystems are highlighted.
130.prereq_text: (BIO 001 or BIS 002B); EVE 101 or ESP 100 recommended; or consent of instructor.

134.title: Herpetology
134.description: Evolution and ecology of the world’s diverse reptiles and amphibians. Emphasis on adaptations to environments, species interactions, management, and conservation.
134.prereq_text: (BIS 002A or BIO 002); (BIS 002B or BIO 001); (BIS 002C or BIO 003); upper division ecology course recommended.

134L.title: Herpetology Laboratory
134L.description: Diagnostic characteristics and functional attributes of amphibians and reptiles, emphasizing ecological, bio-geographic and phylogenetic patterns. Field experience with common species of reptiles and amphibians in the Davis area.
134L.prereq_text: WFC 134 (can be concurrent); consent of instructor.

135.title: Wetland Ecology & Conservation
135.description: Ecology of wetlands, including wetland formation and physical factors, types of wetland ecosystems, and restoration, law, and climate change.
135.credit_limit_text: Not open to students who have previously completed ESP 155.
135.prereq_text: BIO 001 or BIS 002B; or consent of instructor; EVE 101 or ESP 100 recommended.

152.title: Ecology of Human-Wildlife Conflicts
152.description: Ecological approaches to managing wild vertebrates that come into conflict with agriculture, public health, or the conservation of biodiversity.

154.title: Conservation Biology
154.description: Introduction to conservation biology and background to the biological issues and controversies surrounding loss of species and habitats.
154.prereq_text: BIO 001 or BIS 002B; or the equivalent.

168.title: Climate Change Ecology
168.description: Ecological responses to current and expected future climate change, across levels of biological organization from individuals to ecosystems.
168.prereq_text: (BIO 001 or BIS 002B); EVE 101 or ESP 100 recommended; or consent of instructor.

192.title: Internship
192.description:
Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the
department. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
192.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Completion of 84 units.

195.title: Field & Laboratory Research
195.description: Critique and practice of research methods applied to field and/or laboratory environments of wild vertebrates. Work independently or in small groups to design experimental protocol, analyze data, and report their findings.
195.prereq_text: (WFC 110L or WFC 111L or WFC 120L); (WFC 121 or WFC 130); EVE 101; or the equivalent of EVE 101, and consent of instructor.

197T.title: Tutoring in Wildlife & Fisheries
197T.description: Experience in teaching under guidance of faculty member.
197T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Major in Wildlife, Fish, and Conservation Biology.

290.title: Seminar
290.description: Seminar devoted to a highly specific research topic in any area of wildlife or fisheries biology. Special topic selected for a quarter will vary depending on interests of instructor and students.

290C.title: Research Group Conference
290C.description: Weekly conference on research problems, progress and techniques in wildlife and fishery sciences.

297T.title: Supervised Teaching in Wildlife & Fisheries Biology
297T.description: Tutoring and teaching students in undergraduate courses in Wildlife, Fish, & Conservation Biology. Weekly conferences with instructor; evaluations of teaching; preparing for and conducting demonstrations, laboratories, and discussions; preparing and grading examinations.
297T.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Meet qualifications for teaching assistant; graduate standing.

138.title: Critical Fashion Studies
138.description: Feminist cultural studies of style-fashion-dress through transnational circuits, personal subjectivities. Fashion as means of gender oppression and liberation. Histories and discourses of  masculinities and femininities. Clothing works on global assembly line. Use of dress in construction/regulation of identities.

182.title: Globalization, Gender & Culture
182.description: Critical gender analysis of globalization as a process of interconnected cultural, social and economic transformations inflected by gender, nation, class and race/ethnicity. Critical self-reflection and social observation skills.
